title: A large impersonal place with an on time check in problem and other issues
text:
If you are looking for a huge, grand hotel experience, this place may be for you, but I found it to be impersonal and the staff lacking warmth and sometimes manners. They seem to avoid engagement with guests whenever possible. Add that to the fact that each morning and evening, there are 2 or 3 bus loads of tour groups gathering in the lobby and right outside the hotel. When I encountered this on my first evening and needed a taxi, I asked the doorman whether he could get me a taxi or whether I should order an Uber. He simply nodded and walked away, so I ordered an Uber.

The checkin counter must be understaffed, as I had to wait in a long line for about 15 minutes, only to be told that my room was not ready. Official checkin is 2pm, but my room was not ready until 5pm. I should have taken seriously the many previous TripAdvisor reviewers who had the same experience. They gave me a drink voucher in the bar as compensation, but I didn’t use it because I wasn’t in the mood for a drink after international travel or any other day because I’m not a bar person. And the checkin person said he would phone me when my room was ready but never did. I only found out it was ready after checking.

The breakfast buffet is fine but nothing special and over my 3 days there, several times I bumped into servers who cut me off or crossed in front of me as I navigated to and from the buffet. I had dinner in the restaurant straight from a long day of exploring and apparently didn’t meet the maitre d’s standards, as he tried everything in his power to avoid seating me in the mostly empty restaurant at 6:15pm. Finally, he phoned the front desk to verify that I was a hotel guest and ran out of excuses. After all that trouble, I found the menu limited, the food mediocre and the service bordering on surly.

My suite was large and nice, although there was very low water pressure in the shower. And oddly, despite mirrors everywhere, not one was full length. Also, all of the glasses and coffee mugs in the minibar were dirty.

So one star for the decent room and for the two people working there who were genuinely nice to me during my 3 days there.

title: Amidst the chaos of Fashion week, their service and warmth shines !
text: We stayed during the Paris Fashion Week Chaos. By Chaos I mean 100% occupancy rates , masses of people in the hotel lobby daily , packed breakfasts, traffic jams and no taxis available in the middle of Paris. However, this hotel managed to keep things running efficiently & effortlessly, with every staff giving a smile, polite greeting or a simple Bonjour Madame each time you walk by. You feel the warmth of service even though you know that they are stretched . Yes, I didn’t get my guaranteed upgrade as an Ambassador member but I get it that the hotel is so full and appreciated that they gave me a very large Premium room on the top floor as per my request and even threw in a bottle of champagne and platter of macaroons to celebrate my anniversary with my hubby. This was better than any upgrade. Room was nicely refurbished, bed was very comfortable and the housekeeping team was excellent. Location is excellent as you are at the centre of town. I will return for sure!

One small negative was one day I sat for maybe 30 minutes in a  quiet area in the back of the lobby and a security guard passed me a number of times and then rudely demanded by room number and I think I was only left alone because I answered him quickly. Overall everything was lovely and we would be delighted to return some time.

title: Beautiful, but not sure I would return.
text:
To start, I am an Intercontinental Ambassador and a Diamond member with IHG. I have been a loyal chap for a decade. I was very excited to spend my annual one weekend-night free certificate here. Mind you, the first night was well over $800 but included lounge access.

I entered, but honestly the doormen, there seemed to be several were a little stark. One smiled and said bonjour, the others stood there with not even an attempt to smile. Well anyway, at check-in I was delighted that my room was ready early. Leo was very kind and welcoming. However, no mention of the lounge when given my key. I inquired about access etc, and Leo told me lounge access was not included in my room. Luckily I had saved my confirmation and showed it to him, he then had to ask someone else about it. I really felt as if they were doing me a favor by allowing me entrance to the lounge that I had paid for. I am not sure what Ambassador-Diamond benefits I received, I wasn't asked if I wanted points, a drink, etc. and I am not sure that I received a room upgrade. I am assuming so because my room was great with a view of the Eiffel Tower from not one but two small balconies. 

The lounge is great, there are a lot of snacks and beverages available, the setting is lovely, and it is a quiet and lovely place to sit and relax. 

The hotel is beautiful and in a perfect location, but I just felt out of place for some reason, almost like an intruder, and did not quite belong.

title: Nice Room , Good Location that's about it. Book Ibis instead.
text:
It was a few weeks ago now since I visited the hotel. The hotel is still unfortunately etched in my memory. We’ll start with the good points, it’s a clean hotel, great location, and the room was nice. 

Now for the not so good side. 

We’ll start on arrival and check in, the room wasn’t ready although it was past check-in time. Still, I decided to wait about a bit as surely it doesn’t take that long to clean a room! An hour past and my patience was starting to wear thin. I went back up to the check-in desk and was greeted with total nonchalance. I was informed my room would be ready in another hour, maybe an hour and a half. At that point, it was no more mr nice guy, he rarely comes out as it is. Put me in France, and give me this attitude at a supposed 5 star hotel where I’m paying top summer, inflation, rip-off prices. Think again. The GM was summoned. Told him that we were already 1.5 hrs past the stated check-in time and he was about to see me get a whole lot worse. 

I advised that one would expect, at the minimum, an apology perhaps for not having the room ready, an offer of perhaps a tea or coffee, or glass of champagne whilst we waited. Nothing. Absolutely nothing, at which point he asked if I wanted a drink. My response. No! I may have wanted a drink 1.5 hrs ago, but now I’d like my bloody room! He ran off to personally check the room was up-to standard and came back down to inform me it was. Now why I was supposed to wait around another maybe  1.5 hours for this I’ll never know. When we got to the room it was very pleasant. 

The concierge on the desk were useless throughout our trip, even before our trip when we asked them to book some restaurants for us. Their excuse. They forgot – and now the restaurant is fully booked. So you can’t go. They recommended another place, it was terrible. See my review for Chez Monsieur. 

After one particularly hot day, we got back to the hotel mid-late afternoon and wanted a cold drink at the bar. Approached the bar and was told we’re shut. We’ll open at six, maybe seven pm. What? A five star hotel in the middle of Paris in the middle of summer and your bar is closed at 4pm on Wednesday afternoon??? Explain that one to me again! Obviously no staff around to get a drink so left. Final straw placed on said camels back. 

On the whole, go spend your money somewhere else. This hotel, whilst pleasant offers the service of an Ibis, and you can pick that up a hell of a lot cheaper than this place!

title: Another wonderful stay thanks to Gilles and team
text: We returned again and had a great stay.  We checked in at the Executive Lounge and Gilles gave us a great room on a high floor, but it smelled of mold and mildew so we returned to the lounge and got a room that we could breath in.  Typical Le Grand room.  The main attribute here is the location.  Our view was of the Rue Scribe.  I don't care about Opera views as I don't look out the window too often.  We booked a room with lounge access using our Ambassador weekend certificate.  This time, we had breakfast both morning in the Cafe de la Paix.  Great omelets and many choices of pastries, meats, cheese, etc.  The 2nd morning we were seated in the corner by the window and ignored so I had to go report to the check in area; we then received over attentive service.  The Club Lounge doesn't have the views it did when a 2 floor lounge at the top but is getting better.  This time they had very good evening snacks.  One night shrimp and raw oysters!  Enough so no need to waste money on dinner at a fancy restaurant.  We received drink coupons at check-in and had champagne in the lobby lounge.  Only issue was it took over 15 minutes to receive once we ordered??  We had to check out at the front desk since no one was in the lounge.  (Gilles was off on our last day)  No big issue except we had a bus to catch to Gare du Nord and then a train to Amsterdam.  When Gilles is there, the lounge runs like clockwork, and nothing is too much.  We will be back in the near future and understand the glitches (musky rooms, slow lounge service, staffing issues, etc.)  Merci encore!

title: Simply the Best
text:
Upon arrival we were welcomed by the friendly professional cortege and reception staff who fully explained the hotel layout how to access our room, when and where breakfast was being served.

We had been upgraded needless to  say the  large bright room was amazing! all that you would need. It was spotless  throughout with more than ample supply of teas coffees and hot chocolate and lovely comfy bed .  Great nights sleep with no noise or banging doors with well insulated windows and doors made for perfect rest.                                                                 
   
 Having multi size  compatible  phone charger integrated in the electric clock was a really clever idea  if we had already known this we would not have needed to purchase two international adapters.

The bathroom was a great size ,plenty of towels and toiletries with both shower and  a bath with slippers and robes provided .  

Breakfast the next morning was a slick operation during a busy breakfast service , we were escorted to our table the buffet system was explained there was such a wide selection catering to all needs the hot food was delicious especially the eggs benedict freshly made to order,waiting staff always ensured you had plenty of tea or coffee and helpful to any request.
 
Well feed ready for a days sight seeing in Paris there is a beautiful perfume shop just down from the hotel which has a perfume museum worth a visit. Upon returning in the evening the room daily cleaned and refreshments restocked and fresh towels etc. .

We ate twice in the hotel restaurants  food excellent and very reasonably priced, 
 service fantastic, so attentive and courteous and before dinner selection of nuts olives and warm rolls lovely touch, a big thanks to Sebastian our waiter,the desserts so beautiful especially the apple and cinnamon tart .  

The ambience of this hotel is stunning and level of service exemplary and friendly, that oozes class from top to bottom, the hard working staff from front of house ,to cleaning staff always courteous and helpful complement perfectly their colleagues  in the restaurants and the great food by their chiefs.

Many wonderful memories in a truly beautiful hotel, La Grand have set very high standards and in modernising over the Covid lockdowns was innovate putting their mark as a Parisian leader in the hospitality business and this complements perfectly the service they friendly provide.  

Excellent location for accessing shops and museums located in a bustling area  that overlooks the Opera House acts as a great landmark, well recommend this hotel for a stay.

title: Just misses being 5 star hotel
text:
The first impression of this hotel is that is a grand and beautiful, well located place. It is that, and I would give it a higher overall rating, but there were just some missing details, that, IMO, keep this from a true five star hotel status when compared with others. The beds and pillows are super comfy, the food in Cafe de la Paix is exquisite, and the front desk staff had a room for us when we arrived at 8:00 a.m. 

All good, but then there are a few things that need attention. Only two bath towels in a room for two persons. Even a cheap motel in the US provides three ( albeit THIN) towels. Also in our room, there were no drawers. It made it very difficult to unpack properly. One big problem in our bathroom….no soap in the shower. We needed to bring in large reusable pump bottles of shampoo and body soap. That’s okay, but there was not even a shelf to place them on!!

Also, service from the front desk and concierge were a bit weak. I know we are just at the start of normalcy and staff is short……but MANAGEMENT!! Pay attention to this. We made a request our first day to have the alarm clock fixed. No one came. Our last day we called down to the concierge to ask about assistance with a question. We were told they would call back. Again, no response. Not a five star experience.it’s a shame, it could be a great hotel, with just some stronger oversight and management.

title: Beautiful hotel, inconsistent service
text:
We booked this hotel for the 2nd part of our Paris vacation as a treat & to celebrate couple of milestones. I was in touch with the hotel prior to my stay so that i could organise a surprise and I was assured that would be taken care of complimentary. We checked in slightly early with the intention of leaving our luggage and then coming back in late afternoon to do the ‘actual check in’ of the room but thankfully our room was already ready. We were not recognised for our IHG loyalty at checkin which was really surprising considered this is an Intercontinental and my husband is Platinum and myself Gold and neither were we offered points or drinks (husband checked account later and saw he was given the welcome points but would have been nice to
be given the option). We were hardly given any information at checkin and had to
probe for general queries such as breakfast and was given short and curt replies.. it was a very uncomfortable exchange to say the least.
Room was beautiful as was the hotel however there were few minor issues with the room (stains on the bathtub, shower head leaking from the sides) which wasnt a problem with us and hence we did not mention to the hotel plus as i felt extremely thankful for the early checkin and the ‘supposed surprise’ they were organising for my husband. 
As we left the hotel for the day, i discreetly mentioned to the front desk about the surprise i had organised with their colleague but i was told ‘well u came early, it will be there when u come back as normal check in is not now’ and the lady (another receptionist) seemed almost annoyed and judgemental - might i add that i wanted to pay for the ‘surprise’ but was told it will be complimentary as a ‘welcome amenity’ on the email exchange i had prior. 
We came back to the hotel around 6pm and there’s still nothing. I called the front desk again and the gentleman was far kinder and understanding and he said he would look into it. A knock came to our door almost an hour later where someone brought a bottle of champagne and 2 glasses and left. Husband was in room so no surprise and just the whole thing felt pointless having to continuously ask the front desk 3 times by now. There was no note along with it and at this point i wished i had arranged and paid for this surprise at the crowne plaza we had stayed for the first part of the trip as their service was outstanding. Champagne was not touched til our last night in the hotel where we opened it for the sake of opening it and hardly drank.
Check in went far more smoothly and the receptionist was alot more polite with the Intercontinental standards.
Might i add that the concierge staff we encountered were all amazing, they work so hard and tirelessly and so do the housekeeping team.
All in all, a beautiful hotel in an amazing location but inconsistent service levels across the staff.

title: A room made just for me
text:
We are checking out today, and we absolutely loved the hotel. 

The room 2506 was as it had designed with all my inner thoughts in mind.

The room was large bright and airy with two windows opening to the inner side.
The bed was divine and the cover and pillows excellent l.
It was a big premium room, I would absolutely deem it more like a junior suite in size. Loved the little chaise long and the comfortable chair with the puff.

The welcome amenities were the best strawberries I have had in years, usually the fruit given as ambassador is some not very ripe fruit, but not here and the box of biscuits were appreciated.

The bathroom was without a bath, but honestly I will much rather have a good walk-in shower. And I was pleasantly surprised that the shower had both waterfall and regular shower head. I am actually not a big fan of waterfall shower. Installed it at home and have regretted it - but my husband loves it - soooo

The best part of the stay was the club lounge. Absolutely the very best I have seen. Free flowing champagne, foie gras, oysters, prawns, cakes, candy, etc etc. and few hotels have a better breakfast.

One thing not to miss were the croissants and pain au Chocolate. They were absolutely the best I have tasted, and we go to France around 4 times every year. Spending around 6 weeks of the year in France.

title: Beautiful but no brains
text: Beautiful hotel. Opulent and classy. Unfortunately, during our 3 nights there, we didn’t have hot water in our shower  2 out of the 3 nights when we came back to the room  before dinner. The first time it took 20-30 minutes for someone to come to the room, another 20 or 30 minutes for the first guy to realize he didn’t know what to do, and another 45-60 minutes for the second guy to come and ‘fix’ the problem. By the time they finished it was too late for us to shower and make our dinner reservation. Not a big deal the first night. I was really disappointed when it happened the next night too! At this point we complained to a manager. To his credit, he let us use the shower in a nearby vacant room so we could shower before dinner. They fixed the shower again while we were out. They also gave us a 1 night room credit towards a future stay. The same night we lost power in the middle of the night and when it came back on the HVAC screen flashed on for a long enough period that it woke us up. One final note:  we had a rabbit stuffed animal in the room that disappeared one day. It was white and we assume that it got caught up in a change of sheets. Nonetheless it sums our our experience-disappointing. The hotel is nice and I suspect not everyone there had our issues since people were not lined up complaining. I think they compensated us appropriately but I would much rather have had everything just work and not spend so much of the limited time we had there dealing with these issues.

title: Let down by the reception
text:
We booked for a twin room. We arrived at the hotel way past the check in time and was given a double. Reception  then changed our room to another wing with the two beds pushed together appointed with one single linen set of linen in the room like its a King bed. Had to go down to reception again who assured us that the beds will be separated by housekeeping, We went out for dinner and came back near midnight with nothing done. We called reception again and they went as far as to say that they already did their part to call housekeeping and it was not their fault, and they didn't know why it was not done. Luckily housekeeping finally turned up and separated the bed with 2 set of linens. I found the reception totally off standard. When asked about happy hours at the club lounge and other factual information such as the restaurants, there was a lot of "I think so", and "should be", before trying to get us on our way. She did assured us that the bed would be done in the evening which did not happen. Such reception will not meet the standards of Holiday Inn express. 

We recounted the incident to the manager the next day and the hotel quickly made it up giving us a bottle of champagne and late check out which was very much appreciated. That aside, the staff at the lounge was great. So were the staff at the entrance. of the hotel. 

The room was on he small side but very comfortable and artistically finished. But a lack of USB points was glaring in this day and time.  

The offerings in the lounge was above average but I have experienced better ones. But you do get wines and champagne all day which is a big plus for drinkers.

This is a very beautiful hotel with most staff polite and willing to help. But reception has to seriously buck up. With the rates that the hotel is charging, there are plenty of choices around the area.

title: A fantastic Intercontinental in the heart of Paris.
text:
We returned to the hotel for the 3rd time now, after the major renovations, this time also for a 2-night weekend.

We checked in at 3PM.
Check in was quick, efficient and courteous.
The hotel was kind enough to make sure we got the same room as we did the previous time - Executive Suite 3126.

You could see the stunning results of the renovation the minute you walk in the corridors. Everything look absolutely stunning and you could almost feel the smell of the new materials.

Our room was fantastic and we could hardly recognize it from our last visit, as it was fully renovated and now feels much more modern, but still with a classic Parisian touch.
The room featured 2 beds, a TV and (brand new) sofa, a desk and chair, an armchair and a large coffee table.
There were 2 large cupboards, an empty minibar, a safe and 2 windows facing the opera house.
The windows were renovated as well, and now include 2 sets of windows to eliminate completely any possibility of noise coming from the square next to the opera house. However, this also meant we couldn't get out to the small French balconies of the room.

The bathroom was also completely renovated and included a window facing the opera house, a toilet (with a bidet hose), a sink, a bath tub and a separate shower (with a rather weak water pressure).
The bathroom amenities were from Algoterm and were very nice.

Our welcome gifts included a champagne, some fruits, macaroons, a box of cookies, water and a note from the management.

Breakfast at Café de la Paix was fantastic and included a full breakfast buffet and made to order eggs and hot drinks (I've written a separate review about it).

The new Club lounge is located on the first floor and is absolutely stunning. The renovation process included a brand new lounge, which is perfectly located (although it has no view).
First of all, the lounge feels airy, very large, comfortable, inviting and very modern.
It is open from 7AM until 9PM and features several food offerings as well as all day long drinks:
7:00-11:00 - breakfast.
14:30-17:00 - tea time with numerous macaroons, pastries, sandwiches, cheese and fish.
17:00 onwards - a stunning evening buffet with exquisite selections of foie gras, shrimps, escargot, fresh oysters(!!!), breads, sweets and drinks.
This is BY FAR the best lounge experience we've ever had in Europe and the hotel has certainly raised the bar when it comes to the quality (and quantity) of the food offerings in the lounge. Bravo!!!
The staff at the lounge (and Gilles in particular, as always) - were outstanding.

We were really sad to leave the hotel and finally checked out at 6PM.

A big thank you goes to the hotel's wonderful GM, Mr. Laure, for his incredible hospitality. Merci beaucoup!

Bottom line - this is a spectacular hotel, with a fantastic Club Lounge and team, located in the best area of Paris, and it is now even more gorgeous than before, having completed a major renovation.

This should be your only hotel while visiting Paris, period.

title: nightmare
text: I check in 19 Feb for a 2 night stay, room 3211, shortly after checking in and going to my room a staff member barges in, as an IHG Ambassador/Platinum member he was carrying a welcome gift of 3 satsumas, 1 litre water and a welcome card, I don't believe he knocked/did not hear him knock, luckily was not changing my clothes or similar when he suddenly entered. Tried using phone in room, it didn't work. When I received calls I had to answer them on the phone in the bathroom. Bathroom toiletries (shower gel, conditioner, shampoo) of a very low standard and quality considering the prices this hotel charges, have come across this brand of bathroom toiletries in other hotels of a much lower price (admittedly hotel standard questionable, maybe their overall service levels were even better than this hotel but at a much lower price...), even the standard Intercontinental verbena varieties of bathroom toiletries would have been better. As an Ambassador Platinum member I get a card for a welcome drink, valid only at Le Bar du Grand Hotel, when I try to use it the Bar is closed, a staff member directs me to the Cafe (where a hoovering staff member directs me further on to another public bar where a surly staff member tells me I will have to wait 45 minutes for a table, makes me question why I am staying in this expensive hotel for this level of service....). The room is not even equipped with a pen/pencil or notepad, standard issue even in most 2 or 3 star hotels I think. On my second day I get accosted by a doorman who seeks to block my entering the hotel, asking if I am a resident......... I ask the concierge for a city map, normally one has the expectation of getting a fresh/new map, instead I get one used by someone before with various attractions and routes already marked by pen, being charitable perhaps the hotel is trying to be environmentally friendly and reduce its carbon footprint by recycling such previously used material to new guests............

title: Superb concierge: a great asset for the hotel especially during COVID-19 with frequent flight cancellations and PCR test
text:
(Updated review on this newly renovated Paris Le Grand Hotel.)

LOCATION: 45 minutes to 1 hour and 15 minutes’ drive from CDG Airport, depending on the traffic. The taxi price from the airport is fixed. Since the hotel is located on the right bank of the Seine, the price is EUR 53 all inclusive. 

HOTEL: We stayed here twice in early December 2021. The first time was for 5 nights and the second time for 3 nights. 

The first 5 nights we stayed at a Capucines room on a higher floor. This room was extra quiet due to the additional thick, reinforce glass, 15 cm in front of the traditional French glass windows. The room was clean with comfortable mattress, pillows and duvet. Bathroom has a bathtub with a separate shower cubicle. The shower water pressure was very good here. There were two heaters in the bathroom, one for the towel rail, the other one was under the sink. The heated towel rail was easy to turn on and off, the heater under the sink is another matter entirely. You would have to be a child or a very skinny adult to be able to get under the sink and regulate this heater. 

The last 3 nights, we stayed at a Scribe room on a higher floor. This room has ordinary French glass windows, but since it was located on a higher floor and Rue Scribe was a quiet road, we did have a good night rest here without being disturbed by the noises from the outside. The mattress, the pillows and the duvet were also very good. This room also had a bathtub and a shower cubicle. The shower head here was of an older model and the shower water pressure was not as good as the one at the Capucines room. There was a separate toilet at the entrance, without a hand sink, which we found a bit unhygienic. Otherwise, there was a heated towel rail and another heater under the sink, the same types as the ones in the previous room. 

The housekeepers were all very courteous and fast. 

The Lounge had now been renovated and moved down to the 1st floor by the lifts. It was definitely nicer and brighter than the last one. The food served here however was a total let-down compared to before. The same could be said about the breakfast at the Café de la Paix. The food served here was very basic and bland. Most of the breakfast staff seemed to be very inexperienced. On two separate mornings, we had to tell them to change a coffee cup on our table because it was not properly cleaned. Now and again, they would drop knives or forks on the floor even though the café was rarely busy during early breakfast hours. The breakfast hostesses were also very inexperienced. They often have problem seating and advising guests arriving for breakfast. Once, we were told if we chose to sit away from other customers, due to our social distancing practises, we might not be served coffee or tea because our table was 4 metres away from the nearest waiter station. It turned out she was wrong of course. 

We specifically chose this hotel because we had very good experience with their concierges a few years back. We knew if there was a time for an exceptional concierge, it would be during this COVID-19 pandemic. The concierges here were very helpful and knowledgeable. They would go to great lengths to understand different countries’ arrival requirements for PCR test, paperwork and quarantine hotels. We were especially impressed by one of their concierges, Ms. Léa. She arranged for our PCR tests to be carried out from our hotel room. She also tirelessly made sure all our paperwork was in order and printed them out on time, well before our flights. (The PCR test results were available within the same day. It cost EUR 150 per person. Please make sure to triple-check the laboratory test results for spelling mistakes, names, date of births, passport numbers, test date, signature and stamp chop. We found several mistakes on our laboratory test reports. Without the help from Ms. Léa, it would have been a huge headache to have them rectified on time before our flight back home.)

Lastly, front desk staff would check your pass sanitaire, vaccination record, when you checked into the hotel. All the staff were very good at wearing masks and wore them properly, including the bell staff who were often outside carrying heavy luggage. Surprisingly, not many hotel guests here were using mask at the public spaces of the hotel, such as inside the lifts and on the corridors.

title: An empty mini-bar because of COVID!!!
text:
Incredible experience at the Intercontinental, a reputed 5 star hotel just beside the Opera Garnier.

We arrived late after a long journey at the room and opened our mini bar to get a drink. Our Mini-bar was totally empty, not even a bottle of sparkling water… We called the reception to inform that our mini-bar had been forgotten… A nice gentleman at the reception told us that it was due to Covid instructions. I asked for explanations to better understand the connection between a mini-bar and the covid pandemic. The gentleman said he was not responsible for such decision.

Question to the management: 
1) Don’t you think you could give decent reasons to your staff about such decisions! At least, respect your employees by helping them not to feel stupid by not being able to answer and justify YOUR fool decision!
2) maybe this excuse was invented by the financial department in order to save a bit of money? but in this case, did you have the elegance to decrease the price of the rooms? To that question, the staff said no.
3) Did the management listen to the illuminated French Professor Raoult and was afraid by one of his infamous prophecy? Eventually, in a new delirium, Raoult pretended that one of the main source of Covid was originated in the mini-bar of 5 star hotels ? Actually, it is definitely safer to open a bottle in his private room rather than to go down to the restaurant to have a drink without any mask!!!

Come on management: heureusement que « le ridicule ne tue pas »  but one’s should reflect on such decision and the impact of the image of your hotel. Greedy little guys!

Enjoy my post!

title: First Time Since Remodel
text: This was our first visit in several years so it was the first time since the remodel was finished.  We checked in at the front desk but will not do that again as Gilles advised us to come directly to the lounge.  We received a small shoebox of a room with a great view of the Opera.  I don't look out the window too many times so I prefer a room upgrade rather than a view upgrade due to my IHG status.   I called and stated my case and was told that someone would bring the keys for a new room.  I have pictures of both rooms and will post.  The second room was a suite with separate living room.  There was no tub as in the first room (the only thing better about the first room).   Our view was of the Rue Scribe and the neighbors across the street who must get some interesting views as well?  The a/c worked well, but we mainly used the room to sleep, bathe, and relax after our days in Paris.  We spent much time in the lounge.  We had breakfast both mornings in the lounge unlike our last visit when we ate in the restaurant a few times.  Not as much is available in the lounge, but it is more peaceful and relaxing.  I had omelets both mornings plus bacon and other meats, lots of flaky pastry, and more.  I had 3-4 expressos in one large cup plus about 2 bottles of flat water.  During the afternoon and evenings when we were there, we had wine (maybe a glass of champagne) and some snacks.  Unlike before, there is no dinner in the lounge and the afternoon snacks and desserts are much less than before.   Gilles and team though were as welcoming as always and treated us like royalty.  Armand (as one of the guy's name in La Cage) was a great evening assistant.  The early (morning and early afternoon) staff was great but not as personable since they were new to us and also very busy taking care of everyone's needs.  I always try to include lounge access (now on 1st floor-2nd in US/Canada) as they've turned the old lounge into several high priced suites!  We were on the same floor as the old lounge after our upgrade so I saw the entrances to such.  In conclusion, we plan to be back next June before our Amsterdam cruise.  We used an Ambassador weekend certificate on this stay and have also reserved similar for June.  It is always better when Gilles is there so we let him know our dates when we checked out (in the lounge not at the front desk).  Merci encore pour tous!

title: Lacking air-conditioning
text:
My husband (who has Spire status) & I stayed for 4 nights at this hotel.  We have always had wonderful experiences at InterContinentals-Sydney, Prague, Bordeaux, etc. and expected the same at this hotel.  Our room on the 5th floor was lovely but the last night the air-conditioning wasn't working.  I called guest relations around 5pm and a technician was sent to the room.  He looked at thermostat and said he'd return.  When he didn't return after a couple of hours, I called again.  When he returned, he stated nothing could be done that night and it was too late to move us to another room.  I called guest relations and asked the young lady who answered to send a fan.  She agreed but said it might take some time.  By then, it was 10pm.  We had an early flight so opened the windows  to try to let air into room & get a few hours of sleep.  It was impossible.  Sirens throughout the night and the room was still hot.  When I called guest relations the next morning, the gentleman said I should have continued calling throughout the night requesting the fan "we are here all night, you should have called again and again".  Why should a guest have to make a request several times?  The first day I had to call twice to get a luggage rack.  The second day I made 3 requests for a top sheet or light blanket which was never acknowledged.  I didn't have faith I'd receive a fan no matter how many times I called.

It's a beautiful hotel but for the price we expected a comfortable rest each night.  

And this is a small thing but there was never a smile or greeting from the doorman or from most of the staff.

title: Beautiful hotel in perfect lovation
text:
This is a breathtakingly beautiful hotel in a perfect location. 

The staff are friendly, polite and helpful. 

When we arrived our room was not ready, but we were given vouchers for champagne and a meal in the restaurant, which was wonderful.

It was for my 50th birthday celebrations and we were given champagne, fruit, biscuits and water in our room, which was a lovely gesture and made my day. 

The reason I gave 4 stars was in relation to my stay.. I had requested an opera view room with a balcony as this was for my 50th birthday, but unfortunately I did not get it.

It didn’t spoil our stay, and I understand that these things are not always available but if it had been possible it would have made my stay perfect. 

The room we were given was beautiful, but felt as if it might have been prepared in a rush.. the mini bars were empty and despite having a fabulous coffee machine there were no cups. We rang down to ask for cups and eventually some arrived, but then the used ones were taken away but not replaced for the following day.

Just tiny things, that could have been better but overall it was a wonderful hotel and I hope I get the opportunity to stay again.

title: Four nights of disappointment
text:
On the plus side:
The location of the hotel, the appearance of publicly available rooms.

Unfortunately, there are more minuses than pluses:
Let's start by contacting the hotel before arriving, I received three messages regarding the payment of the first night, because for some reason they could not use the card indicated during the booking, but they did not care what time we would arrive, whether the stay was for an important occasion, room preferences etc., nothing...
We booked a Delux Room with Opera view, arrived around 1 pm, the room was not ready, the reception was not able to give an approximate time of room availability, but tired of the journey, we waited until 3 pm, the reception was still not able to inform us how much time it still needed, so we left the city not wanting to waste any more time, around 4:15 pm the phone rang that the room was ready, after returning to the hotel it turned out that we did not receive a higher category room as a Spire Ambassador, the intervention at the reception did not give anything - no Junior Suite available on that day ...
A guaranteed upgrade does not work there, in addition, it is difficult to understand why a half-empty hotel cannot be planned so that the room is waiting for the guest?
Breakfast is the worst experience in an Intercontinental hotel in the world, long waiting, low quality of products or no such products, after the second unsuccessful attempt to order ordinary breakfast cereals for our son, we found it would be easier to buy it ourselves and from the third day we carried our own so that our child would eat anything else. cold pancakes, the size of the buffet aroused amusement not only for us, most of the guests reacted with disbelief, unfortunately what was coming from the kitchen was of little quality, the level similar to Holiday Inn Express or worse.
Beautiful refurbished building lacking organization, procedures and standards for a good 5 star hotel. Staff are polite but do nothing to change anything to improve if things go wrong very disappointing wedding anniversary stay.

On the occasion of our wedding anniversary, the hotel did not even leave a greeting card, it is just that the guests here are not important what we felt.

title: Excellent location and beautiful traditional hotel
text: Hotel is located right next to the Academie Nationale de Musique and right in the middle of the Opera area and thus centre of Paris. Metro station 1 minute from hotel and The Louvre and many main sights within walking France. Huge selection of Bars, Restaurants and shops all around hotel including a main branch of the famous Galeries Lafayette department store just around the corner. Superb location. Hotel has clearly very recently been fully refurbished with traditional Parisian decor restored to its former glory. Immaculate decor throughout  the hotel and most with views over the neighbouring Acadamie National de Musique which also looks fantastic following a recent renovation. Rooms were not that large but functional and again recently refurbished. The main Opera Salon was closed for food and drink at time of visit but this is a beautiful traditional Paris Hotel Salon. Staff throughout the hotel were super friendly and helpful. Highly recommended hotel for a Paris visit.

title: lost its charm
text:
Started staying at this property soon after it converted to a Marriott in 2005/6. It is wonderfully located in the 1st near the Louvre and Place Vendome.
When it first opened it had all the charm of a boutique Parisian Hotel. Gracious staff, clean well appointed rooms; along with nice welcoming gifts and exceptional toiletries; plus local chocolates on your pillow at night.
From 2006 to now it has evolved from being unique to an chain hotel with little charm and a loud bar that is open till the early hours of the morning on weekends. Pity those folks on the bottom floors.
The local chocolate has become a piece of penny taffy and  the toiletries are now  bottles on the wall of the shower as you usually see at your local Courtyard Marriott. Amazingly, if you book with points, which I did for part of my stay, the  rates are some of the highest in Paris.
The rooms see like they are showing signs of wear, even though hotel has recently been remodeled. Leaking shower, toilet that ran, burned out lights, dirt under the bed. Not what you would expect from a hotel charging $800 + per night on the nights that were paid for.
This is no reflection on the staff, which is very accommodating. The breakfast was excellent and as I said, location is great. Sadly it has lost its charm and, probably, me as a future guest. 
Just as FYI,  I am a loyal Lifetime  Marriot Titanium member.

title: Needs Improvement
text:
We stayed at this property about 10 years ago and really enjoyed it. Wish I could say the same for our most recent visit.

 On the positive side, the location is good. Near the Louvre. Check in was very easy and the desk staff was very nice. Things went downhill from there. When we went to our room in the afternoon, there were trays of food outside many other rooms. The next morning, the same trays were still there. It was disgusting. The bathroom door would not shut. We noticed it was held together with duct tape. REALLY!!  The windows were not sealed well, and unfortunatley our room was above the front entrance to the hotel. People were mingling and smoking below our room well after midnight. It was very loud.  The rooms are rather small and dark. The bathrooms are a good size though. Perhaps because we used points to pay for the room, we were given a worse location. 

Finally, we requested a taxi for the airport, but when we went down at the appointed time,there was no taxi. One of the hotel staff had to run down the street and get us one, which took about 15 minutes.  When I inquired as to what happened, the front desk person  said the taxi they ordered came early and left. Couldn't they have called us to come down. 

Perhaps because we used points to pay for the room, we were given a worse location. 
However, I would not stay at this hotel again.

title: Sub par
text:
First, the location is great and the on site restaurant is a must. 
However, very small king size rooms make accommodations for two with luggage very difficult. 
Room service comes from the restaurant on site but you need to call reception and they order for you. Something as simple as coffee and croissants can take upwards of 40 minutes and only arrive because you have to call a second time. This happened 3 times. 
Housekeeping needs to pay attention to things like empty water bottles in the room. We had eventually had 7 just to see if they would be thrown away but they were just left there on the table. Funny enough, water was not always provided when the room was straightened up so we had to ask the front desk for it. We also ran out of bath gel and hair conditioner that is supplied by the hotel. This is something that should be checked daily. 
The elevator ended up being out of service -which happens. But before it was deemed out of order, I smelled sewage which they tried to cover up with very strong air freshener. Come to think of it, this may have been from the toilets being closed. One of the rooms on the street level was provided for bathroom use. Unfortunate for this to happen when the hotel was completely booked. 
In addition, the wifi was constantly going on and off. 
Marriott can do better.

title: Comfort, convenience, and friendly staff!
text:
This is a lovely hotel and the staff goes beyond expectations to make your stay more comfortable. My room wasn’t ready when I arrived. I was exhausted from my overnight flight and a horrendous delay at the airport where I had to stand in a crowd of people to get through customs for around one hour. I was so disappointed and mentioned that I wanted to take a shower so badly. I was offered use of one the showers in their spa. I had my own 2 room bathroom suit where I was able to open my suitcase, shower in privacy, and use a vanity. I felt like a new person! 

After my sister arrived that afternoon, they sent us a complimentary bottle of wine to thank her for returning. 

The room was small, but it was so comfortable and it overlooked a courtyard. The adjoining restaurant was perfect for breakfast, and the lobby was cozy enough to have drinks, after dinner. 

And, of course, the location is perfect. We were blocks away from Place Vendome which was beautifully decked out for Christmas.

title: A disappointing stay!
text:
This was my first stay at this property, as the Westin, where I stayed earlier for one week, then left France for a day, was sold out for the nights following my return.

I stayed for years at the Westin Vendome, got a very nice suite facing the Tuileries on the 4th floor upgrade, although 5 of the nights were booked on points. That hotel earned my loyalty a long time ago by treating me very well with those suites with an incredible view.

I definitely knew that I would not get a view at the Renaissance, but, with a the SNAs that I had applied to my reservation and a discussion to the Front Desk Manager (the is no FOM and no DOR at this property, the last one being understandable in view of the size of the hotel). Two days prior to my arrival, there was still no reply on my SNA's request, which was very unusual. The FDM said that she would contact Marriott and one the next day, I received an email stating that my SNA request had been denied.

When I checked in in the evening, the Duty Manager, who tried to be helpful, told me that there was no suite or larger room available. He said that that there no message from his FDM, who had told me that she would try to find something for me, even if the SNAs were declined. He looked embarrassed but was not available to give me something better than a room that was 2 SQM larger than the one I booked. He told me that he would try to find something better for the following nights (I never heard from them again about this).
My reservation and my profile indicated a "High Floor" request, but I was assigned this small room on the 3rd floor / 2eme etage just above the entrance of the hotel, so I had the noise of the car doors closing when cars were dropping off or picking up guests at night time). My 3-night reservation was at an average of 650 euros per night (certainly the worst deal that I have got in my long guest "career".

On the next morning, on my way to breakfast, I saw the FDM who asked me how I was doing (no mention of the upgrade that did not happened). I told her that the only room of that size that I ever stayed at, in a hotel, was in Narita, where ANA booked me after a flight delay that made me miss my connection).
Having stayed at Starwood, then Marriott properties over 1,500 nights (with well over 1,400 in suites, following upgrades) since the programs started, I have seen (and talked many times to management people) about the training and way to handle customers, but did not recognize anything that this FDM told me that was fitting the Marriott's way. It was more like "If you want a suite or a large room, I would advise you to book what you prefer". She tried to educate me about small hotels (when I recently had nice suite upgrades at the Edition Barcelona, city that she is very familiar with, or the JW Marriott Bosphorus in Istanbul, both small hotels).

Apparently, this person (or the hotel) is not big on "Elite" recognition, as she did not bother to make any effort to offer me anything to somehow keep me at a certain level of happiness, which is what I have always experienced with Starwood or Marriott (but also with Hilton & IHG). No "Is there anything else that I could do to make your stay more comfortable or to keep you happy?" at this property (although I believe that it is included in Marriott's training).

Breakfast is at the hotel only restaurant. It is small and set up a little bit like The Pain Quotidien, with some large tables which can be shared. It is trying to have a very casual, home style, but that can be awkward.
On the first morning, when I got in, there was a guy standing next to a pole, making the pathway even more difficult, but I thought that he was a guest. It turned out that he was part of the staff, that did not bother to make things easier for the guests. This long curly hair guy had a shirt open almost up to his belly button - definitely another F&B standard. No exchange with him.
On the 2nd morning, it took him forever to bring me an espresso coffee. Just the order, followed by a thank you exchange with him.
On the 3rd morning, I was with my 84-year-old mother (with some asthma issue) and I was trying not to sit right next to other people, to make her feel more comfortable. A young trainee, that I had not seen during the previous mornings, was first insisting that we sat next to a couple when there were several larger tables available, but then let us seat at the table I was preferring. Problem easily resolved, but that previous mornings guy shows up and asked if there was an issue. I started to tell him that it was taken care of, when he interrupted me with "First of all, you are going to change your tone!" and he was not talking about the tone level of my voice.
Totally inappropriate (not to say "weird") attitude, to end up saying that we could sit wherever we wanted, contradicting his trainee. Hard to believe that this guy was given some kind of manager or supervisor position.
My mother, being upset with the rudeness of this guy, asked me if we could leave, so this is what we did, without having had breakfast.

The Renaissance was my plan B, in case the Westin was sold to become a luxury hotel. It is no longer my plan and needless to say that I will not return to this property. I'll probably switch to an IHG hotel in case the Westin is sold out.

Too many tiny rooms in that hotel located in a narrow street with a narrow-minded management which does not seem to understand the importance of loyalty (on both ends).
I also noticed an unequal cleaning service and burned my arm on the towel heater that had been set up at the maximum temperature before I checked in - beware of that heater in the small bathroom, if you stay there).
At the end, the responsibility falls with the GM.

I assumed the fact that I am spoiled, but it is only because Starwood, then Marriott have been spoiling me for a long time and I have been trying to be very loyal to them in return (will return to the Ambassador level this year, after a 2-year interruption).

To end on a good note, most of the staff is pleasant, even in the restaurant (in the afternoon, you will see the restaurant staff occupying the adjacent sidewalk during their break, forcing people, some with luggage, to move on the street.

title: Great hotel and great location
text:
I am a Marriott Ambassador+ member so I have stayed a few nights in hotels and may know a thing or two about them.  (hahahaha!)

Our stay at this hotel was fantastic.  The location is amazing.  Walking distance to the Louvre and amazing shopping were the main reasons we chose this hotel.  The clean, beautiful rooms and fantastic service are the reasons we are coming back next time we are in Paris.

Check in was easy and the staff was very professional, polite and spoke/understood English very well.  The concierge was able to get us great reservations and gave excellent  recommendations for places to explore and eat.

The room was small (as most hotel rooms in Paris are) but it was very nice, the beds were VERY comfortable and clean and the hotel appears in general to be recently renovated.  The bathroom was beautiful and VERY clean which is very, very important to me.  The amenities in the bathroom were upscale (Le Labo).  The towels were actually soft which is unusual.  The noise level in our room (412) was better than we expected.  We were able to sleep quite well each night.

The breakfast we had was delicious and worth getting.

We will definitely be coming back.  Thank you so much for an amazing stay!

title: Great location, nice people but too many flaws
text:
I am a Marriott platinum member.   The location of this hotel is great — lots of what you want within easy walking distance.   Everyone working at the hotel was pleasant and very friendly.  English seemed like the first language here.   

Unfortunately, there were more than a few problems: 1. Our room was tiny.  We’ve stayed in small rooms in big cities, but this was the smallest by far; 2.  There were literally no drawers in the room to store our clothes — none; 3.  The shower is incredibly small.  So small it is almost impossible to turn around.   4.   To make matters worse, there are two very small shower doors that both have to be open to get in and out.   One of our doors was broken and was off the track almost no matter what you did.  I went to the front desk to let them know.  No repair.   Went back next day and the response was that they put it back on track but maybe it couldn’t be repaired.   Never got fixed. 5.  First day used the glasses in our room.  Three days later dirty glasses still there.  6.   Asked for ice and a corkscrew on the first day.  They arrived in less than ten minutes.  Second day asked for ice and wine glasses.   Hour and a half later nothing arrived.  7.  Room cleaned on third day.   Dirty glasses still there and no wash cloths.   Back downstairs and asked for wash cloths.   Called back and said they had no clean wash cloths.  Never got a wash cloth the rest of our stay.  They brought more bath towels which took up way too much room with no drawers.  8.   Restaurant/ bar is very loud.  Some may like that which is fine but there is no where there to have a quiet drink at the end of the day — especially when your room is so small.  9.  Workout room is very small — not even enough room to properly stretch.  The room requires a separate key but we were not told that when we checked in. So went to basement trying to get in and eventually figured out my room key didn’t work.  Upon asking, front  desk gives you a key that looks exactly like your room key so very hard to keep separate.  After two days that stopped working so down and back again.  One of the two elevators goes to the basement.   One does not.  The one that doesn’t still has a button for the basement.   Takes a little while to figure out it doesn’t work.  Sometimes there is water in the workout room but sometimes not. 

I think the really small size of our room and shower colored our experience.  On this trip through Spain and France we stayed at four different Marriott affiliated properties.   All of the experiences and rooms were great except this one.   We will stay elsewhere next time even though we really liked the location.

title: Location & Hotel will not disappoint!
text:
Location, Location, Location! We stayed for 6 nights at this Marriott property and boy; it sure Did Not disappoint. The Place Vendome neighborhood is simply luxurious; this Location was just perfect not too touristy, yet withing walking distance to all the main tourist sites with plenty of Restaurants, Cafes, and Bars around the residential/not so touristy neighborhood and of course the fabulous Luxe shopping all around.  
Towards the left forward-facing street of the hotel is the Jardin des Tuileries, Louvre etc. and the rear of the Hotel Place Vendome with all the Luxe shopping and the cafes, bars etc..
The Hotel staff were very friendly, courteous and helpful especially with managing reservations at hard-to-get restaurants or shows.  The hotel sports small rooms yet very well appointed with all the usual amenities.  We were greeted each evening with thoughtful welcoming surprises; Day 1 our bathroom Basin was filled with ice and a champagne bottle plunged in, with a note “Save water drink Champagne” the next evening a bottle of wine & macaroons from the famous Laudree, Gin and tonics the next, sweet savories from Mado a Paris the next, more wine... and the list endless... Only disappointment was with the house keeper, basic room amenities like coffee, sugar, creamer, coffee/tea disposable cups were not replenished daily same with the case of bathroom amenities like soap shampoo, lotion etc. was not replenished.  The Hotels popular Restaurant Balagan was one of my Favorite restaurants on this trip and naturally the Hotels navigator managed to get us a reservation despite it being full the entire week. I have to say staying here in this hotel at this location made all the difference and made my trip memorable.  Thank you!

title: Great location, clean, and walkable
text:
I booked a junior suite and used my suite night upgrades and had a fantastic room. We had two little balcony windows, one in the king bed room and one in the living room area (pull out sofa). The most amazing part of the suite were the TWO bathrooms. This was a game changer for three people. 
Service: The hotel was very helpful. I was curious to see how things would be coming out of the pandemic. 
Cleanliness: The hotel was very clean. We could request the room to be cleaned up or call for new towels. 
Marriott Status: We were offered breakfast in the restaurant. The food was very good and we had free reign of the menu. It did not feel like they were trying to cut corners or limit what you could eat. My friend loved the coffee. 
Decor: The hotel was beautiful. The decor was cohesive and the hotel was filled with lovely details. The rooms were up to date and had accessible outlets. 
I plan to stay again in a few months. 

I debated between the Westin and this property, but the reviews convinced me and I am glad I booked the Renaissance. I appreciated the updated space and rooms. The Westin has the views, but the Renaissance was worth it. We had views of Parisian apartments and rooftops. 

Parking: When I stayed it was coming out of COVID so parking was free, I am not sure if the garage is still free. The garage is walking distance in Vendome square around the corner. The parking attendant does not speak English. My parking French does not exist so I had  to use google translate. The hotel street is very narrow and there was construction, but I imagine it is complete by now. There are a few parallel spots to unload your bags. The doorman was very helpful.

Large landmarks (park and Vendome statue) made the area easy to navigate. There is a metro station (Tuileres) near by but we didn't take that. The concierge was very helpful/nice and would call for taxis. Free water bottles if you ask the front desk. We had a two room family suite. Consisted of two separate rooms, each with own locking doors, connected by a hallway, and a third locking door to outside hall. One bedroom had two single beds (could be pushed together to make one large queen) and an ensuite bathroom. The other bedroom had one full size (?) large bed and separate bathroom.  Each room had a mini frig, coffee maker, french windows that opened to street. Worked for us 4 ladies. Breakfast was included due to Marriott status & delicious: made to order eggs/omelets, salads, roasted cauliflower, smoked salmon, smoked white fish, apples, oranges, cut fruit, croissant assortment, yogurt, granola, fresh OJ, fresh grapefruit juice, coffee made to order, cold cut meats, cheese assortments, jams, fresh baked cookies,  
Cons: If you have a room with a view of the street, it's very loud from people smoking outside the restaurant/bar on 1st floor. They are outside yelling until at least 2-4 AM on a Mon/Tues night. This restaurant/bar is PACKED at night and we had to close the windows due to smoke/pot.  I asked for a quiet room, high floor, and with a view. They put me on the 4th floor (high), but only rooms with views are those overlooking the street. The quietest rooms have a view of inner courtyard. I wore earplugs so didn't bother me, but other ladies woke due to noise.

title: Excellent location and service. Will revisit!
text:
Title: Excellent service. Perfect location for tourists. 

Pro: Up close and personal service, perfect location for tourists, good buffet breakfast, excellent bed

Con: Nothing major to complain about. Broken USB ports on my side of the bed?

When most staff addressed me when I walked in and out of the hotel, I knew I came to the right place. "Good morning Mr Lam", "Good afternoon Mr Lam. How was your day?", "Good evening Mr Lam. Is there anything I can help you with?" It almost felt like  butler service. Thanks to Tunde, Aude, Thomas, Slim, Nixon, and other staff I didn't get a chance to know their names for doing a great job during my stay, and also to Beatriz for making all this happen. This is one well managed hotel.

Location wise, it is best for tourists who want the convenience to get to most places by foot or by metro. It is right between Jardin des Tuileries and Place Vendome. Louvre? 5 mins. Brand name shopping? 5 mins. Tuileries and Concorde metro stations, 5 mins. Angelina? Parisian cafes? They are everywhere around the hotel. I can't describe in detail how conveniently located this hotel is. We walked to the the Eiffel Tower and to Arc de Triomphe by foot from the hotel.

The Cal King bed was super. I slept like a pig during my stay.

Special mention to Slim for making my daughter super happy, and to Thomas for suggesting an excellent place for escargot. My wife and daughter were very satisfied with the recommendations. 

All in all, I picked the right place to celebrate my wedding anniversary.

Shortcomings? Well, USB ports on my side of the bed (window side) were broken. The SmartTV had problems with its Chromecast. I couldn't get YouTube to work on it. Marriott has standardized customer experience with their smart TV's but this one just didn't work. Some people complained about noise around the hotel. Well, you can't have this much convenience if you don't stay in a busy area. Right? The desk... it is good for light-duty work. If someone wants to put several laptops on the desk to day trade, the desk won't work.

As a Titanium Elite and a lifetime member of the Bonvoy program, I have stayed at many different hotels within the chain, year after year. For a Cat 7 hotel, I would say this one exceeds the experience I had with other Marriot Cat 7 hotels I visited this year. Ritz Carlton definitely did not give me this level of service and satisfaction. Maybe someone from Marriott needs to do a case study?

Once again, thank you to the hotel staff for making my wedding anniversary special. 

We will be back!

title: Poor Service & Loud Street
text: I stayed here for 10 nights on a recent business trip. The desk they provide is too small to work at, and the in-room chair is a bongo-looking wooden stool. There is no overhead light by which to read, and the hotel has no extra lamps to provide. Rue Thabor is incredibly loud, with people yelling in the street until 10pm. There is also a building renovation happening directly across the hotel, so construction begins at 7am and deliveries of materials can occur until 11pm. Room service menu is very limited to the adjoining restaurant and quite expensive (25-40 euro/dish). The staff mean well but are under-trained. I had one employee try to come into my room at 10:30 at night for an unknown reason, and after the chain lock blocked him, he persisted to ring the bell until he woke me up and I answered the door. He was apparently looking to collect some kind of trash? 90% of the people that I saw here were foreign tourists on a day or two jaunt in Paris. For that, the location is very good, and you probably won't be bothered by the way the place operates. For a business traveler, I'd strongly avoid.

title: Overall I am not impressed.
text:
Overall I am not impressed. 

Bed very comfortable and friendly staff. 

Loud music plays all night from the bar, even during the week. I arrived on a Thursday and was unable to fall asleep with heavy bass playing until beyond 1:30am. 

Breakfast limited and not very nice. Croissants and pain au chocolat are not fresh, I didn’t eat them. But nice lattes. 

The ‘fitness centre’ is an OLD multipurpose apparatus with a yoga mat on the floor for stretching. The ‘free weights’ are dumbbells and only going up to 10kg. 

Arrived Thursday and the spa treatments were already fully booked until Monday. 

I stay with Marriotts as a member with Chairman status and the benefits of this hotel do not match others in the group. A sad packet of nuts waiting on arrival (but at least an OK bottle of red also waiting). 

I visit Paris several times a year but it is unlikely that I will be returning to this hotel.

title: LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS HOTEL
text:
THE HOTEL STAFF IS EXCEPTIONAL & brings us back again & again.

1 - THE STAFF
People make the difference here at the Renaissance Paris Vendome Hotel. The front desk staff is friendly, welcoming, accommodating. The breakfast room staff (including a lovely woman named Adele) went way way way above & beyond in making us feel like guests in their own home. Friendly, attentive, helpful, and the energy they projected to accommodate us was a joy and especially appreciated by me - someone who becaues of global pandemic have not traveled in 17 months. Example: One evening we were too tired to leave for dinner, but hungry. Unable to get a seat in restaurant without reservation, and room too small to eat comfortably- the staff welcomed us to order room service but eat in the lobby. Brilliant idea, they went out of their way to think about how to solve for us and make it a great experience. Can't tell you how much we love the spirit of your team!

2- THE FOOD
Breakfast every morning was excellent, with a daily salad changing each day. Loved the choice of oatmeal, eggs, salads, fruits and breads. A limited room service menu - (but the good news is that food quality is HIGH - because it is connected to a dynamite restaurant downstairs)

3-THE ROOM

Fabulous location - Paris is of course a great walking city, but for us virtually everything is walking distance, and we love this as a base. Steps away from the Seine, the Louvre, the gardens.

title: Great location, poor quality, horrible service abs restaurant!
text:
I have stayed a few nights at the Paris Vendome Renaissance hotel a few weeks back. 
I have to say this was one of the most disappointing stays at a Marriott or Renaissance hotels in decades. Below my feedback on the several incidents: 
1/ Staff training: it is so obvious that the majority of your staff at the checking, room service and restaurant are ill trained. A couple of agents at the checkin were extremely professional and knew what they were doing. The rest were at loss: ordering a taxo too 30mns. Getting into my room: 45mns. Printing a document: delays since there is no business center. 
2/ Cleanliness: while awaiting for my room at the reception area, customers couldd smell sewage odors. The same odor remained in the elevators for days.
3/ most importantly: I was very disappointed with the quality of service at the restaurant. I have attended the restaurant for breakfast for 3 days: systematically my orders weren't taken accurately. I literally had to wait for 40 mins to get a cafe latte and a croissant while the restaurant had barely 3 tables being taken care of. On my first attendance, I thought I got unlucky and the person attending me wasn't fast enough. On the subsequent days, different staff members inclusive of the manager behaved with he same disregard. The staff was not organized, the kitchen slow, totally unacceptable for a hotel of this level or for the prices we pay at this establishment. 
I cannot stress enough how disorganized the staff was and how ill trained they were. I honestly have never ever experienced such poor quality of service in 50+ Marriott hotels I've attended worldwide. 
For 500 euros a night, one can expect a minimum of attention and quality of service. 
4/ Rooms: the rooms are tiny (even by Parisian rooms standards). The minibar was empty and the staff didn't even present the offers to fill it in.

title: Horrible Customer Service, Arrogant and A Disgrace to Marriott
text:
Showed up at the hotel to check into a room that was suppossedly a suite for a relaxing weekend.  Far from it. The room had no heating upon check-in.  Despite promises to fix it, it never was done.  At 2am when arriving back to the hotel, rather than them finding a solution to a problem that they know they did not fix, it was left to us!  Had to call the front desk again, explain the problem for the 3rd time and be offered a casual offer to move the room... at 2am!!!!  The last thing you want on a restful stay and being tired.  Rather than proactively offering any concession at check-out, I was left to calling and hoping to get my points back for a miserable stay! 
Despite all the plesantries their "policy" is only to refund a certain amount of points per night which is only 1/2 of what it cost.  Policy at Marriott is fix problems and make your custromers happy as I have been for the past 30 years!  Not give "Policy" advice.  10 years ago, you could brag and trade on your great location.  These days, peple want more than smiles and rejection when dealing with problems.  They want genuine understanding that you failed to provide the service you claim to offer.  Without it, you lose a customer for a lifetime and get slammed on TripAdvisor.  Hopefully the next person will read this and take caution.

p.s.  Save the "We value your opionion" canned response to this complaint.  If you understand cutomer service you will do what is right.  Refund the full points.

title: Great central location, clean and elegant property
text:
Lovely Renaissance property with a boutique feel. Does not feel at all like a cookie cutter Marriott. Property is in a heavily travelled neighborhood, yet it is tucked away on a rather secluded side street.

Room: Rooms are average sized, very clean and efficiently styled. We had a 2 BR suite which was 2 rooms connected by a hallway. There was no living area. Beds were super comfortable. Bathrooms were spotless, though due to the lack of a door or shower curtain - there was only a half glass panel. The floor got really wet anytime the kids took a shower.

Location: Walking distance to high end shopping and the Vendôme area. The Louvre and Musée D;Orsay were both within 10 minute walks. There was a large holiday festival a block away that was rather touristy. Neighborhood was safe, though there was some rather rambunctious street noise in the late hours.

Service: Staff were pleasant and professional. I was a little irritated that i had requested a rollaway bed and had called a week before to confirm. When I arrived, i was informed that there were no rollaways available, which left me with no alternative than to book a expensive third room. Then I when i checked out, they attempted to charge me for the rollaway anyway. The front desk person removed it once I pointed it out. In hindsight, the smallish 2 BR "suite" really did not leave enough room for a rollaway, but i wish they had told me this ahead of time. The whole situation was really messy.

Food: Breakfast was in the restaurant adjacent to the lobby, and offered various pastries, cheeses and fruit, as well as eggs and omelette.

Other: The hotel gave us a nice welcome package with a few bottles of wine, some cookies and chocolates. There were snacks and hot chocolate served in the lobby each night.

title: Nightclub in the lobby - don't stay on a weekend
text:
My family visited Paris over Thanksgiving. We would never stay at the Renaissance Vendome again.  This tiny hotel has a nightclub off of their lobby that plays high bass, high volume music until 2 am.  The hotel deemed it appropriate to place hotel rooms on the floor right above the nightclub.  We were the lucky guests to be given two of those rooms.  The hotel was fully booked so there was nowhere to move us and so we suffered for two nights with the nightclub pumping away below us.  Our children could not sleep until 2 am when the music and shouts and loud singing finally stopped.  I am appalled that the hotel would even consider this appropriate.  

Otherwise, the rooms were small but we were expecting that, given the hotel's size and location.  As to housekeeping, we did not have any issues except that it was disturbing that there is no top sheet under the duvet.  I wonder whether (and hope) they change the duvet after each guest, but I doubt it.  The breakfast was fine, although it had a Mediterranean bent that wasn't our preference and so we only ate there once.  There are a number of great breakfast places close by, though, so we certainly didn't starve.  

Location is great but you have a huge selection of hotels around and we will be selecting one of the other hotels in the future.

title: Stay elsewhere
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Renaissance Paris Vendome for 4 nights in mid November, traveling with two friends.  We had read the reviews warning of the small rooms, but we rechecked the website which says the Paris rooftop rooms are on the 5th floor and are 22sq./m or 237 sq feet—not too bad.  The picture shows a spacious room with two windows and after living in a tiny NYC apartment for over 20 years, we felt this was a non-issue.  Our friends checked in first for a booking identical to ours.  Their room is just as pictured on the Marriott.com website.  However, when we checked-in, there was only one window, a much smaller room than pictured, 30% smaller than our friends.  The room was so small, that if the curtain was closed you had to physically move the fabrics to get into and out of bed.  On the other side of the bed, only one person can access the closet at a time. 

Besides the small room that was less than promised, the water temperature in the shower would fluctuate so badly that you’d be either chilled or scalded.  The front desk said they sent someone to look at it, day after day that we complained, but it persisted throughout our stay.

After filling out the survey upon our return home, the management sent an email assuring us the room we stayed in was the one we booked.  The pictures and dimensions on the website prove this to be incorrect.  Nicolas also said he offered us a different room but we declined.  The truth is he offered to UPSELL us a more expensive room.  Having decided this place was not going to get another dime, we declined.  

The doormen are great, very helpful at finding our Uber, hailing taxis, and opening doors.  The room was kept clean by prompt housekeeping service, though turndown service went 2 of 4 nights.  Beds were very comfortable though there was no top sheet, just a duvet.  The location is terrific, but definitely not worth the money or layers of skin lost in the scalding shower.

This is not a 5 star hotel.  The rooms are not as described.  I’d suggest staying somewhere else.

title: Fabulous stay at the Hotel Renaissance Nobel Tour Eiffel - Paris
text:
My husband and some friends and I had stayed in this lovely Renaissance hotel in April, 2009.  We found the concierge staff to be most helpful and the location near the Eiffel Tower to be very centrally located. Thus, we booked a trip for the summer of 2022 at this same location.
I am Titanium Elite with Marriott,  so I/we have stayed in many Marriotts or their other brands.
I booked a prepaid garden room with a king bed for June 25-29, 2022.  After booking the room, I read a review in Trip Advisor.  It indicated that the terrace and the restaurant were under construction, which made it very difficult to be in a garden room location. I called Marriott’s customer service and spoke to a lady who advised me she would contact the hotel by email and ask them to contact me. I indeed received an email from Damien Belaud in reception about a month prior to my stay.  Damien advised me that the construction of the Terrace had been completed and that it was in the final decorating stage. He assured me that the terrace work would be completed by the time of my arrival.  It was completed when we arrived and the terrace was absolutely beautiful!  We were able to eat breakfast on the Terrace several mornings ~ what to delightful place to begin your day!
The Concierge staff at this hotel is incredible. Prior to my arrival, Oliver Dubray assisted me in finding a location of a business that was near the hotel, since it had many locations in Paris and I was unfamiliar with the geography.
Upon arrival, Gael took a Paris map and pinpointed multiple places that we wanted to visit during our stay.  Since we had visited Paris on prior occasions, we decided we wanted to take one of the bus tours to allow us to see some of our favorite things and places once again.  Gael booked the trip for us. Later, we embarked from the hotel to traverse to the bus stop. We walked down three or four different streets and every single one of them was totally blocked by firemen and police officers, as there had been a significant fire in an apartment near the hotel.  Out of desperation, I called the hotel and reached Lea Baillivet.  I explained the situation to Lea and she asked me where we were located. I told her and she said she would come help us.  Being from Texas, we drive our cars everywhere. We made the assumption she would drive to where we were located. Imagine our surprise, when we saw Lea jogging down the street towards us in her black Renaissance dress and jacket.  She directed us to a street that wasn’t blocked and closed.  She was so kind and humble, as if she had not done anything. Lea, by far, went ABOVE and BEYOND that of what most employees would have done. Her comprehension and delivery of customer service excellence is amazing, especially given her very young age.
This concierge staff at the Renaissance should be given commendations for their efforts in  helping their guests have a fabulous vacation. We will certainly return to this hotel when we return to Paris!  We highly recommend it to you!
name: Renaissance Paris Nobel Tour Eiffel Hotel
