Of course clean rooms (specific hotel giving much attention in the word clean and rooms are indeed VERY clean), to have central metro station that all lines are passing (Nation) close by in order to make our life easier, to offer a coffee (free) in the morning and the most important…. we didn’t want to pay much money for accommodation as we would leave from the hotel early morning and return late evening in order to enjoy the sightseer of Paris thus no reason to pay any expensive hotel.
We arrange the booking without breakfast as there are many options close by. There is a bakery in the corner and also a café plus a small mini market that sell also fruits.    
Rooms were also normal size (for two adults and one child) with modern minimal decoration. People working in the reception were very friendly and always ready to answer any of our questions.
For sure this is a good 3 stars hotel and not a 2 stars hotel.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Boutique hotel with heart
text: We stayed here for seven nights in May, and we're very pleased. The Hotel is located close to a major square - actually a huge roundabout, which is also a major metro and bus hub. But, the hotel is far enough away that you're not aware of the traffic. There are many restaurants within walking distance, post office around the corner, several bakeries and grocers. The local farmers market is open on Saturday and Wednesday mornings, just down the block. The Hotel is small, rooms are small but comfortable, everything is clean, and the decor is calming. The hotel offers breakfast for €10/day per person, but we didn't partake. Coffee is available, and it's good. The front desk staff is very helpful. Zdravko works evenings, and is always will to hear about your day. Wafa and Loretta are on day shift and can help with all things Paris. They all speak English. The manager, Colette, gets things done. Overall, we thought this was a great place to stay in a beautiful city, and a very good value.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Location anda value.
text: This hotel might not be memorable but offers great location (a few blocks from metro) and nice, clean, quiet rooms. Breakfast is a bit pricy, 9 euro I believe. Local tax is not included in your reservation but this is usual in Paris. Staff is not very friendly but then again, not unusual. Good value.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: NIce hotel in nice area
text: Hotel Picpus is a great value of money. Nation area where hotel located is quiet, safe and good atmosphere. There was a small market on saturday, very french style to see when people boungth their food for weekend cooking. Hotel is clean and confortable and breakfast for Paris standard was good.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Tidy, kind, but somewhat claustrophobic
text:
If you are claustrophobic, do not stay in this hotel! Rooms are supersmall, stairs are narrow, hallways are not spacious... There are no common meeting rooms.

Staff are kind and very cooperative. Rooms are tidy and well kept. Bath rooms are ok although very small. Breakfast is served on small tables in the entry hall and has a variety of offers.

The location is convenient, near the metro station of Place de la Nation, from where all central points may be reached rather quickly.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Weekend in Paris
text:
As I have never stayed in Paris before I do not have anything to compare this hotel with- I have stayed in other capital cities however so will compare with them. I booked this hotel, as even though someone had commented that the rooms were small but this was normal for Paris, I hadn't really anticipated the room to be quite this small. We had a double bed but with very little room to swing a cat on either side. 
Location was good- easy to navigate the metro and had plenty of places to explore.
The room itself only had one neighbour and was in a small courtyard - which was nice as my other half could nip outside to have a puff on his e-cig. It was also relatively soundproofed however you did have the rumble of the metro trains running regularly throughout the day and most of the night. 
Breakfast was extra and was a standard buffet breakfast but the staff were very friendly and helpful.
So room size, average breakfast and the rumble of the metro keeps this review as a three. The staff and the location however was good.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Very nice and helpful management
text:
We had a problem with the personal safe in our room, which was quickly dealt with by management.  Thanks very much for seeing to this straight away otherwise we would have gone out sight seeing with all our valuables!

Located in a very quiet and safe part of Paris, which is great, as it is practically possible to walk everywhere.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: New Years Vacation
text: Hotel Du Printemps was excellent. The room (although small) was clean and well presented within easy reach of the City. Staff were friendly, well versed in English and very accommodating. Breakfast was plentiful and all in all it was great value for money (I booked well in advance of the trip).
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Best 2* hotel I have ever been
text: Hotel du Printemps offers good value for money. The rooms are small (what's new in Paris ;-) but very comfortable. Everything is clean and nice. I am not tall so the bed was ok. However if you are taller than 1m 80cm you might find these beds small of size. The great shower will make you forget this. Breakfast is basic but good and tasteful. And the service is very good, the staff is helpful and nice (special for Paris;-) Situated at a good location, close to Metro station Nation and situated in a quit street. I am actually very surprised this is only a 2* hotel. The hotel deserves 3* for sure! Would definately recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Relaxing!
text: Although this hotel is a little far from the attractions, (12 euro on Uber one way) You can take public transportation which is explained by the staff. We opted to go by Uber since there were three of us and it costs about 2 euro each on the Metro. This hotel is excellent! the staff were so helpful, friendly and just amazing! The room is very clean and the beds are so comfortable! I wouldn't mind staying here again!
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Amazing Staff!
text:
This has to be the best hotel staff I have encountered in a long time.  They are so helpful and kind that I cannot say enough about them.  One of them even helped us figure out some of the settings on our rent car.
As for the hotel it self.  It is charming and cozy with comfortable rooms.  It is located in a quiet neighbor hood with fantastic restaurants and convenient metro and bus stops.  We choose this hotel because of an earlier review commenting on how excellent the wheelchair room is.  It to find wheelchair accessible hotel rooms in Paris and this one was quite nice.
I will be staying here next time we come to Paris
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Secret little gem in the 12th.
text: I've stayed at this hotel several times with small groups of travelers on my Artistic Adventures. it never fails to offer what most travelers needs in Paris: clean, stylish little rooms with good bedding and fantastic help at the front desk; all in a safe Parisian neighborhood. You're out of the tourist mania of the Marais and Latin quarter. Nation station, a main metro hub, is a 10 minute walk. Gare de Lyon and Bercy are closely. A wealth of lovely local restaurants are within walking distance, too. The open air market is Wednesday mornings at Nations, to boot.
name: Hotel du Printemps

title: Ok for one night
text: Good location and average service but ok for one night that I spent as didn’t have lot of stuff; I’m not sure how would I move with more things because the room was really small. Breakfast is very poor and it has to be improved. I’m not sure that I would stay there when visiting Paris again, only if I have no other options.
name: Hôtel Gaston
description: Near the Paris Convention Center and a few steps from the Arc de Triomphe and Champs-Elysees, the hotel Gaston welcomes you to an authentic Parisian experience : • Hotel entirely renovated in 2014 • Perfect soundprounding and reversible air-conditionning • HD TV, individual safe, hairdryer • Free internet access

title: Value for money!
text: We booked via Secret Escapes and got a nice deal. title: A perfect gem of a Parisian hotel!!
text:
I was searching for an economical place for my daughter and I to stay for a last-minute trip to Paris during her Spring Break. When I came across the artsy, modern style of Hotel Gaston I knew it was the one for us - we are big fans of modern design. 

Upon arrival, I was especially pleased to find the hotel is conveniently located in a quiet neighborhood of Paris, close to a few restaurants and grocery stores, as well as metro and bus stations. Our room was small, but perfectly adequate for what we needed as we don’t spend lots of time in a hotel room when on vacation. Our bathroom was small as well - only room for one at a time, but again, was perfectly adequate. We fell in love with the (almost) floor-to-ceiling window in our room that we could swing open and fully let the sights and sounds of this quietly bustling area of the city in. We fell in love with the modern design of our room as well as the fantastic artwork in the hallways of each floor. Really fun and creative! 

We mainly interacted with three staff members who were each very friendly and went out of their way to be as helpful to us as possible. Being foreigners in a new country, we had lots of questions and needed quite a bit of transportation guidance at the start. A+ to the Hotel Gaston staff. Housekeeping came daily and remade our bed as well as vacuumed, emptied trash, and left fresh towels. We opted for the two twin beds pushed together and the mattresses were very comfortable! I wouldn’t hesitate to book a stay with Hotel Gaston again on a return trip to Paris!

title: Best boutique hotel in Paris
text:
If you are looking for a "boutique hotel" that is squeaky clean, uniquely Parisian and very intimate, this is it. We stayed 6 nights in room 506 (one of the Privilege Rooms), accessible via a tiny but beautiful blue lift. The room is impeccable and smells so fresh every time you walk in. The bed with 4 pillows and the softest bedding is incredibly comfortable and is just perfect to rest your body after a long day of walking. The room is very tiny, but the space is designed so thoughtfully and beautifully that you just have to look in the right places to find everything you need right there in the room. There's a nespresso machine, a safe, a luggage rack, an open wardrobe, several charging points, a desk with a chair, fog-free bathroom mirror with the cutest bowtie on it. The highlight is undoubtedly, the spectacular view from the Juliet-style balcony. There was a wonderful lady at reception who handled our check-in and was there for most of our stay except the weekend, when we checked out. 5 stars for the non-intrusive, friendly service. 

Check-in and check-out are the quickest (two minutes tops), which we greatly appreciated. We would recommend doing the online check-in before arriving.

Definitely pick Gaston over other hotels in the area like the Novotel, which is very close by but is on a much busier junction. Hotel Gaston is in a quiet, beautiful area, which you'll surely appreciate.

The only negative, perhaps, was the washbasin sink, which got very easily clogged. This was cleaned by housekeeping everyday but the issue persisted. This, however, did not diminish the quality of our stay and we're looking forward to going back to Hotel Gaston the next time we're in Paris!

title: Pied a terre
text:
My wife and I went with friends over to Paris for a weekend, staying the Friday and Saturday nights at the Gaston.  

The receptionist was fast, efficient and friendly on arrival.  

Room 606 was on the 6th floor - the lift could just comfortably fit 2 people and suitcases.  We never had to wait more than 30’seconds for the lift.  

606 is quite small with rudimentary storage and a pleasant enough view through the very tops of the plane trees.  The bathroom was equally compact but well equipped.  I’d advise caution when getting in the bath to shower, as it’s a little awkward climbing in.   The bed was comfy enough but not massive!

There is simple breakfast in the hotel and free coffee all day.  

There is a lounge downstairs from the reception that we only found out about just before we left.  

The Rouergue bistro round the corner is highly recommended.  

To Gard du Nord. 

Hotel Gaston is located about a 5 minutes stroll from Pont Cardinet Station.  It’s 1 stop on blue line L to Gare Sainte Lazare.  It’s 3 levels down to Gare Haussmann Sainte-Lazare (through a shopping arcade with no signage to help!!) and 1 stop on the magenta line to Gare Magenta at Gare du Nord.  This is not a great trip if you have kids and heavy suitcases in tow.  

Another tip - get the app called Taxis Connect, as it is a fantastic way of ordering taxis in Paris.

We had a rear facing room which was v quiet. location is 5 mins walk to railway station, 2 mins to bus stop, 10mins walk thru the village to metro. A wee bit out the way but priced accordingly. The small cafe on the corner sells metro/bus tickets, a pack of ten is 15euro. The village has a nice vibe on a Sunday morning which leads down to a flea market. title: Nice, tidy hotel but off the beaten track
text: Small boutique hotel. Not central location but relatively quiet and 8 minutes walk from two Metro stations and an RER line C station so easy enough to get around. Internally the hotel is clean and tidy, and a little bit funky with their artwork. Rooms are small, typical of Paris, but refurbished to a good standard with very comfortable twin beds (not too firm and not too soft, felt a little like memory foam). Continental breakfast was basic but nice enough and not too expensive. Reception manned by two guys who were both very friendly, spoke perfect English and were very helpful. Overall recommend for a short break, if you are prepared to do a little walking

title: Perfect Boutique Hotel
text:
A few days before Valentine’s Day my wife found a travel offer to Paris. We had previously discussed going as I knew it was on her bucket list and I took a few semester of French in college and always wanted to visit. So we booked this deal which was round trip air with a hotel including breakfast. Lucky for us we were booked into Hotel Gaston, a little boutique hotel in a neighborhood setting a short walking distance to the Arc de Triomphe. We would also utilize taxis to further destinations on our excursions. 
Upon arrival we were greeted by Luic. Since my French was not that good it was a relief that he spoke English. 
The room was quite chic and comfortable, a bit small by excessive American standards, but perfect for our stay. The only thing that did not work for us was the USB port to charge our phones but we had a electrical adapter so it wasn’t an issuer for us and They said they would be repairing it right after we checked out. 
The complimentary breakfast was good with a nice selection. A selection of different croissants and breads, salami, ham and cheeses, fresh fruit, cereals, yogurts, milk, fresh squeezed juices, and a coffe/espresso machine that was available 24 hours. 
The home feel and hospitality of Jennifer & Luic, Who both spoke english, was outstanding!! I feel as if I now have two very good friends in Paris. 
Since the weather was not completely cooperating with us during our stay we were not able to do everything we had wanted to do. The good part about that is now we will have to return to Paris and we will definitely stay with our friends at Hotel Gaston.

title: Charming hotel with friendly staff
text:
Very charming hotel in a quiet area about 20 minute walk from the Champs Elysee. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful in checking us in when we arrived late in the night and in guiding us with things to see and do in the area. There are 2 bus stops close to the hotel, one that takes you to Champs Elysees and another that goes to the Opera House. Since we went in December, Paris was quite cold and we walked a couple of times but ended up taking the bus on the really cold days. The Metro is also close by but we did not really use it much. In better weather, I think it should be a lovely walk to the main attractions. The room was clean and breakfast was pretty decent. There is a cozy room to hangout with books to read. Also, there is a very nice Italian restaurant right across the street and a few other restaurants a couple of blocks away. 
We very much enjoyed our stay here and would definitely come back.

title: OK budget hotel, service could use improvement
text: Stayed here with my daughter.  Hotel is quirky and I wanted to like it.  Good location, short walk from metro and arc.  But the service warrants a lower rating.  My son was planning on coming in for one night and had a separate room booked through a travel agent.  He had flight issues, so I asked if his room could be cancelled..  The women at the front desk said that since the reservation was made through a travel agency, we would have to work through them.  We called the travel agency and were told that since there had been flight issues, they did not think it would be a problem, but they would have to check with the hotel.  The travel agency called back and said they spoke with the hotel (and gave me the name of the same woman at the front desk I had spoken with initially) and that the hotel would not allow for a cancellation - we would have to pay for his room.  It was after the time for cancellation, so I don't object to the hotel denying a cancellation, even for flight issues.  But why didn't they tell me that when I asked in person - I wasted an hour of my time and made two international calls that could have been avoided.  The young woman who worked at the breakfast buffet was also lacking in friendliness and effectively hurls items onto the buffet.

title: HOTEL GASTON
text: Hi we have just returned from a three day mini break from Paris, we stayed in The hotel Gaston, which is situated to the North of Arc de Triomphe, about a twenty minute walk, the hotel is modern with a new feel to it, however the rooms are quite small, probably the smallest room i have ever stayed in, we had room 505 on the 5th floor, there were no tea and coffee making facilities in the room, however there was a machine in reception which was free to use, there is a small lift, capable of taking two people, which is not ideal when the maids are moving their linen, the room has a big window which lets in enough light, a clothes hanger instead of a wardrobe, a tv and a bathroom off the bedroom, which is even smaller, how they got a toilet shower and toilet in there is a miracle. the room was clean but not cleaned again while we were there, we had to ask for toilet roll and towels Reception was a desk with an attendant 24 hours a day, with a few tables to sit about 30 for breakfast, breakfast was as basic as you can get, continental breakfast was cold hard packet croissants with jams and a bread, three choices of cereal, two cooked meats and cheese, not great but we survived, the staff however are the reason we enjoyed our stay, they are helpful and pleasant with the exception of the girl who served breakfast, everyone else bent over backwards and helped book trips and hop on hop buses, the location is 18 minutes walk from Moulin rouge, 44 minutes walk from Eiffel tower so the location is a little too far out for my liking, it was a nice hotel but probably would not return

title: Fantastic service at cozy boutique hotel
text: My wife and I stayed at this boutique hotel in the last weekend of September. The hotel is located in a quiet and cozy neighborhood in the 17th arrondissement. Easy arrival via taxi from the airport (50 euros), about 30 minutes drive, well worth it! We were met by a very cheerful service minded receptionist who gave us useful tips on were to eat lunch nearby. The rooms are small but practical with good standard and comfortable bed. We asked for a room on the upper floors (5th floor), number 506, that was very nice. The breakfast is simple but extremely good! Fresh orange juice, croissants, baguette, cheese and meat condiments. And a coffee machine. You get everything you need for a good start to your day. We stayed two nights (Friday to Sunday) and booked via their own webpage so we got a discount and wine and macrons in the room of arrival. Very nice touch! We’ll definitely stay here the next time we visit Paris!

title: Charming Hotel in St. Germaine des Pres, Paris
text:
This was my 4th visit to this charming hotel over the past 7 years. I felt that nothing had changed. The same friendly Concierge greeted me - he has been at the hotel for over 25 years. The lovely garden was still a treasure to sit and relax in with a glass of wine or to have breakfast in if you wanted to sit outdoors in the morning. The breakfast room and small sitting room was typically French - comfortable and quaint. Very good basic breakfast with croissants, fruit and other typically European food. You could also arrange to have a Continental breakfast brought to your room. 
My room was very pleasant, decorated in a very unique French style of Art Deco, decorated as only the French can!  Very comfortable bed.   I had a lovely sitting room attached to the bedroom, so I had quite a bit of space for a small French hotel.  The bathroom was roomy with a bath. The bedroom, sitting room and bathroom were very clean. I thought that the decor was a little dated and could do with a bit of a facelift but overall I would stay here again and thoroughly recommend this lovely small hotel so well located to many attractions.  The area is interesting snd very safe.

title: My favorite hotel
text: I usually stay at four- or five-star hotels, but when I am in Paris I always stay at this hotel. It is probably my favorite hotel in the world. It is very conveniently located in St-Germain-des-Pres and is easily the best three-star hotel in that arrondisement. I've stayed in a number of others in that area and they all fall far under the living standards of Angleterre. The rooms are varied, and some are really lovely, and the larger rooms are similar in size and decor to a four-star hotel. I guess they are not a four-star hotel because they lack some (to me) unimportant small amenities. Breakfast is standard but fine. The personnel are wonderful here-almost everyone is exceptionally warm, personable and professional, and you feel very welcomed. There is a garden you can have breakfast or drinks in during warmer weather. Housekeeping is very good. The beds are very comfortable. We usually have a room street-side, but it is nevertheless reasonably quiet. The thing I love most about this hotel is that it somehow feels quintessentially Paris. You know you are in Paris when you are in this hotel. I've referred a lot of friends to Angleterre over the years and everyone has told me they loved it there.

title: Incredibly Charming
text: This hotel was incredible charming. The building is old and if you don't appreciate history and the quirks that come with it then I don't recommend this hotel. It's beautiful and ancient but of course has no elevator, the stairs are old and uneven, the doorways are short in some places and there is wear and tear to be found everywhere. If you can look past the minor inconveniences of an old property, there is so much rich history to be appreciated here. We stayed in their suite #51 which is larger than our apartment in Toronto and boasts two incredible fireplaces. The decor is what I'm dubbing as medieval chich and I loved everything about it. Breakfast was simple and very Parisian but the staff were really exceptional, allowing us to check in as soon as we arrived as the room was available and always ensuring we had everything we needed. The area is perfect if you're looking for late night food options and prefer to walk to the major attractions. Very close to Cafe de Flors and Les Deux Magots which are both amazing and should be visited!

title: We LOVE this hotel!
text: This was the fourth time (through 25 years) that we've stayed at d'Angleterre.  I will warn you away from it if you want a chain type hotel. Sebastian at the front desk is wonderful - running suitcases up the stairs and making sure everything is just right.  Look into the fascinating history of the place and you will feel very fortunate to have stayed in this beautiful hotel.

title: Loved it. Would definitely stay here again
text:
Bottom line, we thoroughly enjoyed this hotel. The location is excellent, within easy walking distance of Musee D’Orsay, the Louvre, Notre Dame, L’Orangerie etc, with plenty of buses and metro stops within 5 minutes walk as well.

 Our welcome was delightful and the room was quite large. The room was a bit tired, with smell of mothballs and one of the bathroom lights was more like a strobe (we unscrewed it) and a shower that is guaranteed to get water on the floor, but again, we LOVED the hotel.

 Our room could readily convert to a two room suite, with a pull out couch and pocket doors for privacy. Each area has its own TV. There are plenty of windows and a large fan (NO air conditioning, but the weather was prefect, so the fan was more than enough to keep us comfy). 

 The bed was very comfortable. Bathroom was spacious with both a large tub and a separate shower stall. There were ample amenities and fluffy towels. The room had a large walk in closet with tons of shelf space and a safe. Breakfast was delicious and the dining room is elegant. If weather permits, and you’re lucky enough to get a table, the atrium is a lovely breakfast spot as well. 

Tips: 
 Assanabel (Lebanese food to eat in or kabobs etc to take away) is three doors down. It was exceptional! We actually ate there twice.

 There is a laundromat (Julice Laverie) within easy walking distance.

 Right around the corner is the Serge Gainsbourg House. It is must see for music lovers.

title: NO AC but...
text:
I go often to Paris and I’m always looking to try new cute, small hotels around St. Germain - my favorite area.   
This hotel looked very nice in the website and in fact it is adorable. The only down side(and a big problem for me) is that there’s no ac in the entire hotel. This came to me as a huge surprise, specially because I arrived in Paris on the same day as a very strong heatwave.
I went to the reception to complaint and both ladies were extremely accommodating and polite and offered me another cool which was much cooler. I was quite pleased with the way the situation was handled by the staff but unfortunately the “non ac” is a deal breaker for me so I can’t stay there again. But if an AC is not your thing I recommend you to stay there.
Rafael

title: the good, the bad, the do-so
text: Just returned from our stay at Hotel D’Angleterre. First the good, great location, helpful and kind staff, breakfast included. Second the bad, the room we had was very old, street side (so quite noisy) but the worst of it was lack of a second mirror and a place to charge our devices. The very worst was the hotel hair dryer—probably circa 1968, couldn’t dry even a man’s short hair let alone my thick curly hair. With a few simple upgrades this place could be great. There needs to be a mirror/dressing area outside the bathroom so 2 people can get ready. Please install a charging strip somewhere in each room. Please refurbish the sofas and tables in the room. They are old, saggy, and just tired looking. The breakfast is great! The courtyard is lovely. Our check-in and check-out was easy and pleasant. The staff by and large were great. If you go, ask fora remodeled or upgraded room. Also not sure if hotel is air conditioned so summer might be very uncomfortable.

title: Awful
text:
I booked a room six months in advance of my arrival to the hotel in May 2019.  When I arrived, under the guise of "my room had been upgraded" they took me to a room at the top of a very very steep staircase, the door to the room opened directly onto the top step.

I refused the room which I felt would put me in a very precarious and dangerous situation. In fact after refusing the room I turned to go back down the staircase, fell and sprained my ankle.

I was told the only other room available was room 38 (which is off the courtyard).  Unless you keep the curtains drawn at all times the other guests can look right into the room. In other words, in order to have privacy you could not have any daylight coming in through the windows.

This  room was musty, shabby, dirty, the lighting was minimal (I could barely see to put on make up), the bathroom sink was cracked, the faucets caked with grime, the floor pitted with dirt and the Wifi  so weak I couldn't send emails,  the television screen was maybe 20" (and that's being generous)

The towels were old, stiff and didn't look clean, and there weren't many of them.

I was told this was the best they could do.  The staff was unhelpful and didn't care about my situation.   

This was no way to start a vacation that I had been planning for over six months. After much difficulty and a lot time (which I would have preferred to spend walking around the city) I found another hotel.

I had stayed in this hotel many years prior and was dismayed to see how shabby the hotel had become.

If you want to enjoy your stay in Paris DO NOT stay at this hotel.

title: Seventh trip to Paris, great hotel choice
text:
When we fly all the way from Chicago to Paris, I want that "pinch me I am in Paris" charm, not a generic, Courtyard by Marriott kind of feeling. We always stay in the same left bank neighborhood. We are a couple in our 50s travelling for fun. 

Hotel d'Angletterre has that old Paris charm. We actually had two rooms, the first was the top floor suite, which is all timbered ceilings and huge fireplaces. Very cool, but we liked room 5 better. It was a deluxe room, four poster bed facing a fireplace. Wonderfully Parisian, huge bathroom. 

Also, I am a clean freak. Hotel was very clean. Some of the common areas have furniture that is a little more worn than charming. Breakfast sufficient. Coffee hot. 

Finally, kudos to very nice front desk staff - welcoming and competent. I would very much recommend this hotel.

title: A total dream.
text:
Our hotel room was gorgeous and felt super luxurious - the beds were amazing, the breakfasts were splendid, and the location was fabulous - an easy walk to Angelina's for hot or iced chocolate, or to Laduree for a pastry.  And the beautiful Tuileries gardens are right there for a stroll, too.  Plus it felt super safe as it's hyper-patrolled due to  being right near the US and British embassies.  It also had a historic feel being right near the Louvre (which has a very long history and wasn't always a museum!).  And it's also right by a Metro stop if you need to go elsewhere in town (but we ubered).

If you're traveling with kids, we found our room with a pullout couch to be fantastic.  The bed quality was great, it was nice and large, and the staff put the bed back into a sofa during the day and took it down again at night to conserve space.  Also, the brasserie downstairs has super tasty chicken nuggets (even I loved them) which was very handy when the kids were hungry at night but the rest of us were still full from the day's other gourmandises.

This hotel is pricey but if you can swing it, and especially if you're not often in Paris, I think it's well worth the experience.  I've done Paris on a budget during my broke, youthful years and there really is a whole different feel staying in a place like this. We've also found that if you choose a hotel with an amazing breakfast spread you can save money later in the day by only eating one other real meal.  

The staff we encountered spoke excellent English, but they also humored me in my attempts to use the French I'd been fluent in after my college year in France 22 years ago, but had since mostly lost.  I love all things French, including the language, and if ever in France I hate to miss the opportunity to practice so I really appreciated the staff indulging me!

Magical location, rooms, beds, breakfast, and staff.  We'll never stay anywhere else in Paris!

title: Central
text:
Very centrally located just off La Place de Concorde - as its near the American Embassy armed guards are at the end of the street which didn't cause any issues but might be off putting to some.  Rooms were smaller than the photos suggested but bed was huge and comfortable and Balmain toiletries in the bathrooom.  We had a junior suite which had a sofa, unfortunately it was a sofa bed which made it quite uncomfortable to sit on as the cushions kept sliding out!  We were in room 420 which was the furthest from the lift, our teenagers daughters were in room 421 which sounded  like it should be next door to ours but was in fact at the opposite end of the hotel!  Staff were a little off hand and cleaners took one of our daughters key cards which was never replaced despite numerous requests.

The hotel is nice and centrally located but let down by service - eg we waited 45 mins for suitcases to be delivered and had to chase them in the end. 

Lifts were intermittent and spoke to other guests who had been trapped in a lift.

I was a little disappointed with the hotel - it's fine but I thought could be a lot better.

title: Home away from home
text:
In the heart of the capital of fashion, luxury and culture, the Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg is located in 2 mansions from the 18th and 19th centuries. The hotel was also the former home of the French magazine Marie Claire and was the ideal rdv for journalists stylists and fashion photographers.
Nearby you will find the most prestigious sights of Paris: the Faubourg Saint-Honoré with its numerous luxury boutiques and art galleries and the Place de la Concorde, which marks the beginning of the Champs-Elysées.
The rooms and suites are luxuriously decorated by Didier Gomez, one of the most famous interior designers in France, reflecting his sublime vision of Parisian chic. Summarised as "modern style meets the 18th century".

The rooms and suites include a flat-screen TV, air conditioning and a minibar. you can also use free wifi. Paris Sofitel offers 24-hour reception, concierge and room service.
The staff is very friendly. And the dog is welcome. Very important for us.

We have been coming here for 4 years - we also have an Accor loyalty card (which I recommend to everyone) - and it has actually become our permanent base in Paris.

title: Calm hotel in the middel of Paris
text:
I have been going to Paris 2-3 times over the past 25 years..so trying out new hotels are always nice.

This is my first visit to a Sofitel hotel in Paris.

The hotel is located on a closed road as the Ameriacan Embassy is at the end of the street.  This means polize are controlling who pass through the hotel days and night. Giving you are loving safe feeling.

When arriving the door mens do a very good job.

The room I booked was a Deluxe Room / twin beeds. It was small but clean and newly decoreted. Keep in mind that you shower in a bath tub (which I personally do not like)

Breakfast is very good! I  could come back just for that!

The hotel bare is quite borring. small room with a lot of furtitures and no real 'athosphere'. Which is really the feeling I got from the hotel. It is nice, clean, well located, the employees are sweet.. there is nothing wrong.. but there is no 'atmosphere'.

I might come back as I do like the location

text:
We loved our stay as a family with two young children. Staff were attentive and extremely professional and ensured we had a great stay. Special thanks to Jerome and the concierge team for excellent restaurant recommendations.

Housekeeping staff, who are the “stars” working in the background are extremely professional and very polite.

Location of hotel was excellent in the trendy part of town. Expect to pay above premium rates for eateries close to the hotel.

We would certainly return again and would recommend others to stay here too!

title: Great Location and Suites
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at this hotel for 5 nights and can honestly say that it did not disappoint.  Prior to our arrival we informed the hotel that we would be celebrating our anniversary and the staff went out of their way to make sure this occasion was special for us.  We were upgraded to a suite that was incredibly spacious (room 525) and greeted with champagne and a cake that was one of the best desserts I had while in Paris. 

Breakfast was also great (very tasty) and there was a wide selection to choose from. A personal favorite of mine was the great selection of  fresh juices offered every morning. From green juice, to beets, grapefruit, orange, etc. They had it!

The location is perfect for those interested in shopping, literally next door to Hermes, YSL, Dior, galeries lafayette, etc. Also across the street from Buddha Bar which is a great lounge/cocktail spot or even for dinner. A short walk to other sites such as the Louvre and Eiffel tower (approx 20-25 mins).

The entire staff was incredibly welcoming and helpful. Management (Sabrina) constantly checked in on us to make sure our stay was going well and the concierge and Lea of guest relations were also all incredibly helpful.

I would not hesitate to stay at this hotel again and hope to do so next time I'm in Paris! Highly recommend.

title: Somewhat disappointing I ASSUME due to COVID, and am willing to give it a second chance one day.
text:
My wife and I do not have to go to only the best, five star hotels at all times in our travels. Doing so is a treat for us given how hard we work and how fortunate and blessed we are to afford to do so.  As such, we are perfectly fine staying in an average, run of the mill hotel so long as it is clean, comfortable, and welcoming.  

HOWEVER, if you ARE going to be a five star hotel (and, thus, charge accordingly), then do it the right way, please.  Were it not for the hotel's hospitality manager, Farina (sp?), the rating would get one less star.  For example, at five star hotels, they remind you about reservations they make for you so that you don't forget.  At five star hotels, they have someone escort you to your room upon check-in to see if you like the room.  At five star hotels, they don't place your entire family on separate floors in separate sides of the hotel when you specifically request to be on the same floor near each other just weeks earlier (or, at least, notify you in advance of arrival).  At five star hotels, they have someone in front to hail a taxi at all times.  These are the perks expected from a five star.  These were all absent or, to the extent done, had to be requested.  Not cool.   

Leaving that aside however, it IS a very nice hotel in a key tourist attraction area on a very quiet street, albeit with small rooms (trust me... a suite here is smaller than most).  Also, we received very good pricing for the family for three rooms, and some of the hotel staff was excellent, such as the gentleman who stored and brought out the handicap carts for our parents each day.  The same goes for the female bartenders.  However, the staff serving the cocktails and some members of the front desk need a bit more training and polish (again, it's a five star; so strive to act like one).  That being the case, given we stayed there right off the COVID recovery period, so it may have been a matter of management's struggle to get experienced staff to work.  If that was the case, then we certainly understand and would be willing to go back another time.

title: The best Hotel
text:
The Sofitel Paris Le Fauborg is honestly the best hotel I’ve ever stayed at. My mom and I always visit Paris in the fall, but due to COVID we haven’t been able to go for the past few years. This was definitely our best trip yet - a lot thanks to this charming hotel and their lovely service minded staff. We stayed for three nights, and everything was perfect from check in to check out. We celebrated my birthday, and so upon arrival I was greeted with the most lovely present accompanied by a card and cookies. At breakfast the next day, the staff even brought cake (which was delicious by the way) and a glass of champagne while singing the happy birthday song! Soo nice, and made my day so special. 

As for the rooms - they are wonderful. Everything you need from sowing kits to hair products is accessible. And the BEDS!! They are magic!! You just want to stay in it all day, instead of going out and explore Paris. The rest of the hotels atmosphere is so warm and welcoming - and the decor is so chic, that goes without saying. I also want to mention the breakfast, which was absolutely delicious. Not one thing was missing! 

The staff of the Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg is the real reason for why I would highly recommend the hotel. They are so service minded, friendly and kind - and you can really tell that they want the very best for their guests. A special shout-out to the Breakfast Manager Stephan - which was just so sweet and charming. You could just tell that he loves his job. The housekeepers were also super nice, and did a great job with our room every day. 

I myself work in the Hospitality industry, and therefore highly appreciate experiences like these. I noticed the little things they do - like for instance that they every evening prepare the room with Camomile Tea and lay out slippers on each side of the bed. These are small things, but they make a huge difference! 

Thank you Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg! We will definitely be back. 

Best Regards, 

Tara France and Pia Camilla

title: Again and again, my favorite hotel in Paris
text:
4 years ago, I was the last time at Sofitel Le Faubourg. That time, the strongest point: employees and location. Today, strongest point: staff and location. It is just amazing how this hotel manages to keep all their employees and they continuously manage to exceed our expectations. 

Arriving by car after tough security check (American embassy next door), they parked my car, took our luggage and accompanied us to the check in. The newly appointed GM welcomed us personally (wow!) and we got an upgrade into a junior suite. 

This is one of the only hotels which does not save cost the usual average hotel does:
Saving on services, staff, amenities and with the lousy excuse: Due to covid, we can not provide this and that but we charge you full price.  Yes, the Faubourg charges but it is justified and worth to pay. Services are complete, with heart and soul. No Covid savings which impact customer satisfaction. Well done, I know, how much pressure you have from your headoffice!

Overall a wonderful stay. A good product, nice rooms designed by Didier Gomez and a wonderful crew. Thank you, we will return!

BTW: The best is the Sofitel My Bed. We loved it that much, that we bought ourselves a set for our home! Nothing better on the market!

title: A Big Thank You to Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg!
text:
My son and his fiancé were married in Paris in late August and reserved their wedding night stay at Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg.  Regrettably, the COVID-19 pandemic made in-person participation by his Canadian family impossible.

Wanting to contribute to their special day from a distance, a family member contacted the hotel to enquire about what could be done.  Showing great compassion and empathy for our circumstances, the Sofitel representatives offered several upgrades and amenities free of charge, including upgrading their room to a suite and placing a bottle of champagne, macarons and a beautiful flower bouquet in the suite before their arrival.  In addition, we purchased for each of them a lovely hotel robe, which the hotel's in-house seamstress embroidered with their names and wedding date.  Not only was the embroidery perfect, the staff and seamstress went above and beyond to accomplish it with only a couple of days' notice. 

My son and his bride were unaware of these special items and so were very pleasantly surprised when they checked-in between their wedding ceremony and formal photos.  At that time, we were able to engage in a brief FaceTime call during which their happiness and gratitude for all of the “special treats” came through very clearly!  As the remote father of the groom, seeing my son and new daughter-in-law so happy on their wedding day meant a great deal to me.

On behalf of all of our family, I would like to express our sincere gratitude to Thomas, Jerome, your hotel seamstress and all members of your hotel staff who contributed to making our newlyweds' special day so wonderful and memorable.  As our family contact with the hotel remarked to me, “the hotel staff were a real stand up team and I’m grateful that they chose that hotel for such a special event. You can tell they really cared”.  

My family and I have stayed at Sofitel hotels on several occasions.  Each visit was an excellent experience and I am glad that we can now add the Sofitel Paris Le Faubourg to the list.  We look forward to another Sofitel visit when international travel becomes possible.

title: Rushed at Check-Out
text:
This hotel is a pretty standard 5* luxury hotel in all the expected ways: well located, good service, nice room, etc. However, there was just one part of our stay that soured our experience at the hotel.

On the day of the check-out, we were around 30 minutes past the check-out time when we were basically kicked out of our suite, due to the fact that evidently they had to prepare the hotel for some visiting dignitaries and their retinue. This left a very sour taste in my mouth, as it is generally understood, especially among this caliber of hotels, that one has a little bit of flexibility upon checkout (up to an hour).

Or maybe this is a French thing - but I haven't had this at any of the other hotels I've been to in France or Paris before. Regardless, this experience soured my overall stay.

title: NOT WORTH IT
text:
This is my first time writing a review because i feel strongly about this hotel. I was really looking forward to staying here as the highlight of my trip and had very high expectations before coming. Not just my expectations were not met, i am very disappointed with this hotel. Ok, the location is great for shopping, near all the high end luxury brands and its safe bec its next to the US embassy, but that’s it. 

First of all, being an accor gold member, we weren’t given any preferential treatment at all. I had a bad feeling the moment we stepped out of the elevator. The hallway is narrow and cheap looking. Second, the room. Where should i start. When we entered the room, it smelled strongly of alcohol!!! The disinfectant kind. Yuck! As far as i know we were staying at a hotel, not a hospital. I brought this up with the reception and asked to be transferred to another room but was told that there were none available. Ok, but this happened everyday, everytime we came back go our room it smelled of alcohol. The room itself was blah. Nothing special. Its very small, and old. The bathroom was worse, it was older! The cabinets are small, not enough room to put my stuff, so i had to put all my clothes in the chairs in the room, it wasn’t a relaxing sight. The ref was locked, i could not even put my water to have it chilled 😞And i am not a fan of the shower in the bathtub thing. The bath tub was too high, i was afraid of falling/slipping getting off the bathtub. The fixtures are old. Let me just say that ive had better rooms at airbnb at way way below what i paid for this hotel. If i could rate this hotel with 0 or negative rating. I will! 😠😠😠

title: Expensive and Disappointing
text:
We have stayed at this Sofitel several times in the past (10 years ago) and were always happy. The hotel itself is lovely but our room was small and dark with a shower that was absolutely useless! The bed had an under blanket which had a ridge in the middle which meant that my wife and I kept rolling to the edge of the bed. 

The staff were pleasant enough but the service at breakfast was very poor. The 'very expensive' hot breakfast was stone cold. This was scrambled egg, bacon and sausage. I waited for a fresh delivery but that really wasn't much warmer. The fruit and cereal was OK but the coffee took forever to arrive and was sludgy and undrinkable. I am amazed that the quality was no very poor at breakfast. 

The reason we went back was our previous experience and hotel location which is great - a couple of minutes from the Le Place de La Concorde.

We won't use this hotel again.It was very disappointing.  We are in the Gatwick Sofitel next week so let's hope it's better than Paris!

title: Worst experience & site does not match up with the real deal!
text: This is one of the worst "prestigious" hotels that i have ever stayed in. I had booked a 3 night stay in the prestige suite to spend my last leg of my France birthday trip, however what turned out to be in reality did not match up to the descriptions that was on the hotel website. The room was small and cramped; and felt like they had just turned a one standard bedroom and added in a small little living room. The site also stated that the prestige comes with a walk in wardrobe, bathtub & separate Hammam shower; and to my horror, it is a small little bathroom that looked exactly like what you would get in a standard one bedroom and a tiny little wardrobe. I had also other family members that were staying there at the same time and had booked the same room. When i had compared their rooms to mine, it looked utterly different! After expressing my displeasure to the guest relations, i was given a pile of excuses that the different suites are configured in different layouts, and that my other family members were given an upgrade. I had to pull out the site descriptions to show them what they had promised where not what was delivered and they only had to work through getting me an "upgrade" out of good will for my last night and giving me "free breakfast" (though i had expected that since you do not have a lounge, most 5 star hotels, especially Intercontinental Opera would provide breakfast for free to their suite customers) and a 200 euros off the whole stay.  Not that i care that the free breakfast or free one night (pfft) upgrade - i could jolly well pay that on my own, however what throws me off is the full experience that i had to endure throughout the stay, made in China i could say. What you see online, is portrayed different in reality. Negative and claustrophobic to sum it up. Never again! This will be one and last time whenever i am back in Paris.

It has been a jewel and hidden gem for many years .
Recently it is not to the level of 5 stars anymore .

The rooms
..are small 
..aircon is noisy , need to turn off at night
..TV equipment must be 20 years old, it takes minutes to get it started
..prices changes from simple to double..i got trapped already several times as my assistant was not aware

The reception is the worst
..staff is permanently changing and does not seem to have appropriate training
...no recognition of loyal customers
..last visit my room was not ready ...kept me waiting even after 3 pm
..no help when you need late check out, have to beg them
..no leadership or management available when you ask for it

The hotel does not manage well its popularity and does not invest accordingly...

title: Absolutely Terrible
text:
I have traveled all over the world and have never experienced service this bad. First I was going to Paris to visit a friend who was coming in for business and staying at the hotel. Unfortunately there was a Heath in the family and she had to cancel her trip and room. The hotel was aware of the situation when I spoke with them and tried to cancel my non refundable room reservation. Under the circumstances I would have expected some flexibility but the hotel would not allow me to cancel and was quite rude. My room was 600 euros so not a cheap room. 
I decide to go instead of wasting the money and enjoy Paris for the day. That evening when I returned to the hotel and went to have dinner I was informed that the restaurant was closed on weekends. 
The overall service and attitude from most of the staff was terrible. The hotel is not that nice and with all the choices in Paris don’t waste your time or money staying here. You can get much better service and hotel experience at a cheaper price.
Very disappointed!

text:

title: Ideal Location
text: Lovely small hotel with elevator. Very nice, breakfast offered and it has a full bar. Close to everything in the Latin Quarter. Short walk (4blocks) from Metro. Bus stop at corner.  Restaurants and shopping directly across the street.

title: Charming if a little shabby
text: Classic 3-star in the heart of the Left Bank, so bear that in mind: cramped staircases, slow elevator, small bathrooms, tight-squeeze bedrooms.  BUT also wood beams in ceiling, friendly staff, diligent housekeeping, awesome location two blocks from basically everything cool.  Fifth floor and above get views of the Pantheon and other goodies.  Just wish they paid more attention to the little things.  Broken toilet seat, microscopic soap bars, dusty windowsills, worn-out and fraying "white" (gray) towels, discolored bathtub, chipping paint. . . .   Needs a refresh to keep up with other places nearby.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Excellent location. Clean, quiet and pleasant
text:
This hotel is close to many restaurants and shops in Saint Germain. Easy subway and RER access. Minutes from the Pont Neuf and l'Ile de la Cite, Sainte Chapelle, etc....
It is hard to find a better location. The hotel is smallish but clean with well appointed rooms, a nice staff and a pleasant breakfast.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Charming Hotel with Staff to Match & an Excellent Location
text: This was a wonderful hotel. It's charming, and the charm level is equalled (if not surpassed by) the staff. You can't beat the location. We were able to walk to all of the main sites we wanted to see, and it's surrounded by good restaurants. The breakfast was small but perfectly formed. Our rooms were small, which is to be expected in the middle of Paris, but in one of them we could see the very top of the Eiffel Tower, which was a thrill. I would happily recommend this hotel to my friends.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Fabulous hotel in perfect location
text:
We were delighted with our stay. Fantastic neighbourhood full of amazing restaurants and bars. Walking distance to all the main tourist attractions in Paris.

Room was a good size for Paris, staff were friendly. We didn’t pay for breakfast as there are so many places to eat on the doorstep.

The bathroom could do with being updated and my tall partner wasn’t able to shower as the attachment was too low, but this was a minor inconvenience given how much we loved the character and location of the hotel.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Nice little hotel in a great location
text: We spent 9 nights in mid-June, in a room overlooking the courtyard. The room was small, but that was expected, but it was quiet overall and the bed was comfortable. The room seemed to have been updated recently and was very clean with a hallway leading to the bathroom and shower. My partner was awakened one night from the voices of the guests in the next room, but once I gave him a pair of my earplugs that seemed to solve the problem (they didn't wake me up). One quirk - the air conditioning would go in and out, sometimes it was very cool and sometimes there would be no air blowing and it would be a bit warm and stuffy - this happened sometimes in the middle of the night. When I mentioned it to the desk clerk one day, he said that the AC was turned off for some reason but he turned it on and assured me it would stay on all night, which it did; but I'm not sure exactly why it was ever turned off in the first place. Another oddity was that some outlets in the room and downstairs seemed to charge my phone OK while others did not; not sure what that was about, maybe another quirk of an old building. We loved the central location just a couple blocks off the Pont Neuf, very easy to walk to the Latin Quarter, the Luxembourg Gardens, the Louvre, even the Marais. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. The continental breakfast was good, with croissants, fruit, eggs that you could boil, pre-wrapped cheeses and cold cuts. Special shout-out to Najib, one of the front desk clerks who I had emailed back and forth with before the trip with various questions and who always responded promptly. The hotel is just around the corner from Rue de Buci which has a number of excellent restaurants to choose from in a bustling and fun area - our favorite was Cafe Buci, while Atlas, a seafood restaurant catty corner from it, also was very good. The hotel made a great base for our Paris explorations.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Wonderful location, great rooms, helpful staff
text:
We enjoyed our four nights stay at the Hotel Dauphine very much. 

The location couldn't be beat, with easy access to all the city's sites and plenty of metro/bus options if walking was not preferred. Lots of good restaurants as well very close by.

Breakfast was by buffet on the ground level and very serviceable. The staff were friendly, efficient and helpful. 

The room was immaculate and the bathroom gorgeous, all recently done. Average sized rooms for Paris, but well appointed.

We will look for a room here again on our next visit.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Lovely Boutique Hotel on the bustling Rue Dauphine with great service and good value for money.
text:
Totally recommend this lovely boutique hotel on Rue Dauphine in the historic Latin Quarter of Paris. Rooms have an eclectic modern vibe and the hotel itself has a bright breakfast room looking out into the busy street outside. There is also a small, comfy residents bar where we had no problem getting a late nightcap.

The staff in the hotel are extremely helpful, courteous and very friendly. 

I loved the location and bustling vibe of this hotel and will definitely return for another visit to Paris very soon. All in all I would recommend a stay in Hotel Dauphine and think it is very well priced compared to other hotels in the area.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Good hotel, excellent location
text:
We recently stayed at the Hotel Dauphine St. Germaine, based on reviews here on Tripadvisor.  While I can't give this hotel a perfect rating, there were things I did like about it and others I did not.  

Pros:  The biggest pro is the staff!  They are all very welcoming and did everything in their power to make our stay comfortable and pleasant.  They gave excellent advice, including to be careful of pickpockets and Metro advice.
The location is very good, within a few minutes walk of St. Michel Notre Dame Metro station.  Also, walking distance to Notre Dame, the Louvre, Musee D'Orsay, and of course, the entire Left Bank/Latin Quarter with its restaurants and shops.
Breakfast was available, consisting of cereals, eggs, pastries, yogurts, etc. and very convenient.
It's a cute little hotel in an old building, which I love.
We had a little view of the Eiffel Tower!
Refrigerator and safe in room, appreciated.
Extra pillows were provided as needed, along with anything else we asked for.
Our bed was very comfortable.
We did have a fan in our room.
Room faced the back of the hotel and courtyard and was very quiet.
Nice hot water for showers.

Cons:  little old buildings come with quirks!  The tiny lift SAYS it could fit five people, but I wouldn't want to be one of the five! 
Some rooms (ending in 5 or 6) are a 1/2 floor down from the lift-not an issue for us, but could be for others.
Our room (superior double) was VERY small-it had a hallway, which I think may be part of the square footage of the room.  I've stayed in European rooms before and this was awkwardly small.
Bathroom super small, so is shower.
The decor (in our room, at least) was very tired-it was supposed to be charming but the wallpaper is very scuffed which makes it look not clean. I DON'T think the room was dirty at all, just needs refreshed.
The air conditioning was not the best.  Our room didn't get cool until during the night.

I would stay again because of the excellent staff and location.  I would probably not ask for the superior double and would choose a larger room.
If you want fancy, this is not the correct hotel for you.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Gem in the 6th
text: We had a fabulous stay in this gem of a hotel in the 6th arondissement. The room was small but that’s usual in Paris. Comfortable bed, lovely quiet room and powerful shower. Lots of restaurants in the area and within walking distance of a lot of the sights - Notre Dame, Musee du Louvre, Musee d’Orsay, Jardins du Luxembourg etc. The breakfast offering was a welcome addition, with plenty of fresh juice, pastries, bread, cheese, eggs, yoghurt. The staff were super friendly also. We’ll definitely be back.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Perfect Location and friendly staff
text:
Me and my partner booked here for 4 nights and we were not disappointed. The staff were friendly and the room was clean and comfortable. Other reviews did state there was no safe in the room but our deluxe double room did have one. We had a courtyard view and was very quiet.
Breakfast is €12 euros per person and includes, coffee, juice and continental options. The bread was delicious. Additionally There are plenty of bakeries around the area if you want to grab a croissant on the go. 

The location (6th Arrondissement) is next to many bars, cafes and crêperies. If you’re English and want a pint I would recommend le cavern and le mazet as during happy hour their pints are €4-6 which is a lot more reasonable than €13 euro in most of the more traditional French bars. 

The nearest metro station is St Michel- notre Dame - about a 7 minute walk. The metro system is very easy to navigate. 

 Only reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that the room decor was slightly dated (maybe part of the Paris charm) and my boyfriend didn’t like the shape of the pillows. Overall we had a lovely stay and would happily stay again and recommend to friends and family.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Excellent hotel
text:
We were nine people, and the service was great. 
The staff is nice, welcoming, and help us alot with finding great restaurant. Very recommend. And thanks a lot to Anna, from the concierge. Hope to come back there soon
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Perfect location.
text: Stayed here with my husband, clean rooms and hotel and good service, so friendly! Would reccomend based on location, comfort and service which for me is always important when looking on a hotel to stay at. Thanks, Julie !
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Highly recommend
text: Hotel location was excellent, lots of resraurants and bars nearby at reasonable prices. Hotel staff were great, very friendly and helpful. Room was clean and had everything we needed for our stay, would definitely go back.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: 100% recommended
text:
A fantastic hotel. It is in an amazing location, a 1 minute walk to the Seine, and then Notre Dame is 5 minutes away. A lot of other great places to visit - the Lourve, the Pantheon - are only 30 minutes walk away at maximum, and then you can easily get a 15 minute train to the Eiffel Tower.
Out of all the places we visited in Paris, the area and streets around the Hotel Dauphine were really the best! It's in the Latin Quarter, and so if full of lovely little side streets with great cafes, bakeries, bistros, and restaurants - it feels very authentic and less touristy than I was thinking it would be, especially because it's right in the centre of Paris. 
The staff are all super helpful, and speak great English. The rooms are really comfortable, just the right size, and you can have lovely views from the window. It was all clean and in great condition for us, too. 
This was our first time in Paris, so we didn't really know what to expect, but we loved it and will happily recommend this hotel to friends and family if they ever travel to Paris. And if we ever return to Paris, we would absolutely stay here again. For the price, this location and comfort really can't be beaten :)
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Quaint, Quirky European. A True Gem,
text: If you are looking for a hotel that will give you a real Paris feel and experience then look no further. The location is perfect and close to everything. Located in the 6th Arrondissment it is near Notre Dame, Pont Nuef, and the Louvre and d’Orsay museums. Nearby bus and metro lines making it easy to get around . It is quirky, quaint very French. The hotel staff are very friendly, helpful and speak English. The rooms are very small by US standards but it is clean and everything works. The water pressure is good and it is hot. The AC works. Wifi is good and easy to connect. The breakfast is very good with enough variety for everyone but there are many cafes in the neighborhood that will also serve a decent breakfast. One note of caution is that the hotel consists of two buildings that were joined.  If you have a room number that ends in 5 or 6 be prepared to walk up or down a half flight from the lift. Also avoid a room number that ends in 6 as the bathroom is extra small and awkward. All in all we stayed 4 nights and will return on our next trip to Paris.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Perfect hotel!
text: I stayed here with my sister and niece. We had two rooms that were right next to each other. The rooms were nicely decorated and clean. Each of us had full bathroom that were very nice. The location is fantastic! Very close to transportation, restaurants and shopping. We highly recommend!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Paris trip
text: I loved the location of the hotel, the cleanliness of rooms and the staff!   Thank you Patricia for everything!!    Definitely coming back here!   close to all tourist attractions!   Yes the rooms are small but that is paris for ya… all of Europe is like that.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Cute boutique hotel in a great location!
text: This quaint hotel is located within walking distance of great restaurants, the river, gardens/parks and even the Louvre and Notre Dame!  Rooms were a little small but amenities and service were great.  Patricia at the desk was super helpful overall.  Nice selection for breakfast, too.  We would stay here again!!!  Merci!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Hotel Dauphine Great for Travelers
text: Loved this hotel!  First time staying on the Left Bank and loved it.  The location was fabulous and so convenient to so many attractions.  The staff was incredible and so helpful answering questions.  I highly recommend this hidden gem in the Left Bank.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: My second home!
text:
I travel to Paris frequently for business and usually stay the weekend for pleasure. Over the years I have chosen Hotel Dauphine for it’s fantastic location in the heart of St Germain, close to transport, museums and wonderful restaurants.
The staff are charming and helpful and have become familiar faces. The rooms are well appointed and really thoughtfully decorated. 

I always enjoy and look forward to my next stay at the hotel Dauphine.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Charming hotel; friendly staff
text:
Although our room was very small, the bed was quite comfortable.  The location can't be beat as it is close to so many things that you would want to see, and it's also in the neighborhood of St. Germain.
We were there with a group, and one of them had a medical emergency.  The staff couldn't have been nicer, making accommodations to help her travel partner who needed to stay much longer than originally thought.
I would always come back to this hotel.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Good location
text: Good location!! Next to shops and many cafes. Patricia help us during our check in, she was extremely nice. Can’t say much about the rest of the staff working at the front desk, because they weren’t nice at all. We decided to extend our stay by an extra day, and the guy working at the front desk told us they were completely booked, but I went online and found they had rooms. Long story short since we didn’t like the rest of the staff, we decided to go to another hotel near by in Saint Germain and had a great experience. I don’t think I’ll be back to this hotel, but if we do it’ll be only for the location.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Amazing Customer Service
text:
I am so amazed at how much care the staff took prior to our trip in helping us with arrival questions as well as places to eat near there.  We only stayed one night, yet we felt like very special guests.
The location was great and we enjoyed the quick time we were there.  The room was very comfortable and clean.  A great find!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Merci beaucoup!
text: After a few rearranged visits due to the pandemic, which the hotel staff were very helpful and accommodating with over email, we finally got to visit this wonderful hotel. We had a great stay-the local area and overall location for exploring Paris are fantastic and many sights are within walking distance. Lots of great bars and eateries close by too.  Metro and bus are also handy. Rooms were comfortable and well appointed including a really good shower and comfy bed - exactly what you want after a busy day exploring. Reception staff were all lovely and couldn’t have been more helpful. We loved the Saint Germain area and will return to stay at this hotel on our next visit! Thanks to everyone at the Hotel Dauphine for making our stay so memorable!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Disappointed.
text:
It's a great location, old fashioned charm, I had waited 2 years to be back in Paris and wanted to love it. 
The staff were lovely, front desk folks were helpful , esp. Patricia, no complaints there. But maid service and breakfast room sketchy...toiletries in room consisted of one bottle of shower gel attached to wall in shower and a little bar of soap which was removed after a few days and not replaced until mentioned at front desk. Also had to ask for toilet paper after leaving the empty roll visible.  Towels not replaced consistently and one day the bathmat was a ripped in half towel.
Tables not cleared quickly enough in breakfast room, folks waiting, having to ask for items to be replenished on buffet, choices diminished as stay went on..no baguette pieces!
No English language tv channels working, and half of the others usually not available either. Explanation was weather and dish but this was every day.

Perhaps staffing shortages, other shortages due to pandemic, which I hope will be sorted out.

Otherwise a good stay.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Great hotel!
text: Wow!  Such a great hotel!  Everyone was extremely friendly and willing to help us out.  They looked up the train station as well as additional information for us to get to Chantilly (they even printed it out and highlighted important information).  They worked with our minimal French and were willing to speak English.  They even taught us some French which helped us on the trip.  Great location!  Close to the Louvre, Musee Orsay, Notre Dame, as well as some great cafes.  You can easily walk to a lot of the main attractions in Paris.  I always felt safe in the area!  Comfy beds and very clean!  I will definitely return to this hotel in the future!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Great hotel!
text: We had a wonderful stay at Hotel Dauphine St Germain! The early check in email was so convenient! Once we all arrived (we were traveling with 3 families so had 9 rooms booked) all but 2 rooms were ready for us early- which was quiet a surprise as we did not expect the rooms to ready early. The rooms were clean and cool. The decor was perfect.  What made the stay the best was the friendly service we had from each person working the front desk. We were in and out of the hotel and each time we were greeted kindly and always willing to help! We will definitely stay at this hotel again!!  (And the location is perfect!!!!)
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Wonderful trip to Paris!
text:
My husband and 2 adult children travelled to Paris in July 2021 for 3 nights while touring several cities in France. We were told that the 6th arrondissement was a good area to stay due to the many bakeries and eateries as well as the walkability of the neighborhood. We found the Hotel Dauphin St Germain and it perfectly fit our needs. The St. Germain neighborhood was walkable to the Notre Dame cathedral and the louvre. It was safe for my teens to run along the Seine in the morning- and was highly convenient for bakeries and dinners in the evening . The metro was very close to take us to other tourist spots such as the Eiffel Tower. The staff could not have been more accommodating- always willing to give advice or suggestions- both day and night. We had 2 adjoining rooms - each with a double bed- it worked perfectly and was plenty of space. 
We will definitely recommend to friends considering a trip to Paris!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Gem hotel in Rive gauche
text: Great location Rive gauche, just few steps off Pont neuf. So close to everything that is worth exploring in Paris, louvre, Musée Orsay. Shopping and dining areas like st Germain and Bon Marche. I enjoyed the vibe in the street it was on with the more normal coffee shops and restaurants. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. Good breakfast French style in an cozy salon. The room has everything one needs if staying in paris: a great bed and shower to restore after 30,000 steps of walking. I also had to take some work meetings and wifi was extremely reliable. The only thing to know is that street is busy at night and can take a while for things to cool down. I was personally not bother but other maybe. You cannot have it all!
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Excellent location
text: Lovely place with an excellent location that will allow you to reach almost any attraction in a short time. Everything was perfect despite the size of the room, which is not very spacy: the staff was super kind, the bed extra comfortable and clean and there is a lovely view on the road (ask for a room not on the road if you are bothered by. I’d suggest it.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Devastated to find they don't return belongings!
text: I stayed in this hotel for a week in June 2021. Business/Pleasure trip with 2 other friends. No 2nd key to room was first observed, okay breakfast but no iron provided when asked for. The location is great to walk to all great site seeing, night life, restaurants, etc. The staff was good with English and kind. The hotel is a big shabby chic, but comfortable. The water pressure is great and water is hot. The noise outside as there is a pub nearby continues even during weekdays to 2am. I would have returned for the cost/value but in leaving I left a hanging luggage insert toiletry bag (one where the clear plastic reveals the contents). I left it hanging on a hook on the wall NOT the floor or anywhere near trash.  I had valuable jewelry in mine, contact lenses, skincare, and more. It was more than 12 inches in length and clearly not trash. I called immediately within 7 hours of departure. The desk clerk had to speak with housekeeping. With time difference I am now two days out and despite repeated calls, emails and providing my FedEx account for rapid shipment of my belongings. I am told they thought it to be trash. Unbelievable. The housekeeping must have stolen it and this is not a big or busy hotel. I am shocked to not get "Yes, we found it and held it for your claiming". So devastating to find this out. Ethics are everything and management should know.  As a result I cannot in good faith recommend.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Central location, cozy rooms
text: I felt part of france staying in this cozy boutique style hotel. It is right in the heart of the tourist area boulevard st michel which is very lively yet the rooms were very quiet. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the breakfast kept me going all day.. major metro lines made it convenient to go all around the city.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Delightful hotel!
text:
This is a delightful boutique hotel. The room was bigger than I expected in a Paris hotel. The bathroom was modern and also bigger than usual. The staff was friendly and helpful and spoke English. The included cold breakfast had meat, cheese, yogurt, cereal and of course,  croissants.

This is one of the nicest neighborhoods in Paris. Lots of small shops and good restaurants. If this is your first visit or you already know Paris, I highly recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Lovely Left bank  hotel
text: We stayed here 2 years ago.  Could not go to Paris this year because of Covid, but will never stay anywhere else.  Perfect location and wonderful staff.  The room was spacious and the bathroom roomy enough for Americans.  Breakfast was great, and the bar made evenings very relaxing.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: The nexus of my visit
text: Great location; almost everything I wanted to see was just a short walk away.  Restaurants galore. Very smart and helpful staff, day and night. Comfortable bed and the bathroom was spotlessly clean and fresh. And I am looking forward to the time when I can return.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: My best place to stop in Paris
text: Since I discovered this hotel in Paris, I didn´t tried another one.  It is simple perfect: localization, charming, gentle people... everything!  I can´t wait the end of the pandemic to visit my beloved city once again (I didn´t go in 2020). :-(
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Last Minute Pick
text: Christmas 2 years ago.  My plan was to stay for four days and move on to another part of Paris.  The room was charming, the  breakfast delicious, and the front desk person was very helpful.  The location was incredible, so close to attractions and great places to wander.  I ended up staying at the hotel for the entire trip.  It is my top recommendation for a Paris visit.
name: Hotel Dauphine Saint Germain

title: Charming
text: Charming!.. Stayed 7 days with my sister (I’m 70,she72...so we’re no “spring chickens).. stayed on 4th floor overlooking street.. at night it was quite noisy from bar a few doors down, but what the heck..we’re in Paris!... her first trip there. A few years ago my son took me with his young family and we stayed in very large suites at Hotel Raphael.Although I thought it was wonderful at the time, I’d much rather return to this lovely hotel!! Location , fabulous! Staff, fabulous!! If this “Covid 19” goes away, my sister and I would love to return!..
