On the room, we had a room on the third floor, room 37. It is next to the lift, on the right when u exit the lift.  The entrance to the room is odd.  Why? Firstly, you exit the lift by pushing the lift door outwards, lift door opens in the direction of 9-12 clock wise and its heavy. The room is on the right of the lift but U can't see or get to room 37 unless you close the lift door first. Secondly, The hotel room door, in which u open with the access card, opens OUTWARD towards you, (i.e. You have to pull the door towards you, in the direction of 3-6 clockwise). Then, strangely, you get ANOTHER door that opens into the room). All other rooms on level 3 have only one door that opens inward.  So the issues? In a tight confine of the lift and room corridor, that barely allows for two persons and two luggages, you be opening/closing a lot of doors! And while u at at it, u just pray that someone else don't come to level 3 and pushes open the lift door at you, as you give adequate clearance space to open the first door (that opens towards u)! Room 37 is away from the main road, and opens to an air ventilation shaft or air well.  There is light an de you can leave you window open at all times.  Room 37 is a small room and equally small toilet.  If you are on the larger frame and have large luggages , it's best to avoid room 37. On the downside, the room carpet smell musty (due to ventilation perhaps?). Avoid this room if you can. On the other TripAdvisor report I've read, a lot of contributors lamented on the redlight district, sex shops, noise level etc.  I feel that the noise level would be from those rooms fronting Rue Frochot. Most sex shops are located on the main road of Blvd de Clinchy and gets to be noisier toward Pigalle metro and the direction uphill to Monmarte. That's the nature of this part of town. Overall, Rue Frochot is fairely decent and quite. There is a grocers and carrefours city when u exit the hotel on the right.  The city gets to be better when u exit left and walk down the quieter part of the neighborhood. Go to Buvette for breakfast or Le Petit Canard (Duck confit!), on the same street 5-10 min walk.  Overall, a nice and good hotel to stay, u pay for what you get and enjoy the different side if Paris.

title: Close to train station
text:
The staff makes this place worth it!  I don’t recall the guys name who checked us in but I’ve never felt more welcomed in a hotel. He recommended where we could go, things to do, places to eat, the train station (which is really easy to use). Montmartre is within walking distance and a must see place while in Paris. Train station is close by. When you exit the hotel, if you turn left and then head up that street, you will find a busy street with lots of local places to eat, desert shops and other things. You see a lot of locals walking around and it’s very picturesque. You’re in Europe so the rooms are not that huge but it the bed was comfy. The hotel itself isn’t very modern but it was comfortable. The breakfast was $10, and it was absolutely delicious. We ate there every morning. 

Cons: there is an “adult” club close by, but the area itself is so beautiful, you really don’t notice any of that and we felt safe walking around the area.

title: Nice Hotel Close to the Metro
text:
We recently stayed three nights in Hotel Opera Frochot. The hotel was part of a travel package, but it turned out to be nicer than I would have booked for myself. Although the rooms were small (like all rooms in Paris), they were very modern and clean.

The hotel is located just a block away from the Pigalle Metro station, which was convenient for getting around the city as well as to and from CDG airport. It is also within walking distance of the Moulin Rouge and Sacre Coeur.

However, be aware that this area is known for its adult shops. There are also bars/clubs on the block—one of which still had people in it when we were leaving to sightsee in the morning. Although we always felt safe and weren’t bothered by a little street noise at night, this hotel might not be for everyone. But we enjoyed it and would return.

title: cute, convenient, not particularly safe.
text: Stayed here for four nights, and since it was Paris, we obviously did not spend a huge amount of time IN the hotel!!! :) . the room was probably the tiniest that we ever got. and the bathroom even more so. That being said, it was clean and comfy and everything worked well. the room had a window that opened all the way, with a cute streetview. the furnishings modern, and everything clean, just the way I like it. the staff was helpful. One night we were looking for a liquorstore to go get a nightcap, and the staff gave us great directions. One morning we were looking for a quickie breakfast, and same thing, great directions and exactly what we were looking for. The bad things now: the area is kinda sketchy, one guy was getting arrested in front one afternoon...coulda been a bank robbery. A discarded, stained mattress stayed on the sidewalk for all 4 days we were there, just 30 or so feet from the entrance. The disco/bar almost immediately below/to the side was loud at night. I didn't mind that much because I brought earplugs, and we seriously considered going there anyway, but, some people might find that annoying. Lastly, one thing was pretty  bad. We asked for them to store our bags on our last day, so we departed in the morning, and returned at 5pm. Our bags were still where we left them,8 hours earlier: next to the checkin counter, accessible by anyone. To make matters worse, this is where I lost/ got stolen/ my $40 velvety travel pillow. They couldn't find a safer place? But since this was the only bad thing that happened, I will give them the benefit of the doubt.

title: Lacking
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights. Bought the hotel as part of a travel package deal. Photos make it look larger than it really is. Is in an edgy, gritty, artist, hipster style neighborhood. Lots of bars , near the red light district, and Moulin Rouge in Pigalle district. Rooms are small and especially the bathrooms are tiny and laid out weird. Had to turn sideways to squeeze between the sink and shower. No space for toiletry storage and not even a place to hang towels. We are not huge people, nor are we small, perhaps a bit above average. The shower stall was so tiny that when you turned around you opened the door and water all over.

That being said, looks like they have had somewhat recent remodel. Property was clean and well maintained. It was 2 blocks from a train station that seemed to be one of the more centrally located in the city. Very easy to get around. 

We were underwhelmed but figured this was a decent boutique European hotel......until the last night. A/C stopped working. We asked the clerk to have it checked when we went out. Still the same when we got back. Very hot. When asked about it he said open the window. The block had 8 bars and restaurants, all open late plus an all night sex shop. Way too much noise. He said no other solution and no other rooms. We complained, got some cold waters, and went back to the room. At midnight the phone rings and he said I have a room that didn't sell, you can move there if you want. Not sure why this option wasn't available at 10:30 (actually I am) but we moved and got a comfortable 6 hours of cool and quiet before we had to catch our airport shuttle.

title: April in Paris
text: This hotel is located in Pigalle. 5 minute walk to Moulin Rogue theatre and 15 minutes to Montmartre a great shopping and restaurant district with views of much of Paris. Lots of Artists. Anyway, the hotel has lots of restaurants in the area. Great pozza and Brioche for Coffee and amazing Croissants and Macroons. Anyway, the rooms are pretty nice although not American hotel good. You can get it around the corner though and may be better served but hotel breakfast is ok.  The staff are wonderful,  The desk staff, Housekeeping and kitchen person  are all wonderful.  Very close to the metro and you would do well to use it.  It is a great system.  Next to the coffee shop.  Bring a debit card and get euros that way so it doesn't cost you a lot.  It is Pigalle near Moulin Rouge.  You may want a more central location in the 1st Arrondisement but we did fine.  April in Paris

title: A cosy little hotel with friendly staff
text: The hotel is tucked in a relatively quite area where just a block above has a lot of activity going on. Pigalle is the metro station that is close to. Pigalle is where some of the adult stores and shops are located yet you walk for couple minutes and you come to the Hotel Opera Frochot. The first night, the heater was not working properly, the receptionist (possibly owner) came to our room to see what the problem was. Once he figured out, it is not something he could fix, he gave us an extra cover and told us that we can switch the room the following day. So the next day we changed the room, So we get to stay in two different rooms and we were pleasantly surprised how clean it was, and the bed was comfortable, the room is a bit small and the bathroom is very minimal and the shower you cant really move around much and but we were really happy with the service and cleanliness of the rooms. The receptionist lady lent us the charger/converter which helped us tremendously. The other receptionists were really nice as well. They were very friendly. They had Christmas decorations which was perfect for the occasion. Right down the street, there was a bakery where every single morning we went to get our coffee, sandwiches, and desserts for the day. Particularly the second room we stayed in (room 16), was pretty quite. They did not have a fridge in the rooms but because it was really cold outside, we kept our water outside the room which kept them very cold when we were ready to drink. There is a nespresso machine in the room, each coffee costs 1.5 euros, i had one but did not see the sign in the first room but saw the sign in the second room. so dont think the coffee is free. there is a city tax in the amount of 1.65 euros per person per day aside from the fee. we bought it as a part of package so I am not quite sure how much the daily rate is, but for what we paid overall, it was a great price. we really enjoyed our stay and once you know how to get around by the metro, it is very easy to find and enjoy your stay at Opera Frochot hotel. if we were to go to Paris again, we would stay there again.

title: Efficient but dissapointing
text:
Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights, overall it was efficient. The best thing about the hotel is the location. We were well received at check in, Sabrina I think helped us. We arrived prior to check in time and she was very friendly and did her best to get us into our room as soon as possible. 

The Wi-Fi was easily accessible at reception, but in the room it was virtually non existent- and we were staying on the second floor so it seemed unusual that it should be out of range.

At one point in the day yesterday, the power completely went out in the hotel. I don't know what that was about.

Lastly, and most unfortunately, this morning when we went to check out we were met with a very unfriendly and unhelpful staff member, I think his name was Sascha. Since I was unfamiliar with the city tax, and also concerned about receiving my deposit back ($50 security upon check in), naturally I asked questions to this effect for clarification. This staff member, Sascha, was very short and unhelpful. I was left with no understanding as to whether I would get my deposit back. I don't know if this rude attitude was because of a language barrier, or maybe his fatigue due to the early morning hour- I would hate to think it came from some homophobic disposition (I was with my partner who is also a woman).

If all you're looking for is a place to lay your head in a convenient location, then this hotel is fine.

title: Return Trip
text: I stayed at this hotel while passing through Paris on our way to Rome last February, and will return there again in December. I note a few reviewers complaining about the sex shops near this hotel.  It IS the Pigalle.  It is not Times Square in the 1970s.  You can just walk by, and we never had anyone approach us or do anything that caused concern.  The staff are completely fluent in English and tolerant of my bad French, very friendly and helpful. title: Clean small modern room with tiny bathroom
text:
We has a room on the second floor on this hotel. The elevator is very small (like a  small closet) so it is more convenient to take the stairs. So second floor was ok. There was no view except a small courtyard with some plastic plants placed around for effect and the hotel walls. No other windows visible so at least it was private. 
Mattress had a distinctive dip in the middle looking like a canoe. It was reasonably comfy but probably need to be replaced. Linens were ok. Bathroom small with an extremely small shower, so small you couldn't even bend down to pick up the soap. You have to squat. I had had experience with these showers in Italy so not a surprise. But you need to be flexible.
Decor modernized and attractive. There was AC over the door. Worked fine except the controls glow at night in the dark. So be warned if you need complete darkness to sleep.
Staff is ok--pretty much only speak French. Can get by with fractured French and English. There is a prepared breakfast for aroun d €12 served in the lower level and an express breakfast fo r €7. We had the express once. You sit in the lounge and the staff brings it to you. You get juice, coffee and small pastries. Coffee in the room espresso machine costs €1.50 per cup. 
Best feature is the proximity to the Pigalle Metro station-- only 2 blocks away. Buy a multi day pass to save money. Be warned that the 3 day Metro pass is 3 calendar days not 72 hours. So don't buy one too late in the evening or you will waste a day.
As others have reported, the street where you find the Metro station is also the porn and sex shop center of Paris. Things are quiet during the day but the street is pretty busy and explicit at night. So be careful with kids. We still felt pretty safe being there even at night. As always in Paris be aware of your surroundings and watch out for pickpockets wherever you go.
Heading south from the hotel towards the city center, there is a quaint neighborhood with great little bars and bistros and small fruit and grocery stands. It is a short walk to the Paris opera house where you will find many more restaurants and shopping.
Free wi Fi in the rooms. Tell the desk how many devices you need to connect and they will give you the appropriate number of passwords.

title: Nice small hotel in a good location in Paris
text: We took a 3-generation family trip over the Christmas holidays and stayed in this hotel in Paris.  It was in a good location, near a Metro stop (Place Pigalle) and a street with lots of shops for food, etc.  You should be aware that it's also very close to the Red Light district, in case that's of concern to you.  Lots of sex shops just up the road.  The hotel itself is small with a nice lobby area.  The rooms are also small, but normal for European sizes.  The showers are quite small.  The one in my mother's room had such a narrow entrance that she had to enter sideways.  She couldn't fit through the door otherwise (and she's not a large person).  Our shower size was fine, though.  One thing I will caution for people booking this hotel.  I would recommend asking for a room away from the street.  My mother's room was on the back of the hotel and was perfectly quiet.  Ours faced the street, and we were woken every night between 12 and 3 from street noise.  There is a theater on the same block and I think the noise was from people coming and going from there.  We kept our windows closed but it was still quite noisy.  All of this sounds quite negative, but there were lots of positives too.  Location, friendly and helpful staff, proximity to restaurants and shops.  For a hotel in a major city it is a reasonably-priced choice and one I would choose again.

title: safe, convenient, comfortable, good value.
text: The location is indeed right on the cusp of the red light district. What does that mean? Some sex shops down the street. Big deal! I never once felt unsafe or uneasy with the location. There is a train station right up the street and Sacre Coeur is in walking distance, along with Montmarte. The location is absolutely wonderful and convenient if you ask me! There is some noise outside on the weekends of party goers, but that was to be expected and was not a bother at all. The room wasn't nearly as small as some of the others I've stayed in in Europe, it was very comfortable for the two of us. I wouldn't let the location of the hotel steer you in the wrong direction, it is not unsafe and not dangerous! Would stay again if we are ever in Paris again.

title: great little hotel in a great location
text: picked this hotel from the European travel site Prestigia.  Picked the hotel based mostly on rate, metro access, and traveller rating/reviews, since it was our first time in Paris and were not familiar with all the areas of the city.  It turned out to be quite the gem.  Its very small, just 3 floors with not more than 15 rooms, if that.  Nothing fancy entry-wise, don't expect sweeping marble floors, but very polite, efficient and helpful staff.  The room itself was great, with large windows that opened to look over the rooftops, great big, comfy bed and beddings, and a cool bathroom that had a full tub.  Standard features, TV, coffee maker etc.  We thought it would be a closet-size room, but it was actually quite large.  Location was amazing.  200-300 meters from metro stop (Pigalle), in the middle of the red light district.  Next to it there is bar called Dirty Dick!!!!  But don't be alarmed, the area is very safe.  There is a wonderful organic grocery at the corner and a wine shop.  Tons of restaurants, and cafes.  Walking distance to Moulin Rouge and a bunch of sex shops!  But again, unless you have small kids, don't let that bother you.  I would pick that area over the more touristy and expensive areas any time.  Easy walk to the main train stations for Eurostar etc.

title: Wonderful Hotel des Grandes Ecoles
text: My wife and I returned home from Paris last night.  I couldn't wait to tell people about this hotel.  Behind the doors fronting an active street in a popular neighborhood, Hotel de Grandes Eccles surrounds a garden refuge from the activity of Paris.  Our room was larger than we had the week before on a Viking river boat.  No TV or A/C, but large windows opening to pleasant views. We stayed in room 114, the only one with a terrace, for six nights,  Rick Steves 'Pocket Paris' and Michelin Green Guide both commend the hotel's features, especially the garden setting.  But I must also commend the friendly, helpful, genuinely nice women and men who work there.  They must love their jobs because they do those jobs so well.  When Hemingway lived next door at 74 Rue de Cardinal Lemoine or one street over at La Maison de Verlaine on Rue Descartes (now a very nice restaurant), he had to go downhill to Blvd St Germain for food, drink and interesting people.  Today restaurants close to the hotel offer every cuisine except Mexican and South American (and Russian), The  cafes and restaurants feature outdoor tables, but good ones have nice inside seating;  prices were what we expected for Paris.  We also expected lots of people, but not the eight-piece brass band with three trombones on Bastille Day evening.  We miss Paris and our new favorite place to stay Hotel des Grandes Eccles.

title: Delightful and quiet place to stay in the 5th arrondissement
text:
The Hôtel des Grandes-Ecoles is one of those older traditional French hotels with a closed court and garden - you would hardly know from the street that there's a hotel behind the closed gate on the Rue du Cardinal Lemoine. We had a pleasant room on the 3rd floor of the main building, and it was big by traditional French standards, though small by American standards. A very quiet and calm ambiance. Breakfast was larger than I expected - croissant, bread, eggs, juice, jam, cheese, coffee, tea, or hot chocolate. 
We stayed here because an old friend first recommended it to me 40 years ago, but I had my own habits. This year, however, my "usual" hotel was closed due to Covid, so I found the old recommendation list and chose this hotel. 
The managers of the hotel were polite, friendly and helpful. The resident cat roamed the closed garden and was the delight of the guests. Very homey place - and well situated for a quick walk to the Seine or to the Pantheon, Rue Mouffetard with its well-known street markets, and the whole Quartier Latin. 
We loved our stay and would gladly come again.

title: 25th Wedding Anniversary
text: Just be very careful to choose the most expensive rooms with garden view - we didn't do that and ended up, first, in the tiniest of all imaginable rooms in the oldest part of the hotel - I mean, there wasn't even room to open your suitcase.  After inquiring, we were moved to a larger, barely serviceable room on the second floor, with high, porthole windows that didn't really admit any light.  Nothing in the older part of the hotel has changed in 25 years - particularly the bathrooms - it was barely tolerable.  Ditto wallpaper, curtains, linens - all ratty. Although I was quite sure I'd booked with breakfast, they charged me for it in the end.  In short, unless you pay more, there's no point in staying here.  The garden view rooms have updated bathrooms and modern beds - I nearly cried when I got a glimpse of one.  And, yes, I know that one gets what one pays for, but it wasn't cheap by any means.  I was in Paris in September and stayed in a hotel in the Marais that was the same price and positively luxurious.  We stayed at the Grandes Ecoles out of sentiment - it's where we stayed 25 years ago - and we had a better room then.  Oh - and no TV, no water or drink glasses, no effort at all to make anything comfortable - it was three days before they started bringing us complete sets of fairly ratty towels for two people.  Sorry - Paris je t'aime, but this place not so much -

title: Lovely hotel in a beautiful garden
text: We have stayed at Hotel des Grandes Ecoles several times over the years. These days you could probably call the style shabby chic. But where else in Paris can you find yourself in a lovely, quiet garden for these kind of prices! Breakfast is good and comes with copious coffee. The staff - as always - are friendly and professional. The rooms and bathrooms are Paris sized but the iconic wallpaper is lovely. You'll find several metro stops within a 10 minute walk and you'll find lots of lovely food shops just down the street in Rue Mouffetard. I love the location of this hotel - it's near enough to the action to be convenient without being in the middle of the madding crowd. Highly recommended.

title: Excellent service; outdated rooms; close to the Pantheon
text:
Our stay here was pleasant. The bed was very comfortable. Bathroom was spacious. Carpet and wallpaper were quite old. Although I believe that is what gives this hotel so much charm, the carpet really kind of grossed me out. It was stained and faded. There was no television in the room which was a bummer, but who needs to watch television when you are in Paris? Breakfast was excellent. Staff was very friendly. The outdoor common area was quaint and lovely. We had a room with a private entrance facing the common area, and it felt like our own little home.

The hotel is very close to lots of small cafés, a small grocery store, and banks. For me personally it felt like a bit of a walk to get to the metro, although by anyone else's standards it was quite close. We used the metro stop Cardinal Lemoine. It is also within walking distance to the Pantheon, which is just down the street from the RER line B stop Luxembourg. Convenient and quiet location away from all the major tourist attractions but close enough to the metro that everything is easily accessible.

I would definitely stay here again.

text:

The room for 3 person were small and had no AC, only fan. Bathroom was clean an nice. No TV.
the breakfast was served 07-11 and consisted of an baguette and a croissant together with tea or coffee. It was a nice breakfast.
The neighborhood is absolutely fantastic with rustic streets with small pubs and good restaurants.

When we checked out the receptionist had no idea I already paid for room and breakfast already, luckily I had printed a receit in French to show for it. Otherwise 220 euro down the drain.

In conclusion : don't expect that much from the hotel, it has its charm. But the location is fantastic

title: A real find
text: Stayed here with my husband and two teenage daughters and we all loved it.  Step through the high green doors to go back in time to a beautiful courtyard surrounded by trees and birdsong.  Simple rooms, very comfortable, good breakfast.  Fantastic location, walk up the road and you are in the Place de Contrascarpe - a lovely buzzy square surrounded by bars - great atmosphere, very friendly.  Lots of good restaurants nearby and wander down Rue de Mouffetard for amazing fromagerie, boulangerie, poissonerie and the best crepe shop in Paris.  Cardinal Lemoine metro 5 mins walk away.  Highly recommend this hotel.

title: 2nd stay, best in Paris
text:
First stayed at this hotel in 2013 and enjoyed it then for the exact same reasons i enjoyed it in 2018.

I’ve seen some reviews that say it is antiquated.
That’s the charm! The chintz is character.
If you want mod cons, this ain’t the place for you.

I stayed this time with my 2 friends and our mums.
This place satisfied an age range of 30-70.
The tube stop is nearby, but theres plenty to see within the hotels vicinity.
Lots of bars and restaurants nearby.

There is not tv in the room but why would you want to stay in and watch tv when you’re in PARIS!!!  

Staff are helpful and pleasant.

Breakfast is quick and simple.

Only tip would be, if possible, request a room in the out buildings surrounding the beautiful courtyard, much quieter than the room i stayed in in 2013 in the main house as it was above the breakfast room. 

It’s a slice of calm and tranquilty in the middle of a bustling city.

Simple, clean, quiet and excellently located.

Oh and reasonably priced.
What more could you want?!?

title: Best of the basic hotels,
text: We wanted to visit Paris for a few days on the way to another destination, and we looking for a basic, reasonably priced hotel.  We found 2 rooms at the Hotel des Grandes Ecoles and were very pleased.  We would stay there again.  The rooms are basic—no phone, no TV, no mini-bar or coffee maker—but clean and not too small.  The continental breakfast is similarly basic, just a croissant, bread, juice and beverage.  You must be ambulatory. The good:  the courtyard is lovely in good weather.  The staff pleasant and willing to speak simple English. Hotel elevators were small but in good working order.  Location is great for sight-seeing. Wi-Fi works.  The location is quiet for a city-location. The not so good:  There is no bell staff or room for luggage storage.  Reception is some distance from the street, which is problem if you need help with your luggage.  The dining room is too small for the number of people staying at the hotel.  The staff is limited; if you need information or assistance you would be wise to make your request when they are not overwhelmed with other traveler’s demands.  I believe there are a lot of students in the area and the restaurants nearby cater more to them than to tourists, which means you can find pizza and burgers and basic French food, but nothing outstanding.  If you want good French cuisine, you’ll have to walk outside the immediate area.

We had friends that stayed here as well who encountered problems with the hotel and staff but that is a whole different issue and an entirely different review.

title: Warning Money Stolen from Room
text:
My wife and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary with a cruise to Greece.  We decided to start our trip with an 2 night stay in Paris and off to Venice to start the cruise.  We stayed at the Hotel des Grandes Ecoles over 25 years ago and thought it would be nostalgic to stay again.The hotel is centrally located and close to restaurants and main attractions The courtyard is beautiful.  However, the hotel is in need of remodeling and the rooms are small even for Paris standards. Front desk staff is friendly.

We arrived on Wednesday, October 31st, checked in and everything was fine.  One of the first stops was to the ATM to withdrawn funds as I was meeting someone the next day at the hotel lobby to purchase a piece of art for 750 euros. In the evening I  placed all my US currency ($960) and 650 euros in a zip lock bag and rubber banded the 750 euros for my purchase the next day.  Normally I would store all my valuables in the room safe but there was no safe available in the room.  I placed all my funds in my laptop bag somewhat hidden in one of the many compartments (So I thought) and hid the bag under an table away from sight.  The next morning we leave for the day and return at 3:15 pm as I was to meet the artist at  4:00 pm. I retrieve my computer bag from under the table and noticed it has been moved ever so slightly. I get this uneasy feeling and start to count my money.  The 750 euros that I banded together is missing 50 euros, the $960 is missing $200 (my mother gave me two old style $100 bills and the thief took those which I thought strange) and the 650 euros is missing 150 euros. My wife and I immediately go to the front desk and complain.  They were very concerned and confronted the maid in our presence. Of course the maid adamantly denied stealing the money. The manager and director of the hotel said that they would investigate further and get back to us.  In addition, they stated that they believed the money wast stolen but they can't fire all their staff.  My wife and I return to our hotel room and she notices 260 euros is missing from her small coin purse that she left in an large bag near the night stand.  She goes back downstairs to the manager to report the additional loss.  The manager then states that since the amount of the stolen  funds are so large that we need to file an police report so the hotel can file a claim with their insurance company.  We go to the local police station and file the report and provided an copy to the hotel.

We checkout the next day and the manager said the hotel would file an claim with the insurance company and get back to us. It's been almost an month and no word from the hotel.  I will update this review if we get any resolution.  To the hotel's credit they comp us one day of our stay.  My wife and I travel a lot and thought this would never happen to us but it did. The first purchase I made upon returning home are locks for our suitcases.  Anyways we didn't let this ruin our vacation and had a great time on our cruise to Greece with Seaboure.  Safe travels to all.

title: NICE, VERY ENGLISH, GREATLY LOCATED BUT...
text:
Back at the Grandes Ecoles after four years I immediately realized that nothing, literally nothing, has changed: the exceptional position, the charming garden, the curiously English air of the whole… Unfortunately the negative aspects of this special hotel are unchanged either, with a new flaw: lack of any tv set and any minibar in the rooms, absolute absence of common spaces if not in the garden (obviously enjoyable just in hot weather)… The novelty is the appearance of plain plastic chairs in the garden, not in tune at all with the generally refined aspect of the rest. The most unbearable thing of all, however, is the breakfast: served in a room crammed with small tables for that function (therefore uncomfortable), it is served by a nice lady who takes to you, invariably and mercilessly, a basket with one croissant, one slice of baguette, one small jar of jam, one slice of cheese and, separately, a cup of something hot to drink. No more offering, no buffet scheme, no variety. Such a breakfast is offered for nothing short of 9 euros: at the bar in front you can get for less something more abundant and savory – which is really sad.
Conclusions. My rating goes down in view of the total indifference of the management to customers’ remarks. With some minimum adjustments this could be a place really out of the ordinary in Paris. Don’t they want it to be?

title: A time capsule
text:
If you had a French grandmother, a stay at the Hotel des Grandes Ecoles would be like a family visit. This place is a time capsule of another era, it feels like stepping back into a bourgeois home of the 1950's, aspiring to the elegance of the Belle Epoque. It's well-maintained, clean and depending on your point of view, either in need of serious updating or wonderfully true to another era. My view is definitely the latter: I feel like I've stepped back into the days when I first began to travel in France.
The location is wonderful - the heart of what a tourist wants to do in Paris - is walkable.  Three different metro line stations closeby. Neighborhood is filled with small restaurants. At night, some bars fill up with 20 somethings, the street nearby - Rue Mouffetard - well known for being a center for Sorbonne student life.
The hotel is 3 different buildings around a courtyard, which adds to the sense of being in a country home, you're isolated from street noise and the sense of being in an urban center. 
Several reviews following mine note what the hotel doesn't offer - television, generous supply of toiletries, breakfast in room, air conditioning. No tissues, no lotion. Wi-fi is free and dependable. Has a small library. In good weather, breakfast in the courtyard. Laundromat across the street - a convenience for those of us who don't want to pay 2 euros to wash a pair of underpants.

title: Perfect location for Metro access and walkable (1-2 miles) to many core Paris attractions
text:
The hotel is historic, with lovely room decoration (unique to each room), more spacious (for a double) than we expected, and the location could not be beat for the price we paid.  We spent a week here, and found we were within two blocks walk of Metro subway access,that connected easily to all major Paris Metro lines.  The Left Bank Latin Quarter is historic, next to the University, so many restaurants in the area are very good, often hip, and moderately priced.  The area buzzes with excitement at night, but the Hotel Ecoles courtyard (our room overlooked the beautiful courtyard) is protected from street noise.  Location is just down the street from the Pantheon and Luxembourg Gardens.  1.2 miles walk (or quick Metro ride) to Notre Dame along the Seine, and much more.
The hotel serves breakfast (9 euros per person), but there's a cafe just around the corner (one block away) where you can get a croissant plus coffee plus juice for less than 5 euros if you please.   The hotel has laundry service - our chamber maid took the laundry in the morning and had it ready that evening at a fair price (a large load cleaned and folded for about 35 euros).  All the staff at Ecoles were super nice and helpful, including getting us taxis when needed and information about the area.  We highly recommend this hotel!

title: September Sunshine - outside
text:
We stayed at this hotel in 1995 and were recreating some of those memories.  The same family owns the hotel.  When we mentioned that we had stayed there (and brought a pamphlet from that visit), they had very little interest.
The property has not changed much in 20+ years.  It is dated and small.  I didn't care about the lack of tv and managed 5 nights without a refrigerator.  But it was hot on this week and there is also no a/c.  It is nice that the windows open to the garden but unfortunately travellers drag their suitcases across the stone starting in the very early hours so you either have a hot stuffy room or the noises.
The garden (as many have mentioned) is the best feature and we did enjoy an hour each evening after a day of walking to sit and have a glass of wine and relax.

title: A garden paradise in the heart of Paris
text: The lovely little gem of a hotel is located behind tall gates in the heart of Paris.  Its three buildings surround a garden in which breakfast is served al fresco each morning (10 Euros/person).  There is a dining room for cooler weather or rain.  The rooms are small, but beautifully decorated in French country house style, and the bathroom was cool, sparkling white.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  Marie, the owner, arranged for an airport van for us.  Located near the sociable Place Contrescarpe, once the gates close at night (you can get in using your key after 8PM), you would never know you are in the city.  We were there just as the heat wave kicked in and the garden provided an oasis after a long day of touristing.  Marie and her staff served us iced water in late afternoon to help us cool off!  There is no air-conditioning, but each room has a large fan and the tall windows open wide.  It's located close to the Metro, but you can also walk the two minutes to Contrescarpe for restaurants, cafes, and shops.

title: Perfect Left Bank cosy hotel
text:
My partner and I stayed for 3 nights at the Hotel des Granges Écoles in a superior double to give us more room. We were thrilled upon arrival to find our 1st floor room had a large terrace entered through the French window. The terrace had a table  and 2 chairs on it. Had the weather been warmer, we would have definitely shared a bottle of wine out there in the evening but nonetheless it was lovely to have the space to walk out onto to enjoy the Spring sunshine. 

The room was traditionally and prettily decorated in a pink Toile de jouy with dark wood furniture. The bed was comfortable, with bedside tables and there is a desk. The wardrobe is quite small but for a short break, we managed to hang everything. There is shelving also. The bathroom contained a bath with shower, toilet and basin and a wall attached hairdryer which would be fine for quickly blasting short hair but I would recommend taking your hairdryer if you have longer hair like me! The bathroom was clean and in good repair. 

We were offered a charming welcome from the receptionist and all the staff we met were extremely friendly and pleasant. As it was Easter, a large vase was filled with delicious chocolate eggs which were available to guests- a nice touch. 

We didn’t eat breakfast at the hotel as we prefer to go out and enjoy cafes but the dining area looked busy each morning. 

The hotel is in a quiet street, a short walk from Cardinal Lemoine Metro. At night when the gates to the street are closed, you use the key fob to gain entrance to the cobbled courtyard which is very secure. Across the street is the former apartment of Ernest Hemingway and next door is the former home of James Joyce. It is a 5 minute stroll from the Pantheon, a 15 minute stroll from Notre Dame and around the corner, you have Rue Mouffetard offering interesting restaurants and the market. 

We would stay here again and would recommend it as a lovely place to situate yourself on a trip to Paris. The Latin Quarter is full of history and beautiful buildings and you can easily navigate your way around Paris to explore from here.

title: Comfortable and friendly stay
text:
This is a lovely family run hotel centrally located in the Latin Quarter. Its an easy walk to several metro stations, the Pantheon and plenty of restaurants and bars. 

It’s rooms are traditional- think floral wallpaper and lace table cloths but this is all charming but the WiFi is free and seemed to work fine. 

The continental Breakfast is served in a bright room and seemed to last all morning whilst we were there.

Our room although being right by reception was quiet and benefited from double aspect windows so was lovely and bright. The rooms were slightly larger than expected for Paris and alongside the double bed and wardrobe we had a table and chairs. The bathroom was fairly spacious too, complete with toiletries although the hairdryer could do with an update. It was underpowered and took forever to dry my long hair and required a towel to hold it as it heated up! But this is a small thing.

For sunny days there is a nice little courtyard to sit and chat. I’d stay again.

title: High expectations badly disappointed
text:
The hotel is located at the far end of a cobbled courtyard, which led me to expect a quiet stay, far from the noise of city traffic. However, exchanging city noise for the sound of one's neighbors' showers, bodily functions and conversations through paper thin walls lacks even minimal charm. Even the elevator was abnormally noisy. Still, the staff was friendly and the WiFi very fast (higher than 50 Mbps both for down and uploads).
The room itself was small, with rather harsh lighting and inconveniently located electrical outlets. The bed was wide enough for one guest, but it would certainly be too narrow for two; there was no night stand and the convex surface of the chairs made it inconvenient to use a chair to improvise one. The room itself was well heated, but nothing was provided to heat the bathroom... Since there is no air conditioning, one should obviously avoid this property during the summer months.
The continental breakfast (9 € : rather inexpensive for Paris) sported a piece of (very fresh) baguette bread and one not very crispy croissant ; the only choice offered was between yogurt and applesauce; the individually packaged cheese was tasteless and the coffee was definitely below standard; one may ask for a soft boiled egg, however.
To summarize: quaint and less impersonal than a chain hotel, but lacking comfort and flair.

title: Quaint, quiet and very nice staff
text: Found this hotel on the web.  It does not seem to appear on the usual booking sites so I booked directly with the hotel.  It is in a narrow street in the 5th arrondissement and set back in a large courtyard so it is really quiet.  The rooms are quaint and a little old fashioned with their wall paper, but that is really part of the charm of the place.  No TV, as mentioned by some other reviewers, which I did not find a problem.  Watching CNN in Paris always rather depresses me and makes me think I should be out doing something more interesting.  Our triple room was very nice, with a good bathroom and it was also reasonably spacious and had a nice view of the courtyard and the surrounding buildings rising up towards the Contrescarpe.  A really short walk to Contrescarpe and the start of rue Mouffetard, so in a very good spot and very convenient for the Pantheon and either Gare d'Austerlitz or Gare de Lyon if you are travelling on.  We had breakfast once in the hotel, in a nice breakfast room - not a basement as is often the case.  The staff were really friendly and sweet. Feels like a step back in time, but in a really good way and very reasonably priced.  Highly recommended.

title: Great Location in Latin Quarter and Friendly Staff
text: This was our first time staying in the Latin Quarter and at the Hotel des Grandes Ecoles. The tone of our visit was set by the lovely Marie on the front desk - she is so friendly, knowledgeable, helpful and was most sympathetic to the fact that we had just been scammed by a fake taxi!  If we had thought to go get her while we were haggling with the driver, she most certainly would have come and reamed him out in his own language.  So that was great - and she announced that our room was indeed ready, even though we were a few hours early, so that was even better.  My only complaint about our whole stay was the room itself, but after she had been so nice, I didn't have the heart to make an issue of it.  I had requested a room on the courtyard, preferably in the building across from the reception (main building).  Our room was in the main building, at the back, right next to the elevator with 2 windows high in the wall, one of which my husband had to prop open with his sandals.  (Room 215).  It was nicely decorated and clean and a good size by Paris standards, but not a room you want to spend much time in.  I know we're in Paris, but sometimes you just want to kick off your shoes and enjoy some quiet time in a nice room.  We enjoyed the courtyard out front every evening, and looked longingly at the rooms opposite, with their full length windows and doors all facing the garden.  But, having said all that, we would definitely stay at this hotel again - I would just make sure that the room we were booked for was as requested (my confirmation just said double room).  The staff are great and the location is fantastic - we walked up to the Plaza Contrescarpe each evening for a drink and to just people watch - we will definitely miss that now that we are back home.

Thank you to Leo, Philippe and Sabine for a fantastic stay and we hope to visit again in the future. 

Diane and Niall

title: An excellent, distinctive find
text: This lovely place has many things going for it, and we'll get to that in a moment, but what makes it a great find is its amiable, caring host, Leo. Leo is warm, welcoming and seems genuinely committed to trying to make your stay in Paris as comfortable and enjoyable as possible. He is high-energy, in a postiive way. His presence alone makes this accommodation worth recommending, but consider its other virtues: 1) it has an excellent central-city location, several blocks (a little more than "a few steps," truth be told) from the Eiffel Tower. 2) It's very accessible, on what we Americans would call the second floor of the 1906 apartment building his family owns. So, while there is an old-style elevator (romantically wrought iron and cramped), you can easily whisk up and down the one flight of stairs to your room. 3) It offers a comfortable common area where Leo provides a generous breakfast of croissants, fruit, juice, yogurt, cheese and meat, etc. and is also happy to cook up some eggs and bacon to your order. 4) It offers inviting, spacious (by Parisien hotel standards) guest rooms. Here we can truthfully only speak of our "superior" room, since we didn't view the others. Our room was tastefully-decorated, very comfortable, clean and well-maintained, with an elegant original marble fireplace, a high ceiling, large windows overlooking the street and an amazing bathroom with modern fixtures and nice amenities, most importantly including a very large glassed-in shower that provided the most wonderful rain-shower that we've ever experienced. For all this, you certainly pay a premium price, and it's a personal judgment call on whether it's "worth it." We thought it was. Of course, no accommodation is perfect, and the one downside with the second-floor location is that, if you're the kind of person who wants the windows open when sleeping, the noise level from the street--there are two brasseries down there--is pretty high. The intersection is not a major one, but after all, this is a city that never sleeps. So, it's a trade-off: being conveniently close to "the action" means you also have to put up with the noise generated by that action. We'd doubt that there's much quiet to be found anywhere in the heart of Paris. We should add a word or two about the strike, since we were there while it was ongoing in mid-December. In short, it wasn't really a problem for us. We accessed Paris from Charles de Gaulle airport by taxi without much of a problem, and once in the central city the strike wasn't really an issue except that there were a lot more people crowding the streets, since the Metro, trains and buses had limited service. The police presence was obviously more intense. But none of that stopped us from walking all over the central city and seeing most of the big sights; most of the museums were open, and they were wonderfully accessible--no waiting in line! (The only sights temporarily closed while we were there were the Picasso Musee and Opera Garnier). We ate well, and the people in the shops and restaurants were quite friendly. In other words, Paris is still Paris, and when you see the sparkling lights burst forth on the Eiffel Tower at night, well. . . It's magic.

title: Lovely Intimate B&B
text:
This small B&B is big on charm. There are only 5 rooms on the 3rd floor of a building right around the corner from the Eiffel Tower. The room we had was small but well appointed. The bed was very comfortable and there was a stand alone air conditioner in the room. Our room faced a side street that had quite a bit of traffic, but it was pretty quiet with the french doors closed. You could also open them to a french balcony. The room also had a really nice sized bathroom with a walk in shower. There were bathrobes and house shoes if you wanted to use them. The soap and shampoo were really nice as well. Bath towels were thick and soft.
There is a main lounge area that you can see as you walk in the door. There is a couch with a couple of chairs and a couple of large tables where breakfast is served. Coffee and tea, cold bottled water and some soft drinks are available all the time. There were also always some little cakes on the table for a quick snack. It was fine to bring in food or wine and enjoy that in the sitting room. There were even some wine glasses available for use.
The breakfast was very nice with made to order eggs, fresh squeezed orange juice, meats, cheeses and breads brought in fresh from the bakery.
The building was very secure and you needed a code to get into the front door. We called the owner upon arrival to get the code. There is a second code needed to get into the B&B.
Luggage can be stored in a closet on the ground floor, and you could get your luggage out without having to ask as that door had a code box on it as well.
A father and his son ran the B&B and were very welcoming and helpful. They live in the upper floors of the building so they were always available if there was a problem. The father actually came to meet us and say hello before we checked out as the son seemed to do the day to day work.
The hotel was about a 10 minute walk from the Eiffel Tower, it was also about a 10 minute walk to a central city bus station. There were a lot of restaurants in the area as well.
We would definitely stay here again.

title: One of the loveliest places I’ve ever stayed.
text:
The Relais 12bis B&B is quite easily one of the loveliest places I’ve ever stayed. It is wonderfully bright, beautifully decorated, and centrally located only a few blocks from the extraordinary Eiffel Tower. Adding to its charms is the owner, Philippe (who made me some scrambled eggs I’d rank in my “Top 5”), and his son, Leon. Philippe was wonderful before I even got to Paris, texting me to find out when I’d arrive because he wanted to make sure there was breakfast for me and my friend. On the day we were leaving, we had a morning tour and left to go meet our guide, but we were going to return to the Relais to get our luggage. Philippe thought we’re leaving Paris and ran all the way downstairs because he didn’t get a chance to say goodbye to us. I love this guy!

Our room was big and bright, with an enormous bathroom I wish I could transport back to my apartment in the States. More importantly, the bed was so comfortable, I didn’t want to get out of it in the mornings. 

An important note: this is a Bed and Breakfast—it is not a hotel. That means that you get wonderfully personalized service that includes a home cooked breakfast, coffee, little snacks, and warm greetings each time you return. It also means that you need a key to get in and out, there isn’t 24 hour service, and you cannot just pick up a phone and have a burger delivered to your room. So please don’t come expecting a Marriott and then be angry that it isn’t one. It is the fact that it isn’t a Marriott that makes this place so special.

I liked practically everything about this place. In the final analysis—I highly recommend the Relais, and hope to be able to stay here again in the future.

title: Well Located
text:
Relais12bis is on the first floor (2d floor U.S.) of a beautiful, older building.  It's less than a five minute walk to the Eiffel Tower, and then just a few minutes more to the Rue Cler/St. Dominique area, and the Seine.  A truly perfect location for exploring this area of Paris, with easy access to cross the river to other areas of the city.

The rooms are beautifully decorated, with large windows.  We stayed in two different types of rooms when there -- first in two, separate, rooms at the end of the hall overlooking the street, and then in a family suite overlooking the interior of the backdoors of the apartments and the bottom floor courtyard area.  For our particular family, the first two rooms worked better for us -- we were two adults and two teenagers.  The layout of the family suite may be better suited to parents with smaller children.  The family suite is made up of two rooms connected by a shower room, with the one, small toilet located in the first of the rooms -- meaning those in the other bedroom always had to come through the shower room, and then into the next room to use same.  The first bedroom of the suite also shares a wall with the kitchen, so there was noise from there early for breakfast being prepared.  If you're a deep sleeper, or getting up early with young children anyway, this may not be an issue, but otherwise it's just something to note.  The breakfast was excellent -- lots of different things on offer and all very fresh.  The cake (made, I believe, by the owner's mother) on offer throughout the day was a nice touch, as were the water and other drinks available to guests in the breakfast room.

When we initially arrived at Relais 12bis we buzzed to be let in; when there was no response we called the number on the hotel website -- no one answered.  Luckily for us a very nice woman came up the sidewalk (who turned out to be the mother/grandmother of the owners), and she let us in.  When we left at checkout time, there was no one there except another couple checking out also.  We all looked around but no one was there, so we just left the keys on the desk in the small office and walked out the door.  We usually stay in an apartment when in Paris and that is generally the way it works in that environment, but it felt a little odd to do so in a bed & breakfast.

This was a little bit of a difficult review to write -- the location, the lovely rooms, the excellent breakfast -- all these merit a high rating, and because of that I did not want to give an "average" rating.  I wish Trip Advisor would provide for a "Good" rating between Average and Very Good, because that is what I feel would most accurately describe our experience -- Good.  The arrival and departure felt odd, and I do think the website should note that one room of the family suite shares a wall with the kitchen -- simply so potential guests may know that there would be the normal activity of putting breakfast together for a number of people commencing early, so if noise like that would be an issue for them, they would be better served by booking other rooms.

title: A Wonderful bnb right by the Eiffel Tower
text:
Well what can I say other than WOW! From the moment we arrived til we left we were absolutely spoilt with this bnb. The host is superb and they have though of every single detail! The location of the bnb is wonderful and you really are only a short stroll from the Eiffel Tower but also the Metro.

He even let us leave our luggage in the luggage store as our flight wasn't until 4:40, which was fab as it meant we could enjoy our last day in Paris without lugging our bags around.
I really cant fault this bnb its a true hidden gem in Paris and one that I really hope to return to one day. 
If you want a central bnb with wonderful service you really must book this one!

title: ALMOST A HOTEL
text:
We have stayed at this central Paris B&B three times, whilst our nearby apartment is renovated.  12 Bis is on the first floor of the building, with a lift, and the building is in the classic Haussmann style.  The bedroom and bathroom fittings are all contemporary and first class.

The B&B is immaculately clean with a good supply of first-class toiletries in the bedrooms.  There is a small lounge with a useful array of guide books for tourists, and home-made cake, biscuits, fruits, tea, and coffee are always available.  The adjoining breakfast area is compact but breakfast is comprehensive with freshly-squeezed orange juice, cheeses, ham, eggs if you wish, and pastries.

The hosts are very helpful for tourists who have no knowledge of Paris, and have seemingly endless patience.

title: Our favorite place in Paris!
text: I found Relais 12b through the great reviews on Trip Advisor and they were 100% right. My husband Owen and I booked the King room at the end of the hallway for two nights at the end of our trip and it was Exquisite. Our absolute favorite place to stay in Paris. Gorgeous, minimalist Parisian design and an exceptional, large bathroom--it felt like we were staying in a five-star room, only more personalized. (We were there during a heatwave, but our room had a great, standing AC unit.) Leo, the owner, greeted us the first night and helped us navigate parking/unloading with a rental car. He and his family have thought of everything--they keep a fridge stocked with complimentary cold drinks in the common living room 24/7, along with coffee, tea, and coffee cake made by his mother. And the morning breakfasts? They are heavenly: eggs made-to-order, cheese, bread, pastries, juice, everything you could want. It's an 8-minute walk to the Eiffel Tower--we walked the two flights up one night at 10pm, which was perfect--but they're wonderfully tucked away in an adjoining neighborhood. Relais 12b is the perfect Parisian getaway. We cannot wait to return!

text:
We just returned from a wonderful 8 night stay at Relais 12bis.  We arrived a bit before check-in time and were warmly greeted by Leo, who invited us to relax in the lounge while our room was cleaned. Every morning we had a delicious breakfast in the lounge.  There were breads, cheeses, meats, eggs cooked to order, fresh fruit and yogurt.  Plenty of strong coffee, tea or hot chocolate and freshly squeezed orange juice.  Our hosts were always helpful and willing to make reservations, offer suggestions and went above and beyond on more than one occasion.  

The area is steps away from the Champ de Mars, but tucked around a corner in a quiet neighborhood.  For me the peaceful retreat each evening was much needed after busy days and crowds.  Every afternoon we would come home to refresh and relax in the lounge, have a cup of tea or coffee and a piece of homemade cake before venturing out again for the evening and dinner.

We've always rented apartments for our trips to Paris and I was nervous about trying something new, but everything about our stay was great.  It was so nice to come back to a clean room each day and having breakfast ready for us every morning was such a luxury.  We had a fantastic time and look forward to returning.

title: Home Away From Home
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at this B&B while in Paris over Christmas.  Prior to arriving, Peet, the owner, responded to all my messages and gave me great instructions for how to reach the hotel.  I took the RER B train in from CDG to Gare du Nord.  The hotel is only a few hundred meters away from the station which was very convenient.

The room I stayed in was basically like a bedroom you would find in any home.  They have larger rooms, but I was solo so the room was not huge, but it was very comfortable with a nice view overlooking the courtyard and inner buildings.  Very Parisian.  The bathroom was shared and just down the hall from my room, but I never had any issues using it.  It was clean every time I went in and was completely modern.

Each morning, breakfast was served in the great room.  An assortment of breads, butter, jams, meat, cheese, pastry, and drinks.  Plus, Peet made sure everyone had their own croissant.  This was one of the more pleasant aspects of the stay as everyone ate around a large dining table and conversed with each other.  While I was there, I met people from Australia, the Netherlands, Indian, and some fellow vacationing Americans.  We shared stories about our trip, places to visit, oddities about our own nations compared to others.  It was very enjoyable.

The Hotel is only a short walk around from several Metro lines, not to mention the numerous bus stops nearby.  The area directly outside of the hotel is nothing special, just your generic city block with some restaurants, shops, and businesses, but again, via the Metro, you can be anywhere in Paris in less than 30 minutes.  That is hard to beat.

One thing worth noting.  The floors are hardwood and they do creek when you walk on them or if someone outside your room walks by.  I didn't have any issue with it, but if you are a light sleeper, it might cause you to wake up periodically.  I was typically so tired from being on my feet all day sight seeing that I sleep right through the night.

Great B&B.  Thank you Peet and Thierry!

title: Cozy and convenient B&B
text:
What a perfect place to stay! We traveled to Paris for a 5 day trip in a big group of family and we were lucky enough to rent out all the rooms in the B&B. Many of us were first timers in this beautiful city. Peet was such a great host - he was there to answer all our questions about where to go, which metro line or bus to take, and insider tips on seeing Paris. 

The rooms are spacious and felt very "Parisian." Some have private baths and others are shared. At first I wasn't sure about the shared bathroom but it was no big deal! Staying here feels like you are staying at a friend's house. Breakfast every morning was such a treat (croissants, coffee, tea, fruit, cheese, bread, etc) and Peet is also an amazing chef. The only thing that was missing from the rooms was a tv, but then again we aren't in Paris to watch tv!

I also have to point out the location. The place is in the 10th but literally steps from a major station, Gare du Nord and from many bus lines so traveling around the city is super convenient from this location. 

I would definitely recommend this place to someone who is looking to stay like a local without all the bells and whistles of a pricey resort. I very much enjoyed my time here and the hospitality of the host. Would love to return one day if I am lucky enough to come to Paris again.

title: Friendly B&B
text:
We stayed at "A Room in Paris" for three nights. The building is extremely handy (200 metres walk) for the Gare du Nord, the metro, and the RER B line for CDG airport. There is an extraordinary contrast between the bustle of the road and the area outside, and the secluded courtyard which you enter once you step through the large outside door. 

Peet is a really nice guy, speaks French, English and Dutch fluently. The breakfasts are fine, and there is a good opportunity to discuss things over breakfast. The room we stayed in is across the landing from the main rooms, it is attractively decorated, of good size, with its own shower, fridge and microwave and kettle. The bed is large and very comfortable. The room overlooks the courtyard. You absolutely would not know you were so close to central Paris. There is the possibility of noise from the neighbouring room although this was no problem.

We would definitely stay again, a much more attractive option than so many of the chain hotels.

title: Returning Home to a Room in Paris
text: This was the fourth time my husband and I were fortunate enough to return to "A Room in Paris." Peet Verrest is a superb host and his hospitality is truly what makes our stays so very inviting. We wouldn't think of staying anywhere else while in Paris for our visit wouldn't be nearly as meaningful or special. Peet's fluency in several languages and his friendly personality enables him to converse with all his guests and makes their stays very pleasant. Breakfast is always delicious with assorted homemade dishes and fresh baguettes and croissants but it is the scintillating conversation that makes our visits there so very interesting. One of the many advantages of staying at "A Room in Paris" rather than a hotel is that you truly learn more about French culture, the local Parisian restaurants and neighborhoods and sites that may not be highlighted in the guide books. Peet will give you tips that truly enhance your stay. Our room was beautifully furnished with period pieces of art and furniture and had French doors which opened to a small terrace. After a long day of sightseeing it was always a relief to come home to Peet's where the beds are so comfortable, linens were exquisite and atmosphere was elegant. It's location, close to many groceries allowed us to return to our room in the early evening to enjoy wine, a baguette and cheese while gazing out toward Rue Magenta toward Gare du Nord. He also had free wifi so we were able to enjoy music as we enjoyed the view of Parisian Streets. A Room in Paris is also centrally located to Gare du Nord where one can access trains across France and Le Metro (subway) to Paris. Peet is also very sensitive to his guests needs. I have a dairy allergy and he ALWAYS has had non dairy alternatives for me to eat such as soy yougart, soy milk, and dairy free margarine. Room rates are also very affordable and less expensive than most hotels. We are already planning our fifth stay and have told all of our friends about A Room in Paris. It is truly the best kept secret there and it is all due to Peet's inviting hospitality to make every stay your very best. Each time we stay It is like coming home again.

title: Gracious host
text:
My family of 4 stayed for 3 nights in Peet's lovely B&B.  Peet has been such gracious host, it made our stay really warm and memorable.

1. The reservation was easy as Peet was very prompt in replying his emails.  We were able to tell him our needs and he would recommend us appropriate rooms.  He was also helpful in providing directions, not only to the B&B but also the destinations we were keen to go (e.g. Disneyland etc). 

2. The check-in was hassle free and we were given an orientation of the room (we stayed in a separate unit opposite the main house).  Peet's assistant also helped us with the laundry (at a token fee) while we were out sightseeing.

3. Peet's flight just landed wee hours in the following morning after we arrived, we were sure he was tired after his long flight, but he still prepared breakfast for us and stayed up to mingle with us.  

4. We also met with lovely people from around the world during breakfast.  We would exchange some traveling tips and Peet would share info about where we could visit and the directions.

Just like any cities, staying in big hotel establishments may sometimes be cold and formal.  We were glad that we chose to stay in a B&B despite some concerns we had initially (e.g. the children may disturb other guests, security at B&Bs may be compromised, curfew set by the host may limit our freedom).  The separate unit was ideal for us with children.  The security was also tight with a few secured doors (main door, followed by another door at the courtyard, followed by door to unit) accessible by private secure tokens.  The door can also be bolted inside.   

The location was convenient.  There's a convenience store below, market, bakeries, nice restaurants nearby etc. It's also close enough to the train station, but at a less "rowdy" area.  We were very pleased with our stay there, especially for the warm hospitality we get.

title: Review for the studio apartment
text:
We stayed at the studio apartment, so we probably have a different experience compared to the B&B reviews.

Pros
- convenient location.  The Gare du Nord station is central to a lot of the train lines.  So from the airport we just took one line to get here.
- near cafes, bakery, pharmacy, supermarket
- had our own kitchen - so if we bought food from outside we can just heat it up and eat here
- nice views outside our apartment window

Cons
- the area nearby was a bit scary looking at night, didn't feel very safe.  (But after a few days here we didn't feel as scared as when we first arrived)
- some of the streets nearby had a weird pee smell (but I think this is Paris in general.. several areas we went to would have this smell)
- internet was hardly accessible from the apartment
- at night there were no lights coming in to the apartment.

Overall given the price it wasn't a bad place to stay, but not for those who are used to staying at fancy hotels.. Expect budget accommodations.  For me the big plus is how convenient location wise it is to transportation.

title: Lovely B and B
text: Picked this B and B after reading the reviews. We had Rahim as a host for two mornings while Peet was away, thene Peet for 3 mornings. We had the African room, which was small but big enough for 2 suitcases and ourselves. It was very quiet at night as it faced the courtyard. Breakfast was lovely, always a beautiful croissant (to die for). Cereal, muesli, meats and cheese, plus yoghurt, Peets home made yoghurt was beautiful. We did not go hungry.... The rooms were spotless, and if you needed anything you could knock on the door and just ask. The apartment has lovely wooden floors, high ceilings and is very quaint. Located just down the road to the Gare de Nord, just come out of the big main entrance, look down the road and look for the leader price supermarket and pharmacie., it is about two doors down from the pharmacie, if you get lost just pop in there and they will show you where to go. It is a big old green door, just key in your code and you will be buzzed up. Take the first door in the right and buzz A Room in Paris. It can be hard to find so hope this review helps. If you decide to book this B and B, you are half an hour walk to the Louvre, Notre Dame, maybe 3/4 hour to Eiffel Tower. If you prefer to take public transport,then the Gare de Nord can take you anywhere. If I can take the metro on my own,then anyone can... Bon chance....

title: A Room in Paris a Real Treasure
text: This was the third time we returned to stay at a Room in Paris and the hospitality we received from Peet was just a reminder why we would never stay anywhere else!  Our room was large, airy and beautifully decorated in that art nouveau style that just reminds you of the beauty of the city. There is also a grocer and pharmacy just around the corner. Breakfast in the dining room, with 15 feet ceilings and large windows, and lovely antique furnishings serves as a relaxing and beautiful way to start your day. On the overcast days candles are lit at the breakfast table which creates a lovely ambiance.The breakfasts are delicious – he makes the best croissant and French toast. The coffee is to die for and the conversation is always interesting.  Peet and Thierry are the most gracious hosts, making sure that everyone’s needs are met and they are multilingual so they speak with everyone in their native language, putting each visitor at ease.  During our most recent visit we were hoping to make a day trip out of the city and Thierry gave us wonderful suggestions on what to see in Rouen which allowed us to make good use of our time and spend a day without being hurried.  A Room in Paris is an oasis because of their kindness and hospitality and is as unique as the finds you will discover in Paris. In fact, it is the best treasure we’ve found in the City and this is why we will always return. It is like coming home.

title: Terrific!
text:
I am loathe to write this review as we found a little gem that we don't necessarily want the world to know about but as it would do a great disservice to the hosts I am going to write the truth!!

We had a great stay at A Room in Paris.  To our delight it was no more than a 3 mins walk from Gare du Nord (5 mins with having to wait to cross the streets!!) and had a lift if we required it.   

Peet the host is lovely, very helpful and a great cook too!

Our room was big and airy and we had plenty of room.  It was not ensuite but it really didn't bother us too much as there were a couple of bathrooms we were able to use when required.  We were slightly worried about the noise on Rue Lafayette as with the windows open it was quite noisy, well it is a major street, however when the windows were closed at night we heard nothing. 

Breakfast was the usual array of fresh croissants, ham, cheese, cereal, orange juice, coffee/tea but Peet cooked a delicious 'surprise' for us each morning.  Our favourite was definitely the French toast and if you are lucky enough to have it while you stay you won't be disappointed!  

Gare du Nord is a major transport hub in Paris and from there any attraction in Paris is easily accessible.  It really isn't a problem getting to anywhere from here.  

There is a Leader Price supermarket on the corner of Rue Lafayette however we didn't find this supermarket in any way useful except for bottles of water.  We did find a Carrefour City on the block up (between Gare du Nord and Leader Price - A Room in Paris is a couple of doors the other side of Leader Price) which had everything we could have possibly wanted. We'd recommend going there if you need anything.

We all agreed we would highly recommend staying at A Room in Paris - Peet is a great host, the location can not be beaten and we were truly comfortable during our stay here.

We wouldn't hesitate in going back to stay and will certainly be hoping there is availability for our next trip!

All in all highly recommended and very reasonably priced.
