title: Lovely apartment hotel, but...
text:
My husband and I stayed at Le Roi de Sicile for 4 nights this past week. We rented the studio as it was one of a few apartments available and we didn’t really need a lot of space. 

The apartment itself is nice and well furnished. Nice little kitchenette and a large bathroom. Staff were very friendly and helpful. 

First, we booked this as a couple but had to ask for a second set of hand and face towels. Second the website does not inform you that the only studio apartment is on the ground floor. It is right across from the reception desk and faces the street. 

When we checked in we also asked for a different room and were told that we could move for one night but then had to come back to this room. The gentleman who was checking us in told us the street is very quiet and we could sleep until 11 if we wanted to. Umm. NO. It was loud every night. Even with the window closed you could hear all the street noise. Loud talking, cars honking and the best part the construction crew for the building across the street showed up before 7 every morning. We did not get even one night good sleep. 

The website should state this room is ground floor. 

While we will return to Paris and really enjoyed staying in the Marais, we likely won’t be back here.

title: Nice place but
text:
My boyfriend and I were in Paris for 2 nights for the last leg of our Europe vacation. We stayed at Le Roi de Sicile which was in a great location lots of restaurants and bars nearby. We choose this location because of the great reviews. 

Emily was very friendly and were more than willing to help us with anything we needed. 

Upon check-in we were told that our room was on street level and directly opposite the reception desk. My boyfriend immediately asked if we could switch to a room on the upper level. Emily told us that we could move up for night but we have to switch the next day. So against our better judgement because we were very short on time. The room was new and nice and our BIGGEST issue was that our room was directly opposite the reception desk and on street level. There is a bar directly next door, so there was a lot of noise outside. There was also construction across the road which started early. 

On our first night, the manager was in the lobby talking very loudly on his phone! My boyfriend actually had to tell him to lower his voice. He apologized but his response was "Well I didn't know that you were in the room!" If your the manager you should definitely know that someone was staying in the room. Then the people in the street were very loud and you could hear every conversation. Not to mention that the people staying upstairs from us were extremely loud. We brought this to Emily's attention after the first night, but nothing changed for the second night. Very very bad experience!

If you do stay here make sure you ask for an upper level room or it will be the worst sleep. We did receive a partial refund for our stay for the inconvenience. Overall a very nice place, just think that the room on the ground level should not be rented out.

title: Would definitely stay here again!
text: I had multiple friends recommend that I stay in the Le Marais neighborhood and they suggested I stay at an Airbnb for the most space and best experience. Since I actually prefer the amenities of a hotel, I researched hotels and noticed that hotel rooms in the area are tiny so when I found this hotel/apartment, it was the best of both worlds! It had the homey apartment feel of an Airbnb with the amenities of the hotel.  This is more spacious than most places you will be able to find and in this price range. The service was amazing -- e.g., replenished bottles of water everyday (water is expensive in Paris!), housekeeping services, security/front desk, and they were even able to hold our bags because our flight got in early morning before our room was ready. However, it also feels like you're just coming home because each floor only has one unit so you feel like you have privacy and are completely left alone which is awesome. I would definitely stay here again and would recommend it to anyone.

title: Perfection
text:
I brought my mom to Paris with me for a dream vacation, which kicked off with our check in here! From the first moment, we couldn't have been happier. The staff was lovely, allowing us to store our bags (we were early by several hours) and then calling as soon as the room was ready. Having stayed in Le Marais in the past, I knew this location would be perfect ... honestly, no better area to stay in Paris in my opinion. We were able to walk just about everywhere except the Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe.  When you don't want to walk, the Metro is easily accessed with nearby stops, as well as the bus line that runs centrally through the city. 

The staff is amazing and attentive - we especially appreciated the bottle of wine left for us, the attention to detail in showing us around the apt (which was so well stocked with the essentials), and making dinner reservations for us fairly last minute in a hard to get into restaurant. The apartment was clean, the pull out couch sizeable and perfectly comfortable for 5 night's sleep, well appointed with dishes, hairdryers, coffee pods, hangers, additional linens, toiletries, you name it. 

I will absolutely stay here again and recommend to friends.

title: Wonderful hotel, A Paris Gem - Kudos to Fabien Bouthier!
text:
We'd read all the great reviews so made it a point to stay 5 days & 4 nights at the Roi de Sicile in early May.   It was so impressive that I can say, without hyperbole, that I don't think I'd look anyplace else for future visits - we would stay here again, without hesitation, every time.   

The rooms are beautiful and roomy, the service is impeccable, and the entire hotel is spotless-clean.    It's a relatively new establishment, by hotelier Fabien Bouthier, and he has hit what we like to call in America a "home run" with the Roi de Sicile.  The apartment concept, with roomy kitchen, lots of space to move around, full amenities and cleaning service (they'll even wash all your dishes every day), is just what we were looking for.

We had such a good time, and received such attentive service that one day on our way out the door Mr. Bouthier greeted us and chatted about our plans so we brought him back some pastry from Sadaharu Aoki.  He then returned the favor and the next day presented us with several bars of French chocolate.  I've never brought a hotel owner pastry before, but that's what it's like staying here - it's like you're staying with friends.

Some quick notes and positives:
- The elevator is small, quintessential Paris, but quick and clean and technologically advanced.  If you require an elevator, you'll like it here.
- They provide a shoe-shine machine near the front door, ready to go - I really think they thought of everything
- Unless you aren't physically able, take the stairs at least once - they aren't an afterthought.  With beautiful wall lighting highlighting black and white portraiture and everything new and clean I found myself taking the stairs every day except check-in and check-out.
- They provide a nice power hub with plug converters and USB charging station so you can leave that stuff at home
- The bed is wonderful and comfy
- They provide jumbo bottles of water, both still and sparkling, daily at no extra cost.  Again, they thought of everything.

If you're going to Paris, and are attracted to the idea of an apartment but want the booking ease and service of a hotel, this is your answer.  Fabien Bouthier really has a winner on his hands and I only fear it's going to be very hard to get into this hotel easily in the future once word spreads.

(Fabien - thank you again for the Chapon chocolate!)

name: Hôtel Madison
description: The Madison Hotel, in the Latin Quarter of Saint Germain-des-Pres, is a boutique hotel in a chic, contemporary style. This delightful hotel with its 53 rooms and suites is located on the Left Bank opposite the church of Saint-Germain-des-Pres and a mere stone's throw from the Seine, the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay, and the Cathedral of Notre Dame de Paris. The hotel rubs shoulders on the Boulevard Saint Germain with the Cafe de Flore and the Cafe de 2 Magots, at the heart of a quarter famed for its cafes, art galleries, museums, antique dealers and designer fashion boutiques. The Madison Hotel is also firmly at the heart of literary Paris... Albert Camus spent some time at the hotel in the spring of 1940, and it was here that he completed his existentialist novel "L'Etranger" (The Outsider). Perhaps his spirit still hovers somewhere...

title: Problem during last night
text:
This was our 3rd time at Madison Hotel. We were having a great stay during our visit at the end of August, when in the last night we had a big problem. 
Me and my wife were packing our bags around 01h30 am, when suddenly a man started knocking hardly at our door asking us to let him in on a very rude tone. My wife got really scared, we did not open the door and told the man we would call the reception to understand what was going on. The man kept knocking hardly and saying that he wanted us to open the door so he could get into the room. I answered again that i would not let anyone get in to our room at 2am in the morning. He stopped knocking and left us with no answer. We got really scared and worried if something was happening in the hotel. We got even more worried when we started calling nonstop the reception to try to understand what was going on. Between 2am till 4am we tried to call the reception about 50 times and nobody answered. I tought a few times about calling the police. 
We spent the whole night awake afraid of what could happen and had a very hard last day at Paris because of that. 
In the morning we went to the reception and told the whole story. The staff told us that a guest complained about the noise and the receptionist of the night, instead of calling our room, decided to go knock at our door at 2am in the morning. This problem could have easily been solved with a simple call to our room asking us politely to stop the noise, which we would have done quickly.

title: Small hotel with a perfect location and an amazing staff
text:
Perfect location in Paris with the friendliest and most helpful staff !! 

Although my room was very small it was still confortable (except for the shower … too small ) and had all the amenities one needs. Mini bar , AC , bath robe, coffee machine, etc. 

They serve a full breakfast from 7 to 11 am. It’s 20 euro.  I didn’t take it because I’d rather eat somewhere else in the city. 
The had fruit, eggs , pastries , bacon and a few small desserts. 

Within less than 150 mt. From the hotel you have a Monoprix supermarket, the M 4 Metro line which takes you directly to Gare du Nord and a ton of city buses that take you pretty much everywhere in Paris. 

Norte Dame , the Louvre and D’orsay museums are within a 15 minute walk. 

If you are on a budget, do avoid the restaurants close the hotel.  They are expensive and not that good. 

Again !!! Thank you to all the staff at hotel Madison !!! 
You were very patient and attentive. 

100 % recommended

title: St Germain Boutique Hotel
text: We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. Our room was comfortable and clean. I loved being able to help myself to a tall glass of water on our way in from a long day of sightseeing. The complimentary laundry closet was definitely nice to have as we packed in a carry on. The A/C was a welcome respite after traversing the city in the July heat. I loved the breakfast but there are sooo many yummy options nearby too to grab a croissant or whatever your hearts desire is each morning. The proximity to the metro is also quite convenient. The only con was that the people we were traveling with had a room on the 5th floor, can't remember the exact room, that smelled quite bad and they thought it had a mold issue. They were compensated, after much discussion with the manager, but word to the wise...the hotel is very aware of the issue so jump on getting a different room immediately if this happens to you. I had a perfectly lovely room that did not stink :)

The hotel is situated in the heart of St. Germain with a 5-10 minute walk to the Louvre, The Tuileries Garden, Rue de Rivoli with its variety of brand-named shops, etc.
The hotel itself is very clean and beautiful. Rooms are spacious (we had a Privilege room) and the hotel staff is great, friendly and speaks English well.

The highlight of the hotel is Mr. Sanjay Kaloya - Head Concierge of Hotel Madison, as well as several more hotels in Paris. Sanjay is by far the best concierge you will ever find on the face of this planet. He is the reason for making our (I came to Paris with my 18 year old daughter to celebrate her birthday)  5-day trip in Paris the BEST I could have ever imagined or asked for.

Even prior to arriving to Paris, Sanjay took care of every request promptly. Whether booking us tables at the finest restaurants in town (it was absolutely impossible to get a table without him) or any other request for that matter, Sanjay did not only take care of things, but always followed up a day after to see that all our needs and expectations had been met - that's top class hands down!

We will certainly come back to Madison hotel for the great hotel, but moreover, thanks to Mr. Sanjay Kaloya!

title: Amazing Experience!
text:
This hotel was perfect in every way. It is a gorgeous boutique hotel located in the most charming area of Paris. Perfectly situated on Saint Germain Blvd. set back slightly on a private road in the heart of the most incredible neighborhood, Paris has to offer. My first photo was of the gorgeous exterior entranceway surrounded by flowers and black canopies against the grey stone facade. Tres chic! In addition to the aesthetic beauty & charm, is the exceptional concierge service. Sanjay, Jan & the team helped me prior to our stay by liaising via email for restaurant reservations and obtaining site attractions tickets and drivers. When we arrived, all of our bookings were handwritten on beautiful stationery as a confirmation & reminder. They secured reservations at all the places I had requested. Amazing! title: Will stay here again
text:
Spent 3 night at this hotel in Saint Germain overlooking the Saint Germain Boulevards in our Deluxe View room . The room was quite large and fitted the three of us travel with a queen size bed and a single fold out. The decor was beautiful, I think it’s been recently refurbished as there were little to no blemishes. 2 elevators serviced the floors well or you could you the stairs for a bit of exercise.

Would definitely stay here again.

title: I wish I could give it MORE than 5 stars
text:
There aren't enough superlatives to help me describe our stay at this lovely hotel.  From the moment we entered, I knew our vacation would be memorable.

My husband and I stayed in the spacious suite for 6 nights, and it was even more special than the photos and the description on the website. The views from the room were breathtaking......the Eiffel Tower, the Invalides, St. Germain Church, Notre Dame, the Pantheon.  The room and furnishings were elegant, and the layout of the suite was perfect for us since I was able to relax in the salon before the crack of dawn while my husband, undisturbed, continued to sleep in the bedroom.

Each morning, we enjoyed a delicious, very relaxing breakfast in the breakfast area with a friend, who was also a guest of the hotel.  On 2 occasions, we even had another friend (staying elsewhere) join us for breakfast. One evening, several friends visited us at the hotel, and the lobby provided us with an inviting, comfortable venue.

The location of the hotel can't be beat.....in the heart of the beautiful St. Germain.

The entire staff (yes, every single employee) was truly remarkable. Each one was professional and polite, friendly and eager to assist.  As for Sanjay,  he has surely earned his exemplary status as Clef d'Or Concierge. 

Thank you, Hotel Madison for making our vacation one that we will remember and cherish as we await our next visit to Paris.

title: Our New Home Away from Home.
text: It's taken many years and numerous trips to Paris but we have finally found a small hotel we can call our home.  It was recommended  decades ago by a friend but we never stayed there even though we walked by it many times on frequent trips. Friendly behind the desk, and very accommodating, the hotel was been recently renovated just before or during the lockdown, and the rooms very comfortable. Lovely baths. Very nice public rooms too and great petit dejeuner.  Rooms a nice size and the prices not a killer. In the very convenient and neighborhoody  6th arrondissement right on Blvd St Germain but set back a good distance.  Left Bank bistros and patisseries, my favorite, a step away. New windows, so rooms  quiet. There's even a  low-key cabaret act a few times a month by an excellent American-born singer/Parisian  expat  living in Paris. Terrance knows this city's charms inside-out, and his Porter/Gershwin tunes. Like a Tony Bennett, he's a great saloon singer. Head concierge Sanjay is a gem. Alexandre the front desk manager and Diana who works for him just superb. Nothing falls between the cracks. The overall feel is comfort, warmth, and very welcoming. .

title: Lovely boutique hotel with some issues that need to get sorted out
text: First the positives. The location of this hotel is absolutely perfect. Within walking distance of the Louvre, Notre Dame, Luxembourg Gardens, etc. The St. Germain de Pres area has dozens of lovely restaurants and shops and is great for casual walking around and people watching. The hotel's front desk staff is friendly and their concierge deserves particular accolades as he couldn't have been more affable and helpful. However, their attention to issues that directly affected guest comfort leave a great deal to be desired. We had junior suite which was nice enough but the A/C did not work in the bedroom. After several "technicians" tinkered with it over several days with no improvement, they finally sent up someone who knew what he was doing on day five (we were there for seven days) who simply replaced the simple thermostat (probably a $20 item) and, voila, everything was fine but this was five days into our stay and after the manager offered ridiculous excuses like, "this is just the way A/C works in Paris" and other utterly unhelpful advice. Also our room had a vile smell coming from the shower drain which was noticeable on day two. They sent someone up promptly who did something to address this but the odor came back on day six. I asked the lady at the desk to send someone up to (again) address this early in the morning and 24 hours later nothing had been done. This was outrageous and should never have been allowed to occur in a hotel of this class (or any other, for that matter). Also the Wi-Fi was spotty and you had to sign in and out multiple times to maintain a signal. Again, this is basic stuff that should never be an issue in a first rate hotel. Boutique hotels like this are certainly lovely, but, as you can see, they can be quirky. If I could offer one suggestion to management, it would be to implore their front-facing staff to take full, personal responsibility to address and resolve any legitimate problems brought to their attention by guests and be sure they have the means and authority to do so. Responses like "I've passed on this request to ******" where nothing gets resolved promptly are not in any way helpful and no amount of smiles and polite responses do anything to insure a pleasant stay in the face of problems that aren't getting resolved.

title: Gracious and elegant
text:
which is beautiful and in the most lovely section of St. Germain.  Restaurants, cafes, shops, gardens, and many important sights are within easy walking distance (Les Deux Maggots, Café de Flore, and Mabillion are directly across Boulevard Saint-Germain; St. Sulpice Cathedral is two blocks away; the Luxembourg Gardens are a ten minute walk, La Place des Vosges is about a 20 min walk, etc.).  This is an exquisitely lovely, upscale, and charming boutique hotel, set back a half block from Blvd St. Germain so it is quiet.  This is a beautiful belle epoque townhome building with a charming small sitting area off of the reception desk area. The staff are unfailingly polite, professional, helpful, and friendly without being intrusive.  Perfectly Parisian.  

Room – this is perfectly wonderful in almost every respect, with the one exception of enough floor space to fit two luggage racks with suitcases.  The room is street facing with a long balcony accessed through each of the two French doors; from the balcony the views are sweepingly scenic.  The décor is in cream, silver, gold, and gray, with a very upscale and calming feel.  It is spotlessly clean.  The walls have mirrored sliding doors, behind which are several shelves, drawers, and hanging space for storage (which we did not realize until the bellboy showed us); however, keep in mind they are very heavy. text: I have been to Paris many times and stayed in all different places from 5 star hotels to Air Bnb’s and just about everything in between.  I have finally found the full package. title: Terrence Gelenter croons at The Madison Hotel, Saint Germain
text:
On Monday 15 November, I wandered down to the boulevard Saint Germain, where Terrance Gelenter, our American friend in Paris, had invited us for the launch of his evenings of song at the Madison Hotel, 143 bld Saint Germain. The welcome from the manager Bruno Alleau was as warm as the fire crackling in the hearth of the club room where we were gathered to hear Terrance, accompanied by the wonderful Sheldon Forrest, on piano. The décor was delightful, the crowd enthusiastic, so many New York voices, I felt like I was in a NY jazz club. 
Terrance (aka the Baron of Brooklyn) held the floor, his melodious voice, in old world style; no mic, captivating us with old favourites ‘My Foolish Heart’, ‘Sabor a Mi’, ‘Blame it on My Youth, and ‘Over The Rainbow’. When he sang Tony Bennett’s ‘Smile’, I looked around at the heartfelt smiles, so many of us delighted to be back at a real crooner’s session, in great company and cosy surroundings. Since I last heard Terrance sing in November 2019, many of us smiled “through fears and sorrow” and it was so good to be serenaded back to the good old days.
The Madison’s wine list is excellent and they have a great variety of whiskeys. We tucked into a delicious cheese plate, and the table service was impeccable, discreet, and efficient.  
The Christmas lights will be sparkling on the Boulevard Saint Germain for Terrance’s special pre-Xmas Fest on Dec 23 (Terrance@paris-expat.com). I’ll be there to ring in the festive season – in crooner ‘style’ and cosy glamour. In fact, although I live in Paris, I’m quite far from Saint Germain, and I might make a night of it, book in to the Madison (https://www.hotel-madison.com/) for the night with just one big decision to make - Café de Flore or Les Deux Magots (both just across the street) for breakfast? Perhaps I will have to consult with the Father of Modern Philosophy, René Descartes (of ‘I think, therefore I am’ fame) who died in 1650 and is buried in one of the Saint Germain de Près church’s side chapels just bang across the street. What a location!

I have been to this very conveniently located hotel several times over the years and I noticed that the rooms have been redecorated (in a good way!)recently. I love the fact that a kettle is available in the room and the very adequate breakfast provided! We were a small group of old friends, living in different countries and meeting in Paris after 3 years of forced separation (pandemic). We greatly appreciated the cosy lounges, the availability of thirst quenching fresh water and the willingness of the very nice staff at reception to lure the very elusive Parisian taxis (we needed 2, as there were 5 of us!).
We will be back!

title: Lovely stay at Hôtel Madison!
text:
My husband and I loved our 4-night stay at Hôtel Madison. 
We got a warm welcome by Arthur when we arrived that already made us feel at home.
This is the first time bringing our baby dog to Paris and the hotel is really pet-friendly. 
Decoration of the hotel is very nice and cozy, breakfast was very good, cleanliness excellent and location is more than perfect: close to lots of restaurants, shops and in front of the Saint Germaine des Pré church. Neighborhood very pleasant for a walk and 15 minutes from the Jardin du Luxembourg.
But what really makes the difference in the hotel is its lovely staff that are always willing to go above and beyond to make us feel special. Arthur, Sanjay, the night receptionist, the breakfast team and all the support associates of the hotel are always smiling, willing to help and very polite. They are an amazing staff!
I would definitely make Hôtel Madison as our hotel choice for my future stays in Paris as I go at least twice/year to Paris! 100% recommended for all the different aspects of an excellent hotel!

title: Very nice and well located
text:
I had a lovely stay at the Madison. The hotel is perfectly located in the heart of the 6th arrondissement, so walking distance to just about everything. The hotel room is clean and the windows open wide to the beautiful avenue below. We loved the shower and the water pressure was perfect. We did not have breakfast ast the 17 euro price tag is a bit high, especially when you have a Paul right down the street. 
The only place where improvement could be made is recognizing people who are staying multiple nights, and unfortunately there are some homeless  men who hang out outside, which is a delicate situation for sure.
All in all I would definitely return to the Madison.

title: Underwhelmed
text:
My go-to hotel in Paris is closed until September 2021 owing to COVID, so my online search for a good hotel in the St. Germain area led me to the Madison. I was impressed by the number of excellent reviews for this hotel. Sadly, I think the hotel is overrated and not great value for money.   I booked a premium room without a view which overlooked some air conditioning units covered with green plastic foliage, which was, to be honest, a little depressing, and I wished I'd paid extra for a view. The room itself was a decent size for Parisian hotels and well-designed and equipped. There was a good surface on which to work; a decent bathroom with bath and monsoon shower, full-length mirror, comfortable chairs, a large wardrobe with plenty of hangers and a large cupboard. However, the room was unappealing in a 'beige' way, and the doors to the bathroom and toilet were hideous. The location was good, with metro station and bus stops on the doorstep, though I prefer the rue du Bac end of Blvd. St Germain.  
The staff mainly was kind and professional. However, I have a few quibbles.   Not a very friendly or warm welcome after a long flight, and as a single lady-traveller, I was left to carry my large case to the lift when weak with exhaustion.   Certain staff members were argumentative; I mentioned that no water had been left in my room on one occasion.  A manager swore he had left bottles in my room, which made me seriously question my sanity because they weren't there.  My main quibble was the servicing of the rooms. Because of COVID, one had to request the servicing of the room. As I was on a two-week stay, I told reception that the maids had my permission to access the room and clean it every day when vacant, but this was ignored. Sometimes my room was cleaned very late in the day, on a few occasions not at all.  I literally felt I had to beg to have my room serviced. It felt as though management was hiding behind COVID measures as an excuse for sloppy service.   My room wasn't serviced on my last night, and the duty manager said it was because the hotel was full.  A pretty lame excuse IMO. The website photographs are misleading, making the reception area, breakfast, and lobby seating appear much larger than they are and the rooms more attractive than in reality. 
So, while it is not all bad, the hotel left me underwhelmed.  I was sorely tempted to relocate to another hotel after a few days as I found it very depressing, but I did not have the energy to do so. However, it wasn't worth the money, and I would not wish to return. Another reviewer sums it up perfectly: "You won't be delighted, but probably won't be too disappointed either. In a word, bland."

title: Outstanding meetinig room and service
text:
Blocked a full day meeting room for business negotiation, on a "co-working" package.  

Exceeded our expectation on every count:
* Airy meeting room with direct view to the church St Germain des Pres (see picture)
* Nespresso machine and tea included in the package, with bottled water
* Free internet with good connectivity

Hats off to hotel management.  All in, I paid around half what REGUS would have charged for a similar meeting room with NO view.  
And we had nice lunch rather than some plastic box sandwiches.

title: Great location but otherwise disappointing
text:
Whilst this hotel is well situated (especially during France’s  current ongoing public transport strike), it is overpriced and the level of service provided by its staff is substandard. Having arrived after a  24 hour flight from Australia, I discovered that the shower in my room (which could be adjusted to glow in a choice of 4 different colours) could not, however, be adjusted to provide hot water. It being too late and me being too tired to complain, I had a 30 second ice cold shower and went to bed in my warmest clothes. Maintenance staff confirmed the following day that there was a technical problem with the shower, which they then fixed. But even one cold shower in a hotel costing over 300 Euro per night is not acceptable. Not a word of apology was offered by reception staff. 
The staff at the hotel were generally unhelpful when it came to giving advice about which lines of the metro were operating (indeed giving me incorrect information on the only occasion I asked), but the ultimate insult was delivered when a young man at reception treated me in a dismissive and arrogant manner on my final morning for wanting to leave “too early” to catch my TGV out of Paris from Montparnasse (after, I should add, handing me a bill overcharging me by 75 euros, about which I had to argue so that eventually it was corrected). Add to this a breakfast buffet where guests have to ask if there is any more bread and where a special request must be made if you require your chocolat chaud to be truly chaud, and it is clear that one’s 300 euro plus per night might be better spent elsewhere.

text:

title: Overrated
text:
I am a long-time reviewer for TripAdvisor. One of the first things I do when I’m looking for accommodations is to look at previous travelers comments. Having traveled extensively through Europe I have certain expectations for the type of hotel I am looking for. So naturally when I came upon the Madison Hotel I was very impressed with the very positive feedback that this hotel has received  over time. I booked my reservation in August 2019 requesting a privilege room with a view on a high floor with breakfast included. As I got closer to our stay at the hotel in December I emailed to confirm our reservation. I received an email back stating that there was no room in that category available which had me very upset. So I forwarded my confirmation and received another email apologizing for the error. That particular email confirmed my original reservation.

Upon arrival at the hotel we were early because we had an overnight flight that arrived at 11AM. I had advised the hotel that I would be arriving early and the hotel responded that they would try to accommodate our arrival as best they could. When I arrived at 1pm I asked to see the room that was assigned to us and it was on their first floor across from the laundry room and very small (read previous travelers comments on that room). So I told the desk that I was expecting a high floor with a view and was willing to wait until that became available. At that time the receptionist showed me one room on the fourth floor room number 43 and room 45 (which I would have accepted but was still under construction). It was not on a high floor as I had requested four months previously and I was very disappointed in the size of the room. So I asked if we could be upgraded to something on a high floor and was told nothing was available. Come to find out later during our stay the hotel was not full and that we could have been accommodated on a higher floor.

The following morning I was able to speak with the concierge Alexandre Dourcy. I explained how we had our reservation months in  advance and that I wanted a high floor. I also explained to him that upon our arrival the desk reception had an attitude. He was very apologetic and said he would see me the next morning and would try to see what he could do. Upon the next morning Mr Dourcy did not follow through and I had to approach him. His explanation was that the manager was not available and that he would discuss this with the manager when he became available. That did not happen right up until the day of our departure. In fact there was no effort to make any concessions or accommodation for the hotels failure to fulfill our request for a room on a high floor. Then at departure upon checking my bill I had been over charged by 108€ and also included was a charge for a children’s charity. I had to again show my confirmation for room rate in order to get the billing error corrected. 

$500 per night was what we paid which included breakfast. So these are my recommendations: be certain to have everything that you request in writing and that you understand where in the hotel you are staying. Best if you know the room # you want and request that. 

Here are the positives: very firm beds, good Wi-Fi, good location, limousine service if arranged in advance and clean hotel. 

Here are the negatives: very thin walls(so very noisy) very poor storage for your clothes, no nightstands next to the bed for storage, no good lighting control in the room, construction next to and above us, rude reception upon arrival. 

I would also add that the sixth arrondissement has many beautiful small boutique hotels. While I was there I looked at two other four-star hotels and the Aubusson all exceptional.  

Service in the hospitality industry is everything and  this hotel is lacking.

title: Fantastic Staff, Stylish Hotel
text:
We enjoyed a wonderful 3 night stay at the Canopy Trocadéro. The hotel is new so everything was well appointed and clean. The room was a good size for Paris and sufficient for our family of 3. The rooftop terrace and bar has stunning views of the Eiffel Tower and a great drinks and snacks menu. Breakfast every day was fresh and all the ingredients are very high quality. The food service was limited because of COVID but not in a way that effected us too much.

The staff at this hotel is absolutely incredible and what made our stay truly memorable. They treated our daughter like “the hotel mascot” to quote our breakfast server. She loved seeing them every day and they really made us feel at home. We had an issue with the hot water in the first room we were given and they resolved it right away. They even allowed us to check in early which was a godsend after our red-eye flight with an infant (the baby’s crib was already set up in the room so she could nap)! I would absolutely stay here again and hope to at some point in the future! 

Thank you so much for making our stay wonderful,
Maman de Colette
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Great location, Hilton-style 'lite', would stay again
text:
We loved:
* Walking distance to both Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe
* Nice eateries for breakfast or dinner at nearby Place Victor Hugo and Place Trocadero
* Close to Métro line 9
* Hilton quality rooms and service standards
* Value for money

One curiosity: water is not provided in plastic bottles (bravo!) so instead they provide you with a glass bottle you can fill up at will at the drinking fountain in the lobby.
But after doing the water run with both bottle and kettle in hand once or twice we decided just to use tap water.

Would definitely stay again.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Perfect location and amazing staff
text: Two top reasons to stay at the Canopy-location and staff. The location is absolutely perfect. You can walk to the Eiffel Tower and the Seine in 5-10 minutes. There are restaurants, many little boutiques, boulangerie’s, pattiseries, cheese stores, cafes and supermarkets around the corner. The metro and a taxi stand are right on the corner so you are accessible to everything. The staff in the hotel is outstanding. Ester is fabulous as are all the staff at the desk, in the restaurant, the bar and cleaning the rooms. All kind, knowledgeable, and will make your stay perfect. Breakfast is wonderful-croissants, bread, yogurts, fruit and warm selections. Be sure to try the chocolate croissant. Rooftop bar has a magnificent view and wonderful bartender!  Try the spritz. Rooms are clean, spacious and have very comfortable beds. Be sure to ask the staff for directions and restaurant suggestions-they have the best suggestions!  Be sure to leave time to just wander the neighborhood. Thank you to everyone at the Canopy for making our stay so special!!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Great place to stay in Paris
text: Great location with views of Eiffel Tower. Walking distance to Musee Monet, Plaza Major, restaurants and shopping. Very helpful and friendly staff. Enjoyed rooftop restaurant and views of the city. Great experience!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Excellent Location

name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Stylish and great location
text: We chose this using HHonors points for a long weekend and were delighted to receive a generous upgrade to a balcony room with side view of the Eiffel tower.  Stunning thank you.  All staff we met were engaging and multi lingual.  The room was stylish with industrial chic decor.  I liked the reusable water bottle and the tv had a good choice of English channels.  Breakfast was excellent,  great breads and strong coffee. The weather conspired against the rooftop terrace but it looked like a great space with spectacular Eiffel views. name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

text: This hotel is done well. Contemporary modern design with space in the rooms much like American Hilton hotels. Great place to stay and convenient location to metro and Eiffel Tower. If your lucky enough to get a room on high floor with balcony you can see the Effiel tower. Breakfast was included for diamond member and was a decent assortment/selection to get you going for the day. Hotel staff is all very pleasant and speak English well. Fantastic stay!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: 3 Night Stay
text: Beautiful hotel, lovely staff and overall a great experience. Reception staff are more than happy to help at every opportunity. The rooms are exactly as they look in the photos very clean and very modern. Make sure to take plenty of spending money though as the hotel and Paris as a whole is quite costly. The location is fantastic, 10 - 15 minutes walk from the Eiffel Tower or a 2 minute walk to Trocedaro Metro Station. Couldn’t ask for anything more so thank you to all the staff for an amazing stay.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Overall enjoyable stay
text:
Pros:

1. Hotel environment and rooms are modern and clean
2. Location is only a short walk to the Eiffel Tower and has great views
3. Hotel is in a good location with many conveniences close by (ex. grocery store, laundromat, bank, bakeries, restaurants, etc.).
4. All of the hotel staff were very helpful and cheerful

Cons:

1. Room service menu and breakfast were mediocre
2. Regarding water, they give you a glass bottle and you have to fill it up yourself via filtered water dispenser on the ground floor. It's not a major inconvenience, but it's worth noting.
3. In our rooms, the toilet is in a separate room from the rest of the restroom. From what I've read, this is more of a France thing, and not just specific to this hotel. It's weird if you're not used to it.

Overall, the pros outweigh the cons, and getting a hotel in the Trocadero area can be pricy, so I'd say this is one of the better options overall.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

text: This hotel is in an excellent location for family access to Paris.  Arrival was seamless after a long flight and with views of the Eiffel Tower out there front door.  The Trocadero area is quiet and quaint yet w/ a Metro stop 2-3 min walk away you have super easy access to the whole city.  The Canopy staff is very welcoming and almost all spoke very good English if important to you.  We were welcomed and recognized as Diamond members upon check-in.  We were in a connected King Family Suite with a Twin Double Room.  The kids (3) took the King Suite as it had a King and pull out sofa.  We were on Floor 5 (of 6 room floors).  View of the top of the tower was nice (to help with the feel of being in Paris for the kids but not extravagant).  However, the 7th floor rooftop terrace has a PHENOMENAL view of the Tower.  NOTE: the 7th floor gets crowded and not seemingly  as kid  friendly although we could not get a table and chose to retire.  Service was excellent.  Breakfast and breakfast service was excellent.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND this hotel for a boutique feel and very accessible yet somewhat off the beaten path.  Only one minor nitpick and that is the bathrooms were small and the WC was separated from the shower area but this is due to efficient room layout so it does not change our opinion of the hotel at all…just pointing it out…great stay in Paris.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Great location, helpful staff, would highly recommend!
text: Hotel is in a prime location for sightseeing and staff were so helpful and friendly. The breakfast was the perfect start to the day and the view from the roof terrace of the Eiffel Tower is something to behold. We also managed to get a nice upgrade,  and the room had a view of the Eiffel Tower which was great. Would highly recommend!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Lousy Service Overall. Not a Hilton Experience!!!
text:
Lousy Service Overall. Not a Hilton at all. When you book a Hilton Hotel you expect Hilton Service, it is not the case here. You do not have 24 hour service. Should you need something after 9-10 pm (i.e., soap, ice,  towels etc.) you have to come down to the lobby yourself and wish they have enough. Room service (food) is very limited and not 24 hours. The roof top (bar?restaurant) has a great view but a lousy service; we stayed at the hotel for 6 nights and were never able to have the steak (seems they have only 4 pieces for a more than 100 hundred guests hotel.  Two nights they even didnt had coke zero (told us there was a shortage, but except for here in all other places you could find it. We once ordered a cesars salad for room service and it was awful (no cheese etc); our overall opinion of the roof top is that all they want is to finish their day (and limited food there) quickly so that they can go home.

We book a cab in the hotel for the airport with 2 days in advance for the day we were living (we specifically told them a van or big car as we were a big party with plenty luggage)….they told us everything was booked and then they only could get us a small cab…had to run to the street and found one ourselves.

On our last morning we hadnt made the checkout and they were already “cleaning” our room, but all other days they made it from 4 to 5 pm….we couldnt use it anymore. Fyi…it seems they dont clean the rooms they only make your beds.

Overall we were expecting the Hilton service but we didnt had it…….
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Perfect for our family of four!
text:
We stayed here for three nights in a room with a king bed and sofa bed. Very comfortable and surprisingly spacious for our family of our (two kids 8 and 11 yo). This is a great location for exploring the city--the Eiffel Tower is just minutes away, numerous restaurants nearby, and fairly easy to get a taxi/Uber or or public transportation. 

The staff here is fantastic--from the moment we arrived in the morning after a long flight and they showed us the transfer refuge room to change, to suggestions for restaurants and things to do, to Mouna at the breakfast and the amazing staff who said "yes" to pretty much any request...this hotel was truly a gem.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Trocadero Bliss
text: This is a perfect location, close to the Eifel and the Metro, not to mention the circle near by.  Plenty of fine eating near by, plus the view from the rooftop is amazing.  If you are traveling with family, the pull out sofas have a memory foam mattress making it a very comfortable bed, a huge plus.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Paris after the fall at Charles DeGaulle
text: We arrived from USA and on way to baggage claim my wife fell over her small suitcase injuring her right shoulder badly.  We were able to proceed to get bags and meet our prearranged taxis driver who took us to Canopy.  We were checked into room quickly and given ice pack for her shoulder....I went to pharmacy to get Advil and then staff tried to help us get Housecall Doctor.....Every staff member exceeded our expectations.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Mixed bag -check in poor- breakfast great- rooftop bar not worth wait.
text:
Arrived early (10a) they held out bags as rooms weren’t ready.  We went out for the day and returned about 7p. A nice man checked us in however he didn’t give us any information.  I went back down to ask about Diamond member breakfast perks ect.  He said he assumed the women in the morning had told us which she hadn’t.  My Diamond status wasn’t recognized and having used 80k points per night I was a touch surprised by this.  After freshening up in the room we found no shampoo or bar soap.  Called desk they said the hotel was completely out of soap waiting on a shipment?  Found this cheap as soap is sold on every corner of Paris.  They brought shampoo and body gel.  

The highlight was breakfast-great greeter and servers both mornings. 

Rooftop bar- we had better experience at the hotel Raphael rooftop bar-same view.  The Service was so slow from moment we sat down it took 40 minutes to get our drinks with no apology.  

I would like at least 40k of my 160k points back for the issues.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Terrific Stay for Us
text: Stayed 3 nights - great hotel.  Really close walk to the Effel Tower.  Plenty of nearby restaurants, cafes.  Close to the bus station - which we used frequently.  Great breakfast here and the rooms are sleek and modern.  Easy check in and out.  We would def. stay again.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Fantastic hotel w/ great location & amazing rooftop
text: This hotel was fantastic in all aspects:  staff, location, hotel, food, rooftop view.  We highly recommend staying here!  First, the staff was extremely friendly and went out of their way to make us feel welcomed and comfortable.  This includes the front desk staff and the restaurant staff.  Thank you!  The hotel is very cool looking and our room was very large especially for Paris.  All the bathroom products were nice; bathroom was perfect with a separate room for the toilet.  And it is in a fantastic location right off of Trocedeo.  It was conveniently located but not too crowded and in a residential neighborhood.  The breakfast was delicious! And, of course, the piece de la resistance: the rooftop bar with an amazing view of the Eiffel Tower!  The only one thing missing was an executive lounge for Diamond Members.  But except for that tiny missing piece the entire experience was great!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Just Perfect
text: Location, size, staff, rooms, roof top, cleaners, all of that just exceeds your expectations. I would recommend this hotel for anyone visiting Paris. The location & rooftop are almost so valuable. If you are lucky like me, you will get a view of the Eiffel Tower also!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Stunning rooftop views
text:
Friendly staff, great food, tasteful decor, and stunning views from the rooftop patio and bar.
The location is convenient, too, whether you’re a first time visitor to Paris or a frequent guest.
Walkable to the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Champs Elysees, Arc de Triomphe, shopping, and more. 
We’ll definitely be back.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Very nice

Concierge was okay, you could have more alternatives (also external ones) shown to you. Will definitely come back.

title: Perfect location in Paris close to Eiffel tower

Rooftop bar has beautiful view of Eiffel tower at night
Rooms and beds are very good, hilton standard
Breakfast quality was very good
Staff are extremely friendly
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Great location, wonderful staff
text: We were lucky to nab this hotel on such short notice. Close proximity to the Eiffel Tower, wonderful cafes around the corner. Hotel was super clean, staff was the best. We had a junior suite, which was roomy and had a soaking tub. Rooftop bar with view of the tower!

title: Amazing stay in the City of Lights
text: We arrived in Paris after a long sleepless flight from Canada. The minute we walked into the hotel, we were embraced and welcomed as long missed family members. The front desk staff quickly and efficiently got us checked in. They acquainted us with the amenities on the property. After dropping luggage in our rooms, we went to the rooftop patio for a light lunch and cocktails. The rooftop patio has wonderful views of the Eiffel Tower. That alone is a reason to stay. Then add a helping of great service. Tasmanna, our hostess and server spent the afternoon providing great service and advice. The  next day Dimitri, provided similar amazing service. These two, along with all of the food and beverage staff helped make our stay. The location of the hotel is perfect for new visitors to Paris, the special sights of Paris are all within an easy walk, Eifflel tower,  Arc d'Triomphe, etc..A special note on the day of departure Treyb from the front desk rescue d our departure by speaking to the preorderd cab company on our behalf and getting them there in a timely fashion... that company was 19 minutes late, after speaking to Trey we had a car within 4 minutes. Thank you Canopy by Hilton Trocader Paris !! We will be back

title: Great hotel near the Eiffel Tower and the Metro

Breakfast experience is excellent, with the help of English speaking and friendly staff - shoutout to Tammara and Catriona.

title: Great stay!

title: Beyond excellent

title: Outstanding Stay All Around

Our stay was fantastic

title: Staff was Amazing!

title: Awesome boutique hotel in a convenient location
text:
TLDR: Perfect boutique hotel in a great location in Paris. Breakfast is to die for, do not miss it!

Pros:
1. Location: it’s a 5-10 min walk to Eiffel Tower! And you can even see the tower from the hotel rooftop!
2. Design: the hotel has a great design. Reminds me of the design hotels of Marriott. From the lobby, on-site restaurant, to the room, you can tell they have very design details taken care of 
3. Breakfast: we got free breakfast as a diamond member and it was not your typical hotel breakfast. It’s a full serviced breakfast with staff taking your order with a la cart menu, and they would also bring out specialties for you to try throughout the breakfast service. My favorite is the detox ginger shot and hot cheese and ham croissant. There is also a small buffet section you can get bread, pastries and scrambled eggs if you want. The breakfast is the highlight of my stay!
4. Gym: decent gym with free weights, treadmills, and a couple machines. Again the hotel is so new so the gym is spanking new too, you can get a good workout in here for sure.

Cons:
Not much really, but if I have to be super picky, here are two:
1. Room size: we got upgraded to premium king from regular king room and it still felt a bit small. But I guess that is the norm for Parisian hotels in the city center. 
2. Fish and chips: we ordered fish and chips from the hotel restaurant. It was their take on fish and chips where you really got chips as Americans would say (or for British it crisps). And the fish is fried fish paste formed strip. It was good but probably the British will think it’s blasphemy.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: The Perfect Stay
text:
This hotel and its staff is a perfect”10”. My husband and I were celebrating our 40th wedding anniversary. This trip to Paris was very special to us. Our breakfast was fantastic with Tamanna and the rest of the morning crew helpful and attentive. We had drinks every evening and the bar crew were superb. title: Fantastic Stay at this Gem of a Hotel in the Heart of the Trocadero
text:
Long-time Hilton Diamond member, first-time reviewer.

My partner and I recently stayed at the new Canopy hotel in the Trocadero.  We love the neighborhood and typically stay at a competitor hotel, but as it had been nearly two years since our last Paris visit, we decided to change things up.

We couldn't have been more pleased with the experience and have adopted this hotel as our new home in Paris for future stays.

First, the hotel is brand-new, clean, and hip.  The view from the front door is a majestic vista of the Eiffel Tower bookmarked by two blocks of gorgeous Trocadero apartments. Second, the staff are incredibly welcoming and go above and beyond to make you feel comfortable.  From the early check-in to drinks on the roof and the delicious breakfast every morning, we felt right at home and (as we were staying for a week) felt like we knew all the staff by face, if not by name, by the end of our stay.

The bedrooms are well-appointed, and the gym is one of the nicest I've ever used at a hotel, Hilton or otherwise.

My only two cons - our room, a premier king room, could have benefited with a better occasional chair.  Rather than a comfy lounger, there was essentially a padded office chair in the corner.  Also, the beautiful bathroom has an attractive, translucent wall panel.  It is only until the middle of the night that you realize it completely lights up the bedroom if someone conducts any nighttime ablutions. (This may have just been our room, however.)

All in all, coming back to Paris during Covid was a bit of a trial, but we couldn't have been happier with the trip, in no small part due to our experience at this wonderful hotel.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Best experience I have ever had on a hotel stay
text: 100% recommended. They ladies at the front desk were amazing and made us feel welcome and appreciated. The breakfast was delicious and the service was fast and attentive. title: Great experience
text: This Hilton property is very new and very impressive! We booked 2 rooms and arrived to find a cot already set up in one room. They also put us in a "suite" configuration, where 2 rooms could become one. Parking was very easy, especially given that the hotel is downtown Paris. Location couldn't be beat! 5 minutes from the Eiffel Tower. You can also view the tower at night from their rooftop bar. The hotel staff was exceptional! Great job on this one Hilton!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Wonderful Property, Better Staff
text:
Hotel is perfectly located, absolutely spotless and the customer service is extraordinary.  Staff was professional, courteous and responsive and provided assistance to my family several times throughout our brief stay, including a difficult to navigate car rental issue which they resolved quickly and efficiently.

Views from the rooftop deck are spectacular, great neighborhood with many restaurants.  Breakfast at the hotel was also very good.  Rooms were spacious, clean and well appointed.  

Highly recommend and would definitely stay again without hesitation.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Amazing Staff, Great Location
text:
I cannot say enough positive things about this hotel.

The staff is welcoming and amazing. The rooms are comfortable and brand new. The hotel’s location is a short, 3-minute walk to a dozen restaurants and eateries. It’s a beautiful 20-minute walk to Arc de Triomphe and Champs-Élysées. And the proximity to and views of the Eiffel Tower (from the hotel entrance and rooftop) are the icing on the cake.

Also, during a recent stay with my husband and young son, I had an unfortunate health issue. The entire hotel staff made a really difficult situation more manageable. Their friendly notes and words of encouragement gave me strength, and I’m just very thankful for everything they did and said to make me feel at home.
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Outstanding customer service in this exciting new hotel
text:
The hotel is brand new, with an exciting interior design paying hommage to the French art deco of the 1930s.  It is located in a very nice and upscale residential neibourhgood, just around the corner from a metro station.  The rooms are not very big, but creatively and efficiently designed, and some offer a partial view of the Eiffel Tower.  For the full view of the tower make sure to book a table at the terrace and enjoy a cocktail or a dinner there.  The best thing about the hotel, however, is its outsanding team.  Every employee was very welcoming and professional, but I would particularly like to mention four team members with whom we interacted the most:

The Chief Enthusiast (hotel manager) Ms. Lorent was very helpful in allaying my concerns about this brand-new property which lacked customer reviews when I wanted to book it, and assuring me that everything will be in order by the time we arrive - which was certainly the case.  She also took the time from her busy schedule to speak to me and my family a number of times during our stay and and told us about the history of the hotel, answered our questions, etc.

The Lead Welcome Enthusiast (head consierge) Ms. Ester Barrios-Arshak has been incredibly responsive and attentive to our needs.  She changed our reservation dates when we had to postpone our trip due to the continued COVID restrictions while securing the approval to keep our original room rates; she upgraded us upon check-in; and after learning about my daughter's love of baking she even proposed to organize a private baking class for her with the hotel's chef Mr. Kubarek.  She also provided us with useful information on sightseeing, and checked on our request whether certain museums were open, etc.  In short, she made our stay simply unforgettable!

The Lead Kitchenb Enthusiast (heda chef) Mr. Robin Kubarek cooked outstanding meals (we really enjoyed our a-la-carte breakfasts!) in a sparkling clean kitchen, and we could watch him at work through the window in the restaurant which was an excellent way of showcasing both his and his colleagues' skills and the top hygienic standards of the restaurant.  He also took the time for a private baking lesson for our daughter and introduced her to the secrets of French patisserie.  She absolutely loved the lesson and the unexpected presents she received from Mr. Kubarek - not just the cookies she baked, but also a personalized recipe book, a jar with baking mix and even a personalized chef's hat!  This was a truly unforgettable experience for her and for us. 

Finally the (head?) waiter Thibault provided us with outstanding service during our stay.  In addition to attending to our every need during breakfast time, one evening he offered us a bartending demonstration mixing delicious cocktails (and a mocktail for our daughter) for the family.  He was always very upbeat, courteous and attentive to our every need.  France definitely need more service professionals like him!
name: Canopy By Hilton Paris Trocadero

title: Duplex suite with views
text: Stayed at the Hotel Raphael for 4 days inAugust. The hotel is in a great location walking distance to many shops, sites and restaurants. We were a large group with 8 rooms booked. The rooms varied in decor but all fairly spacious by European standards. Beds are very comfortable. We opted for the Duplex suite with Terrace. The room is beautiful, but the terrace is the highlight. Being a large group, having the option to sit and enjoy a drink on the terrace was fantastic. It is very large and fits many people, with beautiful views of the lit up Eiffel Tower at night. The restaurant rooftop is also lovely, but drinks can be pricey so if you enjoy the rooftop view, I recommend looking into the rooms with a terrace. The rooms are limited in number and there is only one Duplex so good to plan early. Service at the hotel was good and everyone very pleasant. There is only one person taking care of check in and check out so be prepared for a possible wait. I would stay again at the Raphael and definitely try and book the Duplex if available.

title: Outstanding Hotel
text:
This hotel was one of the highlights of our brief stay in Paris, and we would most definitely plan to stay here again on a return trip.

The Room
We stayed in a Signature Suite, which had a bedroom and separate sitting room. The room was huge, comfortable, and beautifully appointed. The hotel itself was tasteful and peaceful. We truly looked forward to returning there each day.

The Service
Staff were helpful, generous, discrete, and it felt like every time we left the room we would return to see that it had been tidied (multiple times a day).

Location
A Metro stop is immediately outside the door (Line 6), with another a few minutes away at the Arc de Triomphe. For most of the places you’ll want to visit, it will require a ride on the Metro. The locations walkable are the Arc and the Champs-Élysées.

Critique
Only two things come to mind, and neither of them were close to being bothers such that it would mean we wouldn’t return. The first, air conditioning: we were in Paris during the summer heatwave (up to 105F one day), and we were sure to book a room that was air conditioned. When we arrived we learned that consisted of a portable A/C unit that was vented out the window, requiring the window be left open. We maneuvered the drapes to cover much of the open window, but leaving the window open in that level of heat did make a difference. It wasn’t what I thought would be the case when I saw the room listed as air-conditioned. We were comfortable nonetheless. The second: the shower temperature was erratic. Over the course of a five-minute shower the temperature would vary wildly. It would never get so cold or so hot that it was unbearable, but it was quite noticeable.

Summary
The critiques are minimal in comparison to the overwhelming quality of the hotel. We loved it, and we’d happily return.

title: Great Hotel in Great Location
text: Great hotel.  We loved the location, it was hot the week we were in Paris and the area was perfect.  The street the hotel is on is a pretty street with some shade and plenty of the things you need to enjoy your stay very close.  We walked to some great restaraunt that the wonderful concierge team recommended, the Arche de Triomohe is right there as well as shopping.  It’s in a beautiful neighborhood and we enjoyed a few early morning walks away from the more touristy parts.  The roof top terrace was amazing!  We had wonderful food and drinks our first evening.  They said only appetizers but the portions were very generous and we did instead of dinner.  We had two rooms- the suites are definitely worth the additional money.  Next time I would just get two suites as there was a appreciable difference between the Room and suite we were in.  But we were so happy we had picked this hotel.  The only thing that we didn’t like was the breakfast.  We didn’t do the breakfast included option - but the way our schedule worked and having 2 different room it was too hard to coordinate breakfast outside the hotel.  Based on the bill at checkout I think we paid  42 euros per person to have coffee and what I would consider mediocre pastries.  The breakfast is a buffet with just coffee, juice, the same 4 or 5 types of pastries and scrambled eggs.  No changes day to day.  You can order omelets and there is a chopped fruit bowl and cereal.  On the upside the staff was great and the coffee was good, it was quick and easy.  Just too expensive for what it was and way too repetitive.  Even having one pastry that varied day to day would have been great.  I always wanted a “good” breakfast and it was not even average and irritated me to pay so much day after day.  Frankly I would have been happier just paying for a cup of coffee and eating a protein bar, but didn’t feel like getting into whether that was possible with the staff so paid the full price and had toast.  There were coffee machines in the room.  We did room service once and it was good and prompt.  The kids did it more and it was always good quality and service.  Overall very very happy with the hotel!

title: A tad short of perfection
text: Where to start with a hotel that displays a Turner - yes a real one or at least a darn good copy - in its lobby. I love ancien regime hotels. The Raphael is certainly that. It feels a little like staying with a wealthy elderly uncle set in his ways. It sits on Avenue Kleber accessible to the chic 16ème arrondissement, the Champs-Elysees and the Louvre beyond, the river and the Trocadero. The Raphael is what you might call a 'grande dame'. Or in its case un grand oncle. The overwhelming majority of the staff are men - in grey suits. They're wonderfully helpful and professional but I think a sprinkling of young women front of house would give the place a lift. The rooftop restaurant and bar especially in summer - is a treat. Sip a kir royale and gaze at the Arc de Triomphe, the Eiffel tower and Sacré Coeur on the heights. Breakfast I thought was dull. Rooms are comfy. Ours was a bit tired. Bath was tricky to negotiate if you're on the wrong side of 70. Terrific shower. They give you one 500ml bottle of water on arrival but do not replenish that which is, as the French say, a trifle mésquin. It's family owned. Where's the younger generation?

title: Timeless luxury with incredible service
text: We stayed in a two bedroom for 4 nights. It was like stepping back in time.  The beds were incredibly comfortable the rooms were large with big closets-room for the large steamer trunks of old. If you like and are accustomed to the more modern decor of the Four Seasons or Peninsula, recognize this is not it. The bathrooms have tub showers that don’t really keep the water in. Needed to just use the hand shower in one or water would have been in the entire bathroom. But they were a nice size with separate rooms for toilet which is always nice when traveling. Service really was incredible. Concierge can help with everything and does so with pleasure. Very good English by almost everyone. Included breakfast is a treat. We had room service once and it was very quick and delicious. While the rooftop was closed we were able to go up at night and see the lights of the Eiffel Tower. Very special. Fitness center is lacking. Very small. Treadmill, elliptical, rowing machine, recumbent and regular bike. Treadmill was broken and elliptical sounded like it was on its last legs. Nice locker room and showers available also a sauna I didn’t use. While they delivered water and macarons and some chocolate on arrival it would have been nice to get some water with the turn down service.  Location is great. Easy metro or walking to everything. All in all really a special trip and we would stay again in a heartbeat.

text:
I stayed for a week. The room is great, spacious, even huge, roof top beautiful. Great breakfast too. But there are many carpets and even fabric on the wall, the one in the wardrobe then smells a lot. I got a horrible allergy, especially when I turned on the air conditioner.

The gentleman told me it was "hotel style". That all rooms were the same. I saw another friend in a room that at least had no fabric on the wall like mine. NOTHING WAS MADE.

I complained again the next day with another attendant. They were to return me. As I had a lot to work with, I slept for four long days with the windows wide open to breathe as well as take. For the past two days I have moved to the hotel across the street, the Peninsula.

Carpeting requires care, cleaning. And listening to the customer would make all the difference. Also, in my room in particular (106), the upholstery in the close-up and even the one on the floor and chair looked very old and full of mites. I felt very disrespected.

title: The most wonderful stay!
text: We truly enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Raphael.  It was so very memorable.  Everyone was friendly, helpful, and interested in making our stay enjoyable: the two attentive staff members(both named Alexandre) as well as Pascal, who facilitated our airport transfers, and Aude, who was always so friendly at the reception desk.  I also want to  thank Jacque Francois, who was so kind as to find a way to freeze our butter purchases, so I could bring them back to the States.  The suite was large, elegant, and refined, furnished with many antiques  We enjoyed two bathrooms, a large sitting room, and all the extras anyone could ask for. Balcony windows opened on to each of four small pediments where one could see and enjoy the streets of Paris. Words cannot due justice to the beauty of watching the Effiel Tower light up from the rooftop Terrace. This five star hotel is one of the best!  The staff is always at your disposal and make the stay at this luxury  hotel an indelible memory of Paris!

title: Team Raphael took care of us
text:
We were a large group composed of Americans from a wide range of states and Europeans from several countries. Camille Allenic managed our group and set up all the logistics from parking to rooms to dinners. She went above and beyond to help us out as we had a lot of moving parts doing a Tour de France cycling trip.  Her help and professionalism made a world of difference. Once there, all the people we interacted with from conciergerie team to reception were impeccable. Joel Cochin especially was attentive and we so enjoyed seeing him at our breakfasts and dinners that it was like he was a part of our group. Everything was beautifully laid out and no request seemed too much. The Raphael team carries themselves with a perfect blend of professionalism and pride yet also interacting with genuine warmth. The hotel has grandeur and a presence but also feels inviting. We found it very easy to walk to shops, cafes, attractions, take the metro if we wished, all while in town to catch the last stage of the Tour de France. BRAVO team Raphaël and chapeau Camille and Joel. 
Iona Wynter Parks

title: Wonderful Hotel in Paris
text: I just came back from another wonderful stay at the Hotel Raphael.  I have stayed there many times, and was so glad to make this my first visit once travel restrictions were lifted.  The hotel is different than all other high-end hotels in Paris.  The style and architecture exude Belle-Epoque Paris, yet it also has a quite intimate feel.  The service, and especially the concierge, is wonderful, always at the ready to help.  The location is excellent -- right by the Etoile with lots of connections by metro to the rest of Paris.  The rooms are incredibly spacious  (the largest hotel rooms I've ever stayed in) and very quiet.  The beds are very comfortable.  To top it all off, the hotel has a magnificient roof-top bar with excellent views of the the Arche di Triomphe and the Tour Eiffel.

title: NYE
text:
We booked this hotel due to its location and rooftop terrace to watch the fireworks.  I’ve stayed in Paris many times before and the customer service is hit or miss.

First thing is I have to say the customer service at this hotel was top notch.  The doormen and concierge were always so kind and helpful.  When asked questions, the concierge was responsive and helped us book reservations right away. 

The front desk staff was also very welcoming.

However, when we got to our room, we were surprised that there were so many cracks and chipped paint in areas.  There was also mold in our bathroom.  We reported our disappointment in the room and we were loved to another room the next day.  They were apologetic and gave some free goodies and also comped our NY day brunch (130€/pp).  The wait staff though did not speak English well. 

The new room was in much better shape.  The rooms overall were spacious.  It is a more traditional and older feel but very clean and comfortable. 

The location is excellent as the train stop is nearby.  But during this time the trains weren’t working due to the strike.  

For NYE on the roof top, you can see both the Eiffel and the Arc du Triumphe.  We enjoyed the amazing fireworks show.

Overall, I would recommend this hotel if you would like to enjoy the rooftop terrace and like a more spacious room in Paris. The service was also excellent.

title: 2 star room in a famous 5 star Parisian hotel
text:
I booked my room via booking.com. I arrived late in the evening after a long busy day traveling and business dinner, the check in was smooth. The lobby and room looked elegant at first glance. There was delicious welcome cakes waiting in the room too.
I got room 015. 
The big horrible surprised hit me in the morning when entered bathroom which was a worn down bathroom with cracked tiles, rusted faucets, fittings and shower head and worst enough black mould at the corner of bath tub and with a discolored dusty hairdryer hangin there (there was a new one in the room) but look this one was horrible!!?
The worst and most unbeleivable part came, I saw a smal half an inch cockroach walking on the wall right below towel rack!! If I had seen this last night I could not sleep there at any costs. The wall paints in the room was peeling near the floor in some areas near entrance. I checked out in the morning, receptionist promise he will send someone to take care of cockroach.
Later booking.com refused to publish my review, which is based on my personal experience in room they booked me in, against the fact I am a member since 15 years; sorry booking.com I never book through you.
I do not think all their rooms are like that but I know cockroaches can go anywhere, specialy the little ones!!!?

Omelette 12
Sausage 4
Tomato, spinach, cheese, mushrooms 3

Avoid this hotel if you plan to take a shower or eat breakfast at the hotel.

title: Eiffel Tower Suite - Lovely Property, a Few Minor Fixes Would Make It Perfect
text:
I had a short overnight layover with my 10-year-old son at CDG. While I had originally planned to stay at an airport hotel, as I was entering the itinerary into my calendar, I realized the layover would be on July 14 - so of course we couldn’t miss the fireworks over the Eiffel Tower! I chose the Eiffel Tower Suite specially to ensure a view. 

We arrived after a very adventurous trip in from the airport as various RER and metro stations we needed we closed for construction and due to protests we could not get a taxi/Uber so had a decent walk (with a large police presence due to the protests). We were happy to be greeted by friendly employees who confirmed we had the Eiffel Tower Suite and we were quickly on our way upstairs. 

The suite is lovely. After our long journey, we were delighted to find chilled champagne, juices, and macarons. The view was fantastic! The suite was spacious and lovely with a very comfortable bed. The balcony was HUGE. We ordered room service, which was excellent, and then watched the fireworks (the view here is to the side of the Eiffel Tower so the fireworks are primarily to the right of the Tower not behind it - we knew this in advance and it made no difference to us but I mention it for those who may be picky about their firework viewing!). My son especially loved this hotel and is begging to return. 

So, with all this excellence, why only 4 stars? A few minor points:
- there was something banging in the bathroom over the toilet, perhaps a loose part of the vent. It was loud enough to hear in the bedroom while we were trying to go to sleep so certainly would have been heard by housekeeping or anyone else entering the room.
- the balcony needed to be swept. 
- there was not a working deadbolt on the room. As a female traveler, this is a basic expectation. 
- the concierge was rude. As we were leaving, we stopped to request directions (we had asked the front desk and they directed us to the concierge). The concierge was on the phone so we waited. When he finished, he greeted us and I politely began asking him for directions. The phone then rang and without a word, he turned away from me as I was talking and answered the phone. I thought perhaps he was going to put the call on hold, but he just kept talking to the caller as if I wasn’t there. We finally just walked away without our directions and asked someone on the street. 

At a lesser hotel, a rude concierge and some maintenance issues might be cause for a lower rating, but with the exception of the concierge, all the employees here were wonderful and the suite was absolutely lovely. We were very satisfied but there is room for improvement.

Overall, this is a good hotel. In the future, I may look to another property to explore a different part of Paris, but otherwise this is one that I would recommend.
