title: Good efficiency apartment, friendly service
text:
I stayed with my family for a single night in a two bedroom apartment at the Hotel Helzear Champs-Elysees back in December, in the midst of the transportation strike.  All in all we had a great experience, and my complaints are all minor.  Still, I would really give it 4 - 4 1/2 stars, but I’m raising the rating to 5 because of the service by staff.

The apartment itself is what I’ve seen described in books as an ‘efficiency apartment “.  It’s designed to take best advantage of the reduced space.  In general it succeeded, but there were a couple of misses.

The two bedrooms were very small, just large enough to accommodate the double beds.  This meant no room for night stands, but also nowhere to put your glasses.  Adding a shelf would be helpful.  The beds were comfortable enough- though as it was the case with all the hotel beds we experienced during this trip to Europe and the Middle East - too hard for our American expectations.  Ditto for the pillows.  One of my daughters slept in the sofa bed, and she had no complaints.

The bathroom was small, but well designed and we appreciated the towel warmer (which seems de rigeur for hotels in continental Europe).  They had very nice toiletries and good water pressure.  

The living room and kitchen were a bit cramped, but we didn’t have much need of them given our short stay.  I did appreciate that they had a minibar, with prices not as ridiculous as in chain hotels.

My main quibble is that the apartment lacked any personality or style.  I was hoping for something that had the basic charm of the rooms pictured here, but there was nothing of the sort. Inside the apartment, there was no sense we were in Paris, as opposed to anywhere else.  Of course, this is ultimately on me for not researching it better.

The hotel location is wonderful, very close to the Metro line 1, which is automated and therefore was running normally during the strike.  We were able to take it to the Louvre.  The hotel itself is a little hard to find, however.  There is only a small sign next to the door, and our taxi driver missed it.  They also need to buzz you in to enter, which can be annoying.  Elevators require a key card, if I remember correctly, and they are tiny.

What made my experience 5-star was the service from the staff at the Helzear, in particular the female receptionist in the morning we left (I wish I remembered her name). After the taxi company she called for us to take us to the airport flaked on us, she used her personal account to call an Uber for us.  When we ended up canceling it, I compensated her for the expected cancellation fee, but she chased my taxi and ended up returning it because Uber didn’t charge it.

All in all, this is a great place to stay in Paris, as long as you are not expecting old world charm in your apartment decor.

title: Very noisy room and bad service
text:
I stayed two nights at this apartment hotel for business trip. The first night was in a junior suite which located on the first floor with all windows directly facing the main street. Because the windows are big and very thin and the street is busy with cars all the time, I can hear all the noises from the street and cannot sleep during the night. It’s as noisy as if you were directly sleep on the street... It was really bad, especially I had a meeting the next day. I wouldn’t consider the junior suite it’s suitable for business stay. For the room structure, it is like a loft. You need to walk up the staircases to your bed, which is on an add-in floor with very low ceiling. Besides, the bed is not a real bed, it’s just a 20cm mattress and you can only sit but not stand in that space in order to not hit your head.

Another bad part is the taxi booking service: they helped me reserved a taxi at early morning to the airport and I confirmed with them that the taxi will drive directly to the airport without picking up other passengers in between. Apparently that is not the case! First of all, the driver is 30min late to pick me up, and then, she drives around the block in the bad Paris morning traffic to pick up another client (who goes to a different terminal than me) from the same hotel chain of Helzear, as the driver said it is arranged by the hotel like this. It made the time arriving the airport very tight. What surprised me the most is: each of us needs to pay the full price of the taxi! That’s was totally not communicated before.

Overall I will not consider again this hotel for my other trips to Paris.

title: Great hotel in a great spot
text: Best of all the accomodation we stayed in on our three week Europe trip. Reasonably priced and close to everything. The staff went above and beyond many times and really helped when we thought we had lost our credit cards!
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: Wouldn't Recommend.
text:
We stayed at Helzear Champs Elysees for 5 nights at the end of September. We had the Junior Suite.
We were disappointed with the accomodation as a whole and will not recommend anyone to stay there. 
Prior to our stay but after booking, we called the hotel roughly 4 times. On each attempt, there was no response. Upon arrival we noticed that when a call came, they would answer and immediately hang up the phone. Staff were not helpful when asked questions about tourism.
The check in time which was on the booking stated 1pm, to which they said it was a mistake and to come back at 3pm. Thus, after a 21 hour flight we had to sit down the road with our bags and wait for 2 hours. We also had been advised when booking that we would have a balcony and a private terrace, but in fact we had no balcony or terrace. When asked, the staff again said that it must be a mistake. No effort was made to rectify this. 
The apartment itself was small, old and the air conditioning was inconsistent.

The only positive to our stay at this hotel was the location. If travelling again though, this would be last on the list.
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: Great stay in Paris
text: My family of 5 had a great stay at this Helzear Champs-Elysees recently.  We had a two bedroom apartment facing onto the Avenue Marceau.  It was a beautiful outlook and a great location.  We could walk to the Eiffel Tower, Arc de Triumph, Champs-Elysee, and George V Metro station which is on Line 1 was 5 minute walk. There are great restaurants around as well as supermarket, cafes, laundromat, patisseries and even a lovely florist not far away.  We really felt like we were in the centre of Paris - which we were! The staff were very nice and helpful. Special mention to Khalil who went out of his way to make us feel welcome.  The main bedroom was large although the second bedroom and living space were not (typical in Paris) especially when the sofa bed is used, BUT as a family of 2 adults and 3 children were had ample space.  The rooms were clean, plenty of storage, lovely modern bathrooms, and beautiful large windows! We will definitely stay here again!!
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: Great hotel close to amenities in Paris
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights over a weekend for a girl’s trip to Paris.  It was ideally located off the George V road and convenient for the metro.  There were cafés, corner shops and patisseries close by which again were ideal to bring some vino back to our room.  Not to mention the fabulous Champs Elyse!!  
There were 4 of us in an apartment which had a mezzanine bedroom plus a settee in the living room which turned into a bed.  The only downside was only 1 bathroom (and mirror!) which can be an issue for 4 women sharing  
The reception staff were friendly and welcoming.
The room was clean and well kept.
The beds comfortable, including the settee bed which was very easy to pull out and in.
The location was fantastic
What more could you want.
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: Location and Quality
text: Perfect location, warm welcome, great friendly local knowledge and lovely room. The bed was super comfortable, room was plenty big enough and the bathroom/shower was great. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a place very close to Eiffel tower, Arc De Triumph and the  Champs-Élysées. The only part that could've been better was having someone at the desk more often, there was many times there was no one at the desk for assistance. The staff happily stored our bags for us and organised a taxi for us on our departure day. Loved our visit!
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: Perfect hotel
text:
We stayed at the Helzear Suites from 31st August until 3rd September and had the best time. The hotel is perfectly located with Hermes on the corner as you enter the street (Christopher Columbus) and the Arc De Triomphe in view on the other side (Avenue Marceau). It’s ideal for visiting Paris and you can easily reach all of the main attractions without any hassle. There are plenty of shops, bars and restaurants around the area and lots of choice in terms of cuisine. 

Our room was actually in the hotel on Avenue Marceau. It would be helpful if the hotel inform you ahead of arrival as to where you are allocated as we had a transfer from the airport and then had to walk over to the other hotel. It is only a few minutes but it’s not the perfect start when you have a lot of luggage or kids or when the weather is bad etc. Wills was extremely helpful, took our bags and walked us over. 

We were allocated Balzac room which is right at the front of the hotel on ground level. The room is very small even by Paris standards but we knew we would only be sleeping in the room so it didn’t really matter although storage was a bit of a challenge. As a light sleeper I was worried about noise from the street however I didn’t have any issue with this and didn’t find it noisy at all. The room had cooking facilities along with a kettle and coffee machine which was handy. Nuxe toiletries were provided in the bathroom along with a hair dryer. The hotel provides free Wi-Fi with individual access codes and the connection was really good. 

One of the main benefits of this hotel is the location however I’d say the most important thing is the service from the staff which is the best I’ve ever received after many many trips to Paris. Ines couldn’t have been more helpful, making sure we took care when out and about and looking after us all the time. 

It’s not a typical hotel, it’s more friendly and has a very homely feel with the informal reception area. There’s nothing worse than having to wait in a long queue to check in or out or to speak to someone on reception if you need something. We didn’t have to wait for anything and the staff would ask if everything was ok every time we were coming or going. 

I’d definitely recommend this hotel and look forward to returning soon.
name: Suites & Hôtel Helzear Champs-Elysées

title: The staff were so lovely and helpful!

title: Worst hotel of trip - left a lot to be desired
text:
The bad news started when we walked arrived at check-in time and noticed a lot of not so happy looking people sitting around the lobby along with lots of luggage. Not so surprisingly, we were told that our 4 rooms would be ready in an hour and we should come back later. The reception clerk  indicated that the hotel would hold our luggage and gave us 8 numbered clam checks. We arrived back more than an hour later and only 3 of our rooms were ready and she provided no indication when the last one would be ready. We handed over our claim checks, but didn’t look at the numbers   or check which luggage we were taking She only pointed to a collection of luggage on the other side of the lobby some of which was ours. So much for secure luggage holding.
Although the hotel had our credit card information when the reservation was made, the hotel makes you pay for your room as you check in (I’ve never encountered this before). You also are asked to decide whether you want breakfast for your stay, which you also have to pay upfront. Given the mediocre quality of the breakfast compared to the prior nights’ hotel, we would not have gone the second and third day had we not prepaid.
We’ve been to Paris a number of times and realize that rooms run small, but this was ridiculous. To get out of bed to use the toilet, I had to turn and walk sideways.
The worst however was service from the front desk. We had passed a restaurant the night before and asked to dine outside, but was told it was fully booked. The host said he could seat us inside, and then pointed to an inside table furthest from the street. We said we’ll come back another time. The next day we asked hotel reception to book an outside table for 8 at that restaurant that evening. She phoned while we waited, and us that the person she spoke to had to get back to her. Later, she told us the reservation outside had been made. I asked her if she was sure the reservation was for outside and she indicated that is why they had to call back. We got to the restaurant and mentioned our reservation for outside and gave both our name and the hotel name. The host then proceeded to usher us to the same back corner table that he wanted to seat us in the night before. I repeated that we had made an outside reservation but he didn’t respond. He offered no explanation or acknowledge whether he saw the reservation, but would not seat us outside.
We relayed this episode to the man on duty at the hotel reception, and he became defensive of the restaurant. He explained that restaurants often overbook. We understand that overbooking is sometimes done to handle situations when people don’t show up, but we were at the restaurant when the restaurant opened and no one was yet seated.  We questioned whether the restaurant might not like Americans, and he dismissed that possibility. In any event, he was totally unsympathetic to the fact that our reservation was not honored and perhaps irritated that we complained about the restaurant.
Prior to going to our rooms for the evening, I asked the same clerk to arrange for two taxis to take us to Versailles the next morning and he agreed. The next morning on the way to breakfast, I saw the same guy and a woman behind the reception desk and asked whether our taxis were all set. They indicated they were set. Later when we ready to leave, I asked the same woman where we should wait for our taxis and she said outside. When the taxis did not arrive, I came back to reception and let her know they were not there. She then told me the taxis in fact had not been confirmed. I then asked her to contact a taxi company and she indicated it was impossible as it was the busy time of the day. Since she would not even try to get us taxis (which she had previously said were confirmed) we were left to our own to find our way to Versailles with timed reservations during a busy time of the day. Given the circumstances, I was left to wonder whether reception purposely sabotaged the taxi ride because I took offence at the restaurant not honoring the reservation the night before. I’m glad we were not relying on the taxi to get us to the airport. 
I’ve traveled extensively both for business and pleasure, but never encountered a situation like this.

title: Perfect Parisian Hotel!
text:
We arrived a bit early to check in, so we killed time at a cafe for an hour.  Clara was very helpful at checking us in. The halls, and elevators, and rooms are small, but it's Europe.  
   There's a great breakfast on the lower level that's in a quaint room which cost 13 euros apiece when we took advantage of it. But it's really good!
   The rooms are small, but very nice and clean. The shower has great temperature and water pressure, BUT the shower only has a splash guard so that awesome water pressure can splash all over if you're not careful.  The toiletries were just a shower gel bottle in the shower, a bottle of lotion, and a bottle of hand soap.  So anything more you'd need, you'd have to bring. 
  I loved having a small fridge in the room, and I think there was a safe in the closet that needed some kind of key, but we didn't look into it.  The TV is a flat screen against the wall and has many French and English channels. There is no iron or ironing board, and even though I saw one downstairs where I ate breakfast, we discovered that was for use for the whole hotel and we had to bring our clothes downstairs to iron it. So I had wrinkled clothes that day.
  But other than that, everything was amazing!! All the major tourist attractions are within walking distance. La Bon Marche', Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, all within walking distance. It's a long walk, but I love it. Also really close is that huge gold domed building which is Hotel National des Invalides, which is must better than it sounds where you can see Napoleon's tomb and other great things.
   But this hotel is GREAT, the staff (ALL the staff!) is SO nice! This was the perfect introduction to Paris for me! Also, if you want to sit outside with a glass of wine from next door, the wifi works there as well! I would LOVE LOVE LOVE to stay here again!

title: Great views of the tower but after that, not much to rave about.
text:
If a view of the Eiffel Tower is what you’re after, then this is the perfect hotel for you. We booked a premium room and had a gorgeous view of the Eiffel Tower. The staff were so lovely and so helpful, the rooms were clean and it is only a 10 min walk to the Eiffel Tower. 
However, after that I would say there are nicer and cheaper hotels out there with better locations. The rooms were quite old, with chipped door frames and old, damaged furniture. It probably is in need of a total revamp. The walls were super thin… so much so that we could hear the people next door using the bathroom and their exact conversations with each other. I’m sure they could hear ours, too. The location is ok, but there wasn’t a lot to do around the area. Not many restaurants or bars. 
All in all… this is a 3 star hotel for a reason. We stayed in another hotel for our first two nights in Paris near the Arc de Triomphe and we much preferred it to Hotel Duquesne. I don’t think I’d stay here again.

If we come back to Paris we would definitely stay here again!

We had a wonderful trip to Paris, and that was partially due to the lovely Hotel Duquesne Eiffel!

title: Convenient, Clean, Well-Apportioned Hotel in Shadow of Eiffel Tower
text:
This hotel is located on a relatively quiet street in a fairly non-touristy district.  We enjoyed our 5-night stay.

You can see the Eiffel Tower when you walk out the front door, and there are several Metro lines in walking distance.  The room was pretty good sized for a European hotel room, and the staff was friendly and helpful.  The main nearby street, on which the Ecole Militaire Metro stop is located, has plenty of places to eat, as well as a 24-hour grocery store.  Rue Cler (a street with a variety of food & wine stores, plus restaurants) is within walking distance and is certainly worth checking out.  

If you are looking for a hotel that is near, but not directly amidst, the main museum attractions of the city, I would definitely recommend this one.

title: Not Great for Friends, Poor Value for Money - Rm 52
text:
My friend and I were very much looking forward to staying in what by all accounts should've been a lovely hotel. Unfortunately our expectations were not met.

Staff: We only had dealings with reception a couple of times, they were efficient and helpful although not effusively so.

Room: Unfortunately this was the main area of disappointment. We paid for one of the 'superior' rooms so our expectations were fairly high, reasonably so considering the more than 300 euro nightly rate for it! The size of room was, by any standard, tiny (the professional photos are unfortunately deceiving). We were travelling as two friends so while there were two separate beds there was no point to their being so as (by necessity due to the size of room) they were pushed right up together. There was only just room for one person to walk round the bed to the bathroom at one time, and even then it was a squeeze.

Night noise wasn't bad considering the central location however on both our nights we were disturbed by another patron screaming and cursing in the hallway in the small hours, of course not the hotel's fault but still a mar on short stay.

A small thing considering the number of cafes nearby but we were also disappointed by the tea and coffee making facilities, 2 sachets of coffee, a small selection of tea bags (one per type), no milk provided. So you will either have to enjoy your coffee black or bring in milk from elsewhere.

Another small issue was there were no instructions in the room as to how to call reception, the hairdryer in our bathroom didn't work and when we tried to call down to enquire we were unable to do so.

Bathroom: Clean but tiny, with the shower door open you were not able to exit the bathroom it was that small. In order to get in and out of the shower/bath you have to manoeuvre yourself out of a 1ft gap. There was a very concerning area in the bath that felt as if it could give way at any time. 

Location: Excellent! A ten minute or so walk from the Eiffel Tower with bus stops and the metro a short walk away. You also have a smaller supermarket and about 100 pharmacies in easy distance. Lots of great restaurants within the area too.

Summary: If you're travelling as a couple or solo and are looking for a cozy boutique hotel and being able to step out at any time to see the Eiffel Tower is worth the price tag, this might be a viable choice for you. 

For us, unfortunately, we felt the value for money was pretty dire.

title: Stupendous View of the Eiffel Tower

We found our room small but well-appointed, with a large balcony and a breathtaking view of the Eiffel Tower. We would definitely recommend the Hotel Duquesne Eiffel and its convenient location to the Eiffel Tower, the Rodin Museum, and the Invalides, all within easy walking distance.  And there are many excellent restaurants nearby as well.  Ask for Room 54, which however they can't promise, if you want the perfect view of the Eiffel Tower.

title: Great Location great price
text:
My wife and I stayed here mid November and were happy with our stay.

Although a little outside the entertainment areas, it was close enough to a metro station to hope on a train to wherever you wanted to go.  

We found the area safe and inclusive of what we needed, plenty of great restaurants and grocery stores to grab snacks and water.

The room was small but offered what we needed, the shower was also a little cramped but we made due.

The staff were nice and helpful for the most part, except for a little misunderstanding when booking a private transfer to the airport...but uber got us their instead.

The breakfast was a great way to start our long days of exploration and included cakes, cereal, teas and coffee and hot dishes - all buffet.

We didnt have much of a view from our room but wasnt a big deal as if you want to see the eiffel tower, just step outside the hotel's entrance. 

Would we stay here again? Totally!!! It is a great value in a great Paris neighbourhood.

title: Long Stay in Paris
text:
I had to stay 3 weeks in Paris and landed into this service appartment which turned out to be a nice surprise.

Conveniently located above the Italie2 mall where you can find a large Carefour grocery shopping, some restaurants and street market on alternate days for fresh fruits and veg! You can enjoy a local Parisian life! Chinatown is nearby if you want Chinese food, Gobelins and Latin district are not too far if you like to walk.

Helpful staff who provided me with an alternate WiFi so that I can connect my work PC.  They can also print your air or train ticket if needed (Kely was even proactively handing me my print out before I asked her).

Clean housekeeping and very disciplined staff who can arrange daily schedule if I need to use the room or ask permission to get in if the cleaning is not scheduled.

Table inside the room as small although long and slim. I had to move back and forth my work stuff if I need to use it for dining.

text:

title: Clean, comfortable, close to shops and the metro
text:
I stayed for 11 days in September/October this year. The metro is 2 minutes from the front door, and there is a large modern shopping centre next door with every thing you could need including a chocolate shop (Jeff de Bruges), a smaller version of Printemps (dept store) and a supermarket. 

My room overlooked the covered shopping mall but was still very quiet and noise was not a problem. You could open the window if you wanted, and then perhaps the noise level could change, but I guess most tourists are usually out during the day, and the a/c worked fine.

There are bistros and plenty of eating places (inc a Mcd’s, which I did not frequent!) in the square itself, including a good boulangerie/patisserie, there seemed to be plenty of locals around, and the square generally had a good ‘vibe’.

On the two saturdays I was there, the atmosphere did change however, due to protest marches by the ‘gilet jaune’ movement and the riot police were out in force, complete with shield helmets, etc. This was hardly the hotel’s fault I guess, the front door is accessible to guests only by access card, and once I worked out there was no particular immediate threat, it was quite interesting watching, from the 7th floor, the sheer numbers of people on the move! Never seen so many....

All traffic in the square stopped and all entrances/exits blocked bar one in and one out by police. Some locals on the street seemed to be watching from the margins too, so I figured, if they were still there, it probably wasn’t that unsafe!

There is a very good local market on sundays (and probably other days too), again minutes from the front door, with fresh cheese/meat/fish/veggies etc as well as pre-prepared cooked dishes which I took advantage of, having a microwave in the room.

2 things to note:
1. A slightly musty odour to the room which might bother some. You could always open the window I guess. It didn’t bother me.
2. There is an inventory of kitchen items in the room, which the kitchenette was supposed to have, and on checking, a few small things which were listed, were not supplied, including 2 drinking glasses/tumblers. No big deal, I just used the wine glasses provided, but when I raised this with reception, I was given a bit of a “Gallic” shrug, they did try to find me two but......no luck.
Generally, reception was helpful though, so no problems at all.

So all in all, a very comfortable, quiet place to stay, with everything on your door step in a non or certainly less touristy part of Paris, but still accessible easily by metro to where ever you might want to go.

I stayed in a standard studio.
I didnt try the breakfast, so can’t comment,  but at 13 euros, you might do better at the bistro across the road!

title: Great Location, Safe, Economical, and as Advertised
text:
I stayed at the Citadines Place D'Italie Paris for 14 days at the beginning of July 2019 and could not be more pleased. First of all, I arrived VERY early on the day I was to check in -- before 7AM -- but was able to check in immediately. This set the tone for the rest of my stay.

I had a studio room with a small but fully functional kitchen. The kitchen had an electric kettle, two burner stovetop, toaster, microwave, fridge, and dishwater. There is a large supermarket and a couple of smaller markets very close (5 minute walk). It was lovely to brew tea in the morning, make toast, and do some work at the desk before heading out to the workshop I was attending or the city sights.

The room, and especially the bathroom, was larger than I anticipated and very clean. And though the room's window opened up to a busy street, it was extremely quiet and secure. In short, it was exactly as advertised, and though obviously not brand new, well maintained.

Housekeeping is once a week. This was explained to me at check in, and it was provided as promised. I preferred this arrangement much more than someone coming into the room every day. Also, the hotel has a "comfort corner" off of the lobby where guests can obtain extra towels and toiletries if needed between housekeeping visits. The hotel offers guests more frequent housekeeping  (for an extra charge of, as I remember, 16 euros for a studio per housekeeping visit) if they so desire.

The location is about perfect, as it is a neighborhood and not the middle of the tourist-y areas. A Metro station is right across the street that is serviced by lines 6 (modified service until Sept 2019), 7, and 5. The trains run every 5 minutes. You can be in Central Paris in less than 15 minutes without transfers. 

The price is also right -- much less than I would have paid in a more tourist-y part of town.

Highly recommend staying here.

title: Good location but disappointing, run-down and dingy room
text:
The hotel is located on a roundabout right next to a shopping mall and metro station.  The mall has a grocery store in it where you can get everything you need.  The kitchen in the room is very handy and a nice size, well equipped.  There are several restaurants within a block or two and you are well situated to most popular tourist sites in Paris.  There is a (small) elevator and coffee available in the lobby.  The front desk is manned 24 hours a day.  They made arrangements for me to rent a pocket wifi which was handy, although I had to find a mail box to return it.  

The room itself is very disappointing.  When you walk in, the first impression is run-down.  There is one chair in the room and it looked like a cat had attacked it on the seat, with open scratch marks on the seat.  I used it to set my suitcase on.  The paint on the walls is dingy and had stains in and scratch marks in many places. (The stains were not cleaned before or while I was there for 2 weeks.)  The floor looks like very old fake wood, very faded and had a large round stain in the middle of the room.  

The bed was ok and had a fairly heavy duvet with no top sheet, which was too hot even in March because the air conditioning that they advertise they have was still in winter mode and would not cool the room.  They provided a fan after I called down for the air conditioning to be fixed the second time.  (I would not have booked here if I knew there was no air conditioning.)  The walls are not soundproof and I heard noises from adjoining rooms (scraping chairs along the floor, shutting doors, etc., but not voices.)

The bathroom is small but within a couple days you will figure out how to exit without bumping into the toilet.  The bathtub has mold around the bottom caulking and I never did figure out how to close the drain in order to take a bath.

The curtains are a heavy, plain off-white room darkening material, with a large brown smudge of something half-way up one of them.  This, again was not cleaned before or while I was there for 2 weeks.  They did do a good job of keeping the room dark.  The window opens but it is a fairly noisy place so I didn't leave it open at night.  The view straight across is of the rooftops of old buildings which was kind of interesting.  If you look to the right, you can watch the traffic in the roundabout which was also very interesting.  

The kitchen was a decent size, with a small fridge and dishwasher.  There was a small microwave, but the instructions in the room were for a different make/model entirely and I never did figure out exactly how it worked.  There was a 2 burner stovetop and sink.  There was a couple packets of dishwasher soap and pretty much everything you would need to prepare meals.

The night before I checked out, I called down to have them order a taxi in the morning and was told, just come down 15 mins early and they would order one then, which is what I did.  However, when I paid the taxi driver at the airport, he got quite upset because I paid him the $55 flat rate all the taxis charge to go from the left bank to the airport.  He said it cost $70 if the hotel calls and $55 if the customer calls direct.  He offered to get a policeman to explain this to me when I complained.  He said the hotel should have told me this.  (They didn't and I don't know if it's true or not, but he did seem to be sincere.)  

Overall I would not return to this hotel.  It is not as expensive as most hotels in Paris but with good reason.  The pictures on their website do not reflect the condition of the room I had.

title: Birthday Visit
text: I booked this hotel with a deal through Eurostar. I contacted the hotel a few days before we were due to arrive to check they had the family room ready as I had booked a room for one adult three youths and a baby. They had no record of our booking. Now I had paid £715 for this hotel and train and as you can imagine I was nattered. They said they would look into it which they did. They emailed again saying they had no record of our booking but had availability. What did that mean? That I have to pay again???  When we finally arrived they gave us a room. I had requested that we have a room where we could see the Eiffel Tower as we were coming for my would have been daughters 16th birthday and this was our first visit to Paris. My daughter was murdered in the terror attack on 22 May 2017. So you can imagine this was a very emotional and stressful time for me. I had emailed the hotel at the time of booking and asked for no special treatment just that we could have a room where we could see the tower. But that got ignored. No English channels on the tv other than the news. Every other language and the loads of different channels but no English. Not exactly welcoming. Rooms are nice and spacious.  But no one told us the sofa was a sofa bed and was made up already and just needed pulling out.  When we rang reception to ask we had to go downstairs and they changed our room which was mental as the next room was the same and we had to figure it out for ourselves. My parents asked for a twin room and got double so they also had to move rooms. Just what you want when you’ve been travelling on trains for eight hours. Cleaner came in while we were out and swept the floor and took the blanket out of the cot. Didn’t make the beds or anything.  Wouldn’t return really disappointed.

text: At first I was adamant to book this apartment hotel as I am now so familiar with this side of Paris. But due to time constraint I booked this anyhow. Alas, it gave me the surprise. title: my first visit to Paris, wow what a trip!  This was simply the best place to stay!
text:
So central! train station just outside the hotel, big shopping mall with everything including a supermarket right next to the hotel, and you could walk to anywhere from here if you can do the walking.  In the train corridors, there is always a busker whose music wafts through the train corridors making it sound like an Opera Catacomb - amazing!

This hotel, well the photos are exactly what the rooms are like.  The staff were very friendly and polite, couldn't do enough to help us with anything - cannot praise the staff enough.  Our room was immaculately clean, and very comfortable.  There was a safe in the room for us to use, and the room was nice and quiet with great blockout curtains.  Breakfast in the hotel (buffet all you can eat) was terrific and had regular food as much as a french breakfast type food.

I loved staying here, it gave me a great authentic French experience, the location made going anywhere easy, and the food places nearby were brilliant!  If you can't handle local food there is a MacDonalds within about 100 metres.

Our stay here was so great this is where i want to stay every time we come to Paris, which will be alot while we are on this side of the world.

Great hotel/apartments folks, keep up the superb work and i cannot praise this hotel highly enough - to top it off, the price we paid for out room simply could not be beaten by anywhere i am quite sure.

Oh, bath and shower in our room, as was a full small kitchenette so we could have cooked all our own meals if we wanted to.

They also stored our bags when we checked out, as we had about 5 hours until leaving for the airport.  Nice and secure.

text:
The location is good with easy access to the metro and buses.

This is my second time at this property and the staff at reception consistently provide poor service. 

I do not recommend this property.

title: NOT A HOTEL!
text: We stayed at this property in June 2018.  Please don't be fooled by the photos on the website, all the rooms vary in size.  We were placed in a tiny and stuffy room and staff indicated upon check in that the cleaning service would come once during our 10 day stay and would be timed during the middle of our stay as to maximize use.  However, the cleaning service rudely awoke us on the second day of our stay after repeated attempts to open the door that was clearly locked from the inside. title: Great Location but poor service
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my boyfriend during the dates of Friday 11th May – Monday 14th May.

POSITIVES:

The location of this hotel is perfect, there is a metro station right outside that takes no longer than 15/20 minutes to get you into central Paris. Good working and quick wifi and a free to use safe in the room.

NEGATIVES: 

Other than that I would say that was the only perks of staying at this hotel. Upon arrival our room was not ready for us to check in to even though we requested an early check in.

Our room was fine overall – we did not spend much time in it as we were out and about pretty much all day. But, not once over our weekend break did our room get cleaned or did our towels get changed bearing in mind we were out of the room every day at 9am (there was no excuse for it!).

We also had breakfast included in our stay – but if I am honest I would not bother. There is no choice at all accept cereal bread and croissants. The sausages were not fresh, I noticed a member of hotel staff taking some out of a package from the fridge and microwaving them before putting them out for the guests. We went to breakfast twice out of our 3 days and even that was a struggle in itself.

title: Tending towards the bland but with a few individual touches.
text:
We spent quite a long time researching 3* hotels in Paris for this trip, having stayed in several previously.  At this price bracket, in central (ish) Paris,   you can get good quality but not luxury and all hotels will have at least some flaws.  We weren’t in the Marais, but just a short walk away.
This hotel was very clean and well maintained -a bit corporate in feel,  but with more tasteful use of colour and a touch of the almost-stylish here and there.   Very comfortable beds (we had two different rooms) and high quality sheets.   The rooms weren’t spacious and storage was not generous,  but there was a suitcase rack in each room and the upgraded rooms have more space and had just about sufficient space to fit the yoga mat in.    Staff all friendly and helpful.
It’s on a busy street, so we didn’t open the windows at night on the front of the hotel.  Air conditioning worked well though.
Don’t bother with the breakfast (we didn’t have it but it looked just above basic) or expect much from the gym (just a few cardio machines).      No fridges in rooms or ice available from reception though they put a bottle in their fridge for us.   The electricity in the room goes off when you leave the room with your key (they only give you one) so you can’t charge batteries etc. when out.

title: Nice stay in Le Marais
text: I recently spent 24 hours in Paris after a European beach vacation and my friend highly recommended that I stay in the Le Marais district. From the reviews, I would have thought that this hotel was much different than what it wound up being. I had a perfectly pleasant experience, but it was not what I was expecting. I thought I was going to be in a trendy hotel in a lovely Paris neighborhood (much like a chic hotel in the Soho or Tribeca area of NYC or Covent Garden in London) and that was not the case. The staff was perfectly lovely and accommodating — they allowed me to check in an hour and a half early and they also helped me book my ticket to Museum D’Orsay so I could skip the line and didn’t have to buy a ticket there. However the hotel is a bit more dank than I thought it would be — I had an incredibly small room that almost made me claustrophobic. Had it been appointed better, I don’t think it would have bothered me as much, but because the aesthetic was really lacking and it was so small, it made the experience that much less appealing. The room felt very clean, but incredibly bare bones. (The night table was basically a tiny TV tray with hardly any surface area to place a book and a pair of glasses!) There was not even a luggage wrack to put a suitcase on (there would not have been space for one any way, as there was a closet with space for hanging clothes and shelves instead) and everything was a bit dated. There was also a shaggy dark carpet covering the whole room which seemed clean enough, but I much prefer hotels with hard wood floors so you can really assess the cleanliness. I was a bit skeeved out by the carpet and wore sandals the whole time to be safe. There was also absolutely no view and the elevator was so small only one person could fit in it comfortably. I asked the front desk for a bottle of water when I returned for the night after dinner, and they gladly gave me a lovely bottle of Evian, which I was charged for upon checkout. They considered it a mini bar purchase. For a hotel charging €250 per night, I think they should be able to accommodate their guests with a complimentary bottle of still water. It didn’t break the bank to buy the water, in my opinion it’s just a lack of courteous accommodation that I would have expected from a hotel in Le Marais. The breakfast was also not included — they charge €14 or €16 for the breakfast buffet. Again, not expensive by any means, but that is something that really could be included in the price. I decided to go to a lovely boulangerie around the corner for breakfast and that wound up being a great choice. Overall the experience was just fine for what I needed, as I was only there one night and spent 10 hours out and about sight-seeing, so I was only in the room to freshen up upon my arrival and sleep before heading out to CDG. (A half hour drive with no traffic.) Overall it was a perfectly fine experience, but there were certainly no frills and I felt like I was in a clean but dated Best Western of Paris. If you’re looking for something more elegant or trendy, this is not the place for you.

title: Average hotel in a great location
text:
We had very high hopes for our stay in Paris at Hotel Marais Hôme, however unfortunately a few things meant the stay in the hotel itself was in the end average. Firstly the first room we stayed in was very cramped and made it difficult to navigate around the room with 2 people staying. We paid for an upgrade for the remaining 2 nights and the room was much better in terms of size, but an AC system with no option for using it on fan only and only able to heat (winter mode) meant sleeping was a little uncomfortable. We also couldn’t leave the window open for air circulation because the main road was quite busy and therefore noisy.

The plus point was by far the location, with shopping, restaurants and attractions (Louvre, Picasso museum) all within either a 20 minute walk or 10 minute scooter from the hotel. If the hotel could do something with their AC system, I would give it 4 stars, if the rooms were a little bigger then 5!

title: Fair cost for excellent service, comfortable bed and location
text:
The front desk service was excellent, by all service providers at all hours of the day.
We took a room without breakfast but one of the days we went down to eat - the payment was fair (compared to the cafes around) and the food was satisfying.
The bed was very, very comfortable.

We were upgraded to a deluxe room and it was gratifying.
The location of the hotel is good, we got along well during the train strike.
The center of the lively Mara district can be reached  between 600 meters and a kilometer. We were also able to reach other tourist areas without a problem.

A number of things that are missing / problematic:
There was cold coming out of the window beside the bed - the cold was felt at night to those who slept on this side of the bed (the windows probably did not close well or were not well sealed).
There was no minibar in the room and it is a shame because there is a coffee machine but there is no where to store milk for those who want. And there were no tall glasses of coffee with milk.
The room was small (and this is also a deluxe room).
The hotel staff did not fill the bathtub soap (but we did not ask).

Overall very pleasant and reasonably priced hotel and service was really excellent

title: Simply lovely
text:
The Hotel Marais Home was a wonderful hotel experience. First is the location. Away from tourists, but close to a large metro stop (Republique), and within a short walk of a couple of others. The nearby Republique square is a lively spot, with plenty of restaurants and bakeries to enjoy. Most of the people in the area seemed to be locals, which makes this hotel centered on a truly authentic Parisian neighborhood. You wont find the large tourist attractions outside your door, but we had no problem traversing the city within minutes on the Metro. 

Second, the hotel itself is simply lovely. The modern decor wraps itself around the older brick interior of the building. The front desk staff, of which we saw at least four (maybe more) different employees working during the week, were very friendly. They all spoke English which is nice for those of us who lack advanced French. 

They have a beautiful little breakfast area. We encountered two different employees working the area during our stay, both were very nice. The food is pretty good, we ate there every day. There should be something for everyone for breakfast, from croissants and baguettes, to eggs, sausage, cereal, juice, and yogurts. The rooftop terrace was nice to check out, but we stayed up there only briefly. If you look up at night, and look closely, you will notice the spotlight from the Eiffel Tower passing by. 

Third, the room was modern and charming. We got a two level room with a spiral staircase. It is true that compared to American hotel rooms it is smaller. We liked it even more for that reason. Lack of space makes for a creative room. The bathroom was modern, the bed made for an amazing afternoon nap (after our redeye filght) with soft covers and pillows, and the tub on the upper level made for a relaxing cozy space. 

Do your trip a favor and stay here. It is not steps away from the tourist traps, but it is steps away from real Paris, and that is what we came to see.

title: Paris Trip 2019
text: We travel to Paris yearly and have stayed mostly on the 7th arr and central Marais area.  I must say this stay was very pleasant because of the professionalism of the staff.  I can only remember Xavier's name but all of them have been patient, helpful and knowledgeable.  The daily interaction, asking how our stay is and making sure everything was OK really made up for a few days residence at the Citadines Place d'Italie.  Hotel Marais Home is lcated <15 min walk from central Marais- Place de Voges, Picasso Museum, Holocaust Memorial, Breizh Cafe, you name it is within a comfortable walking distance.  No hills, just cobblestones so leave your stilettos at home. Two blocks away from the beautiful Place de la Republique,  cafes, restaurants and a couple of Metro stations are within stone's throw away.  The rooms are standard for Paris so don't expect a Vegas size space.  It may seem small to your average American traveller but it worked really well for my husband and I.  The staples are in the room including a Nespresso coffee maker, daily clean sheets, great air-conditioning (a must in the summer time), and a nice quiet space to chill after seeing Parisian sights.  Sadly, I forgot about the rooftop terrace.  Will definitely check it out when we return next year... And yes, we will go back to this place.  For the price, convenience, great reception staff, you cannot beat that.

text:
This is Paris, so an extremely small room in a relatively central hotel, wasn’t entirely unexpected, even for nearly €500 for 3 nights. It smelled distinctly stale on arrival. The bed and pillows were comfortable and clean.

The light in the shower began flickering if used for more than a few minutes - not good if you are epileptic! I reported it to the front desk but it wasn’t addressed during my stay.

The sink in the bathroom had a musty smell - perhaps due to the overflow being clogged and dirty.

The front desk wanted to charge me €10 for an adapter, but after a little coaxing, agreed to loan me one for my 3 nights, which I returned. 

Couldn’t find an English language tv channel. First 20 were all French and there was no guide in the room, so I gave up. 

There is a small kettle, with 2 tea bags and 2 mills. No coffee. Nothing was replenished during my stay.
