title: Filthy air filter in room made me sick 🤢  SHOCKING attitude of the staff when trying to resolve the issue
text:
Upon checking into my room I noticed the room had a funny stale smell so I reported it and they kindly moved me to a new room. The second room was better but after 3 days I could barely speak as my throat was closing up and I was coughing up all sorts of mucus which was grey (TMI I know) I tried turning the AC unit off and the air vent still would trickle air through and therefore I called the maintenance guy to come and fix it. What he found in the air vent was shocking!!!!! The air filter was filthy and for 3 nights I had been ingesting this filthy air causing me to get very sick. I immediately addressed it with the manager on duty and he moved me to a new room and straight away I could feel the difference as the air was CLEAN!!!! The manager on duty was not very accommodating in taking care of the charge for the first three nights and said that it was not his fault the air vent was dirty and was trying to make me feel as if I was at fault for not reporting this sooner!!!! I told him that in most countries they would be begging me NOT to sue them let alone give me a free room (only for the 3 nights) The manager said that we are in a France and we are NOT the rest of the world. His tone was very offensive and unacceptable for someone in Customer service. He went by the name of Romain. I am sure they went on to sell this filthy room to another customer and would not be surprised if there are several other rooms like this. 

Anyway. Just look at the picture of the air filter 🤬🤬🤬
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Amazing stay!
text:
Just returned from a night away in Paris staying at this hotel for my friends 40th birthdays. 
We were upgraded to a 2 floor suite. 
From start to finish all the staff were absolutely amazing and we couldn’t have wished for a better stay. 
It’s a few minutes walk to the metro making it easy to get around.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Perfect bedding only downfall breakfast in a box
text: Best night ever, bedding moulding to your body. Only downfall was room service breakfast! Breakfast in a box and item in there really not worth the price at all. Aside from poor breakfast the room was nice! I would come back but next time just have breakfast in the restaurant!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: The brunch is great for kids
text: The staff is really nice (Benjamin) and the magician who is doing the balloons is incredible. It is worth going on a rainy or cold day to occupy the kids :) The food is good, and the cakes with a theme also.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: nicest hotel lobby I have seen
text:
We have visited this hotel in the past; service has improved once again, but the most amazing achievement is the renovation of the hotel lobby. In this lobby, you feel wellcome to do whatever you like: play table tennis, have a drink in the attactive bar, do some computer work, ...  Guests seem to feel at home in this lobby.
The breakfast room can be busy at peak hours,  but staff is extremely friendly and busy.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Great service bar
text: In the bar at the Pullman is always a good atmosphere and great service. This evening I was served by Sandeep, who was very friendly and thoughtful. Even learned new French! As a regular guest the staff does great effort to remember you by name which adds to the experience.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Always one!
text: I visit Paris on a regular basis and this is the first time I have stopped at the Pullman in Bercy. For me and my family our stay was ruined by one member of staff who has no customer service skills at all. What made it worse was the fact we later found out she was the manager/supervisor of the cafe area in the foyer. She made us all feel uncomfortable and my wife felt intimidated. We came back to our hotel after a wondiful day in Paris to relax with lovely hot chocolate in our hotels cafe area (well this is what we thought we would do) on the way back we passed a lovely shop that sold different biscuits so we purchased some. Like you do in this wondiful city. On arrival at our hotel we sat down and ordered 6 hot chocolate just like the ones we had the night before. Whist we waited for our drinks we though we would try our recent purchase. Well what a mistake that was! The cafe manager sent one of her staff over to tell us off! Then she kept throwing dirty looks over our way every time she walked past. In the end I had to speak with the hotel manager who said we were more than welcome to relax and enjoy our purchase of a biscuit! Suprising our hot chocolate arrived late and was nothing like the one we had the night before. I would like to add the rest of the staff were amazing and it is such a shame they were let down by one individual.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Pullman at Bercy
text: Conveniently located to the Accor Arena at Bercy, the Pullman has comfortable and well equipped rooms. The breakfast buffet is excellent and I cannot speak highly enough of the catering staff who went to a great deal of trouble to provide for my various food allergies.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Lovely hotel, perfect for business or pleasure
text: Friendly staff and English speaking, breakfast was great and they had a wonderful cafe with an amazing wine selection. The hotel is very clean and modern and walking distance to non-touristy cafes and a small grocery.  The area seemed very safe and full of commuters and families.  A great way to see the everyday Paris.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Fabulous hotel
text:
We visited in October half-term (M-F) with our children aged 1 & 5. 

We arrived at 11am (3 hours early) but our room was ready for us!

The hotel has the wow-factor: very clean, lovely facilities, helpful staff, bar, restaurant & table tennis tables. The only problem was the swimming pool was closed (maybe for refurbishment). The free WiFi is easy to use and available in rooms, no need to keep logging in!

We requested a travel cot and when it arrived it was a a fully-assembled traditional wooden cot on wheels with bumpers, bedding, baby bath, changing mat and nappy bin. 

There are tea facilities in room and a fridge which is refilled with Evian water every day. We used the fridge to store milk and beers from the Carrefour shop in Bercy village. 

There are towels, flannels, robes and slippers in rooms!

Breakfast was perfect. Served from 6.30-10.00. All fresh and delicious. A wide variety of foods and drinks. 

We happened to stay at the same time as the Rolex Paris Tennis Masters so there were professional tennis players everywhere. There was a great atmosphere! The event was being held at the Accor Hotels Arena which is next-door!

Bercy Village is stumbling distance and has lovely bars and restaurants, open all day and into the evening.

Taxis are always available from hotel. It cost €20 to Luxembourg Gardens. €60 to CDG airport.

It would take 2 hours to walk to Eiffel Tower (5miles) but following the river, you can’t get lost! Batobus hop-on boat speeds up the journey. There is metro station in Bercy Village.

Can’t fault this hotel 😃
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Love this hotel.
text:
Stayed for the weekend with the girlfriend and i cant fault it! From the check in to how clean the room was given to us. i would be recommending this hotel to friends and family. The staff was very friendly and helpful. 
Thank you Pullman.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Bercy in October
text: It is a very good hotel. However, the person who checked us in said we had not pre-paid for our breakfasts for our 6 day stay. According to Dylan, the person who checked us out, we had indeed paid. But we lost all those breakfasts because we went to a small bakery in the morning to avoid the nearly 30 dollars per person that they charge for breakfasts,.When I wrote a complaint to the hotel, I was offered points through Accor. I accepted the offer but never heard back from the agent who made the offer. A very disappointing situation given the level of the hotel, our long stay and the fact that we had a suite. If you decide on the Pullman, be aware that the check-in is problematic. And if they insist you did not pay for something, be sure to keep all your records and receipts close at hand to prove you did.  If I hear back from the agent, I will follow up with another message to this site.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Very nice
text: Excellent hotel.  From the front desk to the restaurant, everyone is friendly and helpful.  Our room was exceptionally clean and spacious.  Very quiet, peaceful hallways which was nice for sleeping.  Stayed here for three nights before heading to Normandy, would book again.  The Metro is across the street which made access to the attractions easy.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: 10 out of 10
text:
Absolutely enjoyed everything about our three day break at the pullman.From the efficient welcoming reception to the spacious comfortable room. Immaculately clean toilets in room and reception.10 out of 10.
The Bercy village adjacent to the hotel with its numerous restaurants, shops and metrolink was very convenient, with the added bonus of security gaurds reassuringly making it feel safe and relaxing.
Nothing was too much trouble for all the reception staff from helping with sight seeing bookings to providing umbrellas on a rainy day and booking taxis, first class.
For 10 euros you can get a 24hr metro ticket which allows you to get to all the main Paris attractions within15 to 30mins of leaving the hotel.
The only down side is 3 days isn't nearly enough time to appreciate all that Paris has to offer, so we will be returning in the future. At the pullman of course.

Excellent hotel & wonderful loving staff which made hotel so enjoyable to stay at next to Bercy Village where you can experience the local activities among Persian & away from crazy tourists crowds... but my new friends from Pullman staff were certainly the heights and they made my trip much more enjoyable... Mehran

title: Sloppy and lazy in everything
text: At hotel for conference and seemed to have lost booking. Took an hour and half to check in - staff didn’t seem to care and required several reminders before checked in. Room was totally souless and without character. Fish and chips room service was v v poor. See pic. Basically fish fingers and cold chips with plastic cutlery for >€25.  Do not stay or eat here. However area around Bercy metro looks great with lots of bars and restaurants.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Great location and perfect service
text: My husband and I stayed here for two nights whilst on a longer trip in France and Italy. I booked via a secret deal so wasn't sure what to expect but I was blown away. The location is not central in Paris but the connection from main stations via the metro is easy and quick. If you don't know about Bercy village then check it out. The hotel is amongst restaurants and shops which was so convenient. The hotel itself is beautiful and the service is amazing. I booked two flights whilst there and staff printed out the boarding passes for me in an instant. Don't be put of by the distance from the centre. The metro ride is worth it.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Thank you for your kind hospitality and warm welcome!
text: Choosed Pullman when visiting Paris to celebrate a special occasion. The special welcome, the friendly and kind service at the reception, the beautiful and clean room with a magnificent view of skyline Paris, the symptous brakfast and the busy lobby bar...,all contributed to making our trip to Paris unforgetable. A big thank to all of you !
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: @oluwaferanmi
text:
The hotel was comfortable and all the staff very friendly and always available to help and advise. Lise was extremely kind right from our check in. She went above and beyond to sort out our botched booking and was kind enough to book our activities for the week. She facilitated sight seeing trips, restaurant and cabaret bookings and ensured we knew how and when to get to each location. 

Aurore was equally friendly and kind and was willing to answer all our questions and give directions. Hamid and Sandeep also helped to make our stay a pleasant one. 

The nearby Bercy Village down the road has exceedingly convenient shops and a plethora of restaurants which proved very useful. 

My husband and I would be quite happy to stay at the Pullman Bercy again and again.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: First class hotel in a lovely location
text: My sister and I enjoyed a very comfortable 3 night stay at the Pullman in Bercy.  Friendly and efficient check-in, spacious room with two double beds, excellent toiletries etc and efficient air conditioning (it was very hot outside!).  It is only 4 stops from Gare du Nord - change at Gare du Lyon so very accessible.  We spent our days in Central Paris and it was nice to spend the evening in Bercy Village where there are numerous shops, bars and restaurants within less than 5 minutes walk. The metro station is also in Bercy Village so again just 5 minutes walk from the hotel.  We stayed at the Pullman in 2011 and hope to return next year.  Excellent buffet breakfast with everything you could wish for!  There was a mix of leisure travellers, conference delegates and business travellers in the hotel and this worked well.  An excellent venue for a conference and I would guess much better value than in the city centre.  Highly recommended!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Modern comfortable hotel in superb area
text: The Pullman is a large modern hotel with everything you would expect from the brand. However, the clincher for this place is the nearby Bercy Village with chic restaurants, shops and a cinema. Close to Metro line 14 so everything going for it.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Seriously, Room is ready but I can’t check in!
text: Arrived after a red eye. Was told the room was ready, but I couldn’t check in till 3pm- unless I would pay $89 euros or he would be happy to upgrade me to a nicer room for $50euros/night and he would give me free early check in. I own a hostel in Central America if I did that to my customers I would be out of business. Would never recommend this hotel.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Nice but flawed
text:
My wife, daughter and I stopped here for two nights in August. 
This is a modern hotel with chic interior, and fantastic staff. 
The metro station is a very short walk away as is the funky Bercy village (shops and restaurants), which offers plenty of alternatives if you want to dine out locally.
Our room was smart and very clean with a very comfortable double bed. However our daughter's (less comfortable) fold-out bed did obstruct free movement, especially to the curtains and windows situated in the same corner of the room as that bed. 

When we checked in to our room we found the air-con was off, with the digital thermostat showing the room temperature at 27 deg C. We immediately adjusted it as low as we could, but when we checked out two days later it was still showing an, uncomfortable, 23 deg. C; the hotel management needs to ditch the bogus environmental agenda and give guests the facility to cool down. The double-glazed windows didn't help, their inability to significantly suppress street noise perhaps evidencing poor thermal resistance too. 

On the first night we were missing the towels etc. for the third occupant - we asked reception to correct this as we went out to dine, but it wasn't done. The chambermaid got it right the next day.

Breakfast was disappointing on both mornings. Coffee was served at the table from a single multiple choice dispensing machine (I would expect a proper coffee bar at this level) and was therefore watery and tasteless. The pastries were bland and stale - a poor imitation of those glorious croissants of old.

And then there is the parking! 78 Euros to park our car two nights. This is extortionate, regardless of whether the car is parked on the hotel's forecourt (as was ours) or whether it is parked in the hotel's "private" car par (which is, I gather, a reserved zone in the adjacent, public multi-storey car park). Had I had the forethought of using one of the parking apps on the internet I could have secured parking in the same multi-storey, for 60% of the price charged to me; still pricey but 40% less so - do your homework and avoid the rip-off.

On first encounter a lovely hotel, handy for transport, with great staff, in an enchanting area. However too many minus points; hot room, mediocre breakfast and nebulous and pricey parking arrangements.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Great Experience at The Pullman
text:
This is a Modern hotel just slightly outside the tourist areas of Paris. The Metro is located directly across the street from the hotel (5 min walk). Within 15 minutes or less, we could be in any tourist area of Paris via the Metro. We also took taxis to and from the city for around 20 Euros when desired. The Bercy Village shopping and dining complex is right next door to the hotel and is a picturesque outdoor venue with good restaurants and shopping options. 

The hotel staff was amazing!!!!! The Concierge, Hamid, worked persistently to help me resolve an expensive reservation I had missed. Everyone on staff was very professional. The bar and onsite restaurant were pleasant, and the breakfast Buffett was quite good. The rooms were clean and modern in style. The bathroom was similar in size to similar American chains. The hotel had an overall upscale feel full of modern touches. 

We really enjoyed our stay and will return soon!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Friendly Large Hotel
text:
Recently stayed at the Pullman Paris Percy, which is located just outside central Paris.(3 metro stops)
Even though the Hotel is extremely large the customer service that all staff show us on our three day visit was very personal and helpful. Rooms are of a high standard and the breakfast offerings was  of a high standard.

If I were staying in Paris again, I wouldn’t hesitate in booking once again at the Pullman Paris Bercy.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Amazing hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel in July 2019 and absolutely loved it. Once we checked in, we were upgraded to a duplex suite. The manager was kind enough to walk with us to our room and explain the various landmarks we were seeing from our room. The room was beautiful with an amazing view of the Notre Dame cathedral and the Siene river. The hotel is located very close to the Bercy village with lots of restaurants nearby. We loved the breakfast, staff was very helpful... We'll definitely stay at the Pullman - Bercy when we visit Paris again.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Great stay but far from City Center
text: We stayed at this hotel in July.  The rooms were bigger then I would have thought and 4 of us fit well with our luggage and my son sleeping on the floor (he prefers it to the bed).  The only bad thing about this hotel is if you want to be close to the city of Paris, this isn't it.  We would take the Metro every day into Paris, about 25 minutes depending on where you were going.  Metro was very convenient, across the street.  There was a nice outside village of restaurants, shops and movie theater across the street as well, so plenty of places of different places to eat from breakfast to dinner.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: An excellent base for a family break
text:
We stayed at the Pullman as a family of 5 in adjoining bedrooms for three nights. The rooms were spacious, comfortable (the bed in particular!)  and spotlessly clean. 
All the staff were very friendly and helpful. They helped us with advice on how to travel to Disneyland before we went and my daughter loved the free chupa chups lollies.
We were a bit disappointed that the pool was out of use and will be for the foreseeable future as it was such a hot weekend. But so much to see and do in Paris we didn't dwell on that for long! 
The area was absolutely perfect. We loved Bercy village and ate most of our meals there.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Wonderful stay at Pullman bercy
text:
It's our 2nd stay at the Pullman since the new opening. And it's always a pleasure to stay in this hotel. The staff is lovely, special mention to Benoît who give us a free upgrade in deluxe room.
Food is ok, room spacious and quiet.
The swimming pool was closed, we will have to wait until the end of the year.
Very good 4-star hotel in Paris.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Nothing special....
text:
Good location.... but the breakfast wasn’t special... scrambled eggs and bacon... poor and uncooked...
Room cozy and quiet... but non so clean...I found the toilet brushed full of....**** and the shower was clogged ...
Disgusting!

title: Amazing hotel and service
text: We are currently staying at the hotel. We checked in yesterday and it has been an amazing experience from the very moment we stepped in. We were greeted by the concierge - Aurore and she is a star! Our stay has been made special by the exceptional service of everyone. Fab hotel and the device is even better. Highly recommend.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Mr
text: We stay at June 26 for 3 nights at room 1008.  We booked the duplex suites. Please avoid this hotel during summer and fall and heat wave!!!! They do not have AC. They only have air cooling. And the air that coming out from the “AC” outlet is veryyyyyyyy little of air. When we stayed over there, there were a heatwave in europe, so we sleep in sweat and cannot sleep until 3 AM every single night!!!! They know it is a common problem so they have a fan to cooling down the room, which did not help at all. The hot water in the room is also a problem. It is only HOT water. No warm/cold water in the shower. Be carefull with this, can scald your skin!!! They just waiting a lawsuit happening to this hotel. We try to look for different hotel (avoiding accor hotel even though i have a platinum accor membership), it was hopeless because it is a high season of traveling in europe. So most hotel that accomodate family is fully booked. Next time, we will avoid all accor hotels in paris except during winter. Most of their hotel is ONLY have air cooling. Not Air conditioned!!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Lovely Location!
text: We stayed here for 3 days prior to a trip further North. Lovely location outside of Paris, close to the train and next to lovely Bercy Village and Park. Our server, Sandeep, was kind, friendly,  always smiling, and was more than happy to make sure we had drinks and snacks! Since our stay was during a terrible heat wave, having a refreshing cool drink outside or in the lobby was wonderful!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Excellent
text: Le personnel est souriant, content et serviable. C’est très agréable. Employees are relaxed and hard working and happy to serve and to help. It ‘makes A very pleasant change to many other hotels, especially parisien hotels and restaurants!
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Location Location Location !!!
text:
This is such a nice hotel , newly renovated in Pullman Bercy. Reasonable and very close to Saint Emillion which offers EXCELLENT connections to the center of the City where you will need to go everyday.
For Food, there is the Bercy Village and I loved the Restaurants there. Vapiano is great on the great. A Nice fresh live Pasta stations.
In the Hotel there is a pool and a spa. The food is not the best at the hotels restaurant you are better off eating at Bercy Walk.
The concierge Hamid was awesome in giving advices. He guided us to Montemarte which was not on the plan and it worked out very nice.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Pullman Bercy -UN GRAND MERCI
text: We chose this hotel for our trips to Paris and it was a first for us, since we had never stayed at a Pullman before. Our choice was smart, ultimately staying here was a pure joy. The feeling we had from the very entrance was that of a comfy, modern structure, inspiring vibe, good karma, awesome smell. The suite we were assigned left us speechless (located on the 10th floor and actually built on two levels). It was provided with basically everything you need (we compared it to Sofitel and Radisson we usually stay at) and it had the most amazing view! The location of the hotel is perfect, no surrounding street noise, the sleep quality was great, the spaces exceptionally clean and luminous. The breakfast selection was generous, everything you could think of in terms of morning appetite was actually there. Mr. Hamid, we kindly thank you for the upgrade on the occasion of our double anniversary and for going to so much trouble preparing our surprise, for the delicious chocolate cake and for the truly warm and professional welcome we had at the reception. Our appreciation also goes to Maria, your Romanian employee covering the night shift; she was extremely kind, professional and helpful. I truly recommend this hotel, for everything it offers, we will most definitely choose a Pullman again for our future trips. UN GRAND MERCI donc, à vous tous, c’était un réel plaisir de vous connaitre et d’être logé dans cet hôtel tout à fait nouvel et surprenant pour nous.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Super service
text: We stayed 2 nights at the duplex suite. And all I can say is that the way the staff treated us was beyond our expecations. Super friendly and service minded. The rooms was clean and spacious. Good for families. Not a typical familiy hotel but that I was aware of. The only drawback was that the pool was closed. But the staff aranged us a good deal that we were happy about. Highly recomended. Close to metro and good restaurants.

title: Good location, friendly staff
text:
Pullman Bercy is a good option for a central Paris stay.  Not over crowded and no too far from most of the main attractions.
I arrived early on the day of check in and opted for the 50 Euro early check in fee - it was worth it to recover from the 24 hours in the air.
The check in staff were very friendly.  I had been practicing my French, but it never comes out right when you need it the most - she was very understanding and patient as I "practiced" my French with her!
The food was OK.  Breakfast buffet was a bit repetitive, but was well prepared and tasty.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: Fantastic! - Road Trip With Family.
text: This was our first stop on a EU Road Trip from the UK, destined for Malaga and what a fantastic stop it was. Traveling with two young children for days on end in a car is not easy, so the evening stops are always very important. I had stayed in this hotel before on business and when I was looking for a Paris stopover, it seemed like a good opportunity to re-visit based on the hotels excellent location, parking facilities, nearby park and Metro stations. I could not find fault with anything. The staff were warm and welcoming and even coped brilliantly with my two young boys who were over-excited having only just been released from a 5 hour drive. The family room was excellent consisting of two double beds and brilliantly appointed bathroom with all the in-room creature comforts. My wife became particularly attached to the in-room Nespresso machine. Bercy Park next door was a great place for the kids to roam free and the Metro station gave us excellent access to the city centre for a lighting tour of the sights and attractions. In the evening the kids loved the swimming pool and breakfast the next day was superb, and really set us up nicely for our days driving to the Spanish border. Thank you Pullman, you were a great start to our holiday.
name: Pullman Paris Centre - Bercy

title: two nigths trip to Paris
text:
Main reason for our stay was to watch a show in the nearby Accor Arena…
I write this article as a Platinum member.
Arrival into Paris with our private car was fine. Parking at the hotel is very difficult, even just for check-in.
Only two check-in counters were available with a view people waiting.
When it was my turn, I presented my booking details as well as my platinum membership card.
No greetings as a loyal member was given, as well as no upgrade. Even for the welcome drink vouchers I had to ask at the end of check-in.
So the check-in experiences, compared with other Pullman hotels, was not so good.
Our room was a family room with two big beds. Nice and clean perfect for our stay.
I made my self a cup of tea, before we left for the show. After we came back we discovered, that the water kettle was spoilt and water was leaking all over the area. Spilling water on some of my documents and my mobile phone, luckily the phone was still working. The kettle was exchanged after we complained to the front desk, but when we returned to the room after dinner the next problem happened. Our room was without power. So I had to go back to the front desk, to ask for help again. We had to wait for 15 minutes till somebody came up to the room, just to check on some fuses, which caused the problem with the power fail.
Next morning we went for breakfast around 09:30, hopping to avoid the big Chinese’s travel groups, but unfortunately they were still there. So we had to wait for a table and it was very load. Once we had a table, we discovered, that a lot of breakfast stuff was not available. For example the complete tea section was out of stock, glasses were missing at the juice section and lots of food was not available. So the breakfast experience was not very pleasant and we were looking forward to it, because we read, that Pullman has one of the best breakfasts in town.
After my breakfast, I wanted to collect my tickets for a river cruise on the Sein, which I was included in my room package.
Unfortunately the tickets were not ready yet and I was ask to wait another 30 minutes, before the responsible person would arrive.
Of course I don’t wanted to wait again, so we left without the tickets and bought them latter on directly at the cruise company. At check-out we were reimbursed for the tickets and the room rate was reduced as well for one night to compensate the price different. This was nice of the hotel, but still I can’t believe a 4 star hotel can’t even handle a sim

title: DO NOT TRUST YOUR STAY WITH THIS OR ANY ACCOR HOTEL!
text:
The only reason this review gets any stars at all is for the sheer fact that the hotel was in a very accessible location to many bars, restaurants, and sites. The shared spaces for the hotel (lobby, restaurant, lounge) were relatively nice as well.

Here's where the zero star review would come in if it were possible:
For the price, our room was small and felt dirty. The carpet was visibly stained in quite a few areas and looked like it may not have been vacuumed thoroughly recently. The shower setup was lacking and it was impossible not to get water all over the bathroom floor when taking even a quick shower. One of the elevators consistently had issues taking either of our key cards to actually get it to move.

Much more concerning than the items I mentioned above, was the way one of the front desk staff handled a major problem that the hotel had created for us:

I thought my fiance had placed my passport in the hotel room safe, but the day before our flight out of Paris I noticed that it wasn't there. That's when we realized that we never got it back from the front desk clerk the night that we checked in. We immediately went down to the front desk, but when we asked the man working (on Monday June 27th 2022 between 11:30am-1pm) if he would please look around for it he seemed as though we were annoying him and that he could not be bothered to look. He specifically said, "we have no passports here". We urged him again to look and he opened one drawer, took a quick peek and assured us there was no passport. We felt the lack of respect from the front desk concierge when asked about the passport was completely unwarranted especially because at this time there was currently no one else at the desk to attend to.

Because he refused to help us, we had to spend the rest of our day going to multiple Paris police stations, then going to the US Embassy to get a replacement passport so I could fly to Dublin the next day and continue on our trip around the UK for the next few weeks.

This put an extreme damper on the end of our Paris trip and was unfortunate because we had to cancel our plans to spend our last day in Paris visiting the Palace of Versailles. Instead, we spent it running all over town, wasting the day, and spending 165 Euro’s on a replacement temporary passport + the cost of the Ubers to get to and from the police stations and Embassy. I will also have to incur the time/process of getting an actual replacement passport once back in the U.S.

Even more frustrating was that when we got back to the hotel late afternoon/early evening that day (Monday June 27th) the new front desk clerk recognized us immediately and said he had my passport at the front desk. It was in one of the drawers at the front desk…the same drawer that his colleague we asked earlier to check for the passport looked in half heartedly and said he didn’t have it.

I submitted a request to the hotel, Hôtel Mercure Paris Montmartre Sacré-Coeur Hotel, and hotel parent company, Accor, to tell them the issue and to ask them if they would at least cover the unnecessary replacement cost I incurred since it had been their fault my passport was "lost" in the first place. 

After I reached out respectfully to them twice and got nothing more than them questioning me why my passport was at the front desk and a "no" on helping cover my passport cost, I've been forced to leave this review due to their inaction. When again, the entire reason it was there was because their front desk employee forgot to give me my passport back upon checking in and then another refused to help us look for it.

After the way this situation was handled by one of the front desk staff as well as Marc Villeger, one of Accor's internal staff, I would urge you to not risk your stay with Hôtel Mercure Paris Montmartre Sacré-Coeur Hotel or any other Accor hotels and properties. It's unfortunate they would not admit their financial responsibility for their neglect.

title: Not as bad as others suggest.
text:
I am currently staying in the hotel and can offer no harsh criticism of it. 
The twin room on the 5th floor is spacious, clean and has 2 comfy beds. My only moan would be the pillows. Too soft for me but that’s a choice thing.

The hotel’s location is superb. Turn right from the hotel and you’re metres from the hustle & bustle of Place de Clichy with loads of shops, bars & restaurants and the Moulin Rouge area. 
Turn left, across the bridge and explore the Montmarte area which is absolutely fabulous. Quaint cafes, restaurants, bars and shops are all over this area on the rise to the Sacre Coeur Basilica. It’s an area you MUST explore.

title: Terrible for cleanliness
text:
After 10 wonderful days in France with my family, we decided to spend 2 nights in Paris on the way back home.

We wanted a hotel that would be easy to get to the A1 and close to Sacre Coeur so we booked Mecure in Montmatre Sacre Coeur. This was a mistake.

Their family room was booked so we got two double rooms, next to each other. However, the rooms were not up to the standards we expected.

1. There were pubic hairs and scalp hairs on the floors of the shower room and toilets of both rooms
2. There was urine on the floor in the toilet of both rooms
3. It was very clear that both toilets were not cleaned with a brush for a while
4. The beds were hard. If you like sleeping on the floor you would love their beds
5. Hair on the bed
6. The safe did not work in one of the rooms
7. The kettle didn’t work in one of the rooms
8. There was a crack on the floor in the shower
9. Blood on the wall
10. Stains on the carpet
11. Towels had a bad odour

In the toilet, there were pubic hairs and urine stains on the floor. There were also hairs on the floor in the shower room and more in the corners.

I called reception to tell them that the toilets and shower needed cleaning. The gentleman at reception said he cannot help me as there were no cleaners in the hotel at the time. He offered to change our room but that would mean as a family, we couldn’t stay in rooms next to each other. 

I was ready to leave this hotel, but they had taken full payment at check in and they had no manager on site on a Friday evening.

I was left with no choice but to clean it myself.  I asked for disinfectant wipes and gloves but I was offered a cleaning solution and towels to clean the toilet and floors. Yes, towels! Do the cleaners use the same towels they give to guests, to clean the toilets and floors? Although washed (or maybe not) the smell of the towels were horrible. 

In one of the shower rooms there was a red spot on the wall just where the towels were hung. I used a wet tissue to wipe it off and I’m certain this was blood.

The worse thing however, was the white smears of bodily fluid found on the underside of the throw on the bed and on the valance. 

I cannot recommend this hotel and most certainly not for families.

Glad we didn't include breakfast in our stay - can’t imagine the state of their kitchen. 

I have stayed in many Accor hotels before, when on holiday with my family and for business trips, but this one is by far the worse and I will never stay in another Mercure Hotel.

Moulin Rouge is closer to this hotel than Sacre Ceour. Perhaps it should be renamed “Mercure Montmarte Moulin Rouge”.

text:

We would definitely return to this hotel

title: Perfect stay in the most beautiful city
text:
Really shocked at reading some negative reviews about this hotel. We have just returned from a weekend in Paris and were blown away by the levels of service by the hotel staff - nothing was too much trouble. 

We travelled to Paris as a gift for my wife who turned 40 last month. Initially I emailed the hotel speaking to  the amazing Amandine Passicos about potentially doing something to help make my wife's stay special. When we arrived, we were delighted to find out that we had been given a voucher for welcome drinks in the bar, a Happy Birthday balloon, French chocolates and most importantly an upgrade to the Priveleged rooms with a stunning view of the Eiffel Tower. This started the weekend off perfectly for us. 

Regarding the hotel itself, the rooms were nice and big - free drinks which were replenished each day and large bed. The location of the hotel - albeit in an area that looked a little off - is absolutely perfect for a jaunt around the city with all major attractions being close by. Additionally it was within 10 minutes of Gare du Nord so getting too and from the Eurostar was straight forward by Uber. Breakfast was varied with plenty of choice and the bar food and drink were spot on also. 

All in all, we were delighted with our stay at the Mercure and would happily go again. Don't be swayed by the negative reviews and give this hotel a chance, it was perfect for us and we'd like to thank them for making our stay so special.

The stay in this hotel went from bad to worse. Decor is really nice but that was the only positive about it. The stay here cost us almost £600 for 3 nights and it is extremely disappointing to spend so much money on a place that is not worth it. This hotel really needs to re-think the staff that are representing the brand as it is clear from other reviews that service is a massive problem. 

We tried to file a formal complaint through the hotel company to be reimbursed but this is near impossible to do as the complaint route is not easy to go down which is clearly very convenient for the hotel. 

Worst experience in a hotel I’ve had. Ruined our whole time experiencing Paris. Will certainly not return!

title: A good three-star hotel
text:
A good three-star hotel located next to Montmartre and Sacre Coeur. The rooms are OK but need some upgrades.

I recommend this hotel based on the location; it has a reasonable walking distance to many essential places. But there's room for improvement in the overall quality compared to price.

title: If you are considering this hotel...
text: This is an excellent hotel. The room (superior double) was very nice and the bed was massive and very comfortable. The room was quiet and well sound proofed (we were on the 5th floor looking out onto the Rue Callaincourt). The room was air conditioned and with the window closed there was no street noise even the dreaded motorcycles/ scooters.  The room doors are designed not to slam - never heard a door slam (the curse of hotels) all the time we were there. The shower was excellent - powerful and hot. There was fridge in the room and a kettle so we could make Yorkshire tea (bring own tea bags of course).  The breakfast was brilliant; beans and egg and tomato and bacon and sausages in the hot buffet and tons of everything else including cold meats, fruit, croissants, pain au raisin etc etc. The location was excellent with lots of cafes bars and restaurants nearby. The Chinese restaurant in the road next to the hotel (Chez Feng - been there 32 years family owned) serves the best Chinese food I have ever tasted (ever ordered beef with black bean and been asked how you want the beef cooking?). We paid bugger all with a Eurostar deal and we were sorry to leave.

title: Very disappointing, not good value for the price
text: I was given a room that was the furthest possible from the elevator, with the only pluses being that it was mostly quiet, and the mattress was fine, although rather firm. The room layout was very awkward, with almost no space to move around. Fine, that’s not unusual for big city hotels. But it was also one of the most hideous hotel rooms I’ve ever stayed in, and I’ve traveled to over 40 countries on nearly every continent. Too many competing shades of red, with dark, muddy gray-brown walls and headboard. The carpeting was dark and ugly, and also worn and stained. The tub / shower was difficult to climb into, was exceedingly slippery, and of course, did not have an adequate enclosure or curtain, so ended up with water all over the floor. The toilet smelled bad, and water started leaking from the base of the toilet onto the floor. That happened during my last night, so I felt it was too much trouble to ask to change rooms. Did I mention cheap, thin towels? And all of the surfaces were quite dusty, and the safe was broken. To add insult to injury, I was treated very rudely by a young woman at the front desk at checkout. THEN I saw an additional charge of $111 to my credit card, although the full price had already been charged the day I booked. I was never notified about a security deposit during booking or check-in. I certainly hope that charge is reversed, or I will take away another point from my rating! This does not feel at all like a 4-star hotel, certainly not worth a price 50% higher than the 3-star Ibis next door.

title: Fantastic stay, would recommend
text:
Lovely surprise on arrival to have an upgrade to the top floor rooms! These superior rooms have complimentary soft drinks in the fridge (replenished daily), bathrobes and nespresso coffee. The rooms are really large for Paris too. The hotel staff are very helpful and the breakfast fresh and delicious, everything replenished quickly. We even had a complimentary birthday cocktail in the bar.
The hotel is perfectly located for Montmartre and the nearby bus stop goes directly to the Louvre. Moulin Rouge (amazing show) was just around the corner, without being right on top of the colourful sex shops!

Only niggle was the taxi booked from the hotel reception which we were told would be €15 at the most for Gare de Nord, but didn't mention the additional €7 reservation fee.

Otherwise, fabulous would definitely recommend and return!

title: Good Hotel but Beware!!!!
text: We just completed a stay at this hotel for one week.  All was well enough for what we paid, but the morning we checked out we found out that our car service had canceled our ride due to the ongoing transit strike.  We found out at the last minute and went to the front desk for help.  We understood that this was in no way the hotel’s fault, but they were quite unhelpful and dismissive of us.  One front desk worker simply said “It’s too complicated to get a taxi” and walked away. The other person behind the counter had some advice for us but this hotel is truly not equipped to help their guests especially while this strike is going on. ALSO, when we checked in using our Booking.com reservation, the female desk worker said we were not in the system and walked away.  Honestly, you’re better off paying 5 star prices and getting good service.  Although the rest of our stay was fine (the hotel has a nice design, great breakfast, basic but sufficient fitness center, and is definitely in a good location), we were ultimately disappointed with the service aspect of this  hotel and probably would not stay here again.

title: Nice but needs to be better maintained
text:
A lovely hotel in a perfect location. 10min taxi ride from Gare du Nord, near a metro station which takes you to the Opera Garnier area in 2 stops, close to lots of nice bars and restaurants. The hotel at first looks very good, it has recently been renovated however, some classic and superior rooms look half renovated and half not. Meaning: all new furniture, modern look to it but the bathroom is old/outdated and therefore looks dirty. Bathroom doors with holes in it and not enough closet space. We changed rooms, were placed in another superior room and this one was perfect (how it should be). Completely renovated, also new bathroom and enough closet space. The breakfast was perfect as well, lots of choice (also when on a diet). They have a direct line with the taxi service so a taxi can be arranged by the hotel. One note on the beds: they felt like wooden planks. 
Outside on the terrace they have cute little iglo’s in which you can sit and have drinks. 
Overall an ok experience, I would recommend the hotel just make sure you have a good room. Personally I like the Mercure Opera Garnier better.

title: Great hotel and base for Paris marathon 2019
text:
Stayed here for the 2nd time.

Checking in was smooth and the staff on the desk were very helpful.
We arrived Via taxi direct from CDG, a trauma; my wife left her bag containing passports, paperwork, purse in the taxi.
As soon as we knew this had happened the staff did everything to retrieve our belongings. 
I didn’t really have that much faith but low and behold the taxi guy came back about an hour and half later with the bag and all it’s contents. 
What a nice guy.
So thanks to the hotel staff and to this taxi driver / you’re honestly amazing.

Anyway rooms, as I’ve stayed on previous occasion I upgraded our room to a privileged  room on the top floor. Amazing views of Paris, nice size room and very comfortable.
Breakfast is a buffet type and had everything you need to fuel up and start the day.

Enjoyed this hotel.
Very reasonable price
Thanks 
Simon

title: Disapointing, would not go back
text:
I stay in hotels 40 weeks a year and this was by far the most disappointing hotel that I have stayed in. 
The positives are that it is in a good location, with plenty of good restaurants near by and the rooms are quite and reasonably clean. 
The negatives, the bed was so hard and the most uncomfortable I have ever slept on, the bash/shower was so narrow that I had to stand side ways in it and when sitting on the toilet if you leaned forward you banged your head on the door. The bedrooms are a reasonable size so I don't understand why the have skimped on the bathrooms. 
My rate included breakfast which was not too bad on the first two mornings but on my last morning the bacon and egg servers were empty and were only refilled as I was leaving twenty minutes later. I wanted to have a cup of tea but the hot water machine was broken, I did eventually find one that worked after asking three members of staff. 
A business colleague of mine was also staying at the hotel and he agreed with everything that I have stated above. 
To conclude, when checking out I was not asked how my stay was and I put this down to the number of complaints that they must receive.
I will not be staying there again.

title: Very modern, clean and nice, but sketchy area
text:
I was impressed with how modern this hotel is. The room was a decent size for Europe. I liked how the toilet was in its own little closet from the sink/shower. The shower did tend to spray water all over the tile floor, though, because it only had an artsy glass wall that didn't do a good job of blocking water. It wasn't super noisy. The breakfast was GREAT! Their croissants tasted freshly homemade and were delicious. They had tons of food choices, and the breakfast area was large and nice. The ONLY negative to this hotel is that the area seems a little sketchy... even one of the nearby shop owners told us to keep our bags and things close to our body and to watch out. But... I think a lot of Paris is like that, not just this area.

It's a very short walk to the subway station. We also walked to Moulin Rouge, and there are a lot of great restaurants and shops within a block. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: Paris 2019
text:
Mercure hotel 

We booked this hotel on the Eurostar website as a package with the train.  Having visited Paris regularly in the last 4 years we were pleasantly surprised by the room . The room was a very good size with a large firm bed, wet room, fridge and kettle. Looking out the window you get a view of the Sacre Coeur . Breakfast was fantastic  with both a continental selection and hot choice. Machines for tea and coffees.  Staff were very helpful and friendly.
The hotel is in walking distance of the Sacre Couer and Moulin Rouge and local shops and restaurants . Uber Taxi 🚕 to Champs Elyse was €9 in the day and the Eiffel Tower was €11 .  
We enjoyed a nice glass of wine in the bar and at €6.50 it was a very good price for Paris . 
Thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and will definitely look at stopping here again. 
Couldn’t understand the criticisms on Trip Advisor before we came as this hotel is fantastic compared to others in Paris in this price range .
Taxi from train station €9 to hotel

title: Awesome Service!
text: This hotel is perfectly located close to the Moulin Rouge, restaurants, the subway and the Open Tour hop-on bus stop. (Beware- its competitor, Big Bus, allows hopping off, but not hopping on at some of its Montmartre stops). There’s even an excellent small Chinese restaurant across a side street from the hotel. Although the hotel is not in central Paris, our very modern room even had a view of the Eiffel Tower. I especially cannot thank Bruna enough for making our Paris holiday so enjoyable. She and Melissa helped us find places, get tickets, arrange transportation, and made our stay very memorable. They both deserve the highest praise! Bruna even helped move us to a room closer to the elevator because my husband has trouble walking. She didn’t seem to have any days off during the whole week we were there, so if she isn’t the manager, she should be! I would highly recommend this hotel, and we hope to return in the future.

title: HELP!!!!!
text:
We have stayed at hotel several times but this is definitely the last time. We are in the 2nd night of a 3 night stay and the experience has been awful.

The staff have been spectacularly unhelpful, rude and dismissive. At check-in, the staff member's default response was to say 'No', even before we had finished asking a question. This was particularly annoying when we were giving her our name to allow us to check-in and she did not allow us to finish before saying 'no'! Another staff member's response to our concern about the harm the bed was causing was to say "what do you want me to do about it?" Management obviously have no interest in recruiting quality staff with good customer care skills. Perhaps the current crop of employees are cheaper and less skilled?

Our first room had a defective bed mechanism and we were moved to another room (822) after much insisting.

The second room's bed was so hard that we asked for a mattress topper to provide extra padding but 2 nights later we are still waiting despite several requests. When I woke up this morning, I could not stand straight due to back-ache and advised the hotel of this but there was still no solution offered to help.

When we stayed previously, we would spend an additional several hundred dollars with breakfasts and in the bar (champagne cocktails and snacks). This time, the appalling customer service has meant that we will not be spending one extra euro at this hotel. Not one. If only all customers would do the same, perhaps management would get the message.

Another issue is that this is so obviously not a 4* hotel. There are paper cups in the rooms, plastic glasses, no tea and no furniture at the bed-sides. Please note that we did book the best quality room the hotel offers.  

So, au revoir Mercure Hotels. We will not be staying with you again.

A final message to the management, please do not respond to this message with empty platitudes and a promise to do better next time. Please do better this time during our current stay if you are really serious about customer service. Otherwise, save your time and your comments for those who may believe them. And, if you are really concerned about providing a good customer experience, start with hiring competent staff!

title: Some good points, but some very bad
text:
The staff was friendly and helpful, but not as full of local knowledge as I would like given that they lack concierge service.  The location is great, being near the Pace de Clichy Metro and some bus lines as well as rue Lepic, where one can find a lot of nice restaurants.  The room us small, thought that is not unexpected, but the really brutal part was the bed and pillows. I ended my stay in Paris with a seriously bad back and I give the credit for this to the horrible bed, which also made sleep difficult.

On the plus side, we had a great view from the room and Steve, at reception, was especially nice and deserves a mention.  I know I'm jumping around here, but I also want to mention that the rooms are tired-looking, but clean and well kept up and the maid service was fine.  So all in all it's a nice enough hotel, but the bed and pillows were a serious problem.

title: Fantastic stay at this lovely hotel
text:
Hi. My daughter and I recently had a very enjoyable stay at the Mercure Montmartre, as a treat to celebrate her 18th birthday. On arrival there, we were given a room upgrade and a little present for daughter's 18th. This was hugely appreciated, and got our trip off to a really great start. The staff are very polite, courteous and helpful. Thanks in particular to Jordan for the very warm welcome, and for making our stay extra special!
The room was lovely and very clean. I loved all the little extra touches, like the high quality toiletries and coffee machine (which could also simply heat the water for tea, if coffee isn't your thing). There was also a fridge with complimentary refreshments, and perfect for keeping fresh milk, for said tea! The safe also came in very handy.
Wifi was excellent and never cut out, unlike many other hotels I've stayed at.
Bed was comfortable, thus ensuring a good night's sleep. The hotel was also lovely and quiet inside.
We loved the breakfast and the choice was good too; there was always plenty of food, providing you with the perfect start to a day's sightseeing.
The location is good, and the closest metro station (Place de Clichy) is a couple minutes' walk away. The area is more Pigalle than Montmartre (the Moulin Rouge is round the corner!), and as such is a bit sleazy at night, with all the sex shops. My teenage daughter wasn't a fan, but this was her first time in Paris, and I am well enough acquainted with it to know that it's perfectly safe. And the seediness is easily avoided, if like my daughter you have no wish to embrace it :) 
There is also plenty of places to eat and drink locally, plus a Monoprix supermarket on the main Street near the Moulin Rouge/Blanche metro station. Paris really is incredibly expensive these days, so I found it helped to be able to pack the odd picnic with fresh ingredients from the supermarket, or even just buy treats and bottles of water for the room.
I hope this review helps, and if you have already booked or are thinking of booking, please don't be put off by the more negative reviews. The hotel itself is beautiful and I wouldn't hesitate to return.

title: 5 stars, BUT......
text:
We have stayed many times at this hotel over the past 2 decades and are always more than satisfied, BUT, this time there was a broken shower in our room and repeated requests, to front desk staff and the floor manager over four days had the result of nothing being done to rectify  the problem. A plumber did call on the room, but said he would return the next morning  as he was unable to repair the fault. HE DID NOT RETURN, and the fault remained so for the rest of our stay. Luckily as we are expert bricoleurs and the fault was not insurmountable,we were able to sort the problem with a small length of string.
  Otherwise the stay was more than pleasant, the staff were more than courteous and in the main, helpful. The general public areas are clean and tidy. The Bar is good with an outside terrace, but a little pricey.
  Breakfast is something to behold, fantastic. Hot cooked food, unlimited hot drinks, cold buffets and breads make for a very wholesome start to the day.
  Even with the niggles at the start of this review, I have no hesitation of recommending this hotel.

title: A gem in the heart of Paris
text:
As a business traveller, I focus mainly on Tranquility, Price and Location. And these are the main reasons why I choose Hotel Eden while I am on a business trip in Paris.
Located on a quiet side of the 15th district of Paris, near the subway station Vaugirard,  Hotel Eden is at a 15 minute distance  of all the biggest Parisian  Hotspots : Exhibition center, Eiffel Tower, Montparnasse Tower, Saint Germain des Prés district, the main railway stations,...
Regarding dining options, the hotel doesn't offer any but is surrounded by all kind of restaurants, from the finest like the one opposite the hotel to the famous Parisian brasserie on the square nearby.
Last but not least, I always feel welcome thanks to the very professional and friendly staff.
I often use the salon downstairs as a functional workspace, sometimes even as a venue to meet my suppliers and the staff was always attentive to all the details to make those meetings as professional as possible.
Hotel Eden is a safe choice while looking for accommodation in Paris.

title: Perfect for sightseeing Paris
text:
We (2 adults and one child) had a pleasant stay there for 4 nights. It was comfortable enough for us, also the bathroom was adequate and not too small as others have stated here. In comparison to other feedbacks: we had one of the superior rooms which seems to be the only ones to suit 3 persons. The staff was very friendly in each situation, also during one morning were they forgot to announce before that due to a business event they had a shorter breakfast opening time. We had the choice to choose from the business breakfast which was the same as usual or to be served in our room. We had chosen the business breakfast and were interested of what was going on on the business event :-). The fitness room an sauna was quit nice. Breakfast really not bad with eggs, cold cuts and cheese; cereals and fresh fruits; different choices of coffee, milk and fruit juice. 
The hotel is located in a non touristic area of Paris but only 20 minutes to tour eifel by walk and 5 minutes to one of the metro stations (we used for our daily sight seeing only metro: fast and you can have a stop on all interesting locations). Also the restaurants nearby the hotel were perfect (see my reviews therefore; we tried four different and all were very good).
Thanks to the hotel staff.

title: Avoid
text:
This review is based on the overall booking process and customer service.

I booked a double via the hotel website for a good price but the booking was swiftly cancelled by the hotel with no explanation. I requested an explanation and finally was told they do not accept a certain credit card even though they state the opposite on their official website. Well fair enough but you should simply offer alternative payment option and apologise for the incorrect information on the website. You shouldn't simply unilaterally cancel any booking without valid grounds. That is simply bad and indifferent customer service.

The hotel didn't offer any alternative payment option at this point so I needed to send another inquiry and request to use another alternative payment method. They told me to either send them my card details or make another booking. No-one in one's right mind is going to email their card details so I made another booking. Here comes the best part, at this point they were requesting almost a double rate per night and refused to honor the previous booking rate which they unilaterally cancelled without valid gounds. They twice offered me a lower rate which was still considerably higher than the original one so I ended up cancelling my booking. 

I recommend you to avoid this hotel due to indifferent customer service and spineless reservation policy. There are plenty of similar or better options in the area and closer to city center where you'll find better service and won't risk your booking to be unilaterally cancelled by the hotel without valid grounds.

title: Eden=Scam
text:
Hotel is located about 2 blocks from the bus stop and 4 blocks from the train station. Rooms are clean, but very small, especially the room with the toilet in it. The small room with the toilet was located about 20 feet from the actual bathroom with the sink and shower. They do make it known that they charge an additional tax of 2.53 euros per person per night and 15 euros per person per day for a breakfast that is definitely not worth 15 euros.
 
What they don't advertise is that they scam guests when calling taxis or drinking coffee. There's a coffee machine but as soon as you press the button they ask for your room number to charge you for it unlike in the US, where coffee & breakfast is usually free.

Do not have the hotel call you a taxi. This is the biggest scam they have. A taxi from the right side of Paris (where the hotel is located) to Charles DeGaulle Airport is supposed to be 55 euros for up to 4 people and 4 euros extra for each additional person according to the established rate posted in all taxis and on-line. The hotel scam artist receptionist will say that they cannot find any taxis at the 55 euro rate even if you supply her with a business card from an honest taxi company. Then they will pretend to call another taxi company and start speaking in French, but since that taxi company is only 75 euros, that taxi company will not have any taxis available. Finally the scam artist receptionist proceeds to call the 85 euro taxi company, and all of a sudden that taxi is at the hotel's enterance 10 minutes early. When I questioned the 85 euro taxi driver he shows me a text that the hotel has an established rate with them. The hotel likewise points the finger at the taxi company, but I am 1000% certain the hotel is getting a monetary kickback from the taxi company in order to scam their hotel guests. Any hotel doing business in Paris for as long as Eden knows the established flat rate to airports and Eden is definitely not looking out for it's guests, and instead illicitly profiting from guests' lack of knowledge of French language and Paris taxi policies.

title: Hotel Eden Good Choice
text: We just completed a week long stay in Paris at Hotel Eden.  The hotel is small and in a not so touristy section of town...both of which I think are good things.  Nice modern lobby and shared spaces with nice little workout room as well.   The Vaugirard metro train station is 200 yards away and very accessible.  Numerous restaurants and grocery/utility stores are all within 1-3 blocks in any direction.  Eiffel Tower is closest main attraction maybe a 20-25 min walk at good pace but easy to access via metro train.  The hotel is really quite nice.  We stayed in a Superior Triple room (had 3 adult travelers) and had no issues related to space or cleanliness.  Room was very modern, clean and sufficiently large for us.  Great bath area with huge shower.  Toilet room is separate and small but who cares.  Bedroom is separate room with private door from toilet and bath and had great comfortable king bed with separate twin/pullout which was very good sized and comfortable.  Decent amount of closet space and a small balcony to get some fresh air.  We did not eat at the hotel so I won't rate the food.  Breakfast was available for like 15eur PP which isn't too bad for a big city hotel but there are far cheaper options just steps out the door and we took those options.  Room service was timely each day and did great job.  Front desk staff were kind and spoke very good English (we are American) and made us feel comfortable.  Our only issue was the air conditioning.  We are American southerners who like to feel cool when we sleep.  To be clear the hotel absolutely has A/C.  You can set the thermostat to a maximum low setting of 20C which is about 70F.  That would be fine except the A/C just can't match that output under heavy hot conditions.  Weather was around 90F each day so we were careful to keep the room dark.  Also on our own we purchased a throw away small fan ($20 at local store like Target .5mile from hotel) and plugged it in to supplement the AC.  Once we did and being careful to keep the room dark and the bedroom door closed we were fine at night but surely not as cool as we normally would be.  I suspect this is very normal AC functionality so if you expect arctic cold hotel rooms in Europe during hot weather you probably won't get it anywhere in this price range.  But we bought the fan and left it there and was money well spent.  That was really the only minor negative for the hotel.  Overall great stay and very reasonable rate for a triple so would surely consider staying there again if we ever go back.  If had been cool months would probably have given full 5 rating without hesitating!

title: Staff make wonders
text:
Really nice hotel staffs: Olga, Mohamed, Manager, tall guy with moustache, and 2 breakfast ladies: Nacira and Alexandria.

English speaking, friendly and warm, can engage in small talk. Some even
taught me French language, ;D
Made me feel at ease, relaxed, and Special. :)

Housekeeping is attentive to your needs too, they clean up when i am 
out, and did not disturb me at all. Changes towels and tidies up everyday.

Hotel is near Metro (Vaugirard) and Carrefour and Leaderprix (cheaper, 
smaller), supermarkets are nearby. Downstairs next door a boulangerie sells bread and pastries and nearby 
have a few too..bus stop is not far, 2 left turns from hotel and walk til u see Matsuyama, a jap restaurant, 
bus stops visible from there.

Can see Effiel tower from hotel, walking there takes 25mins if u able to navigate well with google maps..otherwise, just take bus 80, or u end up getting lost for nearly 2 hours like me..:(

Expo is 2 metro stops away. Must enter from right direction, ticket cannot be re-used once u exit station.

Kettle and hot water (eau chaud) available at Lobby. May have calcium (white flakes) in kettle water, normal for france..(I didn know then..haha)

Toilet is separated from Bathroom, a
cubicle by itself. Big size ppl will have difficulty but ok for me. 
 
Breakfast (additional charge) is a good spread, with crossiants, Pain au chocolat,baguettes, white bread, cheese, ham, jams and spreads..my favourites were the fruit puree, honey spread, and EGGs (cook by
yourself, experiment with the time and have fun exploring the doneness of each egg!). fresh fruits like
bananas, apples, kiwis, grapefruit. 
Coffee dispensor and tea bags. 

Just be careful not to go out after 10pm, can hear drunk people speaking loudly, especially more during weekends. 

Overall, I will return to this hotel again if i have a chance to come back to Paris, because it is filled with warm people. 😊

Thank you for making me feel comfortable here. :)

Regards,
Ker Sin

title: Beautiful Hotel, Great Neighborhood, Awesome Staff
text:
My parents and I stayed in one room (City of Love with your parents... why not?) and had the time of our lives. Highly, highly recommend.  We'll return soon... merci!

title: Hotel Eden
text: Just arrived back from a four day stay in Paris in hotel Eden. Absolutely loved this hotel. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We stayed in the superior room which was quite small but so luxurious. However, as we were out for most of the days the room size didn't matter. The hotel is located in a perfect spot. It is nice and quiet away from the crazy tourist spots however you're just 2km from the Eiffel Tower. There is a metro 2 mins up the road from the hotel which was great. I'd advise anyone travelling to Paris to purchase a Navigo pass before they go for the metro, it saves you having to have change constantly for your ticket. There is a Carrefore shop beside the metro which is so handy for drinks and food, rather than paying a fortune for a bottle of water near the tourist spots!! We didn't opt in for the breakfast in the hotel as it was €14pp. We got pastries and coffees in the bakeries nearby for less than €10. Unless you're looking to spend a fortune on food avoid the tourist spots for dinner. We paid €16 for two glasses on Fanta one day. There are a load of lovely restaurants if you get off the metro at Convention which are reasonably priced. Overall had an amazing stay in Paris, I would recommend hotel Eden to everyone and hope to go back soon.

title: Great Location and Quiet
text:
My wife and I stayed here for two nights and *when* we return to Paris, this is the place we'll be staying again!
A two minute walk to the Metro, you can see the Eiffel Tower when you walk a few yards away from the entrance, lovely bars and restaurants nearby - you just can't go wrong.
It was quiet there, the staff were extremely friendly and helpful.
The room was quite small but that doesn't matter. We stayed in a superior room with a lovely walk-in shower, a separate toilet, a safe, mini bar and hair dryer.

We only had the breakfast one morning at a cost of €14 each which was a little steep but we had to leave early to get to CDG. We went to 'Frenchie To Go' the other morning which is also worth looking up.

Cost for a taxi from the Arc de Triomphe to the hotel, 10:30 at night was €12,50, a 10 minute ride.

All-in-all, you can't go wrong here, if you're looking for a room in a great location (about a 25 minute walk to the ET) in a quiet(ish) area, great transport links, this is THE place for you!

title: Great Customer Service
text:
AlthoughI unfortunately was unable to stay in this hotel, I DID experience their excellent customer service.
Our initial booking was made in 2019, for March of 2020.  We all know what happened then!  I had a non cancelable reservation, but the Novotel graciously extended the reservation until the end of 2022.  In October of 2021, we made our planned trip to Morocco, but decided against our intended stop over in Paris, because we wanted to limit our exposure to covid, so got a direct flight to Casablanca instead.  Again, the hotel kindly extended our reservation to the end of 2022, so I intended to visit Paris in October of 2022.  Unfortunately, my husband was diagnosed with a serious illness that needed immediate attention.  The hotel initially extended our credit to March of 2023, but when I gave them more details, Lorena very kindly refunded our payment.

I hope that we will eventually be able to visit Paris, and when we do, we will definitely stay at this fine hotel.
name: Novotel Paris Les Halles

title: Great hotel in a well placed location
text:
The Novotel Paris Les Halles is located just above the Metro station and in front of the big Westfield mall.
The room I got was spacious, clean and well maintained. The hotel is eco friendly which means it tries to use recycled materials and to narrow down plastics use (even the keycards are wooden). The breakfast is reach and tasty and the staff is smiling and helpful. I'd recommend this hotel for anyone that wants to stay in Paris.
name: Novotel Paris Les Halles

title: Why is this hotel 4-star rated again?
text: Not a bad hotel in any sense, just disappointing considering its 4 star status. The location is strong with lots of restaurants right outside the front door as well as a train station. The rooms are a good size, which was surprisingly delightful. The bed was comfortable and the cleaning staff refreshed our room daily. All good. My disappointment was in the overall ambiance and atmosphere of the place. The front desk staff seemed distant and unwelcoming. The hotel was dark and dreary and showing its age. Little imperfections here and there in need of some TLC that have been ignored. These things count. No shampoo, or lotion etc in the rooms. No washcloths available for people who use them. All hotels should have Chromecast capabilities as we approach 2023 as well. As I said, this is a perfectly fine hotel, it just isn't a higher end hotel in my opinion. There's a certain je ne sais quoi you expect at 4 and 5 star hotels that you won't get here unfortunately. Decent spot, but vastly overrated.
name: Novotel Paris Les Halles

title: Perfect
text: Central place, close to the Metro and the RER, nice surroundings, good rooms and comfortable beds for all family, friendly staff and a very nice breakfast. I would like to come back if I go to Paris again.

title: Memorable stay
text:
We recently stayed at Novotel Paris Les Halles with my parents for 5 nights.  The location of the hotel is super convenient.  The Metro station is door steps away.  There are so many restaurants and bars nearby and it is right next to a Westfield shopping centre.  The Louvre and the Seine is only a few minutes’ walk.  The hotel has good facilities and breakfast is terrific. The staff are very friendly.  Everyone at the front desk is super nice, helpful and supportive.  My mother was injured during our trip to Europe and she was in wheelchair.  When we checked in, my mum didn’t come to the front desk.  Before going up to the room, Lada noticed my mum’s situation, she straight away found a different room which right next to the lift for my parents.  Lada enquired about my mum’s health every time she saw me, and helped my mum to call a doctor.  The host lady at breakfast (I forgot her name) was very caring and attentive.  She arranged a sitting close to the breakfast restaurant and help my father to deliver the food to my mum so she didn’t need to walk the stairs.

On the day we left, we need to catch the train to Amsterdam.  Due to Tour de France, there was no taxi.  With my mum in the wheelchair, and many luggage, we couldn’t travel through the metro by ourselves.  Careen and the other gentleman at Reception tried their best to help us.  Paolo also sent us to Gare du Nord.  On the way, he helped with our luggage, managed to prevent us being pocket lifted.  At the train station, he also helped us to liaise with the staff to arrange the accessible services for my mum.

All in all, we have a memorable stay at Novotel Paris Les Halles.  I can’t thank enough to everyone who helped us during our stay.   I highly recommend the hotel, and we will definitely stay again next time we are in Paris.
name: Novotel Paris Les Halles

title: Great stay…amazing location!
text: I do kit is usually write reviews, but with this hotel stay I had to. We stayed here 3 nights as part of a multi-city UK/Fran e family trip with our 2 kids this past June. First off, the location of this hotel is absolutely perfect. It was our first time in Paris and the access to one of the main metro stations was key…it is right out front from the lobby doors. From this location we east went to  Montemarte and the Eiffel Tower area via metro. It is also within walking distance of St Germaine district and the Louvre. Do yourself a favor and get the breakfast buffet. It was very well appointed and had great food…we ate there every morning as it opens at 7:00. The rooms are super clean and quite spacious with the sofa bed up. By the way, the bed and even the sofa bed are very comfortable. The bathrooms are modern and overhead waterfall-type shower heads are a nice touch after a day of Paris sites. The staff was SUPER friendly and helpful with directions and even let us use their house phone to call the airlines as the airline lost a piece of luggage. They let me use the house phone for over 30 minutes…that would have cost me a fortune on my international cellular plan. The only drawback is that the bottled waters are not free, but no big deal. There is a nice little bar/restaurant right outside the lobby doors that is open late and we would get to-go drinks to take up to the room when we needed refreshments. If we ever go to Paris again, we will DEFINITELY stay here!  Great stay!!
