name: Au Manoir Saint Germain Des Pres

title: Lovely hotel fantastic friendly staff
text:
What a great find this hotel is fab location easy to get around Paris from.
Great breakfast and the staff are super friendly and speak very good English thanks Eric for looking after us and booking our taxi to the airport we would definitely recommend Hotel du theatre if you are planning a break in Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Average but many old dirt of cigarettes at the ground and the plants on the space of my terasse !
text: Old Cigarettes on the Terasse and they said they couldnt handle it because of the neighbours ?! Very little Room for Breakfirst. They cleaned the tables with an intensiv and stinky sanitair-Spray while people was eating there. To many little tables for a little room. No space for an realxed STart in the day.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: The Place to be in Paris
text: Ideal place to start every visit. From musea to parcs, historical places and just the 'village' arround Parc Manceau. A ritch choice in restaurants and brasserie. Very friendly familiy-like hotel with a tipical breakfast.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Comfortable stay in the heart of Paris
text: Not far away from Moulin Rouge and the Triumph Arc, very close to Metro, food market, caffes, bistros and restaurants. Rooms are cosy and clean, stuff friendly and helpful, croissant fresh and crispy!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Small but beautiful!
text:
The hotel is in queiet street. You are like in theter. People are friendly and helpful. Room is not big but original and very clean.
We are very satisfied and we recommend it. 
Truda & Peter 
PS. TV just in franch . Will be good some another language
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: A excellent hotel!!
text: The hotel was almost perfect; all the crew are so amazing, the rooms are very cleans and the breakfast is awesome. Very very good hotel, in the heart of Paris, and im sure im going back to stayu here.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Good value
text:
The rooms are small but clean, the location is very nice, close to Rome metro station. The staff is very polite and helpful.
Breakfast is better before 9 a.m., after that you less variety.
Bthroom was also a bit small, but sufficient foa a few days stay.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Paris trip
text: Went to this hotel whilst in Paris, location is really good! Rooms were perfect and they have a breakfast option. The best thing is the staff! They are really friendly and knowledgeable! One person recommended a place to eat fondue and raclette and we ended up going there 2 times. Would defo go back 👍👍👍
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Cozy and good location
text:
it's not new or fancy and I would it's too expensive. But I felt very comfortable in there, also staff was extra nice. 
Good location, so You cant reach Moulin Rouge in 10 minutes by walk, also Montmartre is close. Many nice bars and cafes around.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Excellent welcome and stay
text: Excellent little hotel in Paris. Good value for money given Paris prices. Very welcoming and helpful staff. Rooms a little small and could do with more storage space for clothes.However very clean and comfortable. Breakfast excellent.. Location in untouristy area with a number of restaurants in close proximity. Transport links good
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: A nice stay
text: It was very pleasant to stay this place. Great welcome by cyril, I recomand you the full and healthy breakfast, quite cheap for the amount of food. Great staff, English spoken and really helpful. We definitely would come back there.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Far better value hotels elsehwere...
text:
Very basic room. Booked it as it was located round the corner from friends that we were visiting. We will certainly be looking elsewhere for our next stay as you can get far more for your money. 

Upon arrival the first thing we noticed was an iron burn on the carpet before immediately discovering that both the bathroom door and toilet seat were broken. Rooms were very noisy with no soundproofing and windows that opened up onto the road. 

Despite this I must credit the staff who were very friendly and welcoming - although be warned that there is no receptionist present at later hours and we were locked out of the building!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Nice beds, central and quiet
text:
We were welcomed by the nicest receptionist ever. He was smiling so much it made us instantly happy. All staff was helpful. Bathrooms are very spacious and clean. The rooms are small but the beds are very comfortable.
Breakfast is the same every day. It's quite basic but you can have eggs, there is one type of cheese, different cornflakes, yoghurt,...
There is no airconditioning in the hotel, which makes the nights quite hot. You get a fan if you ask for it, but for me, it didn't get all the heat out as much as I wanted. Luckily there was also water provided.
Location is very central and the metro station is only 2 minutes away
All in all a good experience in a nice, small hotel with great staff and excellent location.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great customer service!
text:
We were a group of eight coming from Scotland, US, and Canada. We were met and guided by these 3 wonderful gentlemen namely Djebrane, Alexandre and Eric. They were very helpful, kind, and funny! Thanks to you gentlemen!

The rooms we occupied were a little bit small but it was clean especially the bathroom! Overall, we were happy with this hotel.
We will be back!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great little hotel for a city break
text: A nice wee place with incredibly friendly service. My wife was unfortunately ill for the weekend and they let us stay in the room until our train was departing later at night completely free of charge. Rooms have all the basics for a weekend of sight seeing, breakfast is varied, and staff are just delightful. Villiers is a lovely area with a great Sunday market and lots of little local cafes and restaurants, plus it’s very easy to get to Gare to Nord and more touristy areas on the metro.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Super nice
text: Disappointed with: Small elevators (fits 3 adults only). No kettle! They expect you to use the coffeemaker in the lobby (imagine late-nights) or use the hotel's kettle which is soo dirty!! Rooms are not soundproof. Flimsy TV wiring. Room keys are heavy (and you can't bring with you when you go out). Obnoxious British front desk guy. Happy with: Location (near to everything, bus no. 30, grocery stores, restaurants, sunday market). Clean bathrooms. Great housekeeping. Very friendly staff (except the British man).
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great hotel. Highly recommended
text: Accueil exceptionnel. Hotel très propre et très bien entretenu. Très central. Res des theatres. Amazing service. Great location. Nice rooms. Very charming place. Even the small rooms are very comfortable.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Paris weekend
text:
One night stay, & found it to be good value, no frills,small but tidy, clean & friendly. Breakfast was ok,plenty on offer,no full English breakfast on offer.
Would use again for short breaks, good location .5 minute walk from subway.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: a touch of france
text: stayed at the hotel in sept for our 17th wedding anniversary as part of an EasyJet city break,located within a few miniutes walk to Roma metro station and so easy to get everywhere from. typical small hotel with nice rooms and bathrooms pleasant staff and really good sleep quality, and a very good buffet continental breakfast a pleasure to give a good review to.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great stay in Paris
text:
We went to Paris and really enjoyed our stay at this hotel!
Great location in Paris center, lovely room and nice reception team who arranged easily our shuttle to the airport
I recommend Hotel du theatre for sure !
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Another fabulous stay at Hotel du Theatre
text: This hotel is our "must go to stay"  hotel in Paris - every time we visit we are never disappointed - everything is perfect for a stay in Paris - the hotel is near metro stations and is in an ideal position to explore the city and its atttractions from. The room and bathroom are clean and the beds very comfortable. The hotel is very quaint in a good way - and the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. Loads of recommendations for restaurants, places to visit and how to get there. Definitely recommend the Hotel du Theatre and we will be back very soon.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Perfectly adequate
text: If you get a good deal under $110 Euros its worth it -- rooms are small but nicely appointed and it is quiet -- in a great location but on a weird street -- sometimes the Uber and Cab drivers cannot get to the hotel -- area is great overall but the street this hotel is on is just plain dead and kind of scary if walking alone -- staff is friendly and helpful.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: All perfect
text:
rapport qualitè / prix excellent
breakfast complete and very nice 
staff is really nice nice and preparated 
hotel was really next to Rome Metro station just 2 minutes walking 
hotel was clean and comlpete with all accessories
Raccomanded
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great french hotel
text: Very quaint well kept hotel, in a classic old french building. Within ten minute walking distance to 2 metro stations which helps. Also near a lot of cafés and restaurants. Free breakfast is plenty to fill up on for us non europeans.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Not good and also Overpriced
text: This hotel is located in a calm area, but it doesn't have many exciting things happening close to it. The tv wasn't working and the wifi was pretty bad. The elevator also wasn't working so I had to use the stairs. The breakfast wasn't worth it and it didn't have many choices. Plus, you had to pay extra for it. The confort in the room was just okay and the heater wasn't good. Can't imagine staying in this hotel during winter with no heater. The people from reception seemed moody. Sometimes they were pretty nice, but other times they barely look in your face. For the same price you can stay in a better place. I wouldn't come back to this hotel and wouldn't recommend to anyone that I know.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Good Boutique Hotel
text: If you are on a budget this is a very good option. The rooms are small (like all Parisian hotels) and clean with renovated bathrooms. The staff was by and large friendly and helpful. All in all, a solid home base if you are planning to be out all day
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Nice hotel with good transport links
text: Booked the hotel for a 4 night stay. Reception is nice and inviting and all of the concierges we dealt with were very helpful and spoke good English which helped as I can't speak a word of French. I had travel passes for the metro and RER delivered here before my stay and they were happy to take them in and I as given them upon arrival. The room was a respectable size with a nice modern bathroom which was clean. Is midway between two metro stations with good links around the city. A few minutes walk there are a range of bars and a nice market. The WiFi was decent but at night when a lot of people were trying to access it pages would take ages to load. The TV was all in French but that's to be expected plus in a city like Paris you probably shouldn't spend a lot of time watching TV. Breakfast was nice with a small selection of continental treats and set us up nicely for the day. A large spread in an establishment of this size would be unreasonable. Only real complaint is that air conditioning would be welcome as the fan in the room did make me feel quite blocked up with a cold. Overall a lovely hotel that I would recommend to friends and family
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Strongly recomend
text: A really nice hotel, friendly staff who is more than willing to help with any information you might think of, fluent speakers of French, English, Italian, Spanish, Romanian, German etc., delicious breakfast, quite close to the subway. A wonderful experience. Would come back anytime 😊
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great atmosphere at budget price
text:
We had a great time staying at Hotel du Theatre. The ambience is great and this hotel will give you anything you need for comfortable stay. Breakfast on offer is very generous (croissant, chocolate croissant and other pastries, yoghurt, fruit, sandwiches, some meats, jam. Coffee, tea, milk, orange juice and more.  Very nice little basement for breakfast. The room was small, but clean and complete. The hosts are helpful. The only comment I have is that we had booked a double bedroom, but we got a twin (with the beds pushed together).

The hotel is very close to one of the many and very popular "Velib" bike self rental stations. Also close to the subway which takes you to anywhere in the city fast. We used it often.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: what a style and what a comfort
text: style, comfort, affordable this hotel has excactly what you need, its modern, the staff is more than helpfull and the try to do the best they can ! it's not easy when you go abroad and dont speak the language very well
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Little hidden hotel
text:
First thing you will notice on hotel board is 3 stars. But this hotel definitely does not seems to be 3 star property
Pros:
> Metro connectivity good. This hotel exact in between rome and villiers station. So you can go to any station. 
> Once you arrive, they will help you with Paris map and provide information for various site seeing place. 
> Staff is really helpful and attentive, I just missed to take printout for Disney so they helped me to get the tickets printed. 
> In this tiny hotel you will get lift to help you with your luggage. 
> Neat and clean room and wifi.
Cons:
> They told me that I got one of the best room. But for me it was the smallest room I have ever stayed. Only 2 people can hardly stay in that room.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Cute little hotel
text: Myself and my wife came here for our second wedding anniversary. We stayed for 2 nights and 3 days. The hotel was lovely very authentic and very clean. Although we didn't spend a lot of time at the hotel we did find our stay very pleasant. The rooms were quite small but had everything you needed in, the beds were comfy and overall it was very quiet. The metro is very near so it's easy to get into the centre of Paris for tourist spots, the staff are very accommodating and provide a 24hr service. The rooms are equipped with a hairdryer and a fan great for warm nights. The only complain that we would have is the breakfast in the morning isn't that great. There isn't a lot of choice. It's a continental Buffett so we didn't expect too much anyway but we got even less choice than we expected no croissants toaster didn't work and half the time the drinks jugs were empty. In Fact we ended up eating out for breakfast at a nearby cafe on the second morning. The only sight you have out of the window is brick walls so I wouldn't expect too much. Overall we enjoyed our stay and would come again! :)
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: comfortable hotel
text: nice hotel,i stayed there for about 5 days. room was clean and comfortable. wifi was perfect. you could found all what you need near hotel like market, pharmacy and many wonderful shops. small room but this is common in paris. staff are very friendly and very co-operative.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Cute Hideaway
text:
It is a cute hotel, not far from the metro, nice neighbourhood.

the reception interior design is classic and the room that I had is just perfect for 2 person. well decorated, comfy bed and clean modern bathroom. 
highly recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great boutique hotel!
text: I recently visited Paris for a holiday and stayed at this fabulous little place!  It was well located with great restaurants and bars and within very close proximity to Rome and Villiers metro stations. It is not amongst tourist spots, but walking or metro distance to all tourist destinations. The rooms, although quite small, were well decorated, clean, dark curtains for sleeping, a good sized safe, flat screen TV, wardrobe with good hanging space and everything a traveller needs! Comfy bed and modern clean bathroom with plenty of new fluffy towels. No, there wasn't a fringe or kettle, but these were available for use in reception. The staff were amazing - friendly and helpful and spoke very good English. They helped with all tourist activities from catching the metro, local eating spots and all great tourist tips plus arranged a reliable and cheap transfer to the airport. Nothing was disappointing, I highly recommend and I will stay again! Great value for money too.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: fantastic
text:
this hotel was fantastic right on the The Seine absolutely fantastic our room was exactly as we asked for view of the Eiffel Tower so close
The staff were excellent very helpful Walid and Lilane were great attentive and friendly
all staff were
I would recommend this hotel to anyone
Marita
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Charming hotel!
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a week during our first trip to Paris. It is just a couple minutes' walk from the Rome metro stop, making it a very convenient location. It is also just off the Place de Clichy by maybe half a block, allowing for the hotel to be right by many local treasures, but also a little away from all the foot traffic so it is quiet. Look down Place de Clichy and you get a great view of the Sacré-Cœur. 

The hotel itself is quaint and charming. It is small as a whole, with only a handful of rooms on each floor. Having done enough research on Paris, we knew to expect smaller rooms. And the room was small...but perfect. I told my husband that it really made me see just how unnecessary it is to have large rooms when you're going to be out all day anyway. I also distinctly remember thinking how perfect it was as we laid in bed during a thunderstorm. The room felt just felt intimate. The bathroom was more modern in style, which was a contrast from the older charm the rest of the room, and the hotel as a whole, had. I think the only odd thing was the shower "door" which only extended about halfway across the entire shower area, allowing for the water to get all over the floor. We laid out a couple towels at a time on the floor when showering, so it wasn't much of a problem.

The breakfast "cave" was fantastic. I loved the look of it, and, if we are being honest, I loved not having to worry about seeking out breakfast while we quickly looked over our daily itineraries. Coffee, tea, hot chocolate, milk, and juice were all available. Food offerings included cereal, fruit, baguettes, ham, hard boiled eggs, cheese, yogurt, spreads, and more. 

The staff was absolutely wonderful! They were always friendly and willing to help! From the first time we stepped in the door to check in until we sadly had to leave and check out on our last day, the staff was always there to make everything pleasant.

Wifi is available and is very reliable. No you won't find "creature comforts" such as an in-room fridge or coffeemaker, but it really shows how spoiled we sometimes are. Enjoy the tea and coffee the hotel offers downstairs. Or better yet, break away from those creature comforts and go to a local cafe instead. 

We have only been back for about a week and a half and I have been repeatedly how much I loved our hotel. I would stay again in a heartbeat. The location, the charming and intimate feel of it, and the wonderful staff made our stay in Paris just perfect. Thank you to everyone there. We look forward to seeing you again!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: 2 day visit to Paris
text:
It's a boutique hotel in central Paris. Very tiny rooms. No refrigerator, no AC and no kettle in room. 

Mercifully they have Wifi and a lift. The only hot item in the package breakfast is the coffee and tea. 

If you are confident about the metro or underground, suggest stay further away and book into a standard hotel - Mercure or even IBIS. You will get more creature comforts. 

Highlight was our French receptionist. Extremely helpful with directions and suggestions. Must quote his memorable statement - 

"You are on holiday. Relax and enjoy. You are not trying to pass an exam"
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: A good base for all the major sites of Paris
text: Okay, so this is a rather basic hotel - there are no fridges or tea and coffee making facilities in the rooms and the décor is a little tired.  The rooms are on the small side but this is pretty standard for Paris.  But.......it is clean, with modern bathroom facilities and is fantastically located in terms of getting around Paris to see all the major sites as it is a 2 minute walk to Rome Metro Station.  What would make me return to this hotel is the wonderfully helpful and friendly staff.  Everyone we encountered during our 3 day stay was absolutely lovely - true assets to the hotel. We weren't due to get the Eurostar for our return to London until 19:30 but staff were happy for us to leave our luggage at the hotel after our midday check out time.   We didn't have breakfast during our stay so I can't comment on that but there are some nice places in the vicinity where you can get a typical continental breakfast for between 6 and 9 euros.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Nice hotel
text: We stayed there for 2 nights. The room was clean and big enough for a couple. The beds were really comfy which was important for me as I have a bad back. Nice and clean bathroom. Staff friendly and helpful. Good location, just a few minutes from Rome metro station. Near to Basilica Sacre Coeur. The only thing we actually did't like was the breakfast. The price was £11 per person and it wasn't too much to choose from so for me slightly over priced ( no fresh croissants which was a bit disappointing as we were in Paris). Because of that we had a breakfast on the day one, and then decided to have it somewhere outside of hotel. For the price it is good place to stay.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: No regrets about staying here
text: I am giving this place four stars because the front of house staff were very professional and helpful. The location is pretty good, near Rome metro station, maximum 30 minutes from anywhere we wanted to go to. Our room was quite small (you have to expect that in Paris if you don't want to pay crazy prices) but it was clean and the bathroom was nice. Breakfast was fine and made a good start to the morning. On the negative side, sleep quality was poor: the bed was uncomfortable and it was a bit noisy at night. Overall though it is a decent hotel and I am glad we stayed there.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Comfortable, well located, Excellent staff!
text:
I found this hotel to be very conveniently located as its a 5 minute walk from two metro stations (Rome and Villiers). My room was very comfortable- it's got a quaint homely feel rather than a modern look- and I was happy with the cleanliness and housekeeping.

I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of Wi-Fi as I could use YouTube without any buffering.

Perhaps best of all though were the staff at the front desk who were very helpful in their suggestions, tips and recommendations. If I visit Paris again I would definitely book this hotel again!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Good value and decent
text: Just one night, but the price was low and the value good. Clean rooms, good service. Ok plus breakfast. Good location. Rooms could be bigger and internet also, but would return. One drawback was the bathroom flooded after showering.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Charming hotel within the city
text: Perfectly located in a well accessible area in Paris just off the main road with two metro stations nearby (Rome and Villiers) in walking distance. Its perfect for a tourist and business traveller alike with everything the city has to offer. The staff is polite and courteous, the rooms are just comfortable enough but very small as is expected from a Paris midrange hotel but serves the purpose.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Un super séjour Saint Valentin !
text: We enjoyed our long weekend break here for St Valentine's Day. The staff are super accommodating. Nice buffet breakfast. Clean if slightly modest rooms. Hotel is full of charm. Very close to Rome metro stop. Kindly kept our bags and let us use the toilets after we'd checked out. If good service is more important than modern décor and you're looking for a little charm and good value, then this is the hotel for you.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Perfect for a Mom and her Child
text:
My daughter wished to see Paris for her 12th birthday and I wanted her to have a great Parisian experience. I booked this hotel for our 2 night stay based on the pictures and name and thought she'd enjoy this quirky little place and she did. The hotel was lovely and perfect for us. The man behind the desk (young and with awesome glasses) was so helpful every day of our trip and even helped us find a restaurant so my daughter could order moules et frites for dinner. We had the hotel breakfast on one occasion (wanted to have it in a French cafe the other time) and had no complaints. I enjoyed the area as it meant we got to see more parts of Paris that aren't exactly "touristy" and yet very easy either via public transport (bus, metro) or walking to get to the main points of interest. I would definitely stay here again on our next visit to Paris as the price for a single mother and the amenities were perfect. 

I do have to agree with the "heating" issue. The room was always hot and opening the window only allowed loads of noise in but I live in England where they don't believe in AC too so I can deal with it. And it wasn't too uncomfortable for a good nights sleep for my daughter and I. 

FYI- listen to the warnings of pickpockets in Paris. I unfortunately had my phone taken on my first day there which involved tracking down a police station, and using up some of our holiday time on filing a report. So always keep everything tucked away in bags.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great simple place
text: I enjoyed the quiet simple place. The breakfasts were great. Improve on TV channels and at least show a few English news channels or sports. We would appreciate if you provide tea-making utensils and mini bars in the rooms.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: small, simple and very Parisian!
text:
hotel sis small, simple and I think very Parisian! It is allocated on small side street and it is quiet. Hotel is small, while there are only some 20 rooms. Lobby is tasteful, I got room on top floor and it was large enough. However if you are planning to travel with large suitcases and 2 persons, than rooms could be a little bit tight.

breakfast is simple, but you got essentials and best thing was fresh orange juice!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Perfect Paris
text: We stayed for 4 nights in November. The location of the hotel is good for sight seeing and relaxing. Not too close to the bustling centre and yet close enough to metro stations to get there. The hotel is a couple of minutes from both Rome & Villiers metro stations. There are lots of really good restaurants in the area. We went to Un Air de Famille on 2 nights, it was that good. The staff were friendly and took time to translate the bits of the menu we were unsure of. Worth a visit. The hotel staff were also friendly and efficient, breakfast was good and the room was clean and comfortable. As for reviewers who complain about the size, I would say, it's Paris, you're there for a few days you're not moving in, and size doesn't always matter!! Enjoy
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Superb value for money, close to all sites.
text: This was an unexpected pleasure. The hotel is just of the main drag and is quiet and quaint. The staff were really friendly and the rooms were clean. 10 minute walk to moulin rouge etc. 2 stations with in a coup,e of minutes walk. We really enjoyed our stay. Bistro 366 was the best food and was just up the road.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Off the Tourist track
text: Chose this hotel because it was close to Gare Lazare. Neighborhood has no tourist sights & felt hotel was overpriced for the area. Room was average Paris, small, no view. But the breakfast was good. Staff not very friendly. It served it's purpose as a departure point from the train station, would not recommend.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great Area to Stay
text:
Comfortable and clean hotel , rooms a bit on the small side and no tea/coffee making facilities. Beds however are comfortable and the bathrooms modern. Upstairs rooms reached by steep spiral staircase or small temperamental lift. Breakfast served in basement cellar and whilst ok the tables are too close together for my liking.
The staff are the stars here, English speaking helpful and friendly and reception open 24/7.
The area is fantastic, loads of bars, cafes, restaurants, quality shops street markets etc and centre of Paris easily accessible by public transport or a 15 minute walk
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Lovely time in Paris
text: The hotel was very well situated, with a great view of Sacre Coeur literally just around the corner. Our welcome on arrival and service throughout our stay was very friendly. Our only criticism was that we visited during a very hot time in Paris and when we reported shortly after arriving that our fan/air conditioning unit did not work we were told that it was the only one they had! No suggestion that they could repair or replace, that was it. Otherwise, as previously stated: friendly staff, nice breakfast and clean, comfortable rooms.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Affordable and Clean
text: It was a comfortable room with updated bathroom. Not as spacious as we are accustomed to in the United States but clean and very affordable , continental breakfast was included. We stayed for 2 nights and enjoyed an evening drink in the small bar right next door to the hotel. Make sure and take a business card from hotel just in case you get lost. Good experience overall.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Nice cosy stay
text: Nice little hotel, good location despite getting lost often enough (our own fault entirely). Very close to the metro and bus stops. Staff were very lovely and helpful. Shame there wasn't tea and coffee facilities inside the rooms.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great stay at a good price
text:
We booked 3 rooms for a Saturday night stay. Hotel is tucked away just a 5 minute walk from Rome Metro station.

There are lots of restauarnts in the local area if you do not want to go into Paris.

The hotel staff were all very helpful.

There are just 4 rooms on each floor.  All very close to each other but noise was not really a problem.

Rooms are small but nicely decorated.  3/4 bath with shower head.  Not a real shower as the head holder was only a little way up the room.  This was the only real problem

We had a free breakfast as we booked direct with the hotal.  Breakfast was usual cread, cake, cereals etc and more than adequate.

If you are driving make use of their special discounts in the near by car park.

We would definitely stay there again if we go back to Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: excellent, Affordable
text: We stayed here 4 days and thoroughly enjoyed our stay.  Helpful staff, clean and great location. Close to the metro-between Rome and Villiers.Definitely would recommend this hotel. We were able to see all the sites of Paris with ease And walked to the Moulin Rouge and restaurants in the evening
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great location, comfortable rooms and very helpful staffs
text: I visited Paris for the first time along with my wife and chose to stay for a night in this hotel. The hotel was easy to locate as it was very near, hardly 200 meters, from the metro station. Since we took the metro to go around the city, the nearby metro station was really convenient for us. The rooms were small but comfortable  for a night with all the basic amenities. There was no air conditioning in the room, but the weather in Paris was great so we did not feel the need for an air conditioner. There was a tall fan in the room though. The morning breakfast was good, but options were limited. We were really impressed with the hotel staff. They were courteous and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel for a short and pleasant stay experience in Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Fantastique!!!!
text: C'est magnifique! Je t'aime le Hotel du Theatre!!!  Brill! Brill! Brill! Friendly, clean, excellent value, high quality! What a find! Thank you for a beautiful one night stay. The brekky was par excellence! Merci beaucoup! 😁
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Fabulous French Hotel
text:
What an amazing stay in this hotel I didn't know ! All the staff is really nice, always here for you. Even if the room wasn't big, it is sufficient to enjoy my stay, with many things to discover not far from the hotel. 
Thank you so much again, i will come back here next time. I highly recommend !
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Nice hotel that should be your pied-à-terre the next time you're in Paris
text:
We stayed here for one week in June 2015, and found the accommodations to be exactly what we needed: a clean pied-à-terre away from the hustle and bustle of central arrondissements.  Breakfast was quintessentially French, and quite delicious.  Front of house staff and the maid service were all friendly, professional and helpful!  They even printed our boarding passes the night before our early morning departure.

For those unfamiliar with the location, it is located close to Villiers station in le huitieme arrondissement.  It feels like (and is) a neighbourhood unto its own, replete with locals, supermarkets, cafes and boulangeries.  Although easily accessible by metro, we just walked everywhere.

The only negatives about our stay was the crashing sound of apartment doors as they close shut - early risers can definitely act as effective alarm clocks for those who are still snoozing.  And although there was no air conditioning, at no point did we feel uncomfortably hot.  Thirdly, some of the tile work in our bathroom is in need of repairs due to water damage.  

And lastly the wifi connection is woefully S L O W ... painfully so. . . . . . . ..  

. . . . . . . s l o w  . . . . .  . . a s . . . . . . . . .   m o l a s s e s .  . . . . . . .

If only they could find a better ISP or buy a new router, they could probably avoid this, their worst, criticism.

Still, at its excellent price point, you probably can't find anything that feels this well-maintained in city as notoriously expensive as Paris.  Definitely book it!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Small but comfortable
text:
My husband and I stayed at Hotel du Theatre during our last trip to Paris. This was the second time we visited this city, this time I was 5 months pregnant so we wanted a clean place to sleep, leave our baggage, with hot water, near train stations and in a nice area to walk around. We found what we were looking for here. 
The room was really small but it had anything we needed for a comfortable stay...we were given a room at fourth floor with a modern bathroom that seemed to have been refurbished recently. Wifi was available. 
The breakfast was included and it was ok, enough for what we needed although the breakfast room at the basement was small (we usually had breakfast a little bit late so we didn't have any problem with finding a table). 
The hotel staff was really friendly everytime. There are two train stations very close as well as shops and restaurants nearby.
It was a great experience for us...we would definitely stay again here.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Like a bad truck stop in France
text: There is no air conditioning in this hotel. If you mention it to staff they say they don't feel hot. If you open windows the streets are loud due to construction. We considered losing our prepayment and going to a better hotel. Our room was not ready on arrival though it was reserved and paid for weeks ago. Do not stay here! You can put lipstick on a pig but it's still a pig. This is a truck stop in Paris trying to say it's a four star hotel.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Good hotel
text: Very good small hotel in convenient area. Very cozy, mostly for couples for a short stay. Close to underground station, close to Moulin Rouge and Montmartre. Liked the bathroom, which was very clean and modern. Room wasn't that big, but enough for two people. There no fridge and kettle in the room, that is quiet disappointing, if you want to store your food or drink a hot tea or coffee. Breakfast is not rich and constant every day. Overall we had a pleasant stay and i would recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: DISAPPOINTING
text:
Stayed yet again in Paris because we absolutely love this city.

To say hotel bedrooms in Paris are on the small side is an understatement so didn't expect too much.  However we arrived to what I can only call an add on of the reception area, I think it was room 1 right next to the reception on a warm day.  The room was dark and extremely hot. 

Trying to open a window proved difficult with the curtains but this looked out on to a courtyard (see picture).

Bathroom was a little tired but as we were only staying two nights we thought we could put up with that.

However it was when we tried getting to breakfast the following morning was the real eye opener!  We had to visit the cellar at least three times before any tables, food, plates, glasses, etc were available.  This hotel needs more staff and food etc.  

As we were only staying 2 nights we decided to venture for breakfast pretty early in order to get some food and somewhere to sit.  The dining area is extremely small.

No fan was available for our hot room when asked.

Will NOT be returning.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Hmmm...
text: I am unsure about this hotel. Staff is kind, the area is very nice. Breakfast was not included in my rate so I preferred to go try a bistrot around the corner and I cannot give my opinion on it. What I didn't like was the size of the room (very small) and the old and basic furniture. I guess it depends on how much you pay. I paid 140 euros for 1 night and I would have expected something better...
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Swann is the best
text:
Very nice hotel in Paris located near train stations. Breakfast area is very cute. Staff are very friendly, Swann is very nice two thumbs up for you!! Rooms are very romantic and beautiful :) 
Very clean.
Can't wait to go back to Paris and book this hotel
From Nabil and Carmen's
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Clean, convenient, close to Metro
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night and we were given a room at the fourth floor, facing the back. We were fine with this as there is no street noise. The bathroom was newly renovated and clean. It has all the amenities that we needed for a night including a hair dyer. There is free wifi in the room. The room is of good size for us too. 

The staff manning the counter during the day was not very helpful as he did not help us book the shuttle bus to the airport for the next day citing that we had to give earlier notice. However, the staff manning the counter at night deserve double thumbs up from us as he was very helpful and helped us book a shuttle bus when we asked again. His kind act has restored our faith in the hotel's service which we felt was lacking during the day. Both staff can speak good English, which is important for us as we do not speak French. On a side note, our email correspondence with the hotel was met with swift and prompt response. Breakfast was good with an acceptable selection of toast, meat and juices. There is only one lift in the hotel and it is quite an interesting vintage experience. 

The hotel is located pretty close to the metro. It is close to either Villiers and Rome station. We have 2 big suitcases with wheels and 2 backpacks and it was not a hassle to use the metro to get to the hotel. We are in our early 30s. Overall, we would recommend this hotel for a comfortable and convenient stay in Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Good budget hotel in a great location.
text: Stayed here on our recent trip to Paris. Lovely comfortable small hotel with excellent and friendly staff who were always happy to answer any queries we had. Rooms were clean with modern bathrooms and the breakfast was great. There are shops and good restaurants nearby and a lovely market at the weekend. It is close to the Metro but you need to change stations to get into the heart of Paris. All in all a great find!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: A really nice hotel in a good location.
text:
I stayed in the hotel for a couple of nights as was over to run the Paris marathon. 
Really enjoyed the hotel which was very comfortable and clean and the staff were very friendly and helpful. 
Found it to be good value for money especially with the free breakfast. 
It is in a fairly busy area but also very close to the main centre. Champs Élysées only 20 mins walk or 5 mins on the Metro. Two stations very close, Villiers and Rome.
Would recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great little find
text:
My husband & I have just returned from a two night stay at this hotel, we wanted an hotel which was central to the attractions but also quiet.....and we found exatly what we were looking for at hotel du Theatre.
The staff were very friendly, welcoming and spoke great english!!!
The rooms were clean, tidy and had everything we needed including the hairdryer.  More importantly there was no noise at night so a good night sleep was had by both of us.
The breakfast was continental and plentiful.
I would have no hesitation in staying here again if we visit Paris and would recommend to anyone who wants a reasonably priced hotel close enough to all attractions, we walked and also took the open top jump on jump off bus.
I have to add that every person from the lady at the tourism kiosk at eurostar to a total stranger most helpful through our stay.
Local eateries were great, food cooked to our liking
Well done to the owner and staff at Hotel du Theatre we had a lovely time

Diana & Pete
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Hotel Du Theatre - trip with friends
text:
Good location.  Nearest tube is Villiers which is about 8 minute walk away.  Hotel located in quiet road rue de Cheroy which is just off main road and next door to a bar and a couple of nearby restaurants.  From the main road you could see Sacre Coeur.
Bathrooms seem to have been refurbished recently.  Bath is not full size but there is a shower (not overhead but rather a hand held one in the 2 rooms we used) and water power was very good.  Room had single wardrobe and on the top shelf of this was the safe (no charge to use, just used your own code to open and close).  Dressing table in the room plus large mirror and also a long mirror which is a must for a woman getting ready.  Small flat screen TV on wall which did have BBC World News and another station in Englsh language.  Bed was very comfy and we all slept well.
Staff very helpful and friendly and all spoke English.
First morning for breakfast we were not able to get in to the room in the basement where breakfast is served and were told there would be a 15 minute wait.  Hotel was full and breakfast room is quite small.  Breakfast continental style so we did not go hungry but nothing compares to a full English breakfast that we get back in the UK!  On offer were croissants and breakfast pastries, yogurts, jams, cream cheese, salami, 3 types of cereal, 3 fruit juices and cold boiled eggs.  Hot water is available in flasks but was not hot enough to brew a cup of tea so that was disappointing.  Hot chocolate was the best hot drink on offer.
WiFi available in rooms but it was slow.
Hotel has a lift which 2 people and cases can fit into comfortably.
We checked out and left our suitcases at front desk until we were ready for our Eurostar train back to the UK.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great value!!
text:
My fiancé and I spent 3 nights at this hotel. The staff were extremely helpful and very pleasant!! They made us feel so welcomed and directed us anywhere we wanted and were just lovely. The breakfast is a bit dire. Not much selection and not very appetizing but nonetheless the value we got for this place made up for it. It's 3 min walk from the metro and to be honest we walked to all the main attractions from here including the Eiffel Tower, arc de triomphe, Sacre coeur and the louvre. We did a lot of walking but it was all feasible. The hotel is just off a main road and it was often quite noisy as we could hear traffic and people outside our window everynight. 
The rooms were lovely and clean. We had a double twin. Cozy but ok. The bathroom was very modern and clean. Wifi was too slow thus wasn't able to really use it. Overall this place is excellent for value, great location and fabulous staff. Would definitely return!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great Hotel
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. Lovely cosey hotel with everything you need. Spotlessly clean with a metro, restruants ect just a walk away. We had a lovely time and will definitely stay at this hotel again.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great little hotel in good location, very friendly
text:
I booked this hotel for a two night stay as reviews were good and it was in a part of Paris that I hadn't stayed in before. Our room was clean and pleasant with super comfy beds and crisp bed linen. We had a view of the street and the large window made the room light. The bathrooms have obviously been recently upgraded and are top notch- better than most hotels of this size. Steaming hot water and contemporary fittings with a large walk in shower made it really good. The location is excellent with an easy metro ride from Gare du Nord to Rome with one change, and easy walking distance of Arc de Triomphe, Champs Elysees in one direction  and Sacre Couer and Montmartre in the other. 
All staff were very friendly and welcoming and happy to chat in English as well as French. 
Breakfast was in a stone cellar but due to good lighting it felt bright and cheerful. Coffee, croissants, pastries, plus ham, eggs & juice - all fresh and tasty. 
I will definitely use this hotel again and recommend it for short stays. Thanks to all at Hotel du Theatre for a lovely stay.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Long Weekend Break
text:
A very cute hotel. 
Fantastic location with access to the Metro at either end of the main road where the hotel is situated. Only 10 minutes away from Arc de Triomphe.

The concierge who welcomed us was very helpful and warm and tended to our questions.

Our room was very warm, fantastic given that we went at the midst of winter.

Unfortunately it was twin beds pushed together rather than a double bed, which is not ideal for couples. 

The bathroom had been recently refurbished to make it very modern.

Overall a really nice hotel and definitely would stay again if in Paris.  

If you are travelling to the hotel by Metro, come off at Villers rather than Rome, as it is easier access and a lot closer.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Very nice and practical
text:
we enjoyed our stay at the hotel very much. The room is small but it was very nice and warm, specially considering the cold outside. The staff was very helpful; checkin was very practical and easy.
Very well located, close to Metro stations and trains. Paris main attractions where just at walking distance. 
The hotel is in front of a theatre and surrounded by restaurants, some of them with very good quality.
For the price we pay we were quite satisfied.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Just marvellous!!
text: I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights a week ago with my fiancee and it was just perfect in every way. Its placed in a lovely parisian setting with a variety of local restaurants and bars and its also walking distance to alot of the top tourist attractions. When we arrived at this hotel the reception staff were so kind and helpful and had a great level of spoken english. The elevator and stairs are a great job and we were very happy that the elevator worked at all hours. We noticed this hotels exceptional cleanliness throughout the hotel and our room. Our room was great due to all the things that were available such as wifi, tv, and a safe deposit. The bathroom was outstanding and i loved the fact there was a hairdryer. House keeping was great and the breakfast in the morning offered a great variety and all was fresh! This hotel definitely exceeded our expectations and we will absolutely be back again and we recommend this place to anyone and everyone the staff were of great help!
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Great place to stay in Paris
text: This is a great hotel in Paris. My husband & I visited Paris for the first time in November and were not sure where to stay. We thought from a map this hotel was far from all of the sights, but it is not. It is right by 2 metro stops which get you to any of the attractions in minutes. The nearest places to walk are Moulin Rouge, Montmartre & Arc de Triomphe if you like a nice 15-20 minute walk. It was a very nice & quiet hotel in a nice neighborhood. We felt very safe walking to our hotel late at night. There was also a good selection of cafes nearby. The room was small, which is normal for Europe, but had everything we needed. A bed, cabinet, desk, 3 mirrors and a nice clean bathroom. The room did get quite warm, but we were able to open the window for some fresh air. The breakfast was included for us and was a nice assortment of juices, coffee, tea, breads, jams, yogurt, fruits, eggs, cheese and meats. There was even a bowl of fresh croissants at the tables each morning. The front desk staff was very friendly and spoke English very well. The elevator was quite small so using the stairs is more efficient. We would stay here again, it was a wonderful hotel at a very fair price for Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Charming Hotel in Paris
text: Hotel du Theatre is a charming hotel in Paris. With a familiar environment, very cozy, very helpful staff, close to Metro line 2 and line 3, close to ‘Molin Rouge’ and ‘Sacré Coeur’. The breakfast room is small (maximum 12 persons in all the tables) but the breakfast is good enough. The rooms are small but cozy and quiet. I definitely recommend this hotel for a short brake to Paris.
name: Hotel du Theatre by Patrick Hayat

title: Perfect stay!
text:
This hotel is a real gem. The rooms are very comfortable, spacious enough and spotlessly clean. 

I loved the bathroom - the shower was glorious, plenty of space to put everything, and nice lighting :) 

Windows open (which is sometimes hard to find) onto a typical Parisan street. The area is away from the hustle and bustle of central Paris, but alive enough so you feel part of the city, and has enough local shops for you to grab some water/fruit/whatever to take back up to the room.

Glaciere metro is a 10 minute pleasant walk away, you can get to most places easily from there. 

Staff are friendly and competent - I asked for a few things and I was responded to immediately and very satisfactorily. Housekeeping staff are great - big shout out to them.

The jewel in this crown though is the pool. You have to reserve it, but it is so delightful to have the pool to yourself (and partner) in a hotel in Paris. You can go down there in your robe, swim, then go back to your room and shower. It makes it feel like a luxe experience for a moderate price.

My only problem (that was quickly solved) was that there was no kettle in the room when we arrived. Being a Brit, I of course had a panic attack :D but we asked for one at reception and instantly got one.

I can't recommend this hotel highly enough, we'd love to go back!
name: Hotel B55

title: Hotel B55 - Great Experience
text: Our experience with hotel B55 was great - the food, the room and especially the service of the staff in general and Julian the manager in specific - Julian has assisted us with the booking of many attractions and helped us a great deal with our trip planning.
name: Hotel B55

title: Clean and friendly
text:
Very clean, great value, great area, a pool in downtown Paris!, staff that goes the extra mile, 8 wines on tap, etc.

We got the family room. 1 bedroom with a big bed connected to a bedroom with 2 smaller beds. Perfect for a family of 4.

I've been to Paris many times and this place takes the cake. Lots of great restaurants close by, yet not a loud party area. 

Best value in Paris!!!!

I couldn't recommend this hotel more....
name: Hotel B55

title: Great hotel excellent service and great value for the price
text: Excellent hotel, great service.  Comfortable and very nice rooms, a good and very varied breakfast, the hotel has a pool and a sauna.  Close to park  Montsouris and to Cité internationale universitaire de Paris
name: Hotel B55

title: Great place to stay in Paris!
text: We stayed at this smashing hotel for four nights. Like all big cities  hotels in Paris can be a bit hit and miss but this exceeded all expectations. Our top floor room (703) was spacious, beautifully furnished and spotlessly clean. The bed is one of the best I've ever slept in and the excellent soundproofing meant our stay was very peaceful and undisturbed. The hotel is approximately 25 mins away from central Paris attractions by bus or Metro (the No 21  bus stops right outside and the City University Metro is 10 mins walk away through a beautiful park) The extra travel is absolutely worth the effort as I have yet to find a reasonably priced hotel of this quality in the centre. The hotels best assets are without doubt the staff. They are the loveliest I have ever encountered in a city hotel. We will be back!
name: Hotel B55

title: First time in Paris
text:
Bare in mind Paris I’ve never been & didn’t know what to expect at all. 
I found this hotel and booked it because it looked the best available with a pool. 
And had two bedrooms which was ideal so our small children could be in a separate room, rather than squashed in our room with us. 

Hotel staff excellent, polite English speaking and helpful. 
The rooms are clean and nearly done fresh. 
Swimming pool was something we’ve never had before which is time slot you book it and it’s only your group this private way we actually found good and made it more enjoyable in the pool as a family plus the pool room sets off a relaxing feeling. 

The only downfall was parking was payment which now coming home and seeing how much and we was there for 4 nights - has added up too over £120GBP. And the pay meters wasn’t working and are very confusing as they will be located on another street on some occasions rather than on the road you parked. So we had to download an app hopefully that has worked out ok and we’ve got the correct location on it.( otherwise we will be expecting a few charges threw the post) 

In regards to a few safety issues within this hotel, for small children ( mine was 3&2 years old) the windows opened wide no safety locks that we could find, and they could very easily pull up a chair and climb out and be splat on the ground( now if you have an adventurous 2 year old like I do who masters how everything works and very curious please bare this in mind, eyes and ears open.) 
There is a small fridge - you can put fresh milk in for kids.
There wasn’t any kettle ( only coffee maker)
However staff offered me one on arrival for me to make bottles for the little one but he doesn’t have powdered milk now so that’s was all good - so if you needed one you could get one. 

Near by loads of shops all types of shops - halal foods - we did it at some but I’ll be honest no flavour - dry burger buns - the food was tasteless for us to be fair. 

English Tea lovers well I found this the hardest thing to get here ( although eventually one cafe 2 mins away managed to do me one although tea bags they use very weak. 

We booked this trip to have a road trip and travelled by ferry & car; for our little ones second birthday so we could visit Disney land.

I personally think this hotel is better for couples, travel for work, adults and older kids. 
But I will say the staff here are absolutely amazing, keep up the great hospitality.
name: Hotel B55

title: 7 days in Paris
text:
We are just back from an excellent 7-night stay in this lovely hotel. The staff were fantastic from start to finish. When I was booking in mid-June they phoned with a solution to a block on my credit card. On arrival home, they quickly sorted out a misunderstanding re our Taxi price. Much appreciated.
On arrival, they greeted us with patience as I attempted to try my little french. That evening they told us how to get to the nearest supermarkets and restaurants. A rain shower that night was not a problem- complimentary umbrellas.
On our second day, we did a Free Walking Tour travelling on  Bus 21  (2 mins from B55 ) to Hotel De Ville. 
This bus service proved invaluable to us as we travelled on it to the Latin Quarter (bus-stop "St Michel -St Germain") each night for dinner - 3-course meals for 15 to 18 euros. Bus 21 was also  our "taxi" home. 
We used daily travel tickets that cost 7.50 euros - Zone 1 and 2 on buses, trains, Metro plus the funicular at Sacre Coeur. We purchased these tickets at the Metro station "Glaciere". These tickets are available either at the desk in the station (card payment only ) or the automated machine with take card /cash.
The room in our hotel, 604, was spacious , cleaned every day and had excellent air-conditioning. Breakfast had a variety of items on offer e.g. cereals, fresh fruit, yoghurts, croissants, bread rolls, jams, cheese, ham, sausages, scrambled eggs, boil your own egg, freshly squeezed orange juice machine and obviously a coffee machine which provided a wide choice of beverages. 
Would I recommend this hotel ? Yes 100%
name: Hotel B55

title: Well worth it!
text:
Visited Paris during peak season with my mom and sister. Overall, the hotel is an excellent value. Ioved the location. Close enough to the city centre but away from the loud traffic and tourists. We had multiple restaurants and cafes right outside of our hotel, as well as a pharmacy and convenience store where we purchased water, snacks, and alcohol. I also discovered a beautiful park with a small lake within a short walk. Made for a great evening stroll for a crepe and a run in the morning. The neighborhood felt very safe. For a more active person, it’s perfectly situated about a half mile walk from the metro, but my 60-year old mother struggled with the walk. There is Uber service available and the hotel staff graciously called taxis for us.

The staff was wonderful. Eager to help and go out of their way. We got the breakfast option which was well worth it. The room was immaculate with some very thoughtful touches. Would stay here every visit!
name: Hotel B55

title: Well run, friendly & clean hotel
text: Really enjoyed our 4 night stay here. This hotel is a little different in the sense that there is no restaurant or bar. There is a dining area for breakfast which has a substantial continental offering, this area is also the snack area which is open 24 hours for you to order UberEats or a similar delivery franchise.  Help yourself coffee machine 24 hours that dispenses free espresso, latte, hot choc etc.  Id recommend not leaving breakfast to the last moment as they clear away the food pretty quickly.  Small swimming pool suitable for 2 & sauna that needs to be booked and costs €35 for the duration of your stay sets up the day nicely or conversely helps you wind down after a frantic Paris.  10 minute walk to Glacière metro & straight in to Paris.  Very helpful front desk staff, shout out to Audric for all his help.
name: Hotel B55

title: Great hotel in Paris!
text: I booked this hotel because it offered a family room and my expectations were surpassed. The family room had actually had one room divided into two separate bedrooms and a very quaint bathroom. Plenty of space!The hotel is modern, yet cozy. Great amenities and even better customer service. Maryam and Antonie were very helpful and friendly. Even though the hotel is not at the city center, it’s a short uber drive away from everywhere. I definitely recommend it!
name: Hotel B55

title: Lots of hidden charges and unhelpful staff
text: We have been here for two nights so far, and so far we’ve been hit with two hidden charges. First, they take a Euro 200 deposit against any breakages or (rather unspecified) costs. Second, they charge Euro 35 for use of the pool, and then it turns out you have to book and it’s almost always fully booked at the time you want to use it. Yesterday the staff made me wait 45 minutes next to an empty pool because someone had, they claimed, booked already, and even though that person or persons had not turned up they wouldn’t bring my slot forward slightly. They also claimed that they had 15 minutes of cleaning time between slots but that clearly wasn’t true: there was no member of staff there either before or after my slot. I don’t like being lied to, and when I put it to them that they should have allowed me to bring my slot forward I got a whole series of inconsistent stories, none of which made any sense. The bottom line is that if they cared about customer service, then if someone doesn’t turn up they should be decent to their other paying customers.
name: Hotel B55

title: Honeymoon
text:
Here at the moment for our honeymoon the room is clean, pretty and we love the swimming pool and sauna.

The staff are friendly and the balcony is great. About 20mins from the Eiffel Tower via car.

The hotel would have 5stars if the following was done:

-  do not disturb sign when on our room - people still seem to knock and disturb asking if they can clean the room. It’s really annoying especially on your honeymoon.

- meat keeps being added to our breakfast when we have said we don’t eat pork.

- considering I have advised this is food our honeymoon a nice touch would have been appreciated - even just a congratulations on arrival.

But other then that nice hotel - id stay again but probably just for a casual visit to Paris not for a celebration.
name: Hotel B55

title: I LOVED This Hotel
text: I cannot say enough good things about this place. From the second you walk in the door, the staff is so friendly. Everything is just beautiful and so clean. The rooms- oh the rooms- are just lovely. Quiet, safe, spacious, comfortable beds and the windows open for a nice breeze and sounds of the city. The only thing better than the comfy beds and room is the breakfast- I would be in heaven if I could eat there every morning. My only regret is getting back every night too late to enjoy the wine they offer. Please stay here when visiting Paris. You will not be disappointed. There are plenty of restaurants within walking distance (Pizza San Giovanni is right down the street and has to die for Italian). Thank you, B55, for making our stay in Paris wonderful. <3
name: Hotel B55

title: A LITTLE GEM
text: The hotel is in a quiet neighborhood and very unassuming.  It is a 10 minute walk to the subway, though there is are a number of buses on the corner.  The staff could not be  more friendly, patient and accommodating.  The interior design is ultra-modern, high quality and chic.  The entire hotel is immaculate.  We had a Queen size bed in a Standard room, as requested.  The bed was The Best, as were the linens.  Amenities in the room and throughout the hotel were great.  The breakfast is fabulous!  Waffles, eggs, sausage, ham, soppressata, fresh squeezed orange juice, delicious coffee and cappuccino, dried fruits and nuts, granola, assorted jellies and preserves, yogurt, fresh baked chocolate and plain croissants, danish, and mini apple turnovers-yum!  A beautiful park is just two blocks away.  If this hotel were in the heart of the city it would cost four times the price.  The hotel is A LITTLE GEM.
name: Hotel B55

title: Beautiful quaint hotel but very poor breakfast menu
text: A wonderful hotel with amazing staff but the breakfast options left much to be desired. A constant rotation of scrambled eggs, mini sausages being your only hot options eventually started feeling like bording school. Everything else on the "buffet" was mediocre. I've never dreaded breakfast at any hotel but this was just becoming unbearable by day 4 and 5. This is the only shortfall at this hotel but sadly it's a big one. They need to do something about their breakfast it's a joke
name: Hotel B55

title: 1st trip to Paris
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at Hotel B55. The service was excellent and Antony was outstanding & made our visit truly memorable. He was so helpful, provided recommendations on local restaurants and made our reservations. Anything we needed, he supplied. Also, the daily breakfast was a nice way to start your morning. The ladies who assisted during breakfast were very kind. The hotel is located in a quiet neighborhood (not far from several local shops, restaurants) and is relatively easy to get to central Paris (the Louvre, Eiffel, etc) via Uber or Metro/Bus. 
Many thanks to our friends at Hotel B55!! It was a pleasure.
name: Hotel B55

title: Hotel B55 Paris
text:
We arrived a t 7:00  AM  following an overnight flight from New York. Although check-in time is 3:PM, the desk clerk found us an available room and allowed us to check in early. (The availability of  short nap was appreciated)
The hotel is located south of the heart of Paris and is a 10 minute walk from the nearest subway station.

The hotel is modern, the rooms are comfortable and the staff is extremely accommodating.  Free breakfast is included and, for me, the highlight was fresh squeezed orange juice. As with many other hotels, the rooms have no drawers for clothing.

The hotel has an indoor pool and bathrobes re provided in room.

If the 10 minute walk to the train doesn't phase you, I highly recommend this hotel.
name: Hotel B55

title: Recommend you stay here if doing Paris parkrun
text: This hotel far exceeded my expectations. Location is near train/metro/bus stations and just a short walk to the parc de Mountsouris parkrun. Easy to commute in and out of central Paris. Rooms were very comfortable, with beautiful bathrooms. The Swimming pool and Sauna were small .....but still luxurious. Will definitely stay here on next trip to Paris.
name: Hotel B55

title: Loved it!
text: Just got back from staying at Hotel B55 for 4 days. It’s super clean and the staff is very helpful. Breakfast is excellent. Loved the malt waffles and the fresh squeezed OJ. Really great. Pool is small but lovely. Bus stop very close by. Bus 21 goes right into central Paris. Metro stop is about 10 min walk. We bought the Mobilis tickets that were good for bus or metro unlimited use for one day. Used it on funicular at Sacre Coeur. Mobilis tix can only be purchased at the machine in metro station. You can buy bus tix at tobacco shop or on the bus but they’ll be only for one use and only good for just the bus. Loved the crepe restaurant, Les Docks, nearby. Definitely recommend that. Also the Circus Restaurant (15 min walk) was the only restaurant serving food around 4pm the day we arrived. Most restaurants don’t open until 7 or so. I’d definitely stay at B55 again!
name: Hotel B55

title: Modern, attractive, and helpful
text: This hotel appears to be very new. The high-tech, eco-friendly ambience worked well. Breakfast was very full by French standards. The staff, especially a very kind night manager, was very helpful (we needed an early breakfast on our travel morning). He pointed out two very good local restaurants. We were unfamiliar with this neighborhood (near Cité Université and not far from Montparnasse), but it was surprisingly quiet and the Metro was a short walk away. Our only concern was that the floor of the shower was very slick and falling was a constant concern (the reason for a downgrade from 5). We reported it to management and I hope they can address it. Otherwise, this accessible hotel met and exceeded our needs.
name: Hotel B55

title: Gorgeous hotel
text:
Our 3 nights were not enough in this gorgeous little hotel. Nestled in a lively but lovely area towards the edge of the inner ring road of Paris, it has various easy transport links, a small but good choice of local food/drink options, really close to a small park and small but clean and tidy facilities in the hotel.

The rooms are spacious and beautiful with huge beds and smart TVs, with windows opening out onto the street below which for this close to the city centre is pretty quiet all night. The front desk staff are great, they can't do enough to make you feel welcome and help with advice on getting around Paris.

I'd advise picking up a 1/2/3 etc day travel pass from the local metro station (10 mins walk), they allow travel on Metro, Bus and RER overground (we got zones 1&2). Bus stops are right near the hotel and very easy to use, validate ticket on entry.
name: Hotel B55

title: Such a nice lovely hotel!
text: I usually complain in here but this time i HAD to come here to write about this hotel.It is located in a quiet nice place in Paris and it is such a clean,comfortable hotel.It has a pool and a sauna and anyone can use them both without extra costs.We had bus 21 very close(1 minute walk) to the hotel and it took us directly to Louvre Musseum(everything else is there close).The staff is nice and helpful and breakfast is delicious!I dont really know if they offer lunch and dinner but there are restaurants and pizza places very close to hotel and opened very late at night:)So if you travel for visiting Paris,i tottally recommend this hotel(coming back at the hotel and going to pool and sauna was so helpful for our tired legs,after walking all day long-a Taxi Parisien from center to the hotel costs 15 euro btw).
name: Hotel B55

title: Get Away from it all in Paris!
text: Hotel B55 is wonderful. It is a lovely boutique hotel with the personal touch. The hotel is located in a residential neighborhood away from the tourist hysteria but also felt safe as a female traveler. The room was very comfortable and the staff friendly and helpful. The Metro and bus were terrific and a Monoprix (France's version of Target) just a 5 min walk in case you've forgotten anything. Breakfast was great, the wine bar a nice treat at the end of the day and finally, loved the sauna and pool. I hope to return!
name: Hotel B55

title: Excellent stay
text:
We stayed here for two nights to see the sights of Paris on our way back home from Spain. I can only assume we were upgraded as we had booked the basic room but instead were given a very spacious room with a king sized bed and a large bathroom with walk in shower. Everything was spotless and the bed was very comfy. There was a small Juliet balcony looking over the outdoor breakfast area. 

The hotel is a wine hotel and you can buy a pre-paid card and then self serve from the vending machines downstairs. You could also help yourself to hot drinks in the atrium and there was a coffee machine in the room. We didn’t have the hotel breakfast but would highly recommend the creparie les docks 13/14 on the road running parallel. 

The spa consists of a small pool and a sauna. It was basic but nice to relax in after a busy day of sightseeing. Dressing gowns and slippers were provided in the rooms to use in the spa. 

I read a lot of reviews about staff being unhelpful and rude in many Paris hotels but this was not our experience. Staff were polite and helpful and nothing was too much trouble.

Although the hotel isn’t the most central it has excellent public transport links and you can get the bus from 200m up the road from the hotel and be in the centre of Paris in 20 mins. We used the city mapper app to find our way around which was very useful and we found the cost of transport cheap at 1.90 Euro per journey.

I will definitely stay here again when I return to Paris.
name: Hotel B55

title: Enjoyable stay
text:
Just back from thoroughly enjoyable 2 night stay at Hotel B55 with my wife

The hotel is very peaceful and modern. Rooms are clean and well kept with a lovely shower. Nice toiletries are provided. 

The pool and sauna was a lovely addition at the end of a tiring day walking around Paris. 

Breakfast was lovely and just the ticket at the start of the day. 

The hotel is a 10 minute walk through the park getting off at the cite universitaire station. 

To get into Paris we got on the no.21 bus just round the corner from the hotel. 

We would happily return again.
name: Hotel B55

title: Good with some greys...
text: Nice hotel in downtown. Good and clean rooms very new with all you can need when travelling. There is a small pool and sauna area and a big dining room. Breakfast very basic and a bit disappointing for this type of hotel with a limited choice.
name: Hotel B55

title: Fantastic place to stay in Paris
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights and had a wonderful experience. The room was super clean and had everything you need for an enjoyable stay. Public transport was very accessible from the hotel. Breakfast was very good with a good variety of choices. Coffee machines were available in the room as well as in the restaurant all day. Staff members were nice and helpful and made their best to make our stay more enjoyable (special thanks to Maryam who helped us alot and provided lots of useful information about going around in Paris). Highly recommended and will book again if we come back to Paris in future.
Thanks
Amir
name: Hotel B55

title: Fantastic 4 night stay
text: Stayed here 4 nights with my daughter in a twin room, can really recommend this hotel. We were able to check into the room on the fifth floor early, access via very efficient lifts. Beautifully presented, comfortable beds, huge TV (with Netflix), wine cooler, USB chargers, Nespresso machine, air conditioning. The en-suite bath/shower was spotless (excellent shower) and a great supply of toiletries, towels, dressing gowns and slippers. Room was serviced very well every morning. We had breakfast twice (not included in our rate) but loved the choice, particularly the fresh orange juicer. Coffee machines very welcome first thing as well. Reception staff couldn't have been more helpful, including organising a taxi for us back to Orly on the last day.
name: Hotel B55

title: Very disapdisappointing
text: No air conditioning available in the room. Weather was 10 degrees at night and the room was so cold with no heating option. Contacted hotel staff but they were so reluctant to offer any help! The rooms have only cooling option. Not even a bottle of water available in the room. No tea / coffee in the room. A cup of tea from the hotel bar is 3 Euros!
name: Hotel B55

title: Had a wonderful stay at this hotel
text: This was my family's favorite hotel out of all the ones we've stayed at in Europe. It's quite new so everything is still in very good condition and I hope that they will be able to maintain that over the years. It is complete with all amenities. They even have a Marshall speaker in each room. While not all staff are fluent in English, most of them are able to carry a decent conversation. All of them are also accommodating. Breakfast is a little better compared to other European hotels as well. While its location is not near the tourists spots, bus stops and metro stops are nearby so it's still accessible. There are also restaurants and convenience stores surrounding the hotel. Would definitely book this again on my next trip to Paris!
name: Hotel B55

title: Magnifique
text: Amazing hotel is specially rception area specifically M. Paulo extremelly nice, polite, intelligent, very accomodated and trying to make your stay in the place extremally plaisant. You fill home away from home. I trully bellieve that world will be better with people like him.
name: Hotel B55

title: Fabulous Hotel
text:
I booked this hotel through expedia, and the ratings on both Expedia and Trip Advisor seemed really good. And when we got there (me, my wife and two young daughters) were not disappointed. The welcome was friendly and the reception was clean. We went to our room and again very clean and it felt new, as the carpet was not worn at all. The bathrooms were fresh. As we booked two rooms (both next to each other with an adjoining door) the girls slept in one room on singles beds, and my wife and I had the double bed in the other room. Bed was super comfy... although the pillows are odd shaped and too soft for my liking.

There are a few (very minor) niggles, like the room temperature is set centrally so you can not control the heating, so if you are too warm you have to open the windows, as if you go to Paris, there seems to be sirens all the time!!! Also, we used up the shower gel too quickly, but in our defence it was a hot weekend so we did have to shower!). Also, there are no drawers for clothes so we had to place them on the base of the cupboard. However all minor niggles.

We had breakfast included and this was pleasant, although the breakfast area was small. We were fortunate to get into the area quickly as shortly after we arrived all the remaining tables were taken up. This happened on a couple of days of our stay. Food included patisseries, breads, cereals, cheese, meats and yoghurts. Hot food there was scrambled eggs and sausages, boiled eggs, and the family favourite, freshly made waffles.

The RER and Metro are about 10 minutes walk from the hotel, so not too far and our daughters were OK with the walk.

I would definitely recommend this hotel, despite the niggles, and if I am in Paris again, would be willing to go back.
name: Hotel B55

title: Would stay again
text: Really lovely little hotel. Pool and sauna are small but a nice addition to relax after long days of being a tourist. Just over an hour walk to the Eiffel Tower or hotel is a 10 min walk from glaciere station which will take you to the main attractions in 20-30 mins. Staff were ok. Room was very clean and modern.
