title: Great Everything!
text:
From the moment I chose this hotel, to the time we arrived and while we were guests at the establishment, we received nothing but outstanding service. The staff were very helpful, responsive to all my emails.  While we were at the hotel,everyone was friendly and helpful.

Location is amazing. A block from the Notre Dame Cathedral. Across from the Opentour Bus Stop. Walking distance to the Louvre, Muse d'Orsay, and of course the Latin Quarter sites.  There is a church across the street, Saint Severin...it is well worth a visit.  It is beautiful.  Down the street is a Formagerie (cheese store); Wine Store and so many cafes, souvenir stores, candy stores, fish market selling crabs, and so much more!

We had a room that accommodated 3 people. It had 1 queen bed and 1 single bed. The hotel is very clean, the rooms are well maintained, clean and the beds were extremely comfortable.  The room is equipped with a small bar fridge.  It does have beverages in it, we used it to keep our food, fruit and store bought beverages cold.  It also offers a safe in the room.

Bathroom was large. Tub, shower, big vanity, full hairdryer, heated towel rack.  

The room was large and comfortable for 3 people.  Plenty of room for us and our luggage.  You can hear some noises when others are in the hallway, and we could hear the neighbours alarm going off, but overall the hotel is quiet.

Air conditioning worked well.  Make sure to keep your windows closed before you leave the room. We forgot one day and the room was rather warm upon coming back.  It took a bit to cool off  The week we travelled, Paris was experiencing 35 degree weather....it was very hot!

We had breakfast one morning at the hotel. It is very expensive.  We had continental breakfast and with the Canadian exchange came out to $60 Canadian dollars.  I recommend walking out and exploring all the wonderful cafes for your meals.  Which this hotel is walking distance to a plethora of options.

I highly recommend the hotel.  If my travels take me back to Paris, this is the hotel that I will be staying at!

Thank you to the hotel staff for taking such great care of us during our stay.

We stayed from August 1 - 5, 2018.

title: Great value, great location
text: Hotel Henri IV (Rive Gauche, which is an important distinction) is in an excellent location just a five minute walk from Notre Dame, and 5-15 minutes from multiple metro stops including St-Michel, Cluny, Odeon and Maubert.  I had a room on the third floor facing the street, and directly across from St. Severin.  It was excellent.  While Rue Saint Jacques is busy during the day, the room was very quiet - very little street noise.  We did not try the breakfast, which is not included with the stay, but it did look sparse so we opted for breakfast outside of the hotel.  The room is air conditioned and there is a lift in the building.  The hotel contacted me prior to my stay to confirm final details including arranging transport from the airport.  It was very streamlined.  The staff is professional, not necessarily warm, but very professional.  The restaurant is within walking distance to many neighborhood restaurants including Le Loubnane, a Lebanese restaurant which was a highlight of the trip.

title: Best Location I’ve stayed in in Paris
text:
We loved this hotel. We booked 2 rooms and both were unique, beautifully decorated and spacious. The best part was the location.

I’ve been to Paris a few times and this was my first time staying in the Latin Quarter. By far the most interesting part I’ve stayed in. The hotel is located literally across the road from all the cute little cobble streets and restaurants. It’s 2 blocks from the train station that takes you to both CDG and Orly airports but also around the town. 

Notre Dame is just a short 2 blocks across the river and down that same street one of the best bakeries I’ve been to in Paris.

The on the same side of the river as the hotel is about a 10-15min walk to the Luxembourg Gardens.

Loved the location and loved the hotel. I would highly recommend.

title: Family with teenagers: great location! suggestion for improvement
text: We just returned from an 8 night stay at the Hotel Henri IV Rve Gauche where we had booked 2 rooms.  Our children (19 and 17) were upgraded to a triple upon our arrival: this is a larger room with a queen size bed and a twin that sits in a seperate alcove.  It was very nice for them as it afforded them a bit more room (the view was of an exterior alcove of the hotel but they just slept there)  Rooms are typical for Europe (small and what I would expect for a 3 star) ) but our A/C worked very well,  the bed was comfortable, and it was clean. Our room faced the beautiful church across the street and though the street is busy, we didn't hear street noise and slept very well.  We ate breakfast one day in the hotel: they serve a smaller breakfast of coffee/tea or hot chocolate, 2 pastries and orange juice for 6 euros from something like 6-9 a.m. and a larger breakfast for 13 euros.  The carafe full of hot coffee was a nice treat. The hotel location is absoluely ideal! The only disappointment: the day we left was a planned train strike, so the day before we had asked the hotel front desk to reserve for us a taxi  for 9:30 the next morning. As I was settling the bill  (the hotel was paid for in full up front but there were added taxes and the breakfast) the phone rang at 9:25 and the woman told us that due to the strike the "taxi was too busy to come get us."  When I asked her what she would suggest we do, she just shrugged her shoulders and said she would take the RER to the airport.  She didn't seem concerned for us and she did not offer any further help.  I would suggest to the staff that having printed instructions (in several languages) as to how to take metro/train to airport would be very helpful to their hotel guests.  It was stressful figuring it out last minute (thank goodness for Google Maps and some very friendly Parisians on the metro) and left us unfortunately with a lower opinion of the hotel front desk staff.

title: My Home-Away-from-Home in Paris ...
text:
This is definitely going to be a short review about this hotel, well the title basically sums it up.  I have also read the rest of the other reviews of the hotel, and generally yes they are all true about this place being terrific with awesome people working here.  Now, I would like to testify this.  

So my story went like this.  We were in our second leg of our Paris trip with the kids, and we arrived at Henri IV newly refurbished hotel on a Friday from Disneyland Paris.  Greeted just luke warmly by someone, we thought we would just be using the hotel as a sleep-over as the plan was to be out in Paris, painting the city red.  So it didn't really bother me like how it would have.  Little did we know, whilst being out in the city on day 2, my son took a sudden turn and fell ill.  It was to the point that he could barely get out to even walk, and of course, we stayed in most of the time after that.  
  
Whilst recuperating very slowly in the hotel (that was probably my longest 3 days of my life), I had a chance to acquaint myself with the hotel even more.  Being in a foreign land with a kid running high fever, and not entirely sure who to contact and how to get my messages across to the medical personnel in Paris, that was truly very unnerving.  
There were instances where I had to activate the medical Dr to visit my son.  Who helped me?  The front desk folks of this hotel.  They not only translated and explained my situation to the folks, and they even had lengthy discussions on our findings and what I should be do next.  Honestly, they did not need to, because I was very very used to hospital visits, but the chats with them did ease off my nerves.  So thank you for that special attention given.    

So, yes - front desk was very very helpful.  There was this elderly man who was first to respond to me, spoke very little English but knew what he needed to help me do.  Then there was Z***, who literally is my hero there in Paris.  Had discussions and gave me some ideas how to manage my situation.  Z*** even helped me explain to hotel management about my arrangements, which I truly truly appreciated it.  

The other interesting part about my stay was after having many meals of Chinese (from a shop called Mirama, 3-4 doors down), it was such a refreshing joy to be having breakfast in the hotel, with fresh continental food and orange juice.  All 4 of us, felt so good after that, and with a very lovely warm friendly lady who waited on us.  We were so delighted (despite the fact that I have read a couple of times that it was not worth it and expensive) - but ye know what, it was truly truly lovely!
On another note, there is a pharmacy next to Mirama, where you can get your medicine, and the lady there was also very helpful.  Most things are closed on Sunday nights though, including the nearby pharmacies.  Hence, I had to walk across to Notre Dame, to the nearby hospital.        

Coming back to this hotel?  A definite yes.  I (and my family) am grateful for the people in this hotel who has helped me.  Hope we can return here and complete our intended hotel.  Until then merci beacoup, Henri IV et a bientot!

title: Top-notch housekeeping service
text:
I chose Hotel Home Paris 16 for the first four nights of my stay in Paris, mainly because of the positive reviews I have read on the tripadvisor forum. What a great start to my France/Germany tour!

I must admit that I was initially a little apprehensive about the quaint little lift that has just enough standing room for 2 persons! But eventually that was of little consequence to me for I was so wowed by the self-sufficient apartment, the warm bathroom (really heavenly on cold December days) and the top-notch housekeeping service!

I'm grateful to Virginia who welcomes guests at the reception. Over the next few days, she ensured that every request, be it for internet service or dishwasher detergent, was quickly and sufficiently met.

But what impressed me most was the service provided by the chambermaids. Our room was always fresh and clean when we returned to the hotel from a day of sightseeing. I was in a particular rush one morning and left a couple of pots unwashed. To my pleasant surprise, I returned to find the unwashed pots done and ready for use! Thank you, ladies, for going the extra mile!

I also love the bathroom, which was always cosy and warm. The heater was fantastic! It certainly does wonders to a tired soul returning from the freezing cold outside.

All in all, the well-located Hotel Home Paris 16, with its impeccable service and yet affordable price, gives true value for money - something to be thankful for in pricey Paris!
name: HotelHome Paris 16

title: A 5 star secret in Paris 16th...
text: Whenever we visit Paris, we stay at Hotel Home on Rue George Sand in the 16th. Hotel Home offers comfortable clean and fully equipped apartments with a friendly and professional service. It is our second home away from our home in Canada.

title: Week worth the stay
text: I will definitely come back to this lovely place again. The location was fantastic- so close to the Met and a walk into Paris. The staff were great and the rooms comfortable. text:

This is but the most recent reason I ALWAYS stay at Hotel Home!

Anyway I was there with my family and we like it a lot!

We had the 3BR apartment and it was well appointed, kitchen had everything we needed, and had such a classic Parisian feel.  To top it off, the location was fantastic & the staff were incredibly friendly & helpful!! Absolutely recommend & will try to stay there whenever we return.

Stores and shops, and restaurants nearby, taxi rack two blocks away by the Metro station, would recommend to family and friends.

text: I chose this hotel for my first family trip to Paris. This is an apartment-type hotel with a very atmosphere. There was a mini kitchen and it was very convenient to buy and cook ingredients at a nearby supermarket and a bakery nearby. It is safe in a safe area. The metro station was also convenient to get anywhere nearby. The staff was friendly and nice. It was a pity that there was a day when towels and linens were not changed. I think some people are worried about hearing the footsteps of the upper floor in an old building, but we felt it very well. I think it is highly recommended considering the price.

title: Amazing for a family break !
text: This hotel is amazing ! I stayed in a twin suite here and it was brilliant, containing one separate bedroom, a small corridor, a bathroom, a separate kitchen and then a living room with a fold out sofa bed. Each of the rooms are of good size ( except the kitchen which is quite small ) but in the kitchen the dishwasher is not very efficient.The apartment is in an amazing area, within 1 minute walking , a small supermarket, a French bakery and ( if you walk for about three minutes ) a metro station. Highly recommend for families if you want a great break in Paris with the ability to cook your own food.
name: HotelHome Paris 16

title: review of stay at Hotel Home in Paris

name: HotelHome Paris 16

title: Feel Paris

title: Not a charming Parisien apartment hotel at all.

Main reason for poor score was madly aggressive response from owner as I arrived on business late at night. Whatever you do, don't press the buzzer more than once to get in or you will get a tirade! Really immoderate, I thought he was going to hit me.  Fortunately, it was only for one night & I was very glad to move on. Basically, you can get better for your money and stay where the manager isn't slightly unhinged.

title: Nice Stay as part of a Business Trip
text:
I stayed at HotelHome Paris 16 as part of a business trip in May 2019 for 3 nights.

The location was actually the main reason i chose the hotel as it is still in walking distance to Expo Porte de Versailles (about 25-30 mins by foot and 8-10 with an e-scooter, which you can find all over Paris). The neighborhood is also very nice, very close to the Seine with a view of the Eiffel Tower.

The hotel is very nice, I had a small apartment on the ground floor (there were some renovations going on outside, but that should be over soon). Comfy bed, small but good bathroom, nothing to complain here. 

I checked in outside of business hours, so there was an envelope with my room key posted inside on a window. Look out for it - I didn't find it immediately (as did the couple checking in with me). 

Overall, I would stay here again!
name: HotelHome Paris 16

title: great service

we had to leave earlier as booked.That was no problem, both the staff and the manager were extremly helpfull and generous.
We will come back for sure.
Location is very good, you can reach Eifel tower by foot in 30min.

title: At least not for old people.

They also charged without to ask before if they can and how they can. Towels were not change during one week. We had already came before and it was good but this time it costed twice for a small room and conditions were really bad.

title: Paris winter art trip
text:
Pleasant classy neighbourhood.  Good bus and metro links to central Paris.  Good shops just round corner, Monoprix stocked all the food we wanted (lots of organic food, which they label as "bio", we really liked the butter), but we got bread from the almost-next-door boulangerie  -  excellent, as were their cakes.

Appartment was in old building, lift very small and old-fashioned.  Accommodation spacious, but dark green walls rather oppressive and gloomy.  Some stains on carpet between bedroom, shower room and living room.  Shower room had some problems -- plastic chipped off shower head, middle shelf missing from (fake wood) storage unit.  Hand-held shower spray only, no overhead shower. Powerful water flow, always nice and hot.  Fabric shower curtain, no door.

Kitchen small but well equipped, with dishwasher (big plus point!).  Ask for dishwasher tablets.  We did not attempt to use "combi" regular/microwave oven.  Good-sized fridge.

Spacious bedroom (with proper twin beds, as requested) with plenty of storage space in large wardrobe and chest of drawers.   Comfortable beds.  Good heating, always nice and warm in spite of very cold weather.

Excellent housekeeping, with appartment cleaned, bins emptied and beds made every day except Sunday.

Office was open when we went out in the morning, but closed early (4.30 pm, I believe, but the office was closed in the early afternoon on the day of our arrival), so was closed when we got back at around 7 pm  -  the purpose of our visit was to see all the art, so we were out all day visiting museums with our 6-day "Paris Museum Pass"  (highly recommended, you can skip the queues and it also works out cheaper if you are visiting everything).

This meant that problems could not be resolved in the evening (not that we had any problems).

We would stay there again, and recommend out-of-season January for an art trip, as nowhere is too crowded, not even the Louvre!

title: Practical Temporary Home in Paris
text:
Without reservation, we returned to HotelHome, and were once again pleased. The reservation process was easy with direct contact with the owner. She remembered us from our prior visit! We were given a lovely 3 bedroom apartment which was huge by Paris standards with 2 bathrooms! The rooms were clean and homey. The kitchen was a big plus for breakfast purchased at a bakery around the block. The welcome package of teas and coffees was very nice. This is not luxury but a nice, clean, practical place to stay at very reasonable cost.  A bit off the beaten path, located in a lovely neighborhood, you must be prepared to use the metro to get to the more touristy parts of the city. Not a big deal, Jasmin metro is a 5 minute walk. We explored the 16th and found a few nice restaurants where we felt welcomed. 

The room comes with daily housekeeping but they do not change the linens or towels. We wish they would give fresh towels on a daily basis. After all, this is a hotel.

Bathrooms were clean, good water pressure, and hot water. We did use the on site laundry which was very helpful. This is a walk-up with a small elevator retrofit typical of Parisian buildings.
name: HotelHome Paris 16

title: Great little hidden gem with Parisienne characteristics
text: On arrival we were warmly welcomed, foyer is very presentable, the owner is immensely helpful and very pleasant, even offered umbrellas for our trip to the Euro game. The hotel is in a quite area, which is good, easy access to car park, easy access to taxis. The room 6 is quite large and had 2 bathrooms, 2 bedrooms, and a kitchen and lounge room, from the bedroom window you can see the Eiffel Tower on the side, this room is needed of a minor update but other than that I strongly recommend it, it was great for a family.

title: Paris visit.

This is why we continue to make it our primary hotel in the Latin Quarter.

text:
The most warmest of welcomes awaits you on arrival, quite tired from a 5am start we arrived to the biggest smile from Carolina and come and sit down, I won’t be long.

I have added some night time photos I took from balcony for this review.

title: Amazing experience *overlooking* a historic church.
text:
We absolutely loved everything about our stay at the Hotel Parc Saint Severin.
The balcony view is breathtaking, actually looking *down* onto the buttresses and stained glass windows of Saint Severin church and across at the bell towers of Notre Dame Cathedral, the dome of the Pantheon in the other direction.  Everywhere you look are wonders of beauty and history.

(warning:  it is heavily sun-exposed most of the day and only about 25% of the balcony is ever in the shade but it's so big we were able to set up the table in the shade anyway in the late afternoon)

We immediately bought a bottle of champagne at a nearby Cave du vin and took it out on the balcony to toast our good luck.

The staff was attentive and helpful, bringing us an ice bucket for our champagne and arranging a cab for our trip to the airport.

A truly memorable experience.

title: I love parc st severin
text:
Over the years we have stayed at many hotels primarily in the 5th and 6th. But never returned. Then we found Parc St Severin, and it has become our favorite. Very friendly very comfortable very nice decor. We have stayed there 3 times the last few years.

As it is on the corner of two very small streets with little traffic, it is very quiet. 

One thing that we just discovered this year is how very convenient the hotel is to the RER line from CDG. The RER is our preferred way of get to and from the airport because it is so fast and dependable. No getting stuck in traffic. Two short blocks from the hotel is an elevator on the Rue Xavier  Privas at the river that takes you directly down to within maybe thirty yards of the train lines. No stairs or escalators to haul your luggage. A ticket out to the airport costs about 10 euros and they start running around 5am and run every few minutes. There's a ticket validation machine as you exit the elevator, but I don't think there is a machine  there that sells tickets.

title: Perfect location - excellent staff - need a little more breathing room
text:
A quite stopover in Paris for the weekend before going to Rabat brought us to this hotel.  Superb on so many levels and charming.  Rooms were a challenge to negotiate at 128 sq.meters.  go for a larger room if you are two people with any luggage.
Our room faced the court of St. Severin church which I could literally get to in 2 minutes for Sunday mass after a quick breakfast. ( a gift for this Catholic who is notoriously late) . the organ is magnificent, for whatever faith you are and the art as well as the stained glass, old and modern, is all you need to get quiet and find your spiritual direction - as is Paris.
Lots of restaurants nearby with fare fair.  Cross the bridge and search the classic bistros for quality.  the concierege will help with that and museum passes and much more.  They are all superb.

title: Outstanding stay
text:
I obsessed over which hotel to stay in Paris, and changed my mind a few times. I like a smaller hotel in large cities, with reputation for good customer service and this hotel did not disappoint!
We had a triple room and it was fabulous! The amount of space was unusual for a European city and in this price range. The room was a single and a double connecting, with 2 bathrooms. So my daughters had their space and I had mine. I really loved the room arrangement. And my single was a full/double bed, not a twin as well as a small sofa and desk.Mattress was so comfortable with nice linens. Room was clean and well decorated in traditional style. It was really a pleasure to come back to after a day of touring.
Location of the hotel is great, I. The Latin Quarter, 2 blocks to the Seine and easy walk to St Germain or the right bank. We walked a lot and hotel was well placed for this. Only used the metro for Montmartre and the Eiffel Tower. The hotel is fortunately on a quiet street d spite such a good location.
Finally, the staff were wonderful. The gentlemen at the front desk , both day and night, were polite , kind, helpful and sincerely wanted to assist us in having the best experience in Paris. They did a fantastic job and deserve recognition.
Really loved our stay here and look forward to returning for our next visit.

title: A beautiful boutique hotel
text: We booked this hotel (room only) via booking.com - if you want breakfast included (a bit pricey at 18eu each) it works out bit cheaper to book direct with hotel.  However, surely it is far more enjoyable to sit outside and people watch whilst eating your croissants?! Situated in the Latin Quarter the hotel is close to bars and restaurants and a stones throw from Notre Dame and the River Seine.  It sits on a quiet, picturesque road next to a beautiful church.  It is next door but one to a club which empties its revellers out onto the street at about 6.00am on Sunday mornings (according to my husband).  Apparently they were noisy for about ten minutes but I slept through it (and I consider myself to be a light sleeper) so don't let this put you off at all.    Rooms are average size for Europe but absolutely adequate for the amount of time you wish to stay in your hotel and decor/cleanliness is maintained to an excellent standard.  From the pictures of the hotel, I was expecting a roof top terrace but these outside areas are only accessible from certain rooms.  All staff were extremely helpful and efficient from the smiley cleaner to all the receptionists - refilling our water bottles with added ice (we were there during one of the hottest weekends on record), providing local information and actually walking us to the train station for our return journey.  A wonderful stay and we will return!

title: Worth 10 Stars!
text:
I really wish that I could give this hotel more than 5 stars!

I cannot thank you all, but especially the delightful Carolina, for making our trip to Paris so wonderful.

We stayed for 2 nights at the end on April, as a special birthday surprise for my Mum.  My Mum and I had the suite on the 7th floor and my Auntie had a single room.  Both rooms were beautiful and although the single room was small, it was perfectly laid out with a very clever use of space.

Our room had a huge terrace with amazing views over Paris, including the Eiffel Tower and the Pantheon.  It was heaven to sit there in the evening, with a glass of wine looking out over the beautiful Paris rooftops, and then to see the Eiffel Tower do its magical twinkling on the hour.

The hotel is in a fantastic location.  Very easy to get to from the airport by taking the RER train, and then simple to find once there.  Many restaurants and bars in the surrounding streets, although it is very quiet.

I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to visit Paris and have a wonderful experience.

title: Amazing stay
text:
This hotel is right in the heart of the Latin Quarter. Excellent location, excellent staff, comfortable, clean, and good value. 

There is someone at the front desk 24/7, which really came in handy for the nights we got in late and our final night, since we needed to leave at 5 a.m. They were courteous and all spoke great English, which was a plus for us.

Our room was very clean, bedding was quite comfortable. Seemed recently renovated, but didn’t lose any of the French charm. The personalized welcome note and gift waiting in the room was an added nice touch. 

The included breakfast (at least with the rate we had, it was included) was simple, but quite good. Pastries, cereals, cold cuts, the usual, and eggs/coffee products made to order. 

Overall, the feel is very intimate. We stayed on the 6th floor, which only has 3 rooms, so we rarely saw other quests outside of eating breakfast.

I would recommend this hotel to anyone as a great value and perfect location for walkable destinations and a metro stop right around the corner!

title: Charming and Cozy
text: My husband and I made a quick 2 day trip to Paris while we were visiting our daughter in Europe. We chose Hotel Parc St. Severin for our overnight stay. What a pleasant surprise! The hotel is nestled at the end of a quaint cobblestone street just off the main busy road. It offers no sprawling lobby but instead a simple front desk. The staff was very polite and friendly. The elevator is very small and somewhat slow but we did not come to Paris for a grand hotel lobby or an elevator! Our room was on the 3rd floor just above the main entrance. What a beautiful view! With a wall of windows looking out over the street, this room was the quintessential Paris hotel room. It is just what I always imagined it would be like. We were able to walk everywhere and found tons of great cafes and shops. If (hopefully WHEN) we ever make it back to Paris, we will definitely stay here again!

title: Lovely boutique hotel with superb service in an excellent location - strong recommendation!
text:

Yet the best part of this hotel is its staff. They are super friendly and helpful - yet genuine, as if you were staying with a family. They really do go the extra mile to make sure their guests enjoy their stay. A special thanks to Ludovic at the reception for all the help and an extra favour!

Thank you Parc Saint Séverin, I can't wait to be back! Highly recommend this hotel, if you're staying at Paris whether you're travelling with a family or solo.

title: Don’t stay in room 55
text: Great location! Ok breakfast, Room small, bathroom tiny, room extremely warm even tho fans were in the room. This room was £250 a night; expected more, asked to change room, unfortunately it wasn’t possible. Very disappointed don’t be mislead by the website, make sure you know what room you are staying in.  Nice wall paper! Paris the city makes up for the lack of functionality. Room was clean.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Gem Of A Hotel
text: Just returned after spending 6 nights here in mid-September on vacation with my husband.  Great location near the Seine and walking distance to the Louvre, restaurants, bars, Metro stops, and shopping.  The staff was attentive, welcoming, and easy to communicate with, even though I speak no French (shame on me!)   For example, on my next to last day the receptionist kindly made sure that I was aware that an air traffic controller strike would affect my return flight, which was cancelled.  I was tired after exploring the city and visiting museums so I was happy to rest in my room after such long days.   My room was comfortable, clean, and larger than expected after reading other comments on this site before booking this trip.  Be aware that the noise level at night is somewhat loud because of the nearby outdoor restaurants, but this did not bother me.  I had no trouble with seating at breakfast, even after 9:00, likely because we came in shoulder season.  Breakfast was located in a small area on the ground floor and was delicious.  It included coffee, orange juice, eggs, bread, cheese, cold cuts,  croissants, and yogurt.  The hotel is vintage, so it's true it has no air conditioning, the hallways are tight, and the stairs are small, uneven and windy, but I considered this part of it's character and charm.  This was my 3rd visit to Paris and in past  I've stayed in larger, air conditioned chain hotels in 2 Left Bank locations, i.e., Invalides and Montparnasse.   In future, I will absolutely return to this pretty hotel.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Cute hotel, fantastic location
text: This hotel is very charming. It has some quirks, like crooked stairs which are half the width of your foot so can be a little treacherous, and since I was on the 6th floor with an archaic and slow elevator, I took the stairs most of the time. But the adorable vaulted room was worth the hike. Also the breakfast area is small when it's busy, but it only happened one day when the room felt inadequate for the number of guests. (63 rooms, 10 tables...). Lastly, I was there during a heatwave and there is no AC, so keep that in mind. However, all things considered I would definitely stay there again. The hotel was so amazingly situated for exploring the Marais and nearby neighbourhoods, with fantastic restaurants, shops and cafes outside the door. Staff were lovely, breakfast was more than adequate and the atmosphere of the hotel made me feel very comfortable, especially as a solo traveller.  Thank you Jean d'Arc for a wonderful stay.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect for our stay
text:
This small hotel is in a fabulous location just minutes from the Place des Vosges, the oldest and most beautiful square in Paris. I stayed with 2 friends for just one night. The entrance had been modernised and is light and airy. We were on the second floor. There is a small lift if needed. Upstairs is still old fashioned but comfortable. Our two rooms both had separate W.C.s which were tiny but ok for us.
The lady receptionist was helpful and friendly. 
We definitely intend to return
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Poor quality for the money. Just does not worth it.
text:
The pluses: The location is good.

The minuse:
1. The room was dark and small. 

The temperature was high inside and there was no AC so I could hardly sleep. I would fall asleep after midnight and get some sleep in the morning when the air outside was cooler. The bad was really hot, I have no idea why, but it was a nightmare to try to get some sleep in it. 

2.  The toilet room was so small that I had the feeling that I was in a tiny coffin on vertical. I am not a big person and cold hardly close the door to the room. If you are bigger, I think this would not be possible :)

3. The room was small for 3 persons and does not look like the ones we say on the hotel web site.

4. Inside the elevator there was a terrible smell and the stairs are prety dangerous to take because there are round and small.

Very poor quality for the money paid.
Never in my travels have I experienced such a thing. Very disaponted with this choice.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Our favorite hotel by far -- beautiful and the best location
text: During the month of June, 2022, we stayed at Hotel Jeanne D'Arc on three different occasions (due to travel logistics).  In fact, it has been THE Paris hotel of our choice  not only in June, but also for the past 12 years (we've probably stayed here 7 times).   Upon entering the hotel one is greeted warmly at the front desk, check in is swift and accommodating, and the rooms are wonderfully decorated (beautiful), well appointed, and consistently very clean.  The breakfast is delicious. The location is excellent -- easy to walk to numerous places one wants to be near in Paris -- and the restaurants and cafe's are abundant right around the corner.  I have traveled alone to Paris a few times as well, and as a woman I have felt consistently safe (and at home) in this Marais neighborhood.  Look no further, this quiet, beautiful hotel is a comfortable delight to be staying in.  You will return again and again, and I am hoping that I do so again before too long.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Pretty disappointed.
text: I was pretty disappointed in this hotel stay. The rooms were small for even Paris standards and everything is in Wed of updating. There was no where to put more than 1 suitcase. The biggest issue I had though was there is no air-conditioning. I didn’t realize that in booking or I never would have booked. We had to leave the windows open for air  but then the noise was terrible.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: great place to stay
text: The hotel was a gem.  We stayed here in May 2019.  We were so happy we stayed here.  The people, atmosphere, decor, rooms, breakfast...all were perfect.  When we return next year we will definitely stay here.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A gem in the beautiful & convenient Marais district
text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Hotel Jeanne D’Arc. We wanted to stay in the Marais district and this was perfectly located - a short walk to the River Seine and key landmarks. We loved the variety and quality of restaurants located nearby - even a few in a courtyard right next door! 
The staff were super-friendly and so helpful. 
We loved the touch of an option of champagne on our arrival - it made everything so much more special. 
The room was lovely and comfortable.
We will definitely want to stay here again!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Unassuming charming hotel in the Marais: WE WILL RETURN! :)
text:
This hotel did not disappoint. It was in the PERFECT location. Near a metro (Saint Paul), and many buses along the super long Rue de Rivoli which runs west to east of the city.

We had a large family room (twin beds one end, double at the other, wholly separated by sliding doors and bathroom) at the top of the building with a glorious vista of Paris rooftops. 

All staff - on reception, serving breakfast, cleaning rooms - polite and helpful. 

Breakfast is simple and fresh. Cheeses, hams, freshly-baked croissants and baguettes, fruit, yoghurt, cereal, and freshly-squeezed orange juice. We didn’t get up and out in time for ‘petit dejeuner’ locally, and it seemed most cafes crank up with their lunch offerings by mid-morning, and coffee/OJ/pastries aren’t so easy to find… so you might as well plan in advance eat in the hotel before launching out for the day. It’s better value to do that.

Best street falafel I’ve ever had in the nearby Jewish quarter, and baked cheesecake. And walks around the Marais just lovely: quick to walk to Places des Vosges, Pompidou Centre, Picasso museum, Bastille etc. Teenage stylish son was in seventh heaven with all the vintage clothing/kilo rummage stores across the area. 

We were in Paris for four nights. The family room was only available for two nights here so we reluctantly had to switch hotels, but we’d have been so happy to have used this as our base throughout our trip. Great unassuming, clean and charming hotel in a perfect spot. I’ve recommended already to friends, who’ve now booked to stay next month!

Hotel tip: we didn’t realise until the 11th hour that there was a fridge in the lobby/breakfast area with cold bottles of water we could help ourselves to at any time day or night and for free… and were needlessly schlepping out to the City Carrefore for cold water as it was SO hot when we stayed. 

Area tips: Le Pick Clops corner bar/restaurant. Le Progrès ditto, and great for people-watching/listening; young people vibe. La Cidrerie du Marais, for delicious, traditional fresh savoury and sweet galettes/crepes, very reasonably-priced (note: opening hours do not go as late as Google suggests!). And L'As du Fallafel on Rue des Rosiers; there is good reason people queue here for delicious pitta pockets rammed with falafel and shun the other take-aways nearby. And Cave du 38 Riv for a ‘proper’ jazz club reminiscent of intimate clubs of the ‘50s/‘60s.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great Location
text: Hotel Joan of Arc is in a great location in Marais.  While pricy, it is worth it for the location.  The staff were friendly and helpful.  Rooms small but consistent with being in a big city like Paris.  Well maintained.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great Location!
text: Super location and friendly staff. Were were three sisters in the family room on the main floor, it worked out very well with having three beds. We were happy that it was on the main floor and not higher up, we had some warm days. Staff were so friendly and helpful.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Good experience all in all
text:
The room is spacious enough for hotels in Paris or London  at this tariff range.
The clean bathroom and the toilette were separate, which was also nice. The safe and the fridge are in the room and the beds are very clean. The only small disappointment was one incidence, towels were short supplied on our check in day, reported this to the receptionist but he told me that we will do it later and deliver it to your room but never had arrived after we returned from dinner. Again reported this discreetly to another receptionist who was in service, he immediately ran upstairs and gave me a set of towels. 10 seconds job. Maybe service level is different from receptionist to receptionist here.
Other than that, positive experience in a lovely, atmospheric old Marais area.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great location, clean and very friendly helpful staff
text: A very friendly, well situated 3 star hotel…close to Notre Dame and the metro. The rooms were clean, the staff were very helpful and I enjoyed my stay. Great food locally and close to the supermarket. I would use this hotel again if in Paris.  The room had a king and a single bed which was perfect for what we needed
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Rooms a good size for Paris
text: I stayed here with a group of friends having researched a number of hotels in the 4th Arr.  We were generally happy with the choice and the location was excellent.  I was put in a family room downstairs (on my own!).  I was concerned about disturbance from noise in the street right outside my window, but this didn't turn out to be a problem.  My main disappointment with the room was that it was very dark, not great for preparing one's toilette, but there was plenty of space.  The bedside lamp on one side was a bit of a mystery as it wasn't clear how it could be switched on.  Breakfast was basic, with coffee from a machine which was a little disappointing.  However overall it was good value, clean and a good choice for Paris where hotel rooms are notoriously small and expensive.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect hotel for a weekend in Paris
text: Loved everything about this hotel - particularly the amazing location, friendly staff, enjoyed the breakfasts, liked the decor and everything was modern and clean. It’s a gem and we’ll be back. Thankyou!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Charming hotel in great location
text: A perfect hotel for a weekend in Paris with my 16 year old daughter. Ideal location, friendly staff, comfortable, clean and modern room in this charming hotel. I will recommend to friends and family and will definitely stay here again when I return.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Quaint Boutique Hotel with a Great Location and Nice Staff
text: My wife and I stayed at Hotel Jeanne D'Arc in March 2022 on a short trip to Paris. We booked directly through the hotel website for the best price and also included breakfast. The breakfast and coffee were a great way to start each day. The hotel is on a quiet street off the main strip so it's quieter but still very close to several great restaurants, cafes and attractions. It's about a 4 minute wall to the nearest Metro station Saint-Paul (Le Marais) on the 1 which connects to larger regional train stations just a few stops away.  The rooms were appropriately sized for this style of hotel but furnished with everything we needed. The hotel staff was always polite and very helpful with recommendations. They even helped us secure a car ride to the airport on our day of departure. We would absolutely stay at this hotel again on future trips.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Cute, cozy, in a hip neighborhood
text: This cute and cozy hotel is in a fabulous neighborhood that is somehow both right in the thick of the action, and also very quiet! Everyone who works at the hotel is helpful, and the room is a good size (for Paris). If you are tall, you might want to double check the height of the ceiling in your room, since ours (on the 5th floor) might have felt low for tall people. Luckily, we are travel-sized, so it was no problem! Also, this is a pet-friendly hotel!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great if you can get a discount!
text:
This hotel is in a great location, my husband and I were able to walk almost everywhere while also staying in an area that felt a little less “touristy” than some areas. The cafes in this area were lovely and the walk to destinations like the Louvre and Notre Dame were quite pleasant.

The staff behind the desk were helpful and kind and their breakfast room was lovely.

My criticisms? I see that there is a deal going on now, but my husband and I paid more to stay here than any other place-we were on our (pandemic delayed) honeymoon and wanted our Paris accommodations to reflect that while we stayed more modestly in our other destinations, and honestly the quality of the room wasn’t as good as we expected from the photo. No, they didn’t fake anything, they just took a very strategic photo and in person it was a little underwhelming. The bed was a little hard and the pillows were quite flat. The bathroom was a little motel like (and yes, I know better than to expect American bathrooms in Europe-even so).

Also, if you plan to have breakfast make sure you wake up early. I am an an early riser and when I went alone early in the morning my experience was lovely. When I waited until 9am to breakfast with my husband we were unable to sit down because the room was full and when my husband tried to go downstairs to bring me up a croissant (reader, I had a bit of a hangover-I blame the excellent cafes- and it was either nibble or vomit), he was told he wasn’t allowed to do this and that charges would be added. Were we supposed to wait more than an hour to begin our day? What is wrong with having a pastry in our room when we had already elected to pay for the breakfast when we booked? It was a rather uncomfortable exchange for him.

Still, our experience was mostly good, if you can get a good deal and you tend to wake before 8am (or don’t eat breakfast or need coffee) then I recommend this place.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Good location
text: Love the location, easy walk to Notre Dame, many restaurants, cafes, shopping very close. Walls are thin, in the city of love that can be a bit of a problem. Breakfast is good, staff is friendly and helpful. Hotel is not luxurious but was very clean, comfortable (not always quiet), and a good value.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A lovely hotel in the heart of Le Marais
text: We were so happy with the family room we got - a queen and 2 twin beds that worked perfectly for us.  The hotel is in a terrific location and the front desk staff could not have been more helpful and accommodating for us weary travelers who arrived very early in the morning.  We speak English and the desk clerk was more than capable of communicating with us.  Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and plan on booking here again.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Location. Location.Location.
text: The location of this well appointed boutique hotel is on point. Walking distance of all main attractions, in the midst of shopping heaven, and surrounded my endless eateries. Friendly reception, quiet location,  and tasteful interior make this gem is my new home away from home in the heart of Paris.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: My Favourite Hotel in Paris
text: Traditional Parisian hotel, spotlessly clean. Met various members of staff during 3 day stay and everyone could not be more helpful. The location is wonderful and we we’ll definitely stay again next time we visit Paris.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Not really value for money anymore
text:
I don t understand how the hotel can justify its price of 330 euros for a single chamber per night. I have stayed here several times over the last years and the prices have more than doubled without much amelioration.
This time I noticed a serious lack of cleanliness, in the middle of a pandemic. For instance the bathroom was not cleaned at all, the coffee making tray was covered in dust and the mornings dirty mug not replaced, and the throw pillows had obviously not been cleaned in a long time, judging from their smell. 
The room was smaller than advertised and the empty fridge placed under the small table, while the only chair was blocking the window side of the bed.
The tiny breakfast room is so crowded you are nearky sitting in your neighbours lap
There are other hotels well placed with much lower prices so I don t think I will come here again.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Gary Kelsberg
text:
We stayed at Hotel Jeanne D’Arc for a week and we felt very satisfied with our stay. It’s quiet, with a comfortable bed and nice bathroom, a small refrigerator, and a safe for our passports.
The location is excellent, a short walk to the Metro (St.Paul on the 1 line), the bus, and necessary shops (bakeries, cafes, pharmacy, and grocery stores).
The hotel staff was friendly and professional, and very helpful with our getting our “anti-Covid” app validated, printing test results and other forms, and arranging taxis.
There are several good restaurants very close by: Salento (Italian) and Les Bougresses (French) across the street, and ChezJanou (Provençal) a few blocks away. Place des Vosges is just around the corner.
It’s a nice walk to Notre Dame and Central Paris too.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect location and cosy
text: We had a wonderful stay at this nice hotel perfectly located in Le Marais. Good breakfast, very good cleaning and a welcoming and helpful staff. Tasteful interior. Good restaurants and a nice little plaza just meters away. Very good value for money:-)
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Lovely hotel on a dreamspot
text:
Romantic old hotel in the middle of Marais, we had a wonderful room this year, windows at the streetside. More French is impossible. Thank you Gwenn at the reception, for your hospitality and very good advise for celebrating 14 juillet on the Pont Alexandre. 
Paris is still a dream, the Marais feels like home with this mixture of old architecture and modern shops. At only 300 meters from the hotel, we could rent a bike from 6clo. 
Unfortunatley no vegan breakfast but for the rest the best hotel for this price.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A delightful home away from home!
text: Away from the crowds, but walkable to all the happy sights, sounds and tastes of our beloved Paris. As soon as Americans can return, I will be back! The staff makes you welcome from check-in, and on through your visit. J'adore Hotel Jeanne d'Arc
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: First visit to Paris, and oh what a MARVELOUS city
text: We had a lovely room; not large but well appointed, clean, and it fit our budget.  Location of the hotel is excellent for all the exploring we did.  Staff was pleasant and helpful.  We would stay at this hotel again.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: After renovations this gems has become even better
text: With a splendid location in the Marais, 2 minutes from the Place de Vosges, this is one of my favorite hotels in Paris. I used to come here for years, and after they did a thorough renovation of the rooms, it is even more attractive. Very cosy, oldfashioned style, with not a hint of cold "chain" atmosphere. Very friendly service and great bed.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Charming boutique hotel in a perfect location
text: Had a great stay at Hotel Jeanne D'Arc in March 2020. I had last stayed there back in the 1990's. The guest rooms have all had a big makeover since then but the hotel still retains much of its charm. The rooms are small by American standards, but are very well appointed and comfortable. The location is the best. In the heart of the Marais neighborhood on a quiet side street and right around the corner from a charming square lined with cafes. Metro stop is a very short walk away.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Love this hotel
text: I love this hotel, it is a cosy comfortable place in one of the most interesting parts of Paris. There are restaurants and shops around and you can easily reach other quarters of Paris. The rooms are not so big but that is the case everywhere in Paris. The hotel is renovated. And the breakfast is also very good for a reasonable price. I absloutey recommand the place.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect 👌
text: We stayed for 3 nights just before Christmas, it was fantastic! Lovely hotel and staff in a perfect location even with the strikes!! Nothing could dappen our Christmas spirit. 100% recommend a visit you won't be disappointed
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc best of all.
text:
Lots of choices in this Marais district, especially popular these last few years.
By far the best choice for location, comfort and price is Hotel Jeanne D'Arc
a unique stay that for us really does check off all the boxes.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: The happiest of memories
text:
We did not realise that our visit in October - a very happy time - was to be such a poignant and lasting memory as we have now cancelled our visit planned and eagerly awaited for.... NOW. (Thanks a lot, Covid  19 . Devastating  impact on lives).
This hotel is wonderful in every way.  The staff are friendly, knowledgeable and efficient.  The breakfast seems to get better every time we visit
The rooms are very well equipped, with provision made according to the seasons.
We are kept in touch by the staff via email so we can plan and make the most of our visit to this wonderful part of Paris and beyond.
We send you all our love and say lots of prayers that we will return in the Autumn.
Ian and Frances xx
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Fabulous in every respect! Highly recommend without hesitation.
text:
Our stay was March 10 - March 15th, the early stages of Covid-19. 

We checked in late on the 10th and the gentleman that checked us in was efficient and very pleasant. He explained everything to us and said if there was anything we needed help with just to ask. We both felt very welcome. 
We had room 32 (I think) third floor and the lift worked well. The room was a double - it was spotless and nicely decorated. The bathroom was updated, great shower ! Of course the rooms are small - it's Paris. I didn't come to Paris to spend time in a hotel room. They two of us are shoppers and had tons of "stuff" - it all fit!
The breakfast was really good, baguette, croissants, pain au chocolat, yogurt, cereal, muesli, cold meat and eggs.Delicious little jars of honey and jam. If you can't find something to eat then it's not from lack of variety. 
Risy was on the front desk the next three days. She informed us that some of the museums might be closed and to ask her before we ventured out.She helped us change our scheduled time for the shuttle. At all times she was smiling and helpful.
The TV in our room did not get any English news channels and they offered to move us. We declined as we didnt want to waste time in Paris packing up our stuff for the short time we had left.
When we checked out Gwenn was on the front desk.  This was the morning after Paris went into "lockdown". People were leaving, reservations being cancelled and basically the Sh** was hitting the fan. Gwenn was also helping out in the kitchen, getting hot milk for people and basically running the show.  We left our bags and went for a walk as the shuttle wasn't coming until 1 pm. When we returned Gwenn offered to print our boarding passes, much appreciated.  Throughout breakfast and as we sat in the lounge waiting for the shuttle he was professional and affable.
I would be remiss if I did not mention the regular breakfast hostess, this woman was well organized, very pleasant and could not do enough to make sure we had what we needed.  Sorry, I did not get her name.
All in all we have absolutely no complaints  -  it was the perfect location, close to the metro, bus 69 and a short walk to Notre Dame for the hop on hop off bus. Loads of places to eat. The Marais is simply my favorite place in Paris to stay and to wander.
You will not be disappointed if you choose to stay here.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A lovely french hotel in the heart of Le Marais
text: A 3 night stay in February was just perfect.  Small but well equipped room with views over the roof tops. A maid attended to the room every day. Extremely helpful English speaking staff on a 24 hour reception. Very well located with two fabulous restaurants in the same road - Les Bougressess and Salento. An abundance of bars within a hundred metres and a taxi rank nearby. We breakfasted in Parisian Cafes nearby. 15 minute walk to The Seine. Despite the location the hotel was quiet with a tucked away feel. Tip - french taxis charge a premium for picking up at the hotel, there is a taxi rank on main drag within 100m - Gare du Nord 10euro.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great Stay
text:
I had a great experience while in Jeanne d'Arc Hotel, the location is very central and the prices are reasonable. I wanted to stay close to Rue de Rossiers and the kosher restaurants. It was a good choice.
Thank you.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: 2. visit, as nice as the first one
text:
My husband and I stayed here in November, and again in February.
We enjoyed both visits very much.
The quiet street, the beautiful decor, pleasant room with coffee/tea making fascilities. Lovely breakfast room with good breakfast in a stress free atmosphere. Nice and clean everywhere. The staff is nice and welcoming. The location is excellent in this historical part of Paris which we love.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Love Hotel Jeanne D Arc
text: We loved our stay. The hotel is in a perfect location to everything. The staff were all very lovely and helpful. The bed was very comfortable and the room was cleaned well everyday. We would highly recommend booking your stay here and we will stay again next trip.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Cramped, stuffy and not particularly convenient
text: We stayed here for four nights with a small group.  Our room was small and cramped with the window opening onto the laundry exhaust and overlooking the interior wall.  There is no air conditioning and even in September it was much too warm.  The breakfast was adequate at best.  The location in Marais is fine, but it is not particularly convenient even for the purposes of exploring the Marais.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Wonderful home in the Marais
text: My mom and I stayed here for a week and I’m going back with my husband in April: it is the perfect Paris hotel. Well situated, cheerful, clean and comfortable, with helpful and friendly staff. I considered trying a different hotel for our upcoming trip but realized that was silly. And the BDJ restaurant around the corner completes the picture.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: My first trip to Paris
text: Ten years ago this week, I made my first trip to Paris with two friends.  They had to leave after five days and I decided to stay, so I took a room at the charming Hotel Jean D’Arc.  It was quietly set on a little street in Le Marais, convenient to everything.   My room had a huge bathroom and was quite comfortable.  I think they have renovated the place since my stay..The staff was  welcoming and very kind and as a women traveling in a foreign city, I felt very safe staying there.  I would not hesitate to stay there again.  I think of my stay there very fondly after all these years.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Stephen Dentone
text: Wonderful small hotel ideally located in the heart of the Marais.  Friendly and helpful staff. We stay every time we come to Paris!  A 5 minute walk to Norte Dame.  Plenty of good quaint restaurants within a 5 minute walk
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Quaint boutique hotel in the Marais
text: We has just returned from five pleasant nights at the Jeanne d'Arc hotel in the beautiful historic Marais district of Paris. For the first two nights, we did not get the corner room we'd asked for weeks before because it was occupied. The "superior" room we got had a plain decor and was somewhat disappointing. On our third day, we were moved to room 32, a much nicer corner room. The hotel is very clean and well-maintained. Each member of staff is polite and welcoming, especially those working at the desk. The Marais is a lovely and conveniently located district of Paris. We would definately stay again at the Jeanne d'arc.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Noisy and not worth the price
text: I stayed here for 1 night and I was given a different room than the one I’ve booked. The room was on the ground floor, extremely noisy from people waking around the lobby and from outside. Bathroom really old, a refurbish would be needed in my opinion. Location is very good. Breakfast not worth it as they have very little food choice and only americano coffee.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Lovely Small Hotel, Great Location and Service
text:
I stayed here last week (January 11-16) and, especially in the midst of the Paris strikes, found this hotel to be so well located that you could walk to everything. I found it clean, comfortable, with an excellent, abundant breakfast that would send you on your way for most of the day. The staff was super helpful, especially Gwenn at the front desk, who helped me arrange transit to the airport as well as provide recommendations for local restaurants. 

I say this without snarkiness -- but if you're a large/bulky person, be aware the bathrooms and the elevator are small. It's a charming place in a historic location, so it's worth the upgrade for a little more space. 

Again, I could not recommend this place more highly. Looking forward to staying again upon my return someday.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A great disappointment
text:
We were attracted to this hotel as a result of the quirky exterior as well as the location. I am not a fan of large impersonal hotels and spend time looking for unusual boutique style places to stay. As a result, I found myself studying the reviews here which were surprisingly good! So I booked a ‘comfort room.’ The most expensive, I believe and described as a twin or double room. At a cost of approximately €200 for one night.

Arrived between 3.30-4pm, room just being finished- the lady cleaning it was in there. I felt this was a little poor. 

My first surprise was the additional single bed in the room, giving it a hostel style appearance (!) certainly hadn’t booked OR wanted a triple room. In fact when I booked it I added the message that this was a special occasion & I would appreciate the best room possible, happy to upgrade. Zero regard was paid to that.  I immediately checked online the availability to see if I could get another room. There were none so
I decided to get on and make the best of it.  

Enter the bathroom to see splash marks around the tiles which I cleaned myself, though I cannot say the room/bed linen or bathroom were unclean. 

The towels were old, I guess they were once white, before they became so threadbare as to be actual holey in places.  WHO GIVES GUESTS TOWELS WITH HOLES? 

The toilet roll was so cheap as to be almost transparent; a false economy as simply the useage gets doubled. 

However the most inconvenient thing was the shower head that couldn’t be moved into any other position, when fixed in its housing, than of having it facing the right hand side of the shower wall. 

Indeed, thee plastic holding rail had seized, making it impossible to rotate the shower head itself, while in a static position. I was unable to easily wash my hair or shave my legs. 

This fault was coupled with the use of a cheap piece of flexi tube delivering the water supply to the nozzle which had then obviously warped into place - presumably because the shower head had become seized into place some time ago. 

This became an issue when having to use the shower head hand-held (the only way one could shower effectively with it). 

The icing on the cake was being left one single milk portion with our two tea bags, and the fact they had forgotten to resupply the room with complimentary bottles of water. We simply helped ourselves to the water when we saw them lying in the cleaning bags sat outside the rooms, on our way to check out, the following morning.

Some good points; the bed was comfy, there was a decent fan in the room, to keep the air circulating and most surfaces were clean. 

This is a hotel where all the money has been spent on the exterior, including the ground floor, making it look good at a casual glance but the absolute minimum of care is given to the rooms or to make the stay an enjoyable one. By stark contrast, we spent a night in a hotel in London for a similar price that was really luxurious and lovely. 

We come to Paris quite regularly but we will not return to this hotel.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A hotel unique in its warm intimacy and location in a historic district not overrun by tourists
text: We have stayed two nights in transit at Hotel Jeanne d'Arc several times in the last years and have always found the hotel itself and its location relaxing. The staff are helpful and friendly, the rooms we have had were quiet and comfortable and the breakfast very satisfying. There is a wide selection of bistros and restaurants in the  immediate vicinity and also many places of historic interest.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great little find!
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Jeanne d'Arc on two different occasions this summer.We'll definitely be back! The staff is extremely accommodating, the neighborhood charming and centrally located, with quick access to the metro.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Hotel Jeanne d’ Arc, in the Marais, 4th arrondisenent
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Jeanne d’Arc on our first trip to Paris in 1998 and have stayed here every year since.  It’s in the wonderful Marais neighborhood in the 4th. It’s a block away from the Place desVosges and 3 blocks from the Bastille and the 11th with its terrific restaurants and wine bars.  The Metro subway stop at St. Paul is a block away.  There are many nice restaurants within a short walk. Go to Chez Janou  or Ma Bourgogne in the Place Des Vosges.    The hotel went through a complete makeover in the last few years with upgrades to every room and the common area the new owner has done a terrific job.  They also have a great breakfast in the morning in the downstairs dining room.  There is a small elevator in addition to stairs serving the hotels four floors.  I don’t know anyone that doesn’t love this small historic hotel.  It’s much less expensive than several neighboring hotels
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: my favorite hotel
text:
I have been staying at the Hôtel Jeanne d'Arc since 2007.  The staff is excellent, the breakfast substantial, and the rooms charming.  I love looking out the windows at the surrounding buildings, from a site that was once a religious establishment where the nuns' expertise was sewing!  I found this out after discovering by accident la Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris, a three-minute walk from this hotel.  It's a place where they let you pull antiquarian books from the shelves and spend a relaxing afternoon. 

Every time I visit Paris, which is at least once a year, I find something new and exciting to explore, and this hotel, in the heart of the Marais, is close to so many cultural and historical places.  If you like opera, or even if you don't but you like good architecture (the inside, not the outside), the Opera Bastille is a 15-minute walk away.  Ma Bourgogne, a restaurant just around the corner in the Place des Vosges, has great food with continuous service.  And there are so many small museums built into some of the old mansions in the neighborhood. 

If you haven't yet visited the major attractions, like the Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Musée d'Orsay, etc. the St. Paul metro station is a brief walk.  It gets you on line no. 1, which hooks up to all the other lines.  Bus stops are also close.  A fun thing is to hop on one of the buses and let it take you to the last stop.  You get a cheap tour of the city.  

My last stay was in November.  I am planning a return in March.  The Jeanne d'Arc is a very special place.  A home away from home.

Jackie Trace
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Excellent stay Hotel Jeanne D’Arc Le Marais
text: The hotel is conveniently located in Le Marais within walking distance of many attractions. The staff was very helpful and the accommodations were very clean and comfortable.  We walked to Notre Dame cathedral and the Louvre. The very affordable water taxi is very close by to take you to other destinations in the city. The neighborhood is very safe and there are many excellent restaurants right near the hotel. We would definitely stay here again when we return to Paris.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Hidden tresuire!
text: I think I’ve been here for the 5th time.. They’ve changed the interior and improve it every time.. Very nice location.. Most of the hot spots are in walking distance.. Metro line 1 close by..The beds are good, for me the mattresses are a little hard, but not too hard.. The bathroom is ok, not the chiquest, but good enough for me..   No noise in the night! Love to have breakfast at La Favorite or on place des Vosges around the corner.. Just a perfect spot!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Best hotel stay ever
text: This is a delightful small hotel in the marais section of Paris. It could not be nicer or more appealing.  The rooms are smallish as is typical of Europe but really very nice with nice bathroom attached. They provide a really nice breakfast in a cozy area with very good choices and attentive service. I took notice of many couples with children who where able to find something for every family member.   The best thing about the hotel, however, is the employees.  These are the nicest most helpful folks you will find anywhere.  From directions, to restaurant recommendations even to looking up information on the internet, nothing is a problem.  Wonderful staff. Can't wait to go back.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: I'm happy with it, just know what it is and isnt.
text:
This was my second time staying at this hotel.  I returned because it was in the neighborhood I wanted to be in (Marais) and the price was good.
Overall, I'm a fan of the hotel.  It's perfectly located, lots to walk to, and easy subway access.  People who work here are friendly.  It's imperative to know when booking that this is a small hotel.  When they say you're booking a single room, it truly is a single room!  The rooms have everything you need, but they are efficient.  My bed was comfortable and I slept soundly.  Shower had good water pressure.  Only thing is is that the bathrooms are tiny - I couldnt use the toilet without having the door open.  Other than that, I like this place.  My expectations were in line.  The only suggestion I'd have for management is that they really should invest in temperature control/ individual units for the rooms.  It was cold outside but my room was a bit warmer than I would have liked.  I cant imagine staying there in the summer when it is warm and there's no air conditioner at all in the rooms.  I dont think that the fans would cut it for me.  Overall, I like this hotel for its location, price, comfort, and friendliness of the staff.  I'd suggest making some improvements/investments in temperature control so that it could be more of a year-round destination (I don't think I could stay there in the summer as I need it to be somewhat cool to sleep).
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Not a great experience
text: I can see why others would have liked this property. The location is very good and the staff were friendly and helpful. However, my room was dirty for the whole 3 days I was there - sand and grit on the hardwood floors that stuck to my feet and had to be brushed off constantly. The bathroom smelled like sewage all the time. The temperature in the room was impossible to regulate - either open the window and it gets freezing cold or turn on the radiator and it gets too hot. Breakfast for 12 E was average at best. If you get a better room it is probably a decent place to stay. Maybe I was just unlucky.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Charming hotel in a fantastic location
text: My husband and I spent five nights here for an anniversary trip to Paris. We loved the location of the hotel it is walking distance to so many restaurants, cafes and shops in the Marais district. We are big walkers and walked everywhere from here. The rooms are clean and well kept and ours included breakfast which was very enjoyable. The staff is very warm and friendly. Don’t hesitate to book this hotel!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: My ideal Paris hotel
text: Pretty little hotel in a fantastic central location. Very stylish interiors. Close to St Paul station on the Central metro line. Several great places to eat within a short walk. For its location the area is quiet. There is a small lift that's a bit slow but worked without fault. The included breakfast was a good way to start the day.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect location, good value.
text: Our second stay at this hotel.  Location can't be beat.  Walking distance to Ile de France or St. Paul Metro stop.  Clerks at the desk are very helpful, and one suggested we visit the Musee Marmottan, a wonderful suggestion.  Rooms are small with no AC, but very nice in October.  Small elevator takes you and luggage to your floor, but you still have to navigate a couple of steps.  Breakfast available, but pricey.  And they do NOT have decaf coffee.  (We got decaf and a cheaper breakfast at a cafe one block away.)
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: A very Parisian and very pleasant hotel in a little street that is the essence of Paris in fabulous vibrant neighborhood
text: Wonderful staff; very French quality to the room. great rooftop view from our window.  Excellent breakfast room at the hight of design. In a vibrant part of town so accessible to all Paris has to offer. Go! Enjoy!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Great Stay in Paris
text: We stayed at the Hotel Jeanne d'Arc for two nights with our grandson for his first trip to Paris. The staff was very welcoming, especially for our jet-lagged 10-year-old. We had a first-floor room with three beds and a large bathroom, which was ideal for us. The breakfast was very nice, with a selection of fresh pastries and excellent coffee. The location allowed us to explore the highlights of Paris  - within walking distance to Notre Dame, a river cruise on the Seine, the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower, and many nice restaurants and cafes. We wish we could have stayed longer!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Another enjoyable stay in the Marais
text: We have stayed here frequently over the years and have seen great improvements over that time. It is now a chic hotel with an artistic flair, modernised rooms & facilities, and of course in a fantastic location to explore Paris.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Lovely hotel in the Marais
text: After a week at this lovely small hotel on a typically narrow cobbled street in the Marais, we would recommend Hotel Jeanne d'Arc to anyone staying in Paris. Our room was small but well designed and comfortable, with an excellent bathroom. We loved the view of chimneypots and rooftops! The staff were warmly welcoming and helpful, assisting us to book tickets for a wonderful concert in a nearby church. The breakfasts of cereals, bread, cheese, fruit and croissants in a beautifully decorated small breakfast room were a pleasant, peaceful way to start the day. And the location could not be better - a short walk to the St Paul metro and bus stops, a short walk to the Place des Vosges and the Picasso Museum, and there are a multitude of cafes and small restaurants nearby - we had a couple of dinners at an outdoor table in the Place Saint Catherine round the corner. One warning: there is no air conditioning so in summer the rooms may be very hot despite the fans provided.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Outstanding staff, great location, good value in August
text: We have stayed here many times and it was a pleasure, as usual, to return this year.  The location is excellent, with so many sights, museums, restaurants, cafes and bars in easy walking distance.  The hotel is situated in a charming, historic quarter, and the beautiful Place des Vosges is two minutes away.  We were given the room we requested.  A big thank you to the staff on reception, particularly Gwen and Risy.  We really appreciate your local knowledge, and your most pleasant and helpful manner.  A note to management:  a stronger light globe in the bathroom would be good.  We always recommend Hotel Jeanne d'Arc to friends, and several have stayed there.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Fantastic Stay!
text:
This hotel was perfect for our first stay in Paris for our little family. We stayed in the family room on the top floor #61. It had all the basics, hair dryer, instant coffee, clean linens and comfortable beds. This hotel met all of our expectations for the price and 3-star rating. La Marais is a great location with lots of boutique shops, restaurants and the Saint Paul metro stop is very close. A special thank you to Gwen (not sure of the spelling) for his help and kindness at the desk. He was so nice to our two boys and his recommendations on the sites to see were genuine. Another thank you to Mary for the help with breakfast especially “le jus d'orange  et le chocolate chaude avec du Nutella! “. Merci beaucoup!

Recommendations to management: perhaps some new/updated towels, ours were looking a bit old and some wine glasses would be nice! Hard to enjoy a glass of wine in Paris while drinking from plastic cups or coffee cups!

Thanks again!
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: fabulous location-hidden gem
text: this was a charming little gem of a hotel in a terrific location with the most gorgeous attic room for two family couples travelling together. The staff were fantastic- the young man on welcome reception was absolutely charming and so helpful and the receptionist on farewell had a great sense of humour and nothing was too much trouble. I would certainly return to this hotel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend to my family and friends.
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: No A/C and could not open window
text: No A/C and can’t open the window because the restaurant downstairs vents next to our window so all the garlic smell come in. Truly a nightmare ! Sleeping in a hot box! Front desk clerk was borderline rude and the manager cannot be reached tonight. Bad bad Bad - DONT STAY HERE
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect location and great value
text: This hotel is a hidden gem with great location and value. The family room (61) was expansive for Paris. The staff was very friendly an helpful. The room was clean and spacious with a sitting  area and two twin beds in one room and a separate bedroom which had a king sized bed. Despite being  on 6 the floor  in 90 degree weather the room stayed cool and comfortable with windows open and the fans provided. The breakfast was very good. Great location and value. Very good restaurants less than a block away and very short walk to the metro. ( FYI there is an elevator). Would definitely stay here our next trip to Paris .
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Perfect location, unique rooms, great staff
text: Classic small, personable hotel. Location is terrific, my room was just what I wanted. Staff friendly and helpful. I requested a specific type room (upper floor) and got it. I traveled several years ago and looking forward to seeing the remodeled rooms,
name: Hotel Jeanne D'Arc

title: Really, the rating should be zero stars.
text:
There was NO hospitality at all upon arrival. The reception woman was seated down behind the counter, on the phone. She knew I had entered. She was speaking softly which led me to surmise she was on a personal call. She was in no hurry to finish the call. When she did, she handed me a key to room 26 and I was on my own. (I had two other encounters with men at the desk. Neither was warm or welcoming.)

I had stayed here twice many years ago. Even tho I knew there had been updates I wasn’t prepared for what I experienced. My room looked NOTHING like the photos on TripAdvisor’s page. (BTW, in the exterior photos of the hotel, the profuse flowers shown are PLASTIC!). The room was dark and dingy. There was a window that looked into an air shaft. There was barely enough room to walk around the bed. The bathroom didn’t have one inch of space to put down one’s cosmetics, etc. There was no outlet in the bathroom for the hair dryer, which I had to search for. 

It was August, it was hot, and I knew there was no air conditioning, but there was a fan. I turned on one small lamp, the fan, and then plugged in their iron which I had borrowed.
