title: Great location, roomy, clean & friendly staff
text:
Stayed 5 nights, this is my 2nd time staying at a Citadine. The concept is great, apart hotel. With lots of the amenities of a hotel except daily house cleaning not included if stay less than 5 nights but you can get your extra towels, toiletries yourself in the stock room ( unless you are a slop, not having daily housekeeping is not a big deal and not getting fresh towels daily is a non issue.. friendlier to our planet). The kitchennette had all the basic utensils, pots, plates, etc...
There is a laundromat available, 9€ for washer ( includes detergent) and dryer. Worked great, very handy.
Super well located, literally across from the rer/metro entrance. 10-15 minutes walk to Les Marais, Louvre and Pont Neuf. 
Staff friendly and helpful. 
Monoprix is 5 minutes away to get groceries, even a Mark &Spencer express at the RER/metro level. Lots of stores, restaurants around the area.

title: Such a convenient location, friendly staff.
text:
Family of four, stayed in July.
Loved the free milk coffee machine in the lobby and chilled water at will. Such a great touch early in the morning.
   Our room faced the one of the Châtelet–Les Halles entrances and therefore was usually quite busy. With the window open we could clearly hear the people on the streets from 4 fours up, the buskers singing which was quite good but always stopped at 10 pm. 
Staff are multi-lingual and very friendly, I'd like to say thank you to the receptionist with the curly hair, whose name I didn't remember, as she was so helpful! Even upon our arrival, after our less than ideal transfer from the train station, this young woman recognised my wife's distress and asked if there was anything she could do to help! She also assisted and organised a dinner river cruise which was fantastic.
We arrived into our apartment and found the sofa bed was damaged, I went back down stairs and told the reception and she said she could sort it in the morning,as it was around 9 pm. The next day it was replaced.
Chatalet les Halles station is immediately next door, making our travel to  Disneyland very easy and affordable. It is a very good base from which to explore Paris.  
We walked past the Lourve often, Notre Dame is also within walking distance as is many restaurants. We used the kitchen facilities most days but did take advantage of the buffet breakfast on the first day which was good, returned later for macarons!
Would definitely return and would recommend this Apart hotel, we'll remember our stay here for all the right reasons.

title: A very good week in Paris
text:
For the first time I stayed in the hotel Citadines and I really enjoyed it.  The location is great, beside the Forum Les Halles, where there is a metro and RER station, besides a shopping center. The hotel apartments are simple and small but have all you need, like a mini kitchen with all utensils, refrigerator, iron, ironing board and even umbrellas!
Beds are comfortable.  The room is cleaned only every 4 days, but you can pay for extra cleaning.
The staff was always very nice.

title: Much much better than what I expected
text:
These aparthotels are really super.
Its really 5 star quality.

Placed in a car free zone, this hotel apt is surrounded by eateries, coffe shops, and ample shopping.

One of Paris's main train staion ' chatlet' , (you get off at exit # 1, runs almost beneath it). A vibrant mall ' les halles' is almost attached to the property. This is the only place to be. Loved the location. 

Enter a spacious reception in the very heart of Paris, climb up a flight of stairs, after some free coffee, and you have a gym, laundry room, business centre, vending machine and a stock room ( here's where you get extra towels, pillow cases, shampoo, toilet rolls tissue etc, after swiping your room card) all this on the 1st floor.

The staff is very friendly, and the room # 724 that I stayed in was super quiet. Everything was almost brand new, so can't really understand the negative reviews. 

Train below takes you to all the main stops, even to the airport.

The train costs approximately 8 to 10 Euros per person, to the airport. 

I arranged for a private taxi from the hotel to the airport and they confirmed a price of 57 Euros,  but, when I got to the airport I was asked to pay 61 Euros. Not a big difference, but why pay extra after confirming a price.....this was the only hiccup.

title: Decent Hotel at a Good Location
text:
Overall, the hotel was alright and I would stay at the hotel again.  The room was clean and pretty big.  This hotel appeared to be designed to be stayed at for an extended period, it reminded me  of a timeshare-like hotel, little kitchen and sink for cooking.  I felt like the the 4 star rating was a little confusing because I expected it to be a little fancier than it was.  I understand that the star rating is based on the amenities not the "fanciness" of the hotel, I just expected a little more.  The price was unbeatable at it was very close to a major train hub in Paris.  We flew into and out of Orly for the night and the commute to and from was super easy.  Those were the two main reasons we decided to stay there.  The price and location (ease of getting to and from airport).

The AC was a little iffy, we just left and the weather was on the cooler side so I'm not sure if that had any impact.  I turned it to the lowest setting but never really felt like it turned on.  I would be a little concerned to stay there in the summer if the AC doesn't work.  I did not mention this to the staff because, we were only there for one night and it was cool in Paris when we stayed.  The staff was very friendly, so I do think they would have addressed my concern with the AC if I had brought it to their attention.  

Ultimately, I would stay there again and would recommend to a friend I would just make sure to level her or his expectations.

title: Tricky gaming of customers when it comes to the servicing of apartments
text: This apartment hotel is nothing like any other apartment hotel I have stayed at in recent years. And I've stayed at a few. For the price, the room was frankly pokey, with a kitchenette that wasn't much use for anything other than making tea. No washing machine or tumble dryer in the apartment. No dining area in the room. It was a very average hotel room with a larger fridge and microwave.  What really bugged med is Citadines don't service your room at all. No changing of towels. No changing of bedding. Not even bin collection.  Unless you pay a fee which I believe was 17 Euros for a room service. My trip was 4 days, but at the very least they could empty the bins on a daily basis.  You are of course welcome to spend several hours yourself (also for a fee) laundering your own sheets and towels in a special laundry room. How attractive does that sound? But everything about this property, apart from the location and perhaps the WiFi was disappointing. The TV in the room was tiny and pretty poor quality, so hard to see when sitting up in bed. It didn't fully articulate out so it was hard to watch from anywhere else in the room. Not recommended. Felt dirty by the end of the stay. Fairly shabby. Certainly didn't warrant the cost.

title: Great location - simple yet effective hotel
text:
Stayed here for the Paris marathon in April - fantastic walk to various bars/cafes/restaurants to enjoy after the run was over. But most importantly, a good location for Metro stops! 

Very central, a close walk to Louvre if you want to see the Mona Lisa!

No cleaner so have to keep the apartment nice, as we were there for a few nights, which is fine but again, imagine some people will expect maid service on a fairly basis.

Staff fine, no bar or restaurant in the hotel but just over from a number of nice locations.

Quite expensive for what we got, we felt. Definitely could get something better for the price but I suppose it’s the location we paid for!

title: Reasonably nice place to stay depending on rate
text:
For a mid to long stay this is a good alternative to home rental, as you have comforts of a hotel with a 24-h reception, elevators (yes, this is a plus against some 'cozy' apartments) good isolation, etc + somewhere to cook and also a gym and a laundry room. The hotel could get some renewal but I guess then rates would skyrocket. For those seeking a long list of satellite channels, this is not your place.
The strongest point of this hotel is its utterly central location. Many metro and train lines converge to this point with an exit right by the hotel. You can catch a train to either airport and metro to almost any point in town. Also the area is very nice with lots of nightlife and shopping. Note that this is not a posh quarter of town... you see all sorts of 'activity' around this area.

title: Great hotel in a great neighborhood
text:
Great hotel in an even better part of town. 

The rooms are small, but we didn't come to Paris to stay in the room. Regardless of their size, they are brand new, nicely furnished with pristine bathrooms, and the bed was nice and firm.

The courtyard is beautiful with nice tables for an evening drink before bed. 

The best part of this hotel is the breakfast. I can't say enough about how delicious it was. The choices were great with everything from eggs and bacon, to cold cuts and cheese (including brie and camembert), smoked salmon, and the delicious pastries you'd expect in France. We also made good use of the coffee machine which had several options. 

I would stay again! Merci!

title: Many others a stone's throw away to stay in
text:
Disappointed as there were so many other better hotels I should have stayed in. It is well located, a few mins from Oberkampf metro.

I was arriving on a flight at 0600hrs so planned to arrive in the hotel by 0830hrs on a Thursday. I therefore booked the preceding night's stay on booking.com (Weds) and emailed the hotel to explain my arrival time/reason they wouldn't see me till late morning. I assumed check in would be after 2pm and knew I would be exhausted and needing a room. I got a response back that they could not guarantee my request and wanted to know whether I would have the credit card I used to make the online reservation when I arrived. An unusual request as those of us used to travelling pretty much know this is a requirement. 

Another email asking about the card was again received as I waited at the airport for my taxi. I ignored it. On arrival at the hotel, I learnt a bit more about their operation and scam. 

Firstly, the receptionist claimed I was a 'no show'. I asked whether they had seen  my email as couldn't understand what he was talking about (this was about 0920hrs on theThurs). He asked for my payment card and proceeded to cancel the payment to booking.com. He then immediately deducted the same amount, from the same card. 

Clearly this was done so that all the money could go directly to the hotel with no commission to booking.com!! 
An hour later, I received an email from booking.com saying I was a no-show!! I promptly set them straight. 

This is Hotel Alhambra's way of diverting all the money to their account if one books via a third party.  As you can see from the receipt, they charged me 10 Euros for 1 breakfast which I never had. 

The receptionist who checked me in didn't know I spoke French and so when the dining lady came  upstairs and asked (as I stood at reception) if she should expect anyone else for breakfast, he said no on that first morning, yet still charged me?

 I asked him again on Sat morning as I checked out why I had been charged an extra 10 euros when I never had breakfast (it is a supplementary fee) and he joked and said, I could have given you a coffee! I didn't see much disinfecting going on. The garden is lovely, shady with lots of trees. The room was clean but these guys are too expensive, double what you pay on the same street and clearly just keen on taking money from clients rather than giving quality service. Metro hotel is literally next door, at half the cost, much warmer and transparent staff, too.

title: Worst hotel experience of my life!
text:
The worst accomodation I have ever experienced and I didn’t even stay here! Read the multiple terrible reviews and DO NOT BOOK HERE! I wish I had read the reviews more thoroughly before booking.

The person I talked with was extremely rude and would not listen to any reason and hung up the phone. We had no where else to go so we went to the hotel to try and discuss the situation in person. 

The situation only escalated when we arrived with the level of rudeness and yelling by the hotel front desk staff. I have never been talked to like this in my life and left in tears! The hotel had taken the full value of the week long stay off my credit card that morning when they cancelled the booking. Even though we were there at the hotel at 9am trying to check into the room which we had paid for, we were not provided access and only abused by this rude man who laughed in our faces when we requested that he then provide the refund for the remaining nights seeing as we were present but he was refusing us access. 

I do not wish this experience on anyone else and you can see from other reviews, this is a common tactic and behaviour from the staff at this horrible hotel.

It’s one thing to stick to policies, but it’s a completely other to yell, scream and laugh in face of your customers. It is disgusting behaviour.

title: Loved it and will definitely go back
text:
I stayed here with my mum and we both though it was fabulous.  It's in an excellent location in Le Marais, has a 24hr reception, lovely staff (especially Murad, sorry if I have misspelt it) and it is spotlessly clean and modern.  

Breakfast (optional at 13 Euros pp) was great value; lots to choose from, and the garden is amazing.  It's that someone has tended to this huge and beautiful garden escape in such a central part of Paris.

They offer a reliable airport shuttle as well, for 16 Euros pp, a far better option for us than a 60-70 Euro cab fare when we were  leaving.  On our way in, we took the RER train from Paris CDG Airport and changed to the Metro. 
 It's a straightforward run, just be aware that there are about 100 steps (no escalators/lifts), something to note if you have a suitcase - I ended up carrying mine and my Mum's because she's nearly 80. It's about a 2 minute (like 50m distance) walk from the Metro to the hotel's front doors.

I stayed in 2 different hotels in Le Marais last year and, while they had their charm, the fact that the Alhambra has been so well renovated and modernised made a very big difference. Everything works like a treat and the freshness and cleanliness is noticeable.  The shower was great and the in-house toiletries, blow dryer etc was good.

My only slightly negative feedback is that our particular room choice was smallish for 2 people and their stuff and that the bathroom needs more shelving/storage for your toiletries and a second towel hook/rack.

title: Rude and aggressive Reception managers - Tiny cramped 'double' room!
text:
It was with relief that myself and my husband checked out of Hotel Alhambra after being cooped up in an extremely claustrophobic and extremely cramped 'double' room for 4 nights. The room looked more like a single with a double bed crammed in which left less than a foot of space between bed and curtains and less if we even half opened the window (which opened inwards) which then left no room to squeeze past.  Attempting to open or close the curtains meant the hanging lamp constantly getting caught up in them..  Attempting to open the wardrobe door even halfway caused the door to bump against the other hanging lamp. Attempting to get dressed meant constantly bumping against the bed or the one chair which entailed having to squeeze past as very little space between that and the bed.  Which left the only space to comfortably get dressed was while sitting on the toilet.  I've heard of small rooms in Paris but this room was not fit for purpose for two people - we felt like sardines in a can and could touch the walls from the bed.  There was no mirror either in the room or bathroom. Only one bedside shelf was provided which meant having to place water, glasses, medication, book etc all on the floor and then trying to avoid stepping on them when placing feet on the floor in the morning.  This room/cupboard was undoubtedly the tiniest 'double' room even seen.  Rooms are described on the Booking.com website as being 'sound proofed'.  However it became quickly apparent that there was in fact no sound insulation whatsoever as we were frequently disturbed by loud voices on the corridor, loud banging of doors which made the walls vibrate - we could also clearly hear conversation and snoring from our neighbours.  On 3 of our 4 nights we were kept awake until after 1.00 am by loud voices and mornings wakened from 7.00 am, added to by noise and loud conversation from staff quarters using part of the courtyard.  Needless to say we didn't get much sleep!

We had breakfast on two mornings (for convenience).  However it's not good value for money at 13E with cold watery 'scrambled egg' (looked like the powdered variety) and fatty bacon (also cold). Unless you get there before 9.00 am there's very little of these or cold meat left. We then found a great boulangerie nearby (Boulangerie Utopia) where we got a tasty filling breakfast for half the cost and enjoyed eating it in the lovely gardens on Avenue Richard Lenoir!

However by far the worst part of our stay at Hotel Alhambra was the extremely rude and aggressive behaviour of two Reception managers.  We were quite taken aback one evening upon approaching the Reception our greeting of 'Bon Soir' was responded to with silence and an angry glare by the grey haired older manager.  Our room card was then aggressively banged down on the counter before quickly turning his attention back to his screen - all without a word of acknowledgement!  It was quite clear that we were an inconvenient nuisance - his aggressive behaviour towards us clearly indicated a complete contempt for guests.  

Next morning on Easter Sunday we witnessed a rather shocking incident of the other manager (the one who's carrying some extra baggage) shouting loudly at an English lady in a very aggressive and intimidating manner, not giving her a chance to speak and just repeatedly shouting her down.  It seemed to be over something minor concerning a few euro which could easily be resolved in a calm and professional manner.  In over 30 years travelling all over the world I have never witnessed guests being subjected to a verbal onslaught like this - not even in the cheapest hostels stayed in whilst backpacking in the '80's.  I felt terribly sorry for this lady who was left visibly upset and distressed by this bully - on Easter Sunday!  Unfortunately we had to rush off to collect tickets before a Sunday service at 11.00 so had no time to offer her moral support which I felt bad about!

Hotel Alhambra is not a cheap place to stay in so surely it's not too much to expect to be treated with some courtesy and respect.  Our experience at this hotel definitely tainted our trip to Paris and we were relieved to leave the hotel each day and return as late as possible - rather anxious about the prospect of either of those two individuals being on duty and having to approach them to request our room card!  The atmosphere generated by them seemed more akin to being in a boot camp (not that I've ever previously being in one).  Well not until now!!  

There are numerous other hotels throughout Paris where for the same price you will be treated like a human being - it's not worth having your trip to Paris spoiled by bullies such as these.  I would strongly advise to look elsewhere.

title: Disgraceful
text:
31 of us from London (11 couples and families) stayed in this hotel for 3 nights over Easter as part of a long planned birthday celebration in Paris. When one of our party attempted online to change her pre-paid booking to a different combination of rooms for her family, the hotel refused to allow this. Moreover, they then declared the original booking cancelled, said it was non refundable, and refused even to reinstate that original booking which had already been paid for. In other words, they took 700 euros of her money in exchange for nothing at all, even though she still wanted to stay at the hotel. Needless to say she was not prepared to pay twice over for the same rooms, and therefore she had to pull out of the trip altogether. 

I am sure the Manager will respond to this review by citing the “Applicable Cancellation Policy”.   Our friend meanwhile is pursuing a legal claim against both the hotel and Booking.com. 

Had simple common sense and standard customer goodwill been applied, this unhappy situation could have been avoided. We as a group consider the Alhambra’s handling of this situation absolutely despicable. Sadly, during our stay, it came as no surprise to experience first hand the manager’s many times reported rude and aggressive behaviour, although an assault on one of the guests was certainly beyond anything we were prepared for.

I stayed here for 2 nights with my friend. The hotel looks nothing like the pictures - it is much smaller and barely any space to move around or even unpack in the room.

Secondly the customer service here is the worst I have ever experienced, the manager (don't know his name but around 40s and short hair) is the rudest man I have ever encountered. Also just to add - we asked for our room to be cleaned and left the sign on asking to do so and the room was not cleaned at all.

The only redeeming feature is the location and proximity to the metro. Pick somewhere else and avoid the horrible staff here.

title: A good value hotel
text:
Within easy walking distance of République - indeed, of Gare du Nord, if you’re not carrying too much luggage - this is a good value hotel in a pretty handy location, especially if you are the “flaneur” type (i.e., you love to stroll around the city with no particular aim). You can be in the Marais in around 30 minutes, and the fast-becoming -trendy Canal St Martin area in 15-20 minutes. There is a métro station just around the corner for those less inclined to walk.

The hotel itself is clean, and staff friendly and helpful (with English spoken should you need it). The rooms are reasonably spacious for Paris (renowned for its teenie rooms at the budget end of the scale) and for the price. There are cafés aplenty in the area should you decide not to breakfast at the hotel, or to enjoy an aperitif on the way back to the hotel after a busy day of sightseeing.

Like most hotels, there is a safe luggage space should you need to store your luggage before check in or post check out.

title: Experience trying to cancel due to illness
text:
Booked into Alhambra 8-11.08.18 through booking.com. We Had to cut short our trip due to the need for an emergency appointment for my partner with his eye specialist.
I went on to booking.com to cancel on 04.08 (we appeared to have free cancellation till the 5th).For some reason I could not see how to cancel, although on a previous occasion when I have had to cancel through ill health it has been obvious and simple.
so I thought  that maybe on this occasion I was supposed to cancel directly with the hotel.  I therefore sent them an email apologizing  that I as going to have to cancel due to ill health and would they acknowledge my email, which they did.
On the  6th I went on to booking.com and found that it had not been cancelled, so I cancelled it immediately as this time it was obvious and simple. However I had been charged for all three nights.
I rang booking.com to see if they could help and they immediately rang the hotel to take it up with them ,which I thought was very good service. However he came back to me and said that the hotel had misunderstood my email and thought  that I was only advising them that I was going to cancel and not instructing them to cancel and they were going to stick to the rules and continue to charge me. At this point I was advised to take it up with the hotel. I then rang the hotel where they refused to discuss it with me and put the phone down on me!!
I would have been content to pay the first night as I had cancelled I day late due to a misunderstanding, but I feel that charging me the three nights even if they could under 'the rules' is unfair. Added to which the person I spoke to on the phone was just rude!!

title: Wonderful Stay
text:
Visited Paris for 4 days and stayed at the Alhambra Hotel. This hotel is a smaller hotel with fantastic access to Oberkampf underground subway station only 2 minutes walk away which has access to all subway lines in Paris. Reception check in was simple and easy and we were greeted with a smile. When we booked the room online we asked if we could check in early as we were arriving from Australia at 7am and hoped we could get in to our room to freshen up and have a shower after a 23 hour flight. When we arrived at about 10am the host at reception informed us that our room would be ready in 10mins as requested. This was a massive relief for our arrival and we were very impressed and thankful that our request was honoured. The room we booked was a standard room which had a a garden view and was modern and clean. Bathroom was clean and modern as well. Like most accomodation in Paris the room was small and was suitable for a couple with smaller luggage. Bed was very comfortable with fresh linen. The hotel offers breakfast and there is also a cafe at the end of the street (where the subway entrance is) that is open early at 6am for breakfast for travellers wanting an early start to their day in Paris. The cafe closes after midnight so is good to have a nightcap on the way back to the hotel. The hotel closes its doors at midnight and if you arrive back at the hotel after midnight you simply press a button and you will be let in personally without waiting very long. There are plenty of restaurants, boulangeries and cafes around the area and felt very safe walking at night. 
Loved our stay at Alhambra and would highly recommend staying here as we will be when returning to Paris again.

title: Awful Customer Service
text:
This review regards the reception staff only. As we were not able to actually check in, I cannot review the rooms.  The hotel has a cute lobby and garden. It is also in a prime location. However, the reception and customer service seem to override any promising charms the hotel may have.  

#1DID NOT HONOR OUR RESERVATION: When we arrived we were told that since my sister was staying in the room with me, we would have to pay an additional 79 euro a night (for 7 nights). Please note that I made and paid for these reservations three months in advance and added my sister as an occupant.  - To some degree this may be the fault of the booking company. Thier site advertises that it's two adults for each room. The hotel says that it's incorrect information. However, they have contracted with the booking site. And we even showed them how all the other booking sites don't charge for two people in one room.   

   #2 RUDE: I know, nowhere in the hospitality bible does it say you have to have a heart, but these people shouldn't be anywhere near the word hospitality. My sister and I are two young women, alone in a foreign city. We paid for a room three months in advance, that they would not allow us to check into. We dissolved into a fit of tears in their lobby. We tried to talk to them to see if we could negotiate something, anything since this was our accommodation for the next week.  We called the booking site (who they refuse to talk to) a total of five times. It was a sad state of affairs. And the staff would not listen to ANYONE! 

  #3 BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE: The way they treated us was reprehensible. I don't think I have ever had customer service this bad in my life. And I've been to a lot of different places. I could have taken it by myself, but this is my sister's first trip abroad. This was her introduction to Europe, France, Paris. Suffice it is to say, it wasn't a great first impression. So what do I mean:
 -Shouting 
-Bullying 
-Cutting us off -
Not listening to reason or even proof 
And then smiling at us and saying there was nothing they could or would do.  Then when we tried to explain that the error was not ours but theirs, they rebuffed us and shouted us down.

 I was really grateful that I had travel insurance with the booking company.  They were able to were able to cancel, get a refund, and then find us last minute accommodations. Unfortunately, it was a bit stressful and traumatizing to be treated thus.  In the end we had a wonderful trip in Paris.

  I would never, ever recommend this hotel to anyone unless...they got rid of or retrained the entire staff. It is a shame because it really seemed like a cute establishment. But there's nothing in the world that would allow me to stay in a place where customer service was this horrific.

Stay at your own risk. Any questions or disagreements may be met with hostility.  I would advise the owners to find different staff. When the staff makes the business look bad, it may be time to reevaluate the arrangement.

text:

Breakfast is a self serve continental affair; croissants, bread, ham, cheese, home made jam, cereals, fruit and of course tea/coffee/juices.

The staff here are very welcoming and helpful and always on hand 24 hours a day.

All in all a perfect place to explore the delights of Paris but without having to pay huge amounts of money.

I would certainly return here on my next visit.

title: A quick stop in Paris.
text:
We chose to spend 1 night in this hotel during a quick stop in Paris. We wanted to be close to the local attractions and Hotel Korner seemed like a great option due price and location. 

When we arrived (at around 10pm) we were greeted by a friendly chap who offered us drinks and got us quickly checked in. Although tiny, this hotel does have a lift where myself and my girlfriend managed to squeeze ourselves and our two suitcases in. We noticed as we walked in that the room smelt clean and fresh and looked modern and appealing. The room as a whole was small however all the necessities were there including a hanging rail, a desk, a fan and an en-suite. The en-suite was small but had a good sized shower with a good head. The only negative was the distance between the tap and the basin was so small that I found it hard to wash my hands sufficiently. 

THe room also had a double opening window with a Juliette balcony. The street had many restaurants and supermarkets close by. There was also a metro station 5 minutes away and around a 15 minute walk to the Eiffel Tower. 

Although we hadn’t pre-booked breakfast, in the mourning we decided to give it a go for convenience. The breakfast area was small and located in the main reception however there was ample space for the number of guests. There were a selection of breads, pastries, cereals, fruits, yoghurts, meats, cheese and boiled eggs. There were also various jams and spread as well as a nespresso machine. The area was very clean and quiet. 

If we are to return we wouldn’t hesitate in booking your hotel again and would definitely recommend to our friends and family. It’s a shame we only got to spend one night there. Your hotel deserves more than it’s 2 star rating! Thank you!

text:
Advantages
-Hotel located close to the metro station (2 minutes walk)
-The room has a pretty big washroom
-Helpful staff

Disadvantages
-Rooms are extremely small. A twin room will be suitable only for one person. For two will be not that convenient

-We didn’t buy a breakfast because it was a bit expensive to pay 9 Euro for a poor one
-It is far from The Eiffel tower really. It took us at least 25 minutes to reach the tower with fast walking. It is tiring to walk this way. Maybe better to use transportation. 
Overall, I doubt if I ever would stay there again as you feel like not in a hotel, but in a corner, same as the name of it.

title: Very nice small, central hotel...(better than many 3 Star)
text:
Fantastic budget hotel, DO NOT be put off by the 2 Star rating, this hotel is better than a lot of 3 star (and some 4 star) hotels I have stayed in.

Brilliant location a 5 minute walk from the Seine (Rue Linois) and a 15-20 minute walk from Tour Eiffel with a Metro station (Charles Michels) only a few hundred meters away. 

Lots of bars, brasseries within a 2 minute walk from the hotel.

The hotel is small and some rooms have a slightly unusual layout but its meticulously clean and with excellent service from very friendly staff, perfectly adequate for a short stay in the center of Paris.

In case you are wondering, you CANNOT see Tour Eiffel from here!! (its 1.6km away), maybe there is some link to Alexandre Gustave Eiffel though...

From Gare du Nord take M4 (line 4) towards Odeon, change at Odeon and take Line 10 to Charles Michels (25 minutes/EUR 1.90)

title: We will be happy to come back on our next Paris trip
text: The hotel corresponds to the many very positive reviews represented here. It is very well maintained, clean, modern, but retains a friendly and welcoming flair. The staff are the warmest I have ever experienced in a hotel of this category. However, the whole atmosphere does not seem forced, but honest through and through. You feel well taken care of and almost at home in this hotel from the first moment. We had a deluxe room and would also recommend this. Because compared to other hotels in Paris, this one is really spacious and has all the necessary and desirable comforts you could ask for in a hotel room. A flat screen TV, a king size bed with lots of blankets and pillows, a bathtub (at least in our room) and two sinks, great amenities - all extremely clean and in a quiet location - what more could you ask for. We can't say anything about the breakfast as we didn't consume it. The hotel also has a spa area with hammam. Despite the quiet location, the connection to public transport is very good and the hotel is very well located. All in all, an absolute recommendation!

title: Lovely summer city break
text: Excellent stay from beginning to end , the hotel is about 15 mins walk from Gare Luxembourg RER line B, quite handy as the train runs direct from Charles de Gaulle airport, costs about 10 euros per person each way. Its also very close to Notre Dame des Champs and  Vavin metro stations. The hotel is located on a very quiet side street in the 6th arrondissement. We found all the staff very helpful, particularly Martin who welcomed us on arrival , speaking in both French and English. We had a superior room which was spacious for Paris . The room was very clean, beds were very comfortable , shower was great, breakfast offered a selection of cereals , fruits, meats and cheese as well as eggs, bacon and mushrooms.  The hotel is just around the corner, five mins walk from Montparnasse with a good selection of restaurants , Golden dragon , is well worth a mention. and is very popular. If you're planning on seeing the main sights it's about a 30 min flat walk to the Seine /Musee Dorsay area , about 40 mins to the Louvre, however there is always the option of the metro which would reduce the time. Would certainly recommend and be happy to stay again

The location was a little out of the way if you want to walk to most places but ok if you take the metro. We usually walk everywhere so found it a little frustrating (and tiring) to need to walk a fair way before arriving into the area we wanted to visit (Seine River, Champs Elysee, Notre Dame) . This resulted in walking 10 - 14kms a day. It was a reasonably straight forward walk to Musee D'Orsay. I realised that the 6th Arrondissement covers a large area and most sights are quite close to the river. 

That said, this hotel is close to an excellent street full of crepe restaurants.

title: Hidden Gem
text:
I booked this hotel based on TripAdvisor reviews and the overall ranking in Paris, so my expectations were probably high going into it.  Yet, Hotel le Six exceeded my expectations in every way.  
The staff was friendly, attentive, helpful and always available.
The room was very comfortable and had plenty of room for us to be comfortable.  The beds were comfy (even the pull-out couch), and the bathroom even had a heated towel rack.
I had booked without breakfast thinking we may want to explore boulangeries, but after seeing it on the first morning, we wanted to eat at the hotel every day.  It was bountiful and delicious.  And again, the staff was very attentive and kept everything fresh.
The lobby/breakfast area is lovely and very relaxing.  We loved the infused water kept on the bar 24/7.
Bottom line - strongly recommend!!

title: Le Six - Great Paris Hotel

The room was smallish, but was modern, well appointed with comfortable beds and had a great shower with L’Occitane bath products. Also, great air conditioning which was lacking a little in our first hotel. The staff was the best - friendly and helpful. Was near a bakery that became a favorite of ours for croissants - Thevenin (not to be missed). Also, many locals go there for their daily bread, dessert and pastries. We will definitely be back here when visiting Paris!

title: Hotel Le Six was a perfect Paris experience.
text:
I found out about Le Six from TravelZoo and I couldn’t be happier about the decision and experience. I am fairly picky and always read reviews but never write them but feel compelled because there are so many options in Paris and want to help highlight this gem. This was my 2nd trip there and this hotel not only surpassed my last trips and by far the best hotel I’ve encountered on my 2 week European trip. Blew England out of the water and I’m glad this is how I ended my trip. From staff to room I have excellent things to say.  I couldn’t be happier to recommend Hotel Le Six. We had breakfast included and it was perfect getting the basics out of the way in the morning to prepare for a full day of walking and eating out. 

Room: 
Gorgeous wood floors and multiple full sized windows! It was quiet enough to open the windows, and equipped if I needed the AC which I did not but it’s worth having and should be a must when choosing a hotel. What’s more important for me is how clean and soothing it was in terms of style and decor. The layout and tall ceilings felt like an apartment, really has a Parisian style and that’s what you want in Paris.  I mean how many places can you take a deep bath and open a ceiling tall window for a peaceful breeze…really enhanced the vacation experience after a long day of sightseeing. Comfy bed-check. Nespresso machine-check. Excellent hair dryer and well thought out location to plug it in-check. Giant towels-check. Umbrellas to borrow-check. Superior toiletries-check check check, L’Occitane! 

Location:
This hotel really enhanced my trip to Paris.  In advance they will reach out via email to see what information will be helpful during your stay from types of eateries to how to get around. It’s a very short block from the metro which we learned how to use and used the entire time. Just use your phones “maps” to map your destination and you will easily figure out which metro to get you around. You are in walking distance to some fantastic destinations like Luxembourg Gardens and like so many areas of Paris I find you can either walk to some of it or just figure out which Metros to take and save the Ubers for when you are super tired to deal with any of it. 

Staff: 
Each and every hotel member we encountered were so knowledgeable, helpful and kind, from day to late night team. I was never I intimidated  to ask for help. They helped us to call a cab to the airport and walked us to our car carrying an umbrella over us as it was raining. Tip: they will help you book a private car to the airport and I recommend you do this the day before to ease your mind. They even guided me to the local pharmacy where I could get a Covid test prior to the airport (within a blocks walk)…the pharmacy took it from there.

title: Excellent stay - great hospitality.
text:
I stayed at Hotel Six recently -- and so glad I did. I was on a group trip in Paris, and extended my stay, opting to switch hotels for the last few days I was there on my own. I arrived at the hotel, and out of precaution prior to meeting a friend for dinner decided to take a COVID test. I had no symptoms, but to my surprise tested positive. So began my quarantine at the Hotel Le Six. The team was so incredibly understanding and helpful. I received room service breakfast that was absolutely incredible each day, and the team helped bring my other deliveries and room service needs up to my door so I never needed to leave my room. They made sure I was taken care of to ensure that I was comfortable and easily able to follow all safety measures - which I can assure you they communicated clearly and are very strict about!

The rooms are beautiful with lots of space compared to most French hotels, with windows to open for fresh air and nice clean bathtubs if you enjoy a good soak. Also smart TVs that made binging on Netflix easy while I was stuck. I had splurged a bit to stay at the hotel, but so glad I did because of all the time I spent there. It really felt like a relaxing vacation despite my circumstances.

Because I was in my room all day I was also a witness somewhat to all of the cleaning going on in the other rooms -- and I believe that they are quite thorough based on what I could hear. They also extended my stay quite easily, especially toward the end when I wasn't sure day to day if I would be able to fly home or not.

I HIGHLY recommend staying here, and hope that if you do that you are able to see more of Paris than I did! If you are unlucky like me, you can take heart that you will have the greatest hospitality and are in good hands with the team at Hotel Le Six.

We checked in early and left our bags with the bellhop - and when the room was ready or bags were waiting for us. Hotel staff arranged transportation to the airport and assisted beyond our requests. The hotel design is lovely and the neighborhood feel cannot be beat. If (when) we come back to Paris this is at the top of our list!

title: Great 2-Bedroom Apartment & Excellent Location
text:
We had an enormous apartment (by Parisian standards) with 2 comfortable bedrooms. The living and dining area was ample and well decorated, and the kitchen had a refrigerator, Nespresso coffeemaker, kettle, dishwasher and washing machine/dryer. 

What we really liked about this hotel is the location.  Situated in the heart of the Latin Quarter, Blvd Saint Germain is busy, buzzing with activities and sights and sounds.  The residence is just a few minutes' walk away to great restaurants, cafes and famous sights, including Jardin du Luxembourg (the Luxembourg Gardens).  The Metro Odeon is nearby.  A really lovely neighbourhood! 

Hotel staff were friendly and really helpful. They generally don't speak too much English but we spoke intermediate French, enough to communicate fine with them. We were met with the Metro strike on the second day of our stay, and the staff taught us to walk to the major monuments (20 minutes walk to Saint Chapelle and Le Marais) and he also advised us to download the Uber app in case we needed transportation which was super. 

All in all, we had a fabulous stay!

Highly recommend this hotel.

title: Location and Convenience
text:
We enjoyed a comfortable stay at Le Prince Regent in early July and would highly recommend this hotel for families travelling to Paris. 
Our 3 bedroom apartment was well presented, comfortable and had the bonus of being serviced daily. For a mother of 3 children there is nothing better than having your bed made daily. Coffee machine, air-conditioning (not always a given in Paris) and really comfortable beds made our stay even more enjoyable. The washing machine was also appreciated after 2 weeks of traveling in Greece. 
The location is exceptional, less than 5 minutes to Luxembourg Gardens and a short 8 minute walk to Rue De Buci (favourite restaurants and gelato shop).. There is a variety of food options within 100m of the hotel,  ranging from Japanese, Italian and traditional French. 
The staff were extremely helpful and hospitable, they organised babysitters for us at night and executed any task I gave them.

We will definitely be staying at Le Prince Regent should we return to Paris in the years to come.

title: Fabulous accommodation!
text:
We stayed as a family group of 6 for 4 nights and loved it. Great location in a quiet street just off the thoroughfare. Plenty cafes, restaurants, shops and bars nearby. Also handy for the metro and RER.

Very spacious by Parisian standards with 2 bedrooms, a large lounge area with bed settee, fully fitted and equipped kitchen, dining area, bathroom, further toilet and a balcony.

There’s a mini bar in the full sized fridge, a dishwasher and a washing machine. Even a kettle and teapot for us Brits, brilliant touch!

Spotlessly clean. TV in lounge and both bedrooms. Air con throughout.

There’s also a spa area though it was expensive so we didn’t try that.

The apartment was fairly pricey, though not bad by city centre standards and certainly worth it.

Staff friendly too.

Watch out for the tiny lift if you’re claustrophobic as the inner doors slide shut quickly like teeth closing!

title: Everything Good to Say
text:
This was my 10th trip to Paris. I already knew St. Germaine is the place to stay in Paris, and have had a variety of experiences with accommodations in StG. It's close to the main museums, other key sites, jazz, has a great cafe culture and not far from the river.

Residence & Spa Le Prince Regent is hands-down the best pick in St. Germaine.

I hesitate to review the hotel because I fear I'll never be able to find a room available!

First, I'll say that what I seek in a hotel is a comfortable room, clean and conveniently located. It's less important to me to have a bunch of staff bugging me for something to do and I refuse to eat any meal other than an occasional breakfast at a hotel restaurant.

The rooms are remarkably large as compared to other hotels in Paris. There's a fully-equipped kitchenette, small sitting area with table and a king bed in the sleeping area. By comparison, most Paris hotels have barely space to store your slippers by the time they get the bed wedged into the room. The bathroom's modern and clean.

The whole property has a quiet, boutique feeling to it, set on a side street, so quite peaceful. It's a home away from home in Paris. Friendly front desk staff and prompt, meticulous housekeeping. There's a clothes washer in the kitchen (whaat?! nice!) or a laundromat next door if you're staying for a while.

No restaurant - but they've made arrangements for room service from a nearby place. You really should be eating in the Vietnamese, French, Japanese, Chinese and Italian places that are no more than 50 steps from the front door of the hotel.

Or go to Jazz at Le Petit Journal or Chez Papa 5 minutes away in opposite directions. Or grocery shop at the full-on Monoprix market around the corner and eat in the room.

Take a walk in the Luxemborg Palace garden a three-minute walk away (be sure to check out the "second Statue of Liberty" in the garden.

You get the point. Great hotel by all measures I care about.

Finally found a home in St. Germaine. We'll be back.

description: "An unique view in the heart of Paris" The Hôtel Brighton, built on Rue de Rivoli by Lord Egerton at the beginning of the 19th century, became one of the capital’s leading hotels, attracting many British customers. This district of Paris, which is now the 1st arrondissement, was very popular with British clients on The Grand Tour, an initiatory trip across Europe and sometimes as far as Asia with the aim of completing the artistic and cultural education of the young middle classes. The hotel has preserved a large number of antique elements down the years, beginning with the period mosaic with the words "Hôtel Brighton" on the ground beneath the arcades of Rue de Rivoli in front of the hotel. Inside, the marble columns in the hall, the sculpted high reliefs in the bar, the set of antique mirrors and the many French windows, the tall ceilings on the "noble floors" and the exposed beams in the rooms on the upper storeys all bear witness to the history of the site and the people who gave it its charm. But what makes the Hôtel Brighton a truly exceptional place is the breathtaking 180° panorama. To the left, the Louvre, once a royal palace, today a museum, the Tuileries Gardens opposite and the Place de la Concorde to the right with the Eiffel Tower in the background. One of your best memories of Paris will be this unique view.

title: Disappointed about not being informed....
text: Very good hotel overall, but we were not told that our room (#10) was actually under the arcade that surrounds to hotel.  So there was no view at all of the Tuileries, just a very restricted view that did not even really include de Rue Rivoli itself.  People booking should be told they would be put into these rooms on the mezzanine floor since it effectively provides no view at all.  Not being told is just very poor business practice--and reinforced somewhat the feeling that the hotel is cutting corners just to make extra money from tourists.  Our room was #10.  Avoid.  Also, there seems to be some room above Room #10 that is being used for housekeeping that woke us up a few times--nothing particularly annoying but still, for 500 euros a night one shouldn't have to deal with this--or at least, once again, be told in advance....

text:

title: Great stay for a great value!
text: Hotel Brighton is located on Rue de Rivoli, across from Tuileries Garden, which means you have quick access to the Tuileries Metro station, the Louvre to the east, Place de la Concorde to the west, Rue Saint Honore on the north, and Musee D'Orsay to the south. What better location is that! What I also found interesting was that there are a lot of hotels in the area, notably a popular five-star hotel that charges more than 1000 Euros a night, and yet Hotel Brighton has all the benefits of location, friendly staff, and comfortable rooms without the five-star prices. So many attraction are within walking distance, and close access to the metro is a big plus. Of note, Musee D'Orsay (only about a 10-15 minute walk across Tuileries Garden) has a RER train station which I used to go to Versailles. I decided to treat myself and get the deluxe room facing Tuileries garden, and I was placed on the top floor with a gorgeous view and balcony. In addition, the staff were very friendly and always offered assistance when needed. Breakfast was a bit steep in price, but that's the price you pay for convenience, especially since some of the mornings I was there, it was raining and I didn't feel like going out. Thank you to everyone at Hotel Brighton for making me feel welcome and safe in Paris.

The hotel is small but charming. We stayed in the Louvre suite and the view of Paris took our breath away. The bathroom is very large esp for Europe and our teenagers loved the speakers in the bathroom. The closet and storage space was very good as well. I will definitely stay here in the future. Thank you, Hotel Brighton, for making our stay a delight!
name: Hotel Brighton - Esprit de France
description: "An unique view in the heart of Paris" The Hôtel Brighton, built on Rue de Rivoli by Lord Egerton at the beginning of the 19th century, became one of the capital’s leading hotels, attracting many British customers. To the left, the Louvre, once a royal palace, today a museum, the Tuileries Gardens opposite and the Place de la Concorde to the right with the Eiffel Tower in the background. One of your best memories of Paris will be this unique view.

title: Great location but tired
text: Great location and I’m sure the views are wonderful if you have a room overlooking the jardin des Tuileries.  I didn’t. Service was hit and miss. And it all lacks ambience not helped by a characterless front communal area.  It’s all a bit tired and not good value.

title: Location, location, location
text:
This was my second visit to this lovely, charming hotel. The location is its best part. It isolated just 5 minutes walk from Champs-Élysées and 3 min walk from metro station, Argentine on probably Paris's most famous metro line. This is a small hotel; nothing fancy. It serves only breakfast (very modest, but filling). No lunch or dinner is served as the hotel has no restaurants. But there are ample of restaurants in Paris and nearby too. 

Rooms are small, but decent enough. Can accommodate two people, but not with a kid or two kids. But rooms are very well - maintained and bathrooms are well stocked up too. Quality of bed and pillows are good. Good housekeeping and kitchen staff..

The hotel's manager is Zoheir Tchouar. He is now the hotel's director. In 2013 when I had visited, he was the front desk manager. It was so good to meet him after 9 years. Zoheir knows everything about Paris. He is your best guide to Paris. Extremely humble person and feels nice to see him when you walk into the hotel; you know you are in good hands. He is in charge of this hotel. 

Other staff was also nice, particularly Ms Sylwia who was extremely knowledgable and patient with my queries. Special thanks to my friend Andre and Micheal also was good. 

The only bad point of this hotel is one particular staff member; i think his name was Fabio. He was a very rude man. He did my checking-in and it was very unpleasant to meet him after enduring a 6-hour train journey from Amsterdam as the train was delayed by 4 hours. I had to rush for an event, and I was really late because of the train delay. So I was a bit fumbled when I reached the hotel and tried searching for the hotel reservation in my phone. Meanwhile, he asked my name twice, but since I was a bit shaken up, i didn't hear him clearly. He shouted: "I AM ASKING YOU YOUR NAME AND YOU ARE LOOKING INTO YOUR MOBILE PHONE??" 

He was extremely unhelpful and un-coperative. He did not even guide me about the proper transport / train pass I should buy. He said to me: "YOU NEED TO GO STATION TO ASK THAT QUESTION." Then, Ms Sylwia was present and she later on helped me a lot after Fabio left the hotel for the day. Thankfully, he comes to the hotel only over weekends. If such an employee were to be working in any Indian hotel, he would get sacked immediately. 

Other than this rude person, this hotel was great, I would highly recommend it. The location is so convenient that you can keep coming and going to this hotel several times in the day if you wish to come back to your room for some mid-day rest or something. 

TIP: Book directly at the website for the best price. Take the Rue St Ferdinand street view room. And preferably on a higher floor.

He clearly enjoys his work and can't wait to help and sort things out for you. Moreover, he can explain you where to go and how and share valuable tips in something like 15 (fifteen!!) languages (7 fluent and another 8 at acceptable level), always wearing a nice and warm smile under his moustaches. His kindness is well worth another star and your visit, especially if you are new in town and you want to make the most out of it.

title: A Lovely Experience.
text: Our tour company booked the hotel for us for two nights before we embarked on a Battlefields Tour of France and Belgium. Apparently we were supposed to be at the huge hotel a couple of streets away. What a stroke of good luck for us. We arrived early after a very long fight from Australia. We received a really warm welcome, being offered comfortable chairs and complimentary coffee/tea in the foyer. The very friendly man in reception checked us in within 30 minutes. Our room wasn't huge but nicely appointed, in a classic french style. There were fully opening french windows looking out on to a narrow street just 800 metres from the Arc De Triomphe. There were many restaurants and bars nearby and even a supermarket across the road. The breakfast room was compact but beautifully decorated and the food was really good. All of the staff we encountered were really friendly and happy to help with anything we needed. If you are looking for modern, shiny and new this is not the place but if you are after a cosy, boutique hotel in Paris look no further than this one.

title: Put Off by Badly Stained Carpet
text:
Let me start by acknowledging that other travellers will have had different experiences from what we had at this hotel.  I understand that others may be willing to tolerate some things in a hotel that my wife and I won't tolerate.  Cleanliness is a must - lack of it is a deal-breaker for us.
We booked the Saint Ferdinand from a Travelzoo offer - it looked fine and the price was good.  The pics looked ok and a google streetview I did seemed ok as well.
We arrived as scheduled but that is where the good time ended.  We checked in and were given room #303.  This is a small hotel - the rooms are not that big, the hallways not much wider than one person and the elevator was just big enough for us and our luggage.
Room 303 is a small room but that wasn't the problem.  The problem was the badly stained carpet on both sides and the foot of the bed.  Trust me when I say, I am not talking about just two or three stains - this was badly stained.  In my opinion, any reasonable hotel manager would have replaced it long ago or at the very least,  not rented the room with the carpet in that condition.
For us, the next question was - just what does this mean for the cleanliness of the rest of the room?  We sat there contemplating our next move - do we stay and put up with this, ask for another room or get out of there all together.  We just couldn't get over the stained carpet so we opted to book elsewhere.  When we returned to the reception desk, George ( a nice guy) was rather shocked when we told him what the problem was.  He conferred with a lady whom I believe was a manager and she offered to find us another room.  We declined again mentioning the stained carpet and said we'd already booked elsewhere (which we had thanks to Hotels.com).  George called us a taxi and we got out of there asap!

Two things I've wondered about since:
1)  why would a hotel not replace carpet that badly stained?
2)  how can they promote themselves as 3 or 4 star (don't recall which it was) when they have even one room as bad as #303 was?

I can't answer these questions but I can suggest to all travellers that they should avoid the Saint Ferdinand or if they do want to stay there, do some research first and tell them no to room 303.

Also note in an effort to be fair to the hotel, I have emailed them twice since returning home regarding our experience - NO response has been received.

So there you have it!  This was our experience at this hotel and I am happy to end by saying the hotel we moved to was a true 5 star hotel and we were able to end our vacation in comfort ....and cleanliness!

title: Good location, lovely staff, shame about the noise
text: This is a small hotel which is located a few minutes walk from the Argentine Metro and only five-10 mins from Arc de Triomphe. There is a Carrefour supermarket across the road from the hotel which is good for getting supplies. There are also a variety of restaurants, shops and a bakery  nearby but sadly in August, a large majority were closed for holidays. The staff are really helpful and can’t do enough for you especially Georges. The beds are comfy and the rooms are a good size and nicely decorated.  WiFi is free and worked fine when my family used it and there is a safe in the room also. The breakfast had a good selection of juices, pastries, yogurts, fruit, cold meats and cheeses and sometimes pancakes. Scrambled and boiled eggs were available along with sausages. The lady who runs the breakfast service kindly provided decaf coffee and toast on request. She was rushed off her feet and could’ve done with help as the tables were always waiting to be cleared when we came down to breakfast and she struggled to keep up with demand. Unfortunately I had to invest in earplugs after not being able to sleep for most of my first night due to the road noise outside and also noise inside the hotel itself. The double glazing is not sufficient when mopeds and delivery trucks are driving by in the night and also the plumbing in the hotel needs updating as if someone flushed a loo, the cistern could be heard filing back up for around ten minutes each time and sounded like a hairdryer on high speed. Soft close fittings to the doors and wardrobes would also stop the banging from other guests rooms. I did enjoy my stay but for light sleepers I’d suggest you seek alternative accommodation or bring earplugs! The keycards didn’t work on quite a few occasions also which meant a walk down the stairs to reception. There was no ironing board or fridge in the room which for a 4 star hotel I would’ve expected. There were free drinks in the lobby (rather than the cheese and wine that had swayed us to book this hotel after reading other reviews)  however no decaf available and the honesty bar wasn’t stocked very well so we bought our drinks across the road at the very reasonable Carrefour, which doesn’t shut until 11pm. With a few tweaks this could be a great hotel but if I returned to Paris I wouldn’t stay again regrettably because a good nights sleep for me is an absolute must!

title: Chicago Guy in Paris
text: As everyone else states, the rooms are tiny, almost dormlike.  Traveled with my wife, ended up staying here as many reviewers commented on the rooftop bar and 2nd floor outdoor space as well as your not in the room all that much.  Stayed 3 nights, which was too long in this small of a room.  Showering/getting ready to go out, etc became a challenge with just my wife and I.  First night it was kinda cute, 2nd night ok, and by the 3rd, became a little tiresome.  Everything else, service, staff, location, etc are great.  The bed was comfortable, it was just too small of a room with little storage/place to put luggage or clothes.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Relax and Shopping Trip
text: very convenient and easy trip including successful hotel choice. The location is marvelous achieved all of my business needs and family shopping requirements. If I am going to visit Paris again which in the near future ! definitely I will choose the same hotel I stayed IN this time.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great Location with Pleasant Experience!
text: We would highly recommend staying at citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees!  The location is right around the corner from the Champs-Elysees; however, the hotel was extremely quiet for the entire week we were there.  We loved the staff, and felt like our business was appreciated.  They were very pleasant and approachable whenever we had questions.  As far as the room, it was quite small, but we really only slept there so that was not a negative at all.  Most importantly, the bed was extremely comfortable and it was fun being able to operate the electrical system with the i-Pad!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great room but small if 2 people
text: Loved the tech, friendly staff, great overall decor. Room was barely big enough for 1 person, but had to put my suitcase on the bed, no rack or place to put it. Recommend, but ask about room size if >1 person.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Expensive, but great hotel. Rooms very small.
text: I loved this hotel! Superb location right in Champs Elysee. The hotel is very modern, nicely decorated, with a rooftop with a view of Effeil Tour! Staff is very friendly. Cafeteria 24 hours. Rooms are very comfortable, HOWEVER, very small! If you have a large suitcase, this hotel is not for you. If you have two small suitcases you will also have problems! The rooms are only 14mts. For that, I found the hotel quite expensive.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: An amazing place to stay right at the centre of things
text: Amazing location. Great room - remember they are small but perfect. Very clean great breakfast. Brilliant staff and the location is really amazing. Rooms are app controlled and the check in and check out was so easy.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Magnificent location fantastic staff
text: Checking in is extremely easy, stuff is amazing, do you speak various languages. Location is extremely convenient, I cannot emphasize this more it’s location it’s fantastic. You can walk from there to many places and you have a subway station within five minute walk. I will definitely go back on stay at the CitizenM
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: CitizenM does it again!
text:
This was our second stay at a CitizenM hotel and the first at the hotel Champs Elysées. Fantastic experience from check in to check out. Location was perfect and had easy access to the metro system allowing us to tour parts of the city that were a little too far on foot. Staff were really friendly and had great local knowledge when it came to places to eat/drink and visit. 

The roof top terrace is definitely worth a visit as it has a nice view over looking part of the Champs Elysées and the Eiffel Tower which of an evening is great to sit back and enjoy a few drinks from.

Having stayed in the the New York CitizenM, the fantastic experience at this hotel was exactly the same if not better. Id highly recommend this hotel for either business or pleasure visits.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great place, great location, great people and very clean
text: The CitizenM is a great location on the Champs-Elysees. The staff were very friendly and it was very clean. Please note: the rooms are very tiny but they make up for it in all of the public spaces. I would definitely recommend this hotel for a single person or a couple. No more than 2 people to a room.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great place!
text: Our second trip to this great hotel! Really friendly and helpful staff. Lovely and clean, and the food and drink was great too. The terrace is a really nice spot to take a moment with a coffee. Looking forward to returning!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great place, great location, great people and very clean
text: This is a great place, great location, great people and very clean. Please note: the rooms are very very tiny. Just understand this when booking so you are not surprised. The cleanliness, staff and public spaces all make up for the small rooms. Say hello to Zac from Alabama. :-)
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Terrific Experience
text: The staff is unbelievably helpful, friendly and nice! the hotel is like home you do not want to leave even in Paris and food was surprisingly yummy! Thank you to the CitizenM team - Can't wait to come back!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: A great experience in the heart of paris!
text:
I really enjoyed my stay with my cousin at this hotel, a modern and beautifully designed hotel with friendly staff.
The lobby, the furniture, the accessories, the colorful ambiance, make this hotel really special.
It really worth the price, the rooms are small but comfortable and clean and cosy.
Definitely will come back everytime I want to stay in paris.
The location, the design, cleanliness, staff and service all great!
Thank you citizenm!
It was a pleasure 😊
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Excellent Choice
text: Excellent location, walking distance to cafes and high end stores. Walk friendly location. Very clean rooms, well maintained and friendly/professional staff. Layout and design of the room is perfect for travelling couples.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Wowzer
text: City center not to far off the beaten path conveniently located near metro stations, shopping and fine dining!!! It was an absolute splendid experience that I would recommend to all my family and friends. The staff is above professional and friendly, they will absolutely treat you with dignity and respect! 10/10 recommend again and again and again!!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: A pleasant stay with a modern twist
text: This was my first time staying at a citizenM hotel and I absolutely loved it! The vibe is so modern, chic and I love how the lobby looks like a living room. The breakfast is delicious, as are the drinks but it's really the staff that makes the hotel stand out. I can't say enough good things about how we were treated on this trip. Nelle and Mahendiran, big shout out to you for being so nice, accommodating and fun! Def will come back when I'm in Paris again soon.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Very good hotel recommendable
text: It was a perfect experience to stay at this hotel for four nights. The staffs were very kind and friendly, and is was a family atmosphere. The room is comfortable and effectively structured, and the food of the breakfast was very good. I would like to recommend to any traveler to stay at this hotel and I will absolutely use this hotel when I come again in Paris.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great location
text:
I was a few days with my daughter in Paris. The location of the hotel is perfect, just a few steps near the Champs Elysees. Clean rooms and very friendly staff. Food is good, nice drinks. 
Would recommend the hotel.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Top notch affordable hotel
text: Great location, great service, affordable, friendly ambassadors fantastic stay, right next to the metro and centrally located to walk to a number of sites, with the added advantage of shopping on one of the best streets in Paris. Great view of the Eiffel Tower too from the roof top terrace. Had the best iced coffee in Paris!!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: great place
text:
excellent hotel right in the heart of paris. Easy to get around, walking and they were great when we needed a cab with the system that they have at the hotel.
We knew the rooms were small but they are extremely efficient as we knew we would be there to mainly sleep, We had small carry on luggage which was fine, but it we had big suit cases it may have been too tight
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Outstandingly location and staff
text: Love the quirkiness and individuality of Citizen M hotels. Tour de France final weekend, the city was buzzing and CloudM rooftop bar gave us a great view of the proceedings. Staff are so friendly and helpful, really do make your stay special.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Brilliant hotel in an amazing location
text: Stayed here for one night on business, and was so impressed. Great bedrooms, very helpful and friendly staff and the design in the hotel is so quirky and cool. I would highly recommend the CitizenM, certainly a brand I will look out for.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Perfect - Seriously
text: I have had my share of drab cookie-cutter hotel rooms where I am treated like a number and worse.  This experience changed everything for me.  I am a fan forever.  I was respected, cared for and the room was superb.  I slept like a baby and that is saying something because I very rarely sleep in hotel rooms.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Paris Business Trip
text: Love the tech and efficiency of this hotel, and in a great location.  Pizza was not bad, rooftop bar was really enjoyable.  Staff is extremely friendly and helpful, even though most things are automated.  The app is the best I've seen with all the functionality it has.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Excellent location and great breakfast
text: You cannot turn off the A/C in the rooms and the rooms are so small - the rooms are not really ideal for a family trip, mostly for couples or for 1 person travel. The location is great and so is the breakfast. Service is the best.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Very central location
text: A great hotel in the heart of the 8th district.  Rooms are rather small with very little storage space, but otherwise good and comfy and loaded with gadgets. Breakfast is good and the common areas are delightful...feels like home.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great location and service
text:
Great location. Staff are very friendly, professional and helpful!
Room is nice, clean and cozy and the bed is very comfortable.
The lobby has multiple indoor and outdoor areas filled with comfortable chairs and tables to enjoy.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Greta stay ruined by incorrect double charge of room
text:
The hotel was in an excellent location. Walking distance for shopping, Uber and taxi accessible. Excellent restaurants around the area. Monoprix in front where you can get essentials. Rooms very high tech iPad controlled everything. Lobby was great. Also upstairs had area where you can actually see the Eiffel Tower. 
If not for the fact that I got double charged for the room I would rate this hotel 5 star.
I booked everything via Expedia and the hotel incorrectly charged my credit card again. When I contacted Expedia the hotel did a refund but maybe because of the currency exchange the refund was less 25 dollars. So I essentially lost 25 dollars because of their mistake. Trying to contact my bank but this is wasting too much of my time cause now my bank is asking for more information. It’s only 25 dollars but it’s the principle of losing money without receiving any service or goods.
Beware of the taxi they use too. Even though it is supposed to be flat rate of 53 euros to go to the airport the driver asked for 59 euros. I did not even bother arguing.
Aside from the fiasco of the double hotel charge it could have been a very excellent stay.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees
text: Excellent service, nice F&B and outstanding breakfast & bar offerings. Rooms are very small which was disappointing but you can always come down to the lobby to do your extra work. Check-in and Check-out is super high-tech as they have self processing machines ready on the spot!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Nice -- great location!
text: Very nice hotel. Tiny rooms (as I find in most European hotels.) The room was overly techy, and it just made for unnecessary complication and a TV that did not work for our entire stay. The location is perfect for the Metro, food, shopping, sights.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Outstanding hotel
text: Best hotel I’ve stayed in for a long long time. Staff were so helpful and friendly, room was spotless, and really useful interactive interface with the app letting you control lighting, climate, blinds etc completely remotely. Fantastic view of the Eiffel Tower from the rooftop terrace, ideal location just off Champs Elysees, 5 min walk from two Metro stations. Would definitely stay here again, and look forward to trying out some of the other CitizenM hotels out there!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Disappointed
text: Nice location!  Very small room lacking adequate storage. Nice shower. Mostly helpful, pleasant staff. However, was asked to leave the lobby area because I had a Starbucks drink I purchased outside.  In all my years of world travel I’ve never been asked to leave a lobby because I hadn’t purchased my coffee at the hotel. Disappointed!!
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Don't bring a coffee in from a morning walk!
text: My BFF and I have been planning a trip to Paris since 2019...Then Covid happened, and finally! We made it! We went for a morning walk through the city and bought some coffee.  When we arrived back to Citizen M we sat in the lobby to plan our day.  A hotel employee asked us to leave the lobby because we did not purchase our coffee from the hotel.  My friend and I waited for three years,  flew 7 and 1/2 hours from the  States, paid for 8 nights at this hotel, and could not sit in the lobby because we brought our coffee in from our morning walk.  Generally, the staff seem nice, the room is fine, but this ruined it for me.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Great location and service
text: Great location and service. Definitely recommend it. Close walking distance to everything. Clean rooms, delicious food, friendly staff and convenient location. Will visit again if we go to Paris. Love it.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: Trendy Hotel, Good Location, But Very Cramped
text: Trendy hotel in the heart of the Champs-Élysées with wonderful staff. Outstanding shower. Lovely rooftop. Very cramped room overall, however, and we had the largest room in the hotel. I had to work during my stay and the room simply wasn’t big enough. The bed was tucked into an alcove such that it was only accessible from one side. If there are two of you, one has to crawl over the other. Closet space was so minimal as to be nearly nonexistent. I would not stay here again.
name: citizenM Paris Champs-Elysees

title: best place to stay

title: A fine hotel that knows how to treat its guests!
text:
Our first post-pandemic visit abroad confirmed that exceptional service and hospitality does, in fact, still exist in the world, at least at the Marriott Champs Elysees hotel.  After a series of barely palatable  Marriott experiences stateside lately this stay has reaffirmed my brand loyalty and reminded me of what it’s like to stay at a fine hotel.

During our five-night stay a portion of the hotel was under renovation but the work was so well organized and segregated that absent a lack of available upgrade suites we never would have known.   The hotel’s location in the heart of Paris’ most exciting boulevard was a perfect launching point for all the typical Parisian adventures, and the Concierge was actually informative and helpful in every manner without once trying to sell us on some tour or upgrade where she might have gotten some commission.   

Front desk staff was consistently pleasant and helpful, greeting each guest with a genuine smile and inquiry as to the day’s activities, and the rooms themselves were immaculate and comfortable — the standard room we booked accommodated a (comfortable) rollaway for our daughter and was actually quite  large by European standards. 

The included breakfast (Elite benefit, but this one I would pay for if I had to) was full of top quality fresh fruits, cured meats, salmon, pastries and juices.  Plus it included kitchen-made to order omelettes, crepes, and French toast, as well as unusually good choices of hot eggs, meats, and vegetables on the buffet line.   And did I mention coffee to order prepared by attentive and enjoyable wait staff?   This is what breakfast at a fine hotel should be.

Aside from the outstanding personal service, the nicest thing about this stay was that the hotel exhibited none of the failures of service (daily housekeeping, toiletries, room service, overall maintenance and presentation) that Marriott and others stateside seem to have embedded as pandemic-excused compromises that have undermined the guest experience. 

This Marriott deserves its name and shines as an example of what the brand should be.  Highly recommended.
name: Paris Marriott Champs Elysees Hotel
