This was my 4th trip to Paris and I have become very fond of the smaller boutique hotels over the larger impersonal ones and the Plaza Elysees fit the bill. The rooms are very clean and each one unique from the other. There were 4 in my party and our rooms were all different and two of us had small balconies that over looked the main street.

I would definitely recommend this hotel as well as stay there again on my next trip to Paris.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Elmozoghi
text:
In general the hotel was nice , it's just a little bit smaller than the photos
So to whom those need wider rooms it wouldn't be perfect!
I've met the owner she was nice lady indeed 
The stuff were very kind,i'll give 5/10 for the breakfast .
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Excellent location cozy (small) room
text: This property was in an excellent location and provided pleasant customer service and basic breakfast. The room was clean but very small for North American standards but cozy. You simply can't beat the price and location. We would stay again.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Great Location, Greater Staff
text:
i have stayed in this hotel for a week. the location is great for a Paris visit. two metro stations within minutes away, many grocery stores and restaurants close by.
the staff were awesome and very helpful. 
Oliver was great and nice, Caroline & Janet were also were very nice and friendly.
Yousif was also great and talkative. they were all ready for any kind of assistance they can provide or help with.
i loved the interior design of the hotel. it makes you feel that you are staying in the Louvre :)
i would recommend this hotel to anybody i know and will definitely stay there again for any future visits.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Our London-Paris Trip: July 2017
text: What a super hotel!! Accommodations were wonderful, the breakfasts were a pleasant surprise...very good and finally, the staff here were so helpful and understanding to our needs.  From the kitchen staff to the custodial staff, we were very happy.  The young people at the front desk were exceptional and pleasant in dealing with our requests.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Charming but poor air conditioning
text: This hotel is in a great location and the staff is very helpful.  However, we happened to be there during a very hot four days and the air conditioning was totally inadequate.  We were on the sixth floor, which I am sure made it hotter.  Plus the elevator was broken for most of two days, so we had to walk up six flights of stairs in the heat.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Loveley place very chic..great staff
text: Rooms a little small,but then again you are in centre of Paris..Very good location for sight seeing.Great breakfast,including Champagne if you want it.best rooms at top of hotel,due to noise from streets
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Small and Chic
text: Located at the Arc de Triomphe  end of Boulevard Haussmann, you will find yourself about a 5 minute walk from the Champs Elysees and the Georges V metro stop. Our room was small, but had everything you need for a weekend break. I'd recommend asking for a rear facing room to save yourself any noise from the street. Staff were friendly and helpful.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Glorious Anonymity in Paris
text:
We had a wonderful stay at this hotel for a short break in Paris.
Its location is perfect being centrally located and easily accessible to most places.
From the outside it is nondescript but a lot of effort has been done internally so it has everything you need with a very comfortable bed.
It is close to many places with a good choice of quality restaurants within walking distance.
The staff are all excellent and extremely helpful and it was a wonderful stay.
If you are looking for quality ,well located accomnodation with the added advantage if you enjoy anonymity it is Perfect.
Merci beaucoup.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Nice Hotel with great but strange decoration
text:
I had a good stay for two nights in this hotel. The room was clean and well equipped with everything you need like a water cooker, a strange food cooker, minibar, safe and a really good hair dryer. 
The balcony was also good with a great view but a bit noisy cause of the street but therefore the hotel is well located.

The breakfast was nothing special for this price. I've had better breakfasts but also more worse ones. 

Definitely a recommendation for this location.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Thieves in there somewhere
text:
We stayed here before travelling on to somewhere else. First impressions were ok. A lot smaller than you'd imagine. The room was very small. The view was appalling. The bed was hard. Can't comment on the food. 
On our second day we discovered that some money we had set aside was missing from our room. 
We reported this to the reception and they passed it in to management. They haven't dealt with it in a way we were satisfied with. We were made to feel like we were not believed. I would never recommend this place to anyone. Only one other person had access to our room. And as far as the hotel are concerned that person would never steal. Well someone has!
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Compact, modern hotel.
text:
This hotel is another example of how much can be squeezed into a relatively small space! It's located about 10 minutes (gentle) walk from the Arc de Triomphe in one direction, and the Elysees Palace in another, with buses and taxis stopping right outside the hotel entrance.
My room was compact, a typical city centre size in my experience, but comfortable nonetheless. The hotel looks like it's been refurbished relatively recently, and my room was very well equipped with plenty of power points and a USB port with which I could charge my phone and tablet without the fuss of a travel plug adaptor. The room also featured a TV, mini bar and safe, with free wifi throughout.
The rooms are triple glazed to block out the sound of traffic, and this is very effective given the fact that the street is cobbled and is very busy with traffic.
The en suite is a wet room, which was a pleasant surprise given the frequency of showers being the ones over baths, and the resultant slip hazard, and providing a dribble of water. This wet room arrangement was perfect!
Breakfast, which is served in a restaurant on the first floor with views across Boulevard Haussman, was very good, with a wide range of choices to suit most tastes.
The hotel's prices reflect its city centre location: Euro 500 for three nights, including breakfasts.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Good central hotel for visit to Paris
text:
Stayed here on business. Small hotel, room wasn't large (I think that's pretty standard for central Paris) but well equipped and comfortable.
Rook was overlooking main road but window insulation was excellent so absolutely no noise from street.
Staff were very pleasant, helpful and friendly.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Wonderful hotel!
text:
This is a lovely boutique hotel in a very good location accessible to everything. The front desk staff is exemplary and very courteous. The rooms are beautifully decorated with a decent size and with all needed amenities. The breakfast buffet is delicious with very nice staff.
My family and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and would certainly stay here again!
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Good choice
text: Staff were helpful and polite. Good breakfast. Well located, a stones throw from the Arc de Triomphe. Good access to public transport. Clean and quiet. Rooms slightly small but we were not there to stay in the hotel it was place to sleep.  Would recommend but keep an eye out for offers as we did. Got a good deal as the price went up considerably the next day.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Safe, extremely clean and within walking to Metro
text: Was a great location, staff was very helpful with directions, adaptors and anything we asked for.  Our breakfast was included in our package and it had more than a variety of coffees, cereals, toppings, cheeses, breads, pastries and lots of other items.  Our room was very clean and comfortable, water, kettle, coffee and tea was available.      I felt very safe with my daughter and I travelling solo, doors were locked and a night door person was present.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Loved it!
text: We booked last minute, andthe hostess was very accommodating. The hotel was walking distance to everything! Very accessible especially the Arc de Triomphe. The food and service was good, the rooms were also very clean and good sized. The toilets were very modern and comfortable as well with great storage. Highly recommend it!!!
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: charming hotel with friendly Parisians
text: Charming small hotel with friendly, knowledgable staff who speak English well.  Cute room and very nice breakfast room with a good buffet, NOT limited to a "continental breakfast," but with freshly squeezed juice, sausages, pastry, etc. For some the location would seem a bit remote, probably 1/3 mile to any Metro stop (closest might be Etoile) but we enjoyed the quiet and the access to lovely  Parque Monceau.
name: Hotel Plaza Elysees

title: Autumn escape
text:
Nice little spot for the lovers of XIXth century Paris
Charming and full of mindful details
Good location
What else to say to reach 200 characters
This rule is so obsolete, should be revised

Anyway, hotel was OK
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Warn out but great lokation
text: Great location, i have stayed here for years. But it is to warnen out now. The shower overflots the hammam drain overfloats and smells like torilet water. roomservice did not pick up the phone sunday morning i tryed 3 times and gave up. Had to drik the plastic  nespresso. They forgot to fill up the tea corner, so no evening tea either. The bar is still cute and the bartender was great. The guy in the reception is not very service minded and talks back at you, but you know it is paris.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Loved this hotel! It is so Parisian!
text:
We chose this hotel because it felt like being in Paris not like a chain hotel.

The room decor is beautiful as is the hotel itself. The hotel is located about a block from the Champs Elysees. The service was amazing. The only reason I did not give it five stars is, while breakfast is served in the morning, the hotel has no onsite restaurant and no room service. If you want a boutique, Parisian experience, I highly recommend.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: My favorite hotel in the world!
text:
I’ve traveled around the world & this is my favorite hotel because of the service, friendliness of staff, attention to details of the hotel design, room amenities & walkability to nice sites like the Eiffel Tower, Seine, Arc de Triumph, Champs Élysées, etc. Walkability is so important. Proximity to restaurants and the train was nice and walkable. The neighborhood is very upscale and felt safe. There is also hotel security for safety. The gorgeous interior design of this hotel really stands out. There’s even an olive tree in the little courtyard next to reception.

We were so appreciative that Daria at the front desk helped reserve a room for us the day before when I called and put in our special request for a balcony. A balcony was really important for us to have fresh air and enjoy relaxing on it with a cop of coffee. There was even greenery on it so it felt like home. The gentleman who checked us in was also very nice and helpful.

Our room is beautiful and relaxing, like a spa. The whole hotel’s ambience feels like a spa with relaxing dim lights and colors. There were robes, slippers, really lovely smelling Hermes toiletries, and even dreamy pillow spray (that put this hotel over the top for me as I’ve never been to a hotel that provided pillow spray😊). The beds were very comfortable with lovely white clean linens. The rooms were very quiet. Our balcony had pretty blue lights that came on at night. The bathroom was pretty with dark tile and a spa like rain shower with a built in bench. There’s also a nice high tech toilet and towel warmer. There’s a fridge, nice coffee maker, hot water kettle, and safe. 

The dining areas are nice and cozy. We chose to eat breakfast on our gorgeous balcony. The breakfast buffet was outstanding and fresh with many choices of food. The coffee was the best I’ve had in France. The staff at breakfast were top notch and very kind, attentive, and helpful. There are so many other nice things to say about this hotel (including the gym, Turkish bath, spa services, terrific healthy vegetarian menu which we appreciated). 

We hope to stay at this hotel again. It really made for a relaxing stay for the end of our France vacation. I simply loved the international feel of this hotel because it felt like the owners took the best from all around the world and wrapped it into this lovely hotel.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Excellent
text: Le Belmont is a real beautiful hotel, with very professional and friendly staff. it also has a very good location, and easy access in Paris. The property is clean and well maintained. Our stay was really pleasant.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Absolutely wonderful!!
text: Great neighborhood. Friendly staff, the bartender is fantastic! Rooms and bathrooms are great too. Highly recommend. Compared to the US, the price is extremely reasonable. I cannot recommend this place enough, it was such a pleasure to stay at the Belmont!
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Amazing hotel and friendly staff
text:
We had an amazing experience! Upon checking in we were given an upgrade (even though often if a hotel is empty they do not do it, and the hotel was quite full!) 

We said it was lovely especially since it was my 30th Birthday trip. We decided to have a drink at the bar and they kept it open even though it was 1 am and empty. They waited for us and served us lovely wine and champagne. When we wanted to pay they said the drinks were on the establishment (again happens so rarely nowadays, huge thank you!)

Overall the hotel is cute, clean, exceptionally lovely. Very central and easy to get around everywhere especially Eiffel tower and Champs Elysées. Super friendly staff, nice breakfast and overall super lovely.

Thank you for making my Birthday trip special, I really appreciate you guys!
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Like visiting your loving family!
text:
Lovely, aesthetic and cosy boutique hotel just off Champs-Elysées.

My wife and I celebrated her 30th birthday in Paris and we’re grateful that we chose Le Belmont as our home during our stay. 

The staff was simply world class. They made us feel welcome and cherished as if we were family. Attentive, kind and genuinely warm.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Hidden Gem!
text:
I have so many wonderful things to say about this hotel. 

The location is perfect. Tucked in down a side street, a block across from the Champs Elysées, you can walk up to the Arc de Triomphe and also be in the 16th or 17th in 5 minutes. Or down to Tuleries and Concorde in a short walk, or across to the Eiffel Tower and the 7th. I walked everywhere.

The staff are so friendly and welcoming. I checked in smoothly at just after 3pm and my room was ready. It was spotlessly clean and very comfortable. I had a great night’s sleep, the room was quiet and soundproofed. It was nice to be able to watch TV from home, as well as French TV. 

Breakfast was lovely and the staff were again very kind and making sure all the guests were happy. The restaurant is airy and comfortable.

Sadly I only stayed for one night as it was a flying visit, but I’ll definitely be back to stay at this hotel.

Merci à toute l’équipe pour un accueil chaleureux et un séjour très agréable.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Great location, pleasant enough stay
text:
A pleasant enough stay all round.
I didn’t receive a particularly warm welcome when I checked in. 
All though by no means rude, he was neither friendly nor welcoming which after a long day of travel didn’t feel great. Later I asked for some additional hangers and was told this wasn’t possible until morning. That’s not 4 star service.

The breakfast team (none of them French) were absolutely delightful. Warm, efficient and generally lovely. Please pass on my feedback to this team.

I encountered two more reception staff. Both professional but very businesslike and also not warm.
When I was checking out, I wasn’t asked how my stay was… which is abnormal for a hotel stay in 4star. Nor was I thanked for visiting. I left feeling a bit underwhelmed.

The room was immaculate, but lacked:
A mirror in the main room area
Cutlery 
A working safe for the first night.
A comfortable chair (just a huge space where there should have been one).
It did however have a tv, and a beautiful Juliet balcony with fully opening doors. 

I would probably rank the room at 3-4 star standard with some improvements needed to raise the bar.

The location is great, and the public areas are spectacular. All in all, it was perfectly nice for business… 

I usually stay in 4/5 star establishments so used to small details and more attentive service. 
I’m not sure I would rush back and I’m in Paris twice a year for 3-4 days at a time.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Wouldn't come back.
text: Hotel is not as pictured. Rooms are VERY small and noisy, we had to change rooms because of the noise in rooms on either side of us even after a room change it was still the same except the noise was from the room above us as well as beside us. Rooms aren't insulated well. Reception acted as if it was a suprise that we had complained about the noise even though a couple before us had the same complaint and argued with us that they have other customers and us changing rooms isn't ideal which isn't something you want to hear as a paying customer yourself. The good part about this hotel is the breakfast staff who were very polite and attentive the whole time we were there.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: The best staff, thank you Ariel
text:
Brilliant stay made all the better by the extremely friendly and helpful staff, in particular thank you to Ariel who was friendly and gave me great recommendations for my stay. 

Great location and rooms were perfect. 

Looking forward to coming back
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Need to Work on Welcome
text:
We arrived very late as our plane was delayed.  After a long difficult journey we were pleased to arrive at the hotel.  We received a frosty welcome from a gentlemen who acted as though we were an intrusion rather than a guest.  After stating our reservation couldn't be found, despite confirming directly with the hotel only days before, we were given a key to a top floor room (cupboard) next to the elevator.  The room was the smallest hotel room that I have ever stayed in. The sloping roof and the velux window directly above the bed added to the crampness. As it was late and I doubted that we would get anywhere with the unpleasant receptionist we settled in for the night.  In the morning a new reception team had arrived who looked very much different so I approached them and I was instantly given a much better much bigger room.  This is the reason for the 4 stars as opposed to 1 star if this had not happened.  Breakfast was very good and the hotel very clean.  The hotel decor is very nice.  Breakfast staff were very friendly also. Location was brilliant - only a 5 minute walk to Champs Elysees.

Hint, if staying at this hotel avoid room 606.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Very comfortable and great staff
text: I normally need to stay in the 16th arrondissement in Paris but have not used this hotel before. It will now be my regular! Very comfortable, excellent and helpful staff and decent price. Definitely 4 star.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Third Time Still Lucky
text: The Belmont is a stylish French hotel in a good location with what I would consider reasonable prices. The staff are excellent - special mention to Aurélie who helped me twice with stupid booking mistakes.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

text:
It’s very nice hotel and the location it’s perfect 👍 , Also the staff it’s Good 👍 And the check in before 12 PM it’s help me 😊 
Thank you for a good time when I stay at hotel. 
When I visit Paris again Absolutely I booking at LW BELMONT HOTEL 👍😀
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Nice, clean, central, good breakfast
text:
Located between Champs Elysees and the Eiffel Tower. Friendly staff. Good bed, silent, nice bathroom with a Japanese style shower toilet. Several nice restaurants close to the hotel. 
An excellent place to stay in Paris!
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Wonderful gem in the heart of the city
text: Very nice hotel in a perfect location, walking distance to the arc de triomphe, champs elysees, and many cafes.  Comfortable rooms that appear to be recently renovated, yet still with some old world charm.  Nice bathrooms.  Welcoming staff.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Business Trip
text: Charming stylish hotel with nice amenities and quality service. The staff were helpful with any request and continental breakfast was quality. The air-conditioning keep the room very cool and balcony was a nice touch. Will stay again next trip to Paris on business
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Stolen credit card credentials!!
text: Never again! I made payment for the hotel through the booking service In advance. After arriving they asked for credit card credentials at the front desk, “in case of something”, they didn’t make payment through the machine just wrote down my card number, cvv. This “fraud-hotel” is the only one place in Paris where i gave this credit card! After coming back to my country in 2 weeks someone used my credit card in France for 89€, 10€, i saw this and blocked the card as stolen and even after someone tried to make transactions for 169€, 20€ etc. Hope you’ll have problems with Police!!
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Great cozy hotel
text: Super cozy hotel with great service. The rooms might be on the smaller side, but they are very functional and cute. The hotel overall has a lot of charm and is well-situated if are looking at exploring the west side of Paris. The staff was very nice and helpful, more than happy to help every time we needed something. Thank you !!
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Good location and cosy room
text: This hotel is close to Champs Elysees, Triumphal arch, and Eiffel Tower.  The room is wide enough and cosy.  Our flight arrived early in the morning, so early check-in was helpful.  Breakfast is average.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Lovely old fashioned hotel nicely situated for Champs Elysee area. Renovated but kept its charm especially bar area. Didn't have time to try the Spa but a useful facility. Rooms very comfortable with everything you need including Hermes products in bathroom. Staff welcoming and friendly. Would stay again
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: excellent hotel near Etoile
text: very nice hotel well managed. The reception team is very good and helpful. The porter made a special effort to find me a taxi to catch my flight. During Friday afternoon strike action which meant no taxis could be booked. Hope to stay here again.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Le Belmont Champs Elysee (and a bit)
text: Location is excellent, hotel is quirky and stylish. Between the Champs Elysee and the Seine, 15 minutes walk to the Eiffel Tower and the dining boats on the river. Couple of decent restaurants around the corner.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Really neat hotel...
text: Hotel is centrally located very close to the Champs-Élysées/Arc de Triomphe and the Eiffel Tower. Rooms are very modern with all modern amenities including stocked mini-bar. Delightful breakfast room with a good variety of food available. No restaurant but with a wide variety of restaurants available, within easy walking distance, there are plenty to choose from. Staff are all very friendly and welcoming. Family run hotel who care about the service they deliver. Would definitely stay here again...
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Nice stay in great location
text: A pleasant hotel in a fantastic location near multiple highlights of paris. The rooms are adequate and bed comfortable, the shower was excellent. The breakfast was good with hot food and cold continental options and nice fresh bakery goods and yogurt. A small hotel but pleasant to stay in.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Nice and well located hotel
text: The hotel is very well located. It has a hammam and a gym. It is located at a walking distance from the Champs Élysées and the Arc De Triomphe. Several restaurants and shops in the neighbourhood. Convenient for business trips and holidays.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: very pleasant stay
text:
I stayed at this hotel bwdore and I really like their service.
so I decided to stay, again to spend time for new year holiday.
I had a very good stay with their exceptional customer service.
a big surprise was a chocolate box, offered for new year!
I will recommend to stay at this hotel to my friends and family.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Always Good
text: This is the second time I stayed at Le Belmont.  It's a great location, the staff are very friendly and helpful.  Great showers!  I also love how I can make the room completely dark so that you can really sleep well.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Nice hotel in  paris.
text: Nice hotel in a good location down town of paris. Breakfast is the same everyday but still nice. Rooms are nice with good size, Tv channels are boring in a way, choice can be much better. Staff are ok. Everyday in breakfast someone must ask you “your room number sir” you feel you are a suspect of a big crime :). Just kidding.
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: My Christmas Stay
text: My stay was enjoyable and I would like to thank Nabeel from Reception as well as the bellboy who made it a very good stay.  Mybroom was changed from room with bath tub to room with walk in shower at my request within 24 hours which was good. I didn’t use any of the facilities other than my room so I couldn’t comment.  Housekeeping was good but one day they forgot to replenish the coffee amenities and another
name: Hotel Le Belmont Paris

title: Do your homework on this hotel
text:
Long time, global traveller and Marriott Bonvoy member. I was very disappointed by my stay at the Westin Vendome in Paris October 5th - October 9th, 2022 and will not return again. I don't write long reviews like this. Check my profile. I fee compelled to share the following. 

Yes, the location is excellent. You couldn't pick a much better location, but that is where the accolades will stop. 

I was on the 4th floor and thought I would be away from ground noise, but my room was on Mt. Tabor in an outside room. The Tabac on Mt. Tabor had yelling and screaming until mid-nite every night. Even with the windows closed you could not escape the noise. The garbage trucks also arrive at 6:30 AM to wake you up. I assume your experience would be far better if you had an inward facing room. Insist on getting this room type or you will have the same experience as I.

Another issue is the room keys. I can go on and on relative to this topic. I experienced multiple instances where I had to have keys remade. The last incident resulted in me having to go down to the front desk for a new key after my key did not work at my door. They created a new key, but when I walked across the lobby to the elevators it did not work. I went back and one of the agents said I must have neutralized it with my cell phone though it never left my hand. He had to make another and take me to my room. Even he couldn't get up one of the elevators with his new key.

Housekeeping was late and spotty. On our second day we called at 4 PM to say no one cleaned our room. They came up after we left, but simply made our bed and provided fresh towels. Again, today, it was not cleaned when we got back to the room at 3 PM.

I could continue. Do your homework.

title: Good Location but has its challenges
text: The hotel is in a wonderful location, especially if you enjoy shopping at high end stores. There is a metro stop very close by making it convenient to get most anywhere in Paris. The hotel itself is beautiful but as it is a Westin I think it is a popular spot for conferences. Unfortunately when we booked our room we did not realize there would be a large conference there. Usually this is not a problem if a hotel is large enough to host conferences but in this instance the number of conference participants far outweighed the available space so the entire common area of the first floor (hallways, restaurants, reception area etc) was packed with people at all times of the day. It made it very difficult to get from the elevators to the front door of the hotel or to enjoy the hotel restaurant because people were grouped together blocking all of the spaces. I would definitely confirm there are no conferences taking place if you are considering booking a room here as it really detracted from the overall experience. The rest of this review is specifically for room 5049. The room was a junior suite with a view of the Eiffle Tower. Pros: the view was spectacular. There are three balconies for this room and I can’t imagine having a better view of the Eiffel Tower. There are little bistro tables on the balconies so very enjoyable to have a glass of wine and watch the Tower sparkle every night. The room itself was large. The Jardins de Tuilleries is right across the street so it is relatively quiet (almost no traffic noise at night). Cons: There was a complete lack of lighting in the room but especially in the bathroom. I would liken the amount of lighting in the bathroom to candle light – this is not an exaggeration. There are double frosted doors leading to one balcony in the bathroom. During daylight hours (8:30am -6:30 pm) there was enough light coming through the windows to make doing makeup possible. Outside of those times it was not. The mirror in the bathroom was not made from glass, it was bendable and had come partially outside the frame so the mirror itself was slightly convex – leading to a funhouse mirror effect. The room itself only had a few lamps and no mirror so that was no better. Additionally, the bathroom had one outlet for electric razors – nothing else. There was only one other outlet in the room that allowed for a hotel provided blow dryer to be plugged in. That was at the desk but there was no mirror so it was impossible to see what you’re doing. In my opinion lighting and electrical outlets close to mirrors are basic necessities in a hotel room – especially at the price of this room. It is possible to “make due” (especially with the view) and assuming you brought your own mirror but for some people this would not be possible. I would not book this room again and although I did not see inside any of the other rooms I would assume that they all had similar challenges with lighting and electrical outlets.

title: The good, the bad, and the ugly
text:
The good: The location of this hotel is outstanding. We were able to walk all over Paris and enjoy the park every evening. Our kids loved standing at the stately windows to watch the Eiffel Tower sparkle. The beautiful courtyard restaurant was a perfect place to relax and enjoy great food and drinks. The staff worked hard, despite clearly being overworked. They were friendly and kind and don’t deserve being yelled at for things beyond their control (and we wonder why the rest of the world is done with American exceptionalism). I felt like our family was sharing space with those who came before us…the fancy travelers of the late 19th century, the wounded WWI soldiers convalescing, the scores of families enjoying their first taste of this magical city, the couples celebrating every stage of love.

The bad: The lobby, guest rooms, and hallways showed their age. Stained Carpets smelled of cigarette smoke and mildew. Furniture was worn and tired. The entire building had an elderly person’s grandma’s old trunk in the attic vibe. The bathrooms were totally fine and the bedding was crisp and clean, which made the stay bearable. I had to put on my big girl pants and tell myself to stop complaining to my husband who didn’t notice any of it and embrace the grubby aesthetic (kind of like mentally preparing for camping or using a porta-potty). 

Also, my family makes fun of me for spending much of my travel time hanging out with the concierge wherever we go. I was looking forward to getting all the inside information from my French concierge. So you can imagine my disappointment when I learned this tourist hub didn’t have a concierge. The manager on duty attempted to answer my questions, but it was like a dermatologist trying to do the job of an orthopedic surgeon. I really, really missed having a concierge.

The ugly: This majestic, historic  building, its earnest, attentive staff, and (most of) the guests deserve better. It takes a lot of money to keep a massive old building looking good and running smoothly. But it also takes TLC. Like many landmark hotels, the Westin Vendome is nothing but a pawn in some mega-corporate-hedge fund-greedy-don’t care about anything but our shareholders and our portfolio game. It’s being tossed around from mega-rich company to mega-rich company with no consideration for the long, storied history of the building, the hard work of every single staff member tasked with managing a myriad of responsibilities while trying to placate cranky guests, or the starry-eyed human travelers who land on the doorstep with hopes of escaping the unrelenting stress of life for a brief moment.

If you are going to complain, consider complaining about the source of the issues at this hotel and many others: raw, unfettered corporate greed. 

To the greedy corporate landholders: Release  some of your gazillions. Do a legitimate renovation (not one of those lipstick on a pig, add new throw pillows jobs). Upgrade with eco friendly materials to marry old bones with new breath. Hire a lovely local concierge (or three)  to give guests all the delicious inside  knowledge to make their trip magical. Pay your staff well. Treat them well. Give your guests a haven from the monotony of life. Be human. And if your shareholders get mad, well… you’ll always have Paris💕

text:
So we stayed for one night at the Westin Vendome after traveling throughout bordeaux and Versailles where we stayed at other luxury properties. There are a lot do pluses about the Westin vendome so let’s start there. The hotel is ideally located across from the gardens and louvre. Finally if you are noise sensitive do not get a room overlooking the Eiffel Tower during summer. They have a summer carnival with rides that make folks scream as they ride and you can hear it all day and night past midnight. I would not have wanted to stay multiple nights in this room during summertime. But admittedly did Love my view dearly. I had noise cancelling headphones so was able to sleep ok. 

All in All I still think pluses outweigh minuses of the hotel. We were able to use points so worked out well overall.

title: Centrally located with a terrific view
text:
The staff at the front desk was courteous, allowing us to check in a few hours earlier than the scheduled time.  Based on a request I'd put in for a room with nice view, they were able to accommodate us on the top floor facing Jardin des Tuileries, which offered a fantastic view of some of the most famous Paris landmarks - Tour de Eiffel, Louvre, and Musee d'Orsay - from our balconies.  As an anniversary present, they also provided us with a complimentary bottle of champagne and macarons, which was a very nice touch.  

Although the breakfast buffet offerings remained the same day to day, there was enough variety to keep us all satisfied for a 6-nights' stay.  My daughter and I especially enjoyed the freshly made croissants and pain au chocolat every morning, in addition to some combination of scrambled eggs, bacon, salami, smoked salmon, cherry tomatoes, bananas, and yogurt.  

This hotel is within a short walking distance to some of the finest luxury stores (which my wife took advantage of) and patisseries (which my daughter took advantage of), as well as the Louvre, Musee d'Orsay, Jardin des Tuileries, and Place de la Concorde.  Being near the Concorde Metro station also came in handy as we explored other landmarks further away. 

Although the hotel is starting to show signs of wear (noticeable from creaks in certain parts of the floor), it still maintains the elegance that I appreciate in older hotels.  I will definitely consider staying at this hotel again.

title: Choose another hotel
text:
I would not recommend this hotel for a Paris stay. Pictures are misleading.  This is specific to hotel and not staff. The staff was doing their best and everyone was nice and courteous. 

Sure the hotel is historic and has some old large hotel historic charm from a birds eye view.  But …

1.  Hotel is old old old.  It’s smells old. The hallways and rooms smell of a old building. It’s very noticeable and unpleasant. 

2.  Carpets and floors are dirty filthy especially in the rooms.  Very old carpets. I wore shoes in my room. 

3.  Furniture in rooms are  very old broken down and dirty.  I avoided sitting in any chairs.  Bedding average w below average pillows snd sheets.  Has zero appeal. Lampshades falling apart. 

4.  Dusty dusty dusty. Coughed the whole time. 

5.  Outside courtyard okay but again lacking what photos portray.  

6.  Location is close to things as it’s glorified in the reviews. But we did not like it.  It was in the middle of the city center , downtown, w very busy noisy traffic , dirty streets , homeless , and overall crowded mess.  We did not sleep at nights bc of street noise. 

Trust me skip this hotel. I promise you will have a lackluster experience.  It ruined my experience.  Everything is a cab ride away so no need to be close to the city center. 

Stay at Hotel Raphael or anywhere near that area. 

People always say “it’s just a room to sleep in you’ll be out the whole day”. 
I disagree. We came from London to Paris snd in London we stayed at the Biltmore a true 5 star experience w updated hotel. Wow. It matters.  You come back tired. You want to spend time at the hotel bar. Eat at the hotel restaurant. Chill in your room w a nice TV or an espresso machine or a music player to chill to or real comfy pillows.  

I don’t like write reviews but I’m sorry I was very upset at myself for not listening to some of the reviews and going w the Costco deal.  

Hope this helps.  
Hotels matter.

title: Westin 2 star Experience
text:
Our experience was HORRIBLE at this supposedly 5 star hotel.  I had stayed here 7 years ago and had an amazing experience which is why I chose to stay again.  The service level has been reduced to a maximum 2 star hotel. No concierge, bars closed without notice, the staff was less than helpful with the exception of one manager, Geremy.  However, he had limited ability to correct the many issues.  When we checked in there was nobody at the counter.  I rang the bell and nobody appeared.  Finally, I asked a gentlemen at a desk if anyone was working and he made a call and they came to check us in.  This was a bad start but continued thru the entire stay.

The hall to our room looked like an storage area and with tables and chairs stacked in the hall.  I thought this would change but it was there our entire 3 day stay.

I was in a Suite that was the worst design you could imagine.  Doors into the bedroom were blocked with furniture and there was No door between the bedroom and the sitting area.  I booked a suite so I could work and not disturb my friend sleeping.  This was wasted on this room.  So, I refrained from working at the desk as I would have preferred.  House keeping did not clean our room either day and I had to call and ask them to send someone up.  So, twice we had people cleaning our room while we in the room because they had not cleaned the room while we were out all day.

When we arrived, the room had no Shampoo. The basics of running a high level hotel were overlooked and the shampoo sounds petty but it was an example of lack of attention to the details that make you special.

They have NO concierge now.  I was totally blown away that a hotel of this caliber had no concierge.  When I stayed in the past the concierge was amazing and made a huge impact on my decision to stay again.  Don’t make this mistake when you are booking.

There are many choices of hotels in Paris and DO NOT  choose this one until they can get the issues resolved.  I am a devoted BonVoy member but will definitely not choose this property again.  I could continue with other issues but feel you have a good idea about the service level.

title: Needs to be updated
text:
My aidfe and I recently stayed here on a trip to Paris. The staff was nice and the bones of the hotel are wonderful with carved plaster cornices, etc that one would expect of a building in Paris of this vintage. 
However, the room was dreary and clearly was way past its prime and desperately needed to be updated. The furniture was cheap. Something one might buy at a Value City. It was also not what one would expect in a hotel with its reputation. We were graciously upgraded to a suite. However, pur neighbors kept us up most of the first night and the staff very readily handled this and we had no more problems. 
The atrium was in the process of being renovated. I don’t know who their decorator is but the final product was way overdone and had a mixture of very nice white furniture but then wooden furniture was added to it creating a very unharmonious result. 
Clearly the hotel needs to be completely renovated and Marriott should do this. They should hire a decorator who is sympathetic to the architecture of the building and decorates it consistently with that architecture. It clearly has the possibility to be a stunning property.

title: Normally 5 Stars...but no longer, and way too expensive!
text:
We've stayed at the Westin Vendome many times over many years. The location cannot be beat - easy couple minute walk to the Metro, walk to the Louvre, Les Jardins across the street, just wonderful. The service is normally the best. Very accommodating, friendly, attention to detail and generally wonderful. The view from the outer rooms or a corner suite are just spectacular! You can see the Louvre out of one dormer, and the Eiffel Tower out of the other - the bathroom dormer looks out on Les Jardins des Tuileries and the carousel. So lovely to  enjoy your morning coffee on. In fact, still to this day I think the room service coffee and croissants is the best anywhere! 

The courtyard lounge area is awesome! The staff is nice, visits with you, provides good recommendations, and the food and drinks are great. We enjoyed aperos every day there. The restaurant has a wonderful breakfast and dinner! Highly recommend.

That said, the last time we stayed the service was not good, with the exception of the courtyard lounge and restaurant (great as always). The reception staff was clearly new and untrained. We had to ask to change rooms because we were given a wheelchair accessible interior room - for a Titanium/Ambassador Elite status repeat guest, this room should not have even been offered! It was not up to snuff. We did move to a Jr Suite, but with an interior courtyard view - again, not what we expect for our loyalty status. We would have gladly taken a smaller room to have the view, but we were told they didn't have the staff to clean a view room for us. ??? 

Housekeeping did clean the room and bathroom nicely, but I had to call down for something every day; toiletries, towels, remove dishes, etc. In addition, the property is getting quite tired. Carpet is old, linen style outdated, bathrooms outdated. I did read this property is going to get a renovation in 2022, but that may have been delayed due to covid? It is time!

This is not what we expect from a Westin property, especially for 600-800 Euros per night. For the high cost of this property, I have to lower my previous 5 stars to only 3 stars. If you're going to spend this much, I recommend researching other properties that are either new, or newly renovated.

title: Very well located hotel with exceptional staff
text:
This hotel is situated in a great location in central Paris! We enjoyed our time here and would highly recommend it to anyone considering a hotel in Paris.

Hotel staff - The staff were very attentive and welcoming, especially the gentlemen who greeted us for breakfast each morning. 

Hotel room - Our room was well appointed with a view of the courtyard. Inside the room we had a really comfortable bed, a mini fridge, a TV as well as ample storage space for our luggage and clothes.

Hotel dining - Breakfast in this hotel was fantastic and truly one of the best things about this particular hotel! A spacious breakfast buffet area with views of the park opposite the hotel. A very wide range of food was available. The waiting staff were very attentive and a credit to the hotel.

Transport links - The hotel is a 5 minute walk from the nearest metro station, Concorde. There are several bus routes very close to the hotel. 

Location - The hotel is very well located in the centre of Paris within walking distance of the Champs Elysees and Louvre. We also walked to the Eiffel Tower from this hotel which is a very scenic and wonderful walk along the Seine. It also has a beautiful park on its doorstep.

title: A once great Paris hotel that is no longer great
text:
I have stayed at this hotel several times in the past (last time being circa 2017) which is why I chose to stay there again.  

We arrived just before midnight at the hotel and on arrival was ignored by the doorman.  As we had limited luggage that wasn’t an issue but not the best service.

Checkin was efficient.  I had checked in on line so reception was able to just hand me the key.  

I had booked a twin room but the room had been made up as a king bed so had to call reception to get this fixed.  As it was already midnight at this point the last thing I needed was to wait.  Ultimately it took more than one call to reception as well as circa 30 mins to resolve. Not great if you just want to go to bed.

The wifi in the room also didn’t work which resulted in more calls to the front desk to try and fix.  Ultimately the night manager called me with a fix - connecting to the wifi in a neighbouring room. I am glad that it was fixed but this is an issue that shouldn’t have happened.

The room itself is tired and outdated.  There were so many things wrong with the room it is hard to know where to start. Furniture was old and had chips out of it, there are no Electrical sockets or USB plugs near the bed so we had to move the bed to access a powerboard under the bed to charge our phones, there is no tea or coffee making facilities in the room, the toilet had what I can only assume was a rust stain, the shower head was so poor that I had to use the hand shower to actually have a shower etc.

I am also not convinced how well the sheets were laundered as I needed to take an allergy medication because I was itchy.  This has not happened to me in a hotel room for years…..

Was it worth a 50,000 points redemption? No. Would I stay there again? No.

A once great Paris hotel that is no longer great.

Breakfast at Le First was excellent. We were genuinely surprised each morning at how good the food and selection was. We would definitely stay at the Westin Vendome again.

Newly renovated luxury hotels in this location start at 4x the price. So to trash this hotel because its not new and modern is unfair. There are certainly fancier hotels in Paris, but they're ridiculously expensive. The bottom line is, all things considered, this is a good value and a lovely hotel.

title: Prime location and great views, but rooms could be renovated
text:
Historic hotel in a fantastic location in the center of Paris - the Louvre and the Tuileries, the Seine and the Left Bank, the Musee d'Orsay, etc are all within walking distance, as is the Metro Line 1, making for very convenient sightseeing. The luxury shops on rue Saint-Honoré are nearby, and the area is also not far from where many authentic Japanese restaurants are. 

At check-in they were nice enough to upgrade me based on my Titanium status to a room overlooking the Tuileries gardens with a view of the Eiffel Tower. The breakfast buffet (included with status) was well stocked. The gym was adequate, would suggest to add more free weights if possible.

The rooms themselves are small and unfortunately a bit outdated and run down - definitely in need of a renovation. Even minor inconveniences are likely due to the age of the rooms, such as the shower temperature being consistently hard to get right (way too cold one second and scalding hot a second later) and the door handle/lock was tough to open every time (you have to really push and turn the handle a certain way). Small details, but given the nightly rate is quite high/at the level of a luxury hotel (plus the fact that there's a Renaissance nearby, along with other non-Marriott properties that are more updated), the rooms here at the Westin could definitely be improved. 

The best parts of the hotel are the location and the views, which are superb. I would stay here again on personal and business trips in the future, but hope the rooms will be updated soon.

title: Great location and wonderful staff
text:
The Westin Vendome is within walking distance of several landmarks: Louvre, Musee d’Orsay, Eiffel Tower and Arc d’ Triumph.  Be sure to exit the hotel and and walk 2 minutes to see the Eiffel Tower lit up and sparkling each night 9-9:05pm.  It is spectacular. 

We were in a superior room overlooking the Louvre.  It was spacious.  The hotel is historic. We did bring several converters for our phones, iPads etc.. 
The  only negative is that there is no outlet in the bathroom for anything other than a shaver.  There is a hair dryer attached to the wall but it quickly over heats and shuts off.  

Housekeeping was daily and wonderful.  We did not know what to expect as during several pervious stays in hotels - there was no daily housekeeping.  Plenty of towels, soaps and daily bottled water at the Westin.  

Reception was amazing!  Always helpful with restaurant suggestions and even made reservations.

title: The Ultimate in Being Hospitable
text:
What I look for at a hotel is the level of service. It’s the way staff behave, how far they are willing to go to “be hospitable” as some of the best hotels put it. 

The Westin Vendome has that hospitable essence. It has the magic.

COVID was very hard on graceful ladies like the Westin Vendome, originally the Continental Hotel. It has been hard to get staff to come back to work, to refresh a shuttered beauty and bring back such a large gem in BonVoy’s crown in the heart of the City of Lights.

My wife and I have stayed at the Westin 3-4 times this summer alone. We have been watching her emerge. It hasn’t been all magic and mystery. 

Today was impressive. 

We have had to use their storage for a lot of bags as we move around Europe and wait for our apartment to become available. They have been generous with us.

This week we are staying at another BonVoy property that is close but hard to navigate in a vehicle due to construction.

Dany, one of the key total experience providers at the Westin, helped us get seven large bags on a bell cart to our other hotel. He is a rockstar. It wasn’t necessarily Herculean, but it meant that he cared, on a very hot and busy day, to make our experience better. It meant a lot.

Thank you Westin Vendome, thank you Dany specifically. You are the best!

David & Sarah Vanderveen

title: Stay here for the location and room with Eiffel view did not disappoint.
text:
Stayed with an Eiffel tower view and it did not disappoint. Make sure you request a high floor (IIRC rooms 304X to 306X). Some maybe be junior suites. Great location. Used the app for requesting services. Fast replies. 

Fête des Tuileries (fun fair) was going on during the stay so was a bit noisy. But it wasn't that bad. After all Parisians deserve a good time after what happened in the last year or so and we celebrated the festivities with their cheers as well.

There's no valet service due to Covid but you can check out a nearby parking lot called Indigo. Want a better tip? Reserve a spot using the app for up to 40% off. 

Some rather disappointing observations.

The hotel is a bit dated. 

King room with Eiffel view is rather small.  If you have two big luggages, you might need to be creative maneuvering around the room. 

There is no ventilation in bathroom. Fixtures are functional but old and moldy.

Onsite staff, especially the doorman and sometimes a staff member standing near the lobby, seemed a bit disinterested in working there as if they didn't want to be there. No greetings whatsoever.

title: Great Location
text: Our favorite place to stay in Paris. It is next to the Tuileries Garden where there is a loverly carousel and play park for the kids. We were upgarded to a large suite.  Close connection to Metro and an easy walk to the Louvre,  Musée d'Orsay and Musée de l'Orangerie.  The rooms are lovely with great views of the Eiffel Tower.  The breakfast at Le First is an absolute must. I think it is the best breakfast buffet among the marriott properties I have stayed. Unfortunately they ruined the previously beutiful Bar Tuilleres.   I will never understand why the owners let this happen.  The Bar Tuilleres was previously a highlight of the hotel with deep reds and edwardian baroque style. there was nothing like it on the rue de la paix and in my opnion rivalled the bar at Hôtel Costes. Now it has been redesigned to a modern dull gray color--all the ambience is gone.  Also it seems like they have no idea what to do with the center of the lobby--the area surrounded by glass.  It has gone through several different redesigns. None of them have sticked and all of them have been bad.  During our stay it was some ill conceived garden restaurant with chairs that stick you with splinters and plenty of hard surfaces for your kids to injure themselves.  Despite this, the westin place vendome will always be our first choice in Paris.

title: Disappointing
text:
We stayed in the Hotel du Petit Moulin from 15-17 September for our honeymoon and unfortunately we were very disappointed with our stay.  The staff were very nice and helpful and even gave us a bottle of complimentary Champagne as it was our honeymoon but given the premium price the hotel are charging I couldn’t recommend it.  

The room that we were given originally did not compare even closely with the photos on the website and felt much more like the decor you’d expect in a budget hotel, not a hotel charging premium rates and selling itself on its original design.  The staff were helpful and moved us to another room.  This was a significant improvement but despite being a non smoking room it smelt strongly of cigarettes and felt very tired and in need of refurbishment.  

The next day we went to the sister hotel to use the spa.  A spa was a key criteria in our search for a hotel as after our wedding we wanted to relax.   Unfortunately though when we got to the sister hotel, none of the facilities were working.  The hamman was not working and the jacuzzi was tepid not warm.  This was a huge disappointment.

We borrowed the bicycles in the sister hotel instead and the bicycles were desperately in need of a service.  The brakes on both bikes were really bad and on one bike barely worked at all so was quite dangerous to ride.

Back at the Hotel du Petit Moulin, we tried to use the wifi but found that the connection kept breaking and we were unable to use it.

Finally, though the beds were made beautifully by the house keeping team on both nights, the mattress felt old and not turned frequently so the mattress had dips on each side of the bed.  Again I suspect that this is probably just because they are probably quite old.

Despite these points, the staff were very nice, the bed linen was soft and fresh, the products of the hotel were very good and we very much appreciated the complimentary champagne provided.  The hotel offered us a free drink from the bar or breakfast but given the number of issues we really expected more substantial compensation.

I think the hotel was probably once worth the premium rates it is charging but even at the special rate we secured on an accommodation comparison website I don’t think it can justify these prices without some new investment to bring the rooms back up to standard.

title: A little jewel box in the Paris Marais
text:
I was lucky enough to be treated to a fabulous weekend in Paris for my birthday, staying on the top floor of the beautiful Petit Moulin.  In the trendy Third Arrondissement, midway between the Place de Bastille and the Pompidou Centre, the building’s modest exterior gives only a few hints to the opulence inside, which extends throughout this beautiful and well-run hotel.  With decor by Christian Lacroix, paradisal beings, plumes and pelts adorn the walls, floors and furnishings.

Our room was spacious with a comfortable bed, lots of natural light and windows that could open - so welcome in a hot city centre.  A tiny sitting room, with minibar and sofa, was a good reading and surfing spot.  The shower room was generously sized with glossy black tiles and a great shower.  There is a lift to the second floor but we liked the zebra-carpeted staircase that felt a bit like a helter-skelter upon descent.

Service is smiling, professional and knowledgeable with the staff speaking excellent English and indulging our school French.  Breakfast is optional with a simpler and more extensive option available - both are good value and great quality.  Evenings are relaxing and understated; an honesty bar awaits you on the ground floor where you can enjoy aperitifs in the small lobby lounge or dining room.  There is a kitchen (room service) but no restaurant - however this is unimportant as loads of bars and good restaurants are within walking distance.  A nearby spa is linked and offers its services and treatments if that’s your thing.

I didn’t see the bill but suspect the price reflects the quality and recommend you too have a wonderful treat!

title: Charming!!
text:
Whenever my husband and I travel abroad , especially to cities like Paris, we much prefer to stay at boutique hotels ( I think you get a real flavor of the city )  rather then large  luxury chain hotels. We chose this hotel based on a friend's  recommendation and it was lovely!!!
 We had the junior suite on the top floor  which was spacious ( even for a European hotel )  with beamed ceilings, slanted in some paces ( not where it matters)  , very cool decor,  completely renovated bathroom, sitting area with a couch , chairs and coffee table, a very comfortable bed and a small well stocked refrigerator The room was immaculate and cleaned every day . There is no elevator to the top floor so you get off at the 3rd floor and then you have to walk up a windy staircase,  even that is adorable ). 

The staff at the front desk ( and everywhere)  is fabulous, very friendly, knowledgeable and  no request was too large or too  small.
 Before we arrived  we wanted to make several reservations and they took care of the arrangements with no problem . In the morning if asked they brought coffee to the room within minutes , excellent cappuccinos !! 
I have read some negative reviews and I am baffled because I am rather discerning about  the places I stay. 
We found the hotel and room looked exactly as they do on the website. The large magnificent Orchid plants that adorn the windows in the lobby   are worth mentioning :)
I have read some complaints about the bar , which is a charming  but very small space,  where breakfast is also served . They use the honor system so I do not see a problem with not having a bar tender There are so many bars and bistros in the area but it is a nice spot at the end of the day to just relax .  The location is fantastic, Marais is a very cool neighborhood!
If you like boutique hotels then this is an excellent place to stay !!

My mother and I had a lovely stay at Hotel du Petit Moulin. The staff was helpful and very friendly. The decor felt very Paris and the bed was comfortable. We liked that the room had a tiny fridge available for use. We didn't have breakfast in the hotel, but it is available if that's something you are interested in. We enjoyed the games in the bar, a little game of chess with aperol spritzes was great! The location was nice. We liked the boutiques and cafes near the hotel. It is also super close to the Picasso museum, which is worth the quick trip to see Guernica. 

The only con was the shower. Our attic room had a bath tub with a shower head and no shower curtain and obviously it's not that big of a deal, but I thought I'd mention it. As an American, we are just used to different types of showers.

title: It's beautiful, but...
text: We loved staying here. From the moment you arrive at the old, original bakery store front you know it's a real original. The decorations are lovely, the staff charming and efficient, our room quiet, the bed super comfortable, the Marais location perfect. Why only three stars? Because small hotels like this, at these prices, are about more than decor and fittings. They are about creating an atmosphere. The bar on our visit was unstaffed and felt dead. No weekend cocktail mixer or vinyl collection as promised on the website. No  book in the rooms telling the story of the history of the place. No guides to the Marais new shops and bars, just an old tourist handout. Cheap plastic shower gels in the bathroom. No fresh coffee to be had in the rooms or elsewhere. No creative thinking at all really. All these touches would take minimum investment. Just a bit of thought and some fresh ideas. It's beautiful but it feels a little unloved. Great wallpaper doesn't make a great hotel.

title: Quirky boutique hotel
text: A quirky and fun hotel in the heart of the Marais. Took the junior suite which gave us some elbow room - except for the head. At 6’4” in the mansard suite (lots of angled, low beams) I was constantly dodging skull-level collisions (often unsuccessfully). That, in combination with tight and awkward staircase climb to the room after elevator ride made this feel something less than a luxury hotel. Decor was interesting, front desk staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Location in the Marais was highly convenient starting point for many pleasant walks. Excellent breakfast. Reciprocal spa privileges at sister hotel a walk away on the Place des Vosges is nice in concept, but not really convenient - you’re unlikely to take advantage.  All in all a fun stay, but a bit pricey for what it really is once you look past the celebrity designer (Lacroix) decor.

title: Quirky and interesting, but far from perfect
text:
We stayed here for two nights and paid more than 550 euros for it. This is not exactly cheap for a 4 star hotel in Paris.

The property is interesting and with a lot of character, due to its history and layout. Our room - on the top floor - was definitely different from the usual hotel room, I would say in a good way. We were glad we had one of the bathrooms with a walk-in shower rather than a bathtub.

Unfortunately there are a few small things that would prevent me from giving more than 3 stars to this hotel.

The continental breakfast is cute and in theme with Paris. However, I felt that the small pastries that were served were not fresh nor of the quality I would expect in France. On the second day we skipped breakfast altogether and opted for a nearby cafe', where we had a much better croissant.

Bathroom and shower gel were not replenished in the room on our second day.

Only at the end of our stay, when we overheard a conversation during check in of a another guest, did we realise that we would have had free access to a beautiful spa nearby as part of our stay. When they checked us in, no one informed us. If we had known, we would've definitely made use of it.

Our rate entitled us to a late check-out, but it was denied to us on the basis that that hotel was full. However, there were still 4 rooms bookable online at the time our request was refused.

Finally, there was one (small) free bottle of water in the room on our arrival. I was somehow expecting another bottle on the second day. Instead, we had to opt for the small water bottle in the minibar. 4 euro per 0.5L is a bit outrageous for a 4 star hotel.

Overall, and sadly, we were not charm enough by this property to choose it as our base for our next Paris trip.

title: Gorgeous little place.
text:
It's been almost 5 years since our stay, but I remember it fondly.

The polka dot carpet, the orchids, the dark moody interiors and the quirky vibe, made for a wonderful choice for my birthday stay.

All correspondence prior to arrival was returned with helpful replies.

We requested the room in the main picture, red damask patterned walls, black & white scene wallpaper behind the bed, high gloss white furniture, and were quickly granted this wish. 
Buttttt, as beautiful as the space was it shared a wall with the elevator (insert sad face). Hubby sleeps well, I on the other hand am lighter, so after the first night of relative constant up down elevator noises, we asked to be relocated. Unfortunately no rooms available. Not a show stopper, so earplugs it was...but lesson learned for next time.

Yes, yes, the rooms are small, but it is Paris!

Wifi was hopeless!

Staff were ok, but not overly friendly.

We stayed in several arrondissements during our stay and this was by far our favourite. Fab restaurants close by, awesome boutiques, and gorgeous little cobblestoned streets that Paris does perfectly.

A memorable experience.

title: A Funky Hotel in Great neighborhood but....
text:
This is a Funky Hotel in a Great neighborhood but.... The rooms are small.  We were put on the 4th floor 401.  The first downside was that there is no elevator to the fourth floor, so you have to go up a tight spiral staircase with your suitcase from the third.  The second surprise was that the room only had a bath.  Been a while since I had taken one of those ;-)  This may vary by room or be a Paris thing, yet was what we encountered, so be warned.  

Lastly the hotel's website touts "Bar of the Petit Moulin Paris

Concept Bar at Le Petit Moulin

Enjoy a selection of cocktails and your favorite vinyl played with our Devialet speakers : power, clarity and preciseness unlike anything you have ever heard before.

Every Thursday, Friday and Saturday, from 5.00pm to 10.00pm.

Open to all. " This Caption is below the picture of a bartender shaking up drinks.  I had booked Thursday through Sunday so we would be able to come home to a vibrant scene before heading in.  Pretty funny when I came in after a full day of sightseeing Thursday only to see the bar dark. I asked the front desk why the bar was dark and where the DJ. was  He laughed and then chuckled "DJ" like I had had too much to drink.  In reality... The bar is an honor bar that is dark, unstaffed, and rarely visited.  This should really be removed from their website.

I gave the hotel an average score because the staff was helpful and it was in a nice neighborhood.  There were two restaurants at the end of the street with a vibrant scene.  You eventually get used to tight spaces and taking baths and hey... your in Paris Right?  Just don't think your going to this rockin hotel in paris, more for the quite crowd willing to put up with a little less to get more.  

Hope this helps...

If you are looking for a comfortable, chic, conveniently located hotel with great service, Hotel du Petit Moulin has it all.

text: I received a nice welcome and was allowed to check into my room early. The staff are pleasant. The room was small but not horribly so for Paris. Be sure to go to the rooftop for a great view of Sacre-Coeur.

title: A lovely hotel with an amazing rooftop bar
text:
I stayed at Hotel Rochechouart in August 2022 with my partner and 9 year old daughter.

The hotel building has been beautifully renovated. We stayed in a Grande Junior Suite. The bed was huge and comfortable, and there was a separate sleeping space with a comfortable sofa bed for my daughter. The air conditioning was good, which was a relief as we were there during a heatwave. The double glazing worked well and there was no noise from the street.

The staff were very welcoming and helpful, and my daughter loved the cake in reception, and the little story and sweets when we checked out.

Breakfast was great - a fairly limited selection, but very French, sourced locally and delicious, served in a lovely old room with a mosaic floor.

The rooftop bar has amazing views of Sacré Coeur and the Eiffel Tower. A great place to escape the crowds and still feel like you're making the most of Paris.

The immediate area felt safe, and there are a few supermarkets and nice bars and restaurants close by. Piglle was really close. The area beyond Pigalle around the Moulin Rouge is full of sex shops and if you go five minutes towards Gare du Nord it's not so nice, but those areas are easily avoided.

It's really close to Montmartre, and the lovely area around Abbesses.

Highly recommended!

title: A real little gem - views to kill for!
text: This hotel far surpassed expectations.  Staff were absolutely amazing, nothing was too much and Lucie spent a long time explaining the areas to go (and not!) within the local area with great clarity. The standard of food was excellent and the hotel had a really luxurious feel. Beds and pillows were incredibly comfortable and had a sumptuous feel. The hotel is a strange mix of really quiet when you need it to be and with a sassy bar on the roof. When I first went up to the roof bar, it took my breath away- not for the faint hearted! But wow what an unforgettable view of the city, whilst you enjoy a drink. It is in the heart of Pigalle with 2 metro stops close by. We much preferred to use Anvers, it had a safer feel. There is a great little supermarket about 200m away, useful for buying drinks that you can store in the fridge. There is also the option of leaving luggage with them for safekeeping before you check in or out, which tops dragging bags around Paris. If you love the Sacré cœur, it's the place for you, access to this unique landmark is close by (although it involves a lot of stairs!). Montmartre also boasts lots of choice in eateries especially around Place de Tetre, food is reasonably priced for tourists. Within the hotel, there are quiet spaces to enjoy and relax as well as enjoying an old world splendor with its graceful decor . Showers in a wet room style- en suite were powerful, lots of fluffy towels and beautiful smelling toiletries. Really not one to miss!

title: Beautiful Roof terrace, let down by small details
text:
The location of the hotel is superb - particularly if travelling from the UK on Eurostar, it is walking distance to Gare du Nord with many beautiful locations nearby. In addition, the roof terrace, and the staff who work there, are superb. As a regular traveller to Paris, it is one of the best terraces around.

However, where it falls down is the rooms and service of the rooms. I had paid for a larger executive room and was given 402, which felt small, dated and a little tired with marks on the walls and carpets, though was clean. It looked out over the street although noise was not an issue, even when market was on outside. There are certain amenities that I would expect and these were not present. For example, when I arrived there was a coffee machine but no coffee was provided, on day two, the bottle of water was not replaced (in Paris at height of summer) and I had to go to local store to purchase as room service did not respond, and on the final day, my towels were not replaced, so had to dry after shower with hand towels - not what I would expect from a 4-star establishment.

title: Beautiful hotel!
text:
This hotel is fantastic. We arrived early evening and were checked in by a lovely man at the front desk - who upon seeing which room we were allocated too, changed our room to one with a view of the Eiffel tower - fantastic. Our room was stylish, clean, good air con (& spacious considering location in Paris city centre). Nespresso coffee machine appreciated. We had several drinks in the hotel bar downstairs which were lovely, bartenders very friendly. Didn't eat at the restaurant but it looked popular. 
Rooftop bar - we went up one evening but couldn't get a seat due to it being full, so went up the following morning to check out the view - absolutely stunning. Eiffel Tower to one side and Sacre Coeur to the other. 
Location right next to Montmartre was fabulous, 2 Metro stations within 5 mins walk, plenty of bars and restaurants on your doorstep. 
Also the luggage store is helpful to store suitcases if you have to check out a while before your flight.
All in all wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel and we hope to return.

title: Perfectly imperfect
text: In an attempt to reconcile my thoughts and opinions into as honest an appraisal as possible of Hotel Rochechouart ,I took time to read a few reviews to compare and contrast the experiences of other guests with mine. While I do recognise some of the anomalies identified by other guests such as the imprecise replenishment of amenities for instance, make no mistake; Hotel Rochechouart is an exceptional hotel. Firstly, It’s an undeniably well thought out  and sympathetically decorated space, with a consistently executed theme with recurrent leitmotifs such as  the wood grain appliqué and alabaster wall lighting. The room was elegantly precise; a perfect exemplar and case study in  reductive luxury. The olfactory identity of this hotel, courtesy of the house scent, is indelible; and the atmosphere in the common spaces, especially the bar after dark, is without equivalent. But all of this pales in comparison to the quality and generosity of spirit of the staff at this property. Across the board; from front of house, housekeeping and everything inbetween, the service was consistently efficient, sincere and humane rather than obsequious, so much so that it seems almost unfair to single out any one member of staff in partuclar. That said, Wilson in the restaurant is a rarity. His unforgettably familiar disposition and joie de vivre in the execution of his work alone justifies a stay at Hotel Rochechouart.  In conclusion, it’s worth contextualising this special hotel; imperfections are, by definition, both priced in and idiosyncratic of any human systems. Hotels are no exception, and ipso facto, neither is Hotel Rochechouart.  Be that as it may, Hotel Rochechouart is an exceptional hotel; a well decorated space staffed by a dedicated ,well intentioned and well dispositioned group of people and as a consequence, this hotel may well be the exception that proves the rule; perfect imperfections.

title: Overall good stay
text:
This is an old, renovated establishment. My father and I stayed in a 'Deluxe' room, where he enjoyed the main bedroom and I slept on a sofa in what appeared to be a former large closet where lighting was barely sufficient. The accommodation was cramped but adequate for our needs, and would have sufficed for a traditional couple. We were puzzled that there was no chest of drawers, and no coat hooks were present on the main door. Bathrobes are a nice touch, but ours were medium-sized and would have been impossible for larger people to wear.

The traditional bathtub has no showerhead but rather a hand attachment. We dislike the slim glass partition (versus a fully enclosed door or curtain) as it allows water to splash everywhere on the floor adjacent. One of the two sinks had a faulty drain plug such that water would drain excessively slowly. We notified the front desk, but the issue was never resolved (perhaps because it was weekend).

The restaurant is probably the hotel's greatest asset. The food is quite good, especially the breakfast buffet. Servers were very welcoming and attentive,  and worked diligently to ensure that we were satisfied. They should find dispensing containers that are able to preserve the temperature of heated beverages like coffee. 

Be sure to visit the rooftop, especially at night, where you can enjoy a spectacular view of the city.

title: Nice hotel
text: In general I enjoyed my stay at Rochechouart, but I have a few important remarks. The main reason why I'm giving three 3/5 is that at first we didn't get the room we booked (we paid for double room suite with a view and we got single room without a proper bed for the third person and without the city view). That was quickly fixed, but I really dislike this kind of situations. I'm sure that it wasn't a simple mistake, because the single room was prepared for three people, so maybe the hotel was overbooked. The hotel looks nice (I love the art deco style, especially the restaurat looks very classy), but requires small renovations. There are few things that are not just unaesthetic, but actually affecting the comfort of stay (for example leaking bath that could be very easily fixed). We got some bathroom accessories only the first day (and the amount was suitable for one person, not three) and they were not later replenished. In the corridor there were used glasses and leftovers left on the ground for the whole day (someone from the service left them in there, not guests). Breakfasts were amazing! Staff was very nice and helpful. The best beds I have ever slept on! Very quiet in the hotel, we really appreciated that. The hotel is in very pretty location, close to Moulin Rouge and half an hour walk from the Louvre Museum. Fair price.

title: Great Montmartre Getaway
text:
Hotel Rochechouart is a fifteen minute walk from Gare du Nord, so if you're arriving by Eurostar it's fairly easy to get to. Walk up Rue de Dunkerque then turn left at Blvd Marguerite de Rochechouart. The hotel is also within walking distance of Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre.

The restaurant clearly takes great pride in their food. The belly of pork was soft, tender and delicious. The pollock was beautifully paired with roast fennel and shrimp sauce. The chocolate mousse was light, indulgent and lived up to it's status as a classic French dessert. It's a good sign to see some of the patrons made up not only of hotel guests who want a convenient bite but also locals who come for the food.

The bar is helmed with similar passion and flare. Watching the bartender make cocktails was real theatre. The drinks were generous and balanced, celebrating both timeless old classics and fresh original mixes.

The rooms are spacious and luxurious. The spiral staircase that coils around the lift shaft, framed with brass fittings brings to mind that quintessential feel of Parisian decor.

The rooftop bar commands wonderful views of Paris. Sacré-Cœur stands on the Montmartre hilltop on one side, while the Eiffel Tower stands on the other.

With it's welcoming and able staff, Hotel Rochechouart makes for a great getaway.
