title: A lovely hotel in a lovely spot
text:
A lovely hotel in a prime spot right on the Place des Vosges square and right in the popular Marais district, it’s spread over about four floors with a pleasant and attractive courtyard at the front. Staff were all very pleasant and helpful. Our room wasn’t ready when we arrived unfortunately, but we were quite early and it was long before check-in time, so that’s hardly their fault. We were though asked if we would like to take a shower in the spa changing rooms which I thought was a nice touch. I was a bit surprised when we returned later that our bags weren’t already in the room instead of having to ask for them. A minor point I know, but this is a 5* hotel.

The room itself was perhaps rather optimistically described as a suite. Perhaps the fact that you walk in to a small hallway with the bedroom and bathroom off of here rather than directly in to the bedroom is what constitutes a suite. Again, perhaps I’m being picky, but for €700 a night I thought an extra lounge area might have been included. That said, it was a decent enough sized room although no view other than the office block opposite. Facilities included a Nespresso machine and a mini-bar although if you wanted anything other than coffee (tea, for example) you were out of luck. There was also a TV on the wall, although we didn’t use this so I don’t know what the picture quality was like, and a safe. The bed was large and comfy whilst the bathroom had twin sinks and a separate walk-in shower and bath. The shower was ok, certainly hot enough, but could have been a little more powerful. A couple of bottles of complementary water were provided, although the turn-down service was ridiculously early some days. They knocked on the door at 5:30pm when we had obviously yet to go out for the evening, and didn’t return later. I thought the sockets might have included USB chargers, but no such luck and it was quite difficult to find a socket that was actually liv e all the time instead of going off with the lights. In the end I had to scramble around under the desk to find one. There was no noise to speak of from outside as we were on a quiet side street, but the internal walls did seem a little thin. Fortunately our neighbours were fairly quiet.  

Breakfast was a help yourself buffet selection, although we were also offered cooked egg dishes such as omelettes. There was a good selection that covered most bases, including hot food (sausages, crispy bacon, scrabbled egg and something that looked rather like ratatouille), a good selection of cold meats and cheeses, smoked salmon, cereals, yoghurts, pastries, fruit and nuts. I can’t really think of anything else that I would have added. The croissants were exceptionally good, but everything else was very nice too.         

Overall, a lovely hotel in a great spot and I’d happily stay here again.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Absolutely wold-class
text:
What an outstanding place. Beautiful. Impeccable service. Meticulous attention to detail and all in a non-pretentious package. 

Probably the best hotel I have ever stayed in. 

From the arrival experience (thanks for the balloons, champagne and chocolate for my girlfriend’s birthday) to the helpfulness of the concierge to the service at breakfast to the lovely ‘honour bar’ - absolutely immaculate. 

And a fantastic location to boot. 

I would give it 6 stars if I could.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Memorable Stay
text: This is a truly 5 star hotel in a great location in Paris. A very  comfortable, clean and spacious room, with a large comfortable bed. The concierge staff are very helpful, with very good English. Has a great casual bar with good range of drinks and snack food. Highly recommend.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Beautiful location and hotel
text: This hotel is located in Place des Vosges, previously a beautiful old mansion. It is quiet and has a wonderful courtyard where you can eat outside for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Service is top notch and very friendly and helpful. However, the room is uncomfortable. It was very dark, and the mattress was extremely hard and uncomfortable.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect choice for service & location
text: Located on the Place des Voges, this property is wonderful. Loved the neighborhood for its quaintness and quiet. At the same time, it's close to multiple Metro stops/lines which made navigating the city quite easy. Breakfast was included (and was delicious). The rooms, while small, are well-equipped and maid service was prompt and thorough. The courtyard is a wonderful space any time of day -- for breakfast or afternoon wine/snack. Service was on point. They also offer airport transfers (for additional fee of course). This was our first visit and if we return to Paris, we'll be back here. Cannot recommend highly enough.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A home away from home!
text: This is a uniquely charming hotel. The decor is elegant country. The staff is warm, respectful and engaging. The breakfast is delicious. The spa is very good. The feeling is like being at home. I highly recommend Le Pavillon de la Reine.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Excellent hotel stay
text: A perfect Parisian getaway! My partner and I stayed for four nights for our honeymoon and could not have been better looked after. From the impeccable service to the beautiful and very comfortable rooms, through to the delicious food in restaurant Anne, we could not have had a better or more special stay.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Warm welcome in Paris
text: Lovely hotel, lovely location, lovely staff. Warm,friendly, helpful staff really make this beautiful place the perfect place to stay in Paris. It’s a glorious building in a glorious location but the standout is the wonderful staff.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect stay in Paris' most beautiful hotel
text: This hotel is a beautiful hidden gem in one of Paris' most gorgeous areas (La Marais). Not only is the location fantastic and walking distance twosome of the best cafes, restaurants, patisseries, and ice cream spots, but the hotel itself is absolutely beautiful. Sitting in the courtyard sipping on a glass of rose was probably one of my most memorable moments during my solo Parisian trip. The breakfast was delicious with an abundance of options. The room, wow. I had asked for a room with a view and was given a room with three views; over looking some of Paris' most beautiful architecture, quaint streets, and overlooking the courtyard. I will be coming back again!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: An Elegant Hotel in Le Marais Paris.
text: We stayed at this lovely hotel for a week. It was extremely busy but the staff were so professional and focused on the well being of their guests. The concierge staff were constantly bombarded with requests and handled everything magnificently. The night concierge staff had found us restaurant reservations prior to our visit and every one was excellent. The food at the hotel was exquisite and the courtyard elegant and welcoming. Our room was very well air conditioned which turned out to be such a blessing because of the high temperatures in Paris that week. The bed was large a very comfortable and I am very particular about beds.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect Paris experience
text: This is my favourite hotel in Paris - in the Place des Vosges, which is a beautiful square in the Marais. I have been coming to this hotel for years, and I feel very at home every time I return. The Place des Vosges is architecturally sublime, and the hotel,is tucked away in its own lovely courtyard which is a real sum trap on a sunny day.. Service is outstanding, the rooms are beautiful and well equipped, the food is excellent - what more can I say?
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Flashback of my hamster Timmy dying.
text: Bad experience! Confusion with my reservation and payment through a their party travel website. Vanessa at the hotel is just flat out dishonest! My room smelled like a dead hamster! Slow wifi, big gap under the front door so anything that happens in the hall you hear everything, snobby staff who don't want to be bothered dealing with fundamental issues. Was over charged and the curreny exchange rate they gave me was a absolute ripoff. Two nights was too long in this property.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: April 2022
text:
Very professional and welcoming staff. We enjoyed breakfast in the dining room and drinks in the courtyard. Rooms are quiet and well done. Location is great for exploring the Marais area and close to the metro stop
I will stay here again
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great boutique hotel
text: This is a very good hotel in a great area, the Marais, with plenty to see and do within walking distance.   Extremely friendly staff, our suite was very spacious and immaculate.   The breakfast was fantastic.   Such a perfect hotel for a stay in Paris!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A beautiful hotel
text:
I can't praise this hotel and staff highly enough. This is our 3rd trip to Paris and we always try to stay in a different area. 
Our room was lovely (room 52), so clean and spacious for Paris. The breakfast was delicious and such good quality. We have stayed in 5 star hotels all over the world and are very fussy.
The concierges recommended two great brasseries in the neighbourhood and were very knowledgeable. All the staff were so great and I work in hospitality myself.
Well done guys.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Charming hotel.
text: The hotel is situated behind a courtyard leading off the Place des Vosges. It is simply lovely. The staff were excellent. We had a double height corner room with a bed on the higher level. Champagne on arrival. Very comfortable public areas. Great breakfasts. We were made very welcome. Ideal for persons looking for a gracious, relaxing stay. Highly recommended.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Excellent stay
text:
Service was great and its location Is fantastic. All was good. Highly recommended !
Restaurant was excellent, very nice terrace and little garden. Decoration was very stylish. If you are looking for a quite and luxury hotel, you just found it
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A precious gem in Paris
text: The most romantic and calm place to stay in Paris at the beautiful Place des Vosges. The staff is great, concierge arranges everything you might need, from dinner reservations, bike rental and transfers. The most tranquil way to get around. A must stay place. Even Parisians love it and they should know.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Quiet elegance
text: It's a fabulous hotel, seeming more like a home , with beauty, sophistication, and welcoming....The interior park, with plants, trees, orchids, and even sculpture is divine. It's fun to sit in the garden with friends, or just alone, imbibing Paris, sipping cafe, and reading a book.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: More Than Satisfied
text: It is so rare that you search for a vision that you have had of a hotel that you not only get what you are looking for but far exceed your vision but PDLR did exactly that.  When you walk off the Square at Place De La Vosges and enter the courtyard you just know you have arrived at something special.  The staff from Nils and Arnaud at the concierge desk to the rest are completely committed to making your experience in Paris nothing less than special.  Our rooms were beautifully appointed, comfortable, spotless, warm and cozy.  The hotel was quiet but in the middle of the Marais which is an exceedingly  lively part of town so it became our oasis.  We will stay here anytime and everytime we are in Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A satisfied customer
text:
Stayed one night with my oldest son and enjoyed every minute
Place des Vosges is well situated, nice restaurants and close to much
Inside the hotel gate it is so peaceful and calm: exactly what one needs
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Charming Parisian Hideaway
text: The Pavillion de la Reine is a lovely, intimate boutique hotel tucked behind the cloisters in the Place des Vosges, a genuine Parisian neighborhood. It's very fashionable and tasteful, though not pretentious or grand. A very easy place to relax in. Very helpful staff. The lobby public rooms work as well any I have set foot in: they serve breakfast, aperitifs, dinner, lobby lounging very effectively. A beautiful courtyard is out front too. Standard rooms are nicely decorated, though the more contemporarily themed ones work better. They are small though. It's not a hotel for the claustraphobic. Still, it's got great atmosphere and one feels as though they are staying at a private club, versus a hotel.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Exceptional in all ways!
text: A beautiful oasis, lovely furnished rooms with excellent toiletries and linens. Exceptionally gracious, thoughtful, knowledgeable concierges, Rudy and Arnaud. Breakfast has a generous assortment of food and very good service. Looking forward to our next stay here!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Small, exclusive, hidden
text:
Wonderful hotel with excellent breakfast. Staff professional and friendly - the best of French hospitality.
Rooms small - as usual for Paris, Wonderful location in place des Vosges, Marais.
Hidden away, a sanctuary...
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Superb Hotel in a great location
text: Happy to recommend this hotel.  Excellent standard.  Great staff, beautiful room/suite, and in a great location.    It is set back from the Place des Vosges making it so quiet and relaxing to return to after a hectic day of discovering Paris!  There are lots of cafes, bars, restaurants, bistros, boutiques, shops, metro right on your doorstep.   It was perfect!  (Hotel drinks - tea coffees etc were very expensive - which is why we chose to go out for breakfast - but you get what you pay for!!)
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Charming home away from home
text: Gorgeous hotel in the heart of Place des Vosges in the Marais neighbourhood.  Friendly and hospitable, staff are at hand to attend to your every whim.  The rooms are uniquly designed, I had a suite which was generous in size with large bathroom, separate WC, large lounge area and bedroom. The breakfast was vast and super tasty.  The spa was so relaxing and thoroughly recommended.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Fabulous stay in a small and perfectly formed hotel
text: This was a super hotel, beutifully furnishes, extremely helpful staff and a cosy honesty bar for an evening drink. We didn't eat in the hotel or use the spa facilities but I imagine they are equally impressive. I would certainy stay here again.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A Lovely, Unforgettable Hotel!
text:
I traveled alone to Paris (just because) - Stayed 6 nights at La Pavillon de la Reine; before I arrived, the hotel concierge staff (Arnaud & Rudy) were extremely responsive to several emails I sent, and they were able to obtain a ticket for me to a long-sold-out opera performance.

The hotel is beautiful and extremely quiet (a gorgeous courtyard between the main entrance and the famous, quiet square in which it is located).  Public areas have gorgeous, sophisticated decor; I didn’t see other guest rooms, but mine was immaculate, spacious, bright, and very colorful - fantastic bathroom btw.

Morning breakfast buffet served in two quiet rooms off the main lobby is fantastic, with options to please anyone.  Room service was prompt and extremely courteous (thank you, Mantie!). Also appreciated the evening honor bar in lobby.

I spent every day enjoying Paris, but at the end of all that, Le Pavillon de la Reine was a wonderful spot to come “home” to.  The hotel is not inexpensive, but it is exceptional for those comfortable with the price.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Very nice hotel
text: Very nice and pleasant hotel at one of the loveliest places of Paris. Family hotel with good service and friendly staff. We would surely recommand this hotel and if possible we will be coming back to this hotel when we will visit Paris in the future.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great hotel with friendly staff!
text: Stayed with my wife and daughter and we all loved this hotel. Excellent location at Place de Vosges and in the hart of Le Marais. Friendly and personal staff, authentic rooms,  a nice spa en fitness and parking. Concierge Fred made us feel very welcome and had great advice for our special night out. Will definitely come back!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great hotel in a great location. Fantastic service.
text:
Loved the hotel and will recommend it to anyone who want to visit Paris and stay in the Marais area. We picked it after much research since we were visiting Paris for longer than a week and we wanted a hotel with great service in a nice location. We were not disappointed. The hotel accommodated our needs excellently and we recommend you to work with the hotel on your needs. The staff was fantastic and were readily available. The property is pretty, the rooms are well done and comfortable and we did not feel any stress of staying in the same room for longer than a week. The hotel breakfast was a highlight and we looked forward to it everyday. The food in Restaurant 28 was of high quality. 

In short, it is a great hotel and we highly recommend it.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: As always - The best
text: Another wonderful stay. Service is personable and warm. If you need more room, the larger suites offer excellent value for Paris. Breakfast and the honor bar are both great. The location can't be beat. What's not to like?
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Fantastic Location, Fantastic Room, Fantastic Staff!!
text: I can't say enough good things about this hotel.  Located within walking distance of most attactions, a fantastic spa and spacious room.  But the best part was the staff.  There wasn't a request, from tickets to museums to help with getting a vaccination pass to getting a knife to cut some cheese in our room that they didn't fulfill with a yes and a smile.  I've never had such attentive treatment in any hotel I've stayed in and I've stayed in a lot.  Will definitely be returning here!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Fantastic experience
text: The stay was simply awesome. Hotel, food, the friendliness made us feel home from the moment we entrerer the hotel. The breakfast was also really great and the dinner both in Anne and in No. 28 was truly excellent. Cannot wait to get back
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A Very Pleasant Experience
text:
.

I should start by saying the hotel seems much smaller in real life than the photos suggest, and of course this being Paris, the hotel rooms are quite small. However, it's a very nice hotel in a good location. The staff were very pleasant and everything went smoothly. Breakfast was also a nice selection, and we liked having the choice of different rooms to eat in, or weather permitting, to eat outside. 

Our long weekend trip was packed so we didn't truly get to relax and enjoy the hotel to its full capacity. If I dare have one gripe it's the fact the rooms do have Smart TV's yet there's no Netflix and you will struggle to find an English language channel unless you want to only watch the news. This being France you can't even watch Amazon Prime on your own appliances. I appreciate you don't go away to watch TV, but after a day out and about, and a good dinner somewhere, watching TV in bed to end the day is one of life's little luxuries when travelling.

Place de Voges is very nice, though rather limited. It wasn't quite as chic as expected. But it's quiet and you can get a good nights sleep, and it's close to all the most important things you probably want to see. 

Probably most importantly, we would stay at the hotel again.
.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Excellent
text: This is our favourite hotel in Paris. It provides everything we want including an excellent location with easy access to the other parts of Paris we love. Its new restaurant, Anne, is worth visiting too. We were blown away by the quality of the food.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Makes you feel that just maybe you could be Parisian too.
text: You can have the Crillon, the Ritz and the Place Vendome, but give me the Pavillon de la Reine, originally built in the 1600s for Louis XIII and his queen. Step out from the charming hotel into the Place des Vosge and enjoy pastry shops, bistros and art galleries all under the gothic arcades surrounding the leafy, arboreal square. Or go for a jog  around the park and the school children at play. Besides it's chic and central location, it's a wonderful hotel. The decor is elegantly colorful and updated. The rooms are cozy, yet spacious The bathroom and amenities are top notch. My shower pressure was amazing! The staff was friendly expeditious, helpful and attitude free.  Will return. Loved it.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: a gem in the Marais
text: Great hotel on the Place des Vosges.  Couldn't ask for a better location.   Good service and the people working there are all very nice.  Room was beautiful and comfortable.  Great location for a walking tour of all of Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Paris Vacation
text: Always a favorite hotel. Love the location, and the staff is amazing and attentive. My room was beautiful and quiet. The area is fun with lots to do, and walkable is you want. Can't wait too go back!!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great boutique hotel
text:
We loved our stay at this small hotel.  It is located in the Marais area.  So close to great shopping and food.

We were upgraded to a loft.  Very spacious room.  

The breakfast was great.  Sorry that the restaurant was closed for evening meal.  

We had a delightful time.  

Would go back.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Best hotel in Paris
text: This is a hotel that gets every detail just right.  It is elegant, but warm and gracious at the same time.  The food was some of the best we had in Paris (and that is saying something).  The concierge Arnaud was amazing before and during our stay.  The location on the Place des Voges was unbeatable.  We hated to leave and there is no other place we will stay in future trips to Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Excellent staff in awkward hotel
text:
We spent two nights here recently and found the staff, and service to be delightful, helpful, and very attentive. The hotel is beautifully situated on the right bank with so many great spots all around - shopping, restaurants, museums, etc. The breakfast is delicious and relaxing, and there is great food the rest of the day with an honor bar for the afternoon and evening.. The courtyard on a pretty day is delightful.
The two distractions for us were the exceedingly small, dark bedrooms and the tiny hallways and elevator. When shown our first room, we asked to be moved, and were given a room that was slightly better. There is no room for suitcases and with two people in the room we felt as if we were on top of each other.  The decor is SO dark - black painted walls and doors, dark colored curtains and carpets, etc. And the lighting in the bedrooms is very dim despite there being sconces and lamps everywhere. It just felt like a basement room and did not have a refreshing feel. The  hallways and elevator were very small also... like a doll house. Though the service was great, the tiny, dark rooms will prevent us from returning.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfection
text:
Everything about our stay was perfection. The location could not be better - across from the park in the center of the Marais, yet it's pin-drop quiet in a blissful courtyard; the breakfasts are amazing and the service is incredibly warm and helpful; the hotel is stylish and intimate, and the terrace is a great place to gather with friends. Best of all was the concierge services. I'd had the unfortunate luck of going to a bad hair salon (not recommended by the hotel) the night before an important work event; it was late at night on a Sunday. The amazing concierge went above and beyond and called every person in her rolodex and somehow miraculously found a fabulous hair stylist to come to our room at 10pm to fix my hair - I was astounded. Another concierge helped me find all of the flea market information and reviews, and another helped with gallery exhibitions. Throughout our stay, the staff was helpful, warm, welcoming, and resourceful. The concierge staff at this hotel should teach a master class. We felt incredibly well cared for throughout our wonderful 8-day stay. 

We hope to return soon and often.

If I could change one thing it would be the room size (this is central Paris - to be expected) - our initial room was small (and had limited place for clothing); but they were able to change us to a different room with much more space.  The WIFI was a bit iffy at times, but I hear that they are working on this.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Amazing service and hospitality
text: What an amazing place to stay in Paris. Centrally located and impeccable service. My wife and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary with a trip to Paris and this was the perfect hotel to choose. All the staff were very helpful, courteous and knowledgeable.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Excelent hotel
text:
Superb location, service and amenities. 
Went there as a couple but also suitable for a family. 
Concierge was really helpful. 
Outdoor patio is outstanding. 
Rooms were big enough for a Parisian Hotel. Would repeat, no doubt
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Gorgeous hotel amazing staff
text:
The location of the hotel is perfect, tucked away in a picturesque courtyard. What made our trip was the hotel staff, especially Fred! He was super helpful, helping us arrange reservations and gave us amazing recommendations.
We cant wait to come back!!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Gem tucked away off the busy Place de Vosges
text:
This is a beautiful gem of a hotel.  The staff are wonderful - nothing is too much trouble.  They make the hotel special. They were friendly efficient and helpful. Our room overlooked the beautiful vine clad courtyard where we also enjoyed excellent breakfasts.  Location is perfect too - super quiet but close to everything.
Highly recommend.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Fantastic hotel
text: Great hotel in the middle of a bustling central part of Paris. Very friendly and helpful staff. Absolutely recommend it. We stayed with a family of five and even the kids loved it. The garden outside particularly is very pleasant o stay and relax.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: My room with a view!
text: Fabulous small hotel in the Marais, close to everything and right off the Places de Voges. The staff was attentive and the hotel has an intimate, luxurious feel. The food was fantastic and the wine list exeptional.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: One of the loveliest hotels in Paris!
text: You feel like royalty when staying in this hotel. From the second the porter rushes out to get your luggage, the service is 5-star and continues to be. The restaurant and courtyard are lovely and the food delicious. The location is excellent and the gorgeous Place de Vosges is a beautiful morning stroll to get whatever you need to go. The beds are comfortable and the air conditioning actually works (unlike most European hotels, where it's minimal). I would highly recommend it and will stay again.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Beautiful quiet hotel in the perfect location
text: Perfect location!! Right opposite one of the most beautiful parks in Paris, Place des Vosges. So many amazing restaurants, boutiques and museums in the area. I loved that I could walk to so many places. The hotel is in a very quiet street and very beautiful with all the vines growing on the building. Great breakfast selection and I love the access to the gym, jacuzzi and spa. We used the jacuzzi and had it reserved to ourselves for 1 hour due to covid rules, which we loved. For a small boutique hotel it has a lot of great ammenities. Highly recommend this hotel in my favourite neighbourhood in Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great location and excellent service
text: We loved our stay at this beautiful boutique hotel. The staff went out of their way to make our stay as comfortable as possible. The hotel breathes a true Parisian vibe and the complimentary valet parking added to the experience.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Wonderful peaceful place
text:
We loved our staying in this peaceful chateau. Staff was very friendly and the facilities were great too.
The restaurant food was amazing. We loved the bbq options too. Not to mention about the nature around the place
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A Short But Pleasant Stay!
text: We stayed here for one night last week and wished it could have been longer.  A lovely hotel in a lovely busy neighborhood of Paris.  Our room was on the top floor, and had all the expected comforts.  The staff was gracious and accommodating, preparing our room quickly.  We enjoyed champagne on the terrace, dinner in the hotel restaurant and a wonderful breakfast in bed before our departure.  I would not hesitate to recommend this beautiful hotel.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect Paris Hotel
text: PDLR is the perfect hotel for a quiet, restful stay in Paris - in the heart of the bustling Marais. Service is great, and while limited by Covid guidelines for certain services, overall the hotel was able to remain accommodating and hospitable for requests. Great concierge service that helped me repair my suitcase same day, arrange for a Rapid Covid Test to be conducted in the comfort of my room, and of course - all general restaurant reservation and museum tickets, etc. I'll be coming back!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect Weekend Getaway
text: I stayed here for a relaxing weekend away with my mother in fall 2019. The hotel is absolutely gorgeous. I particularly loved the breakfast they offered in the hotel's cosy dining room. The location, on the Place des Vosges, has great shopping and culture. It is the perfect location to offer you a glimpse of true Parisian life, while also having lots to do. The hotel is adjacent to the Marais, a wonderful district in Paris. It is also near many museums and just a short drive from other big Paris sites.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Great hotel, great location
text: We were lucky enough to stay here just before lockdown began. We had  a lovely room which was beautifully decorated. We settled in immediately.... the hotel was also very accommodating over dietary issues which is always tricky in France! We met many guest who where hotel regulars (fashion week) which is always a good sign.The only negative was the shower no bath in the room but I hadn't checked before.  I will definitely stay here again.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A luxury hotel in a nice location, but didn't feel welcoming
text: This is a beautiful property in a wonderful part of Paris. The rooms are fine, not that large, but they are very well appointed. The hallways are quite dark and dingy, with low ceilings. Elevators are tiny and quite old as well. I wanted to like the hotel but from the beginning, when I entered the property, I didn't feel well taken care of or as if the staff even wanted me there as a guest. I didn't find the service for breakfast to be helpful or friendly either. Next time I come to Paris I would probably choose another hotel or just stay in an Air BNB as I usually do in Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Chic yet central
text: My favourite thing about this hotel is the private courtyard and honesty bar.  At night the gates close and you are free to linger over drinks on the pretty, ivy clad terrace until late.  Rooms are varied, the one I stayed in was nothing to write home about but the ambiance overall is charming and the location is perfect.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Charming Hotel
text: My stay at the Pavillon de la Reine was a long time coming and it didn't fail or disappoint.  Perfectly located to access many of the Marias' charming cafes and bistros and super stylish shops and boutiques as well as countless museums.  The hotel is so beautiful, hidden away in a quiet courtyard, you would harldy know you were in a city.  Beautiful inside with warm cosy interiors, the hote is bursting with country-style touches and oodles of charm.  Breakfast is absolutely  outstanding with a very wide choice to keep even the fussy eater happy.  The hotel has an honesty bar stocked with many drinks.  I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again,
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect location
text: This is our second stay at Le Pavillon.  We have been visiting the Marais for about 20 years and the location can't be beat.  We opted for a larger suit this time and were not disappointed.  The staff is very helpful and made all our dinner reservations.  During the strike they kept us updated on all transportation issues.  Just made reservations for our next visit.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Beautiful, well located Parisian Hotel
text:
If you are looking for a refined, elegant hotel near Le Marais, this is it.  The Hotel decor is elegant and refined without being stuffy. The patio, lobby and dining areas are welcoming and intimate. There is a open, honor bar off the lobby stocked with quality wine, champagne and spirits for a drink with friends all afternoon and evening.

 My room was truly memorable, which is saying a lot given how much I travel.  It was beautifully decorated with open beam ceilings and deep set character windows overlooking the streets below.  It had a comfortable and lovely living room area, well appointed bath, and large bedroom with period antique furniture. 

 The staff at the front desk was very helpful and friendly. 

My only criticism is that the support staff could be better trained. In the middle of a business breakfast I was holding in the dining room, one of the support staff decided to vacuum the room around us. Which made our business conversation impossible and raised dust around our meal. I did mention something to the front desk and hopefully that will be rectified in the future. 

But it all this hotel is highly recommended and a beautiful find in the heart of Paris.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Iconic, yet...
text:
On our previous visits to Paris, including for our honeymoon, we stayed at the charming luxury boutique Hôtel Duc de Saint-Simon located in the 6th arrondissement in St. Germain-Des-Pres. For this trip, however, we decided to check out Le Marais, the very hip and colorful district straddling the 3rd and 4th arrondissements. A savvy traveler friend directed us to the five-star hotel Le Pavillon de la Reine, located on the Place des Vosges, in the center of it all.

This regal stone and brick structure beckoned visitors through a narrow passageway leading into a lovely courtyard with umbrellaed tables surrounded by greenery fronting the hotel’s main entrance. Given the season, it was festively lit prompting many passersby to sate their Instagram addictions. The lobby and common rooms were tastefully decorated and furnished, though a bit subdued for my taste. The words “cozy, “classic” and “quaint” come to mind.

We reasoned it was a five-star hotel (with a five-star rack rate), so little need to book the honeymoon suite. Any room would be special. Right? We soon squeezed into the small lift and were led to our “classic” room, which was just over the hotel‘s entrance overlooking the courtyard. It was duplex connected by a steep, narrow staircase. The bedroom was in the loft and below it was a small sitting space and the bathroom. Between the two spaces, we had barely enough room for our two suitcases, packed for ten days on the road, and very little shelving or closet space. We also soon realized that the opening and closing of the hotel’s front door did not bode well for light sleepers.

The next morning, we requested a room change, which the hotel graciously obliged. The “superior” room to which they moved us, was in the back and much quieter, but it was even smaller than the first. Oh well. We’re only sleeping here one more night. That said, the bed was comfy and the hotel’s location at Place des Vosges unmatched.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: My favorite hotel in Paris
text: It's a treat to stay at PDLR! Everyone is helpful and eager to please. The rooms are spacious for Paris, and the location can't be beat. The courtyard is the perfect setting for a late-night cocktails. It's also a nice place to unwind after a day of museum-hopping. An oasis in the middle of Paris's bustling street life.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Beautiful, iconic location
text:
Beautiful boutique hotel in the historic Place de Vosges.  Enter through a traditional Paris gate/door into a magical courtyard. Wonderful staff. Beautiful, comfortable, quiet sitting room in the entrance.  There is a spa but we didn’t visit. 
We stayed in one of the cheaper rooms so it was small and beside the elevator but it was still very comfortable and the bathroom was very nice. Clean.  Welcome chocolate too!  I just can’t give 5 stars for a place that costs this much!  Other than price - no complaints.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: A gem of comfort and tranquility in the heart of Paris
text: This lovely hotel offers comfort, delightful service and discreet luxury in a beautiful setting. It is wonderfully located and once you have stayed here you will always want to return. In short, it is special.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Honeymoon of our dreams!
text: As a guest of usually large corporate luxury properties, my husband and I were excited to try a smaller bespoke boutique and we couldn't have been more pleased with our decision.  Everything from the location, decor and amenities were beyond perfect but it was the staff that truly made our stay.  Le Pavilion de la Reine's amazing team assisted us with VIP airport pick up and drop off during the transportation strike, helped us discover new restaurants and secure the perfect reservation times as well as just their overall demeanor of always going above and beyond was TOP KNOTCH, we cannot recommend this hotel enough to family, friends and strangers alike.  It was the perfect spot to kick off our honeymoon and made us feel so welcome and at home.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Lovely hotel on Place des Vosges
text: I stayed here for one night only when my train to Strasbourg was cancelled due to the strike. Stayed 5 other nights at Hotel Luxembourg Parc ( see separate review). This is a very nice hotel on one of the most beautiful squares in Paris. Room was a bit small ( and I didn’t book the smallest option) but nicely decorated and fine for one person. Would have been tight for more. What makes this hotel are the location and really helpful professional staff. Although I only stayed one night I felt well taken care of and found everyone charming and very helpful. There is a lovely place to sit outside in good weather and the bar and restaurant are both very appealing. The location, close to so many things yet quietly set off the square is very special.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Quiet unfussy elegance with very high standards
text: Have stayed at this hotel for the past five years or so. Cannot recommend it highly  enough. Every thing here works really really well in a way that immediately makes you feel at home. The staff, rooms and food are all simply outstanding.  Moreover the excellence is both consistent and sustained.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Superb hotel in the heart of Paris with unprecedented services
text: I am traveling a lot around the globe. Clearly Le Pavillon de la Reine (PdlR) is one of the top 3 hotels in Paris! The entire package is consistent at the highest level. Food excellent, accommodation top notch and above the service conveys an unmatched notion of greatest hospitality. No matter if you are young or old, single or couple, male or female this hotel matches everybody's expectations before you are even aware of your expectations! First choice! Love it! Looking forward to my next stay! Thank you to the whole PdlR Team!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Nice hotel
text:
I stayed for one night in the family suite, it is a 2 bedrooms suite with a cozy salon and 3 bathrooms! Very clean, spacious rooms, and a very generous and tasty breakfast. They even have a chemney!!
Me and my family had a very pleasing experience, and we surely recommend le pavillon de la reine
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Wonderful boutique hotel in beautiful area
text: My 18 year old daughter and I couldn't have been happier at this boutique hotel for a long weekend.  We absolutely loved the Marais area and enjoyed seeing this part of Paris that was not as touristy.  We went to 4 great restaurants while we were there -- Monjul, Le Sergent Recruteur, Le Petit Marche and Chez Janou.  All were great.  The first two were more fine dining and the last two more casual.  We had a great walking tour with Richard Nahem who showed us his "home" of the Marais district.  Breakfast at the hotel included yogurt, pastries and fresh fruit.  A perfect start to the day.  The rooms are beautiful but small.  They use every square inch but they do it well.  Having been to Paris before, anyone who says the Parisians are not polite and kind did not have the experience we had.  Everyone we encountered at the hotel, the restaurants, and the shops were very hospitable.  Would 100% recommend this hotel to anyone!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Well placed, very cosy, good service
text: Great little hotel, beautifully placed at Place de Vosges. Staff is friendly and attentive. I love the self-serve Honesty-Bar were You help Yourself and write a note of what You have taken. Makes it all very relaxed. The furniture is not the best for having breakfast, but great for drinks in the afternoon.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Lovely and beautiful hotel
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 2 nights and it was a very beautiful hotel. The location is quite central with many cafes and shops nearby. We had a room which faced the courtyard which was nice and gave us ample sunshine. 

It can get a little noisy as it is next to a side alley where many cars and scooters use as well as many students access it to walk to the park across the road. 

Like most hotels in Paris the room is small so for two people and two large luggage it is a little tight. The air conditioning was a bit weak especially if we left the curtain opened. 

Overall a nice hotel and a pleasant stay.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Fabulous elegant hotel
text:
My husband and I loved this hotel. It is in the most beautiful location. We stayed there twice in September. The staff were amazing - the concierge and front desk brilliant. Our two rooms - we stayed twice in a week were outstanding. We booked a Junior suite both times and it was beautiful. When we retuned after a few days we were upgraded to the Victor Hugo suite - superb. 
This is the best hotel we have stayed in in Paris - understated elegant and SO comfortable. We want to return!
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Perfect boutique hotel with polished service in an amazing location
text: I booked this hotel for it's decor and location, but I was thoroughly impressed with it's service and amenities. While our room was not large, it was so well thought out that it never felt cluttered or overcrowded. Room service keeps things impeccable, and when they accidentally dropped a perfume sample (not a full bottle even), management sent us a handwritten note and a box of macarons despite the in person apology we had already received from housekeeping. The concierge was also extremely helpful with restaurants. Everything served at breakfast is of excellent quality. Overall, service is smooth, professional and very pleasant. We didn't have the time for a spa treatment but really enjoyed a quick visit to the jacuzzi and steam room which were top notch. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again or recommend it to friends.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Beautiful Oasis
text: This hotel is located in a bustling neighborhood of restaurants and shops actoss from a park. The service was perfect and the hotel had a number of cozy commonn rooms to eat a  nice breakfast (provided) or an after dinner drink. A quiet patio was also a nice place to spend time on sunny days.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: Wonderful service
text: From the moment I set foot in Le Pavilion until I checked out the service was impeccable. Probably equal to or better than the best hotels I’ve visited. My room was very comfortable and attractive. I did change from the first one I was shown because I felt it was small for the price, even for Paris. The front desk couldn’t have been more pleasant or accommodating. I love the location in the Marais and this is the first time I’ve stayed there. My other visits to Paris I’ve always stayed in the 6th arrondissement. I will definitely return to Le Pavilion de la Reine.
name: Le Pavillon de la Reine

title: NOVATEL17 - too far from Paris (no passing taxis)
text:
Booked in for weekend - no bar service because the barman was busy at seminar. Wanted a meal in restaurant - closed Saturday and Sunday, only bar snax. Staff could not recommend a local restaurant and could not book a taxi. Whilst in bar finishing our drinks the barman switched the lights off....without warning - and was extremely rude.
No room in restaurant for breakfast on Sunday - had to wait. We booked a taxi for our departure on Saturday - it was not booked - it was suggested we walk......(semi-disabled person could not walk with suitcase for 1/2 mile to trams). 
Rooms were clean and comfortable but this really is not a friendly place and in the middle of nowhere.......DO NOT BOOK UNLESS IN GREAT NEED!!!!!!

title: Not the hotel itself but the management
text:
I booked this hotel directly after a mix up with Booking.com . I booked this hotel specifically as they had adjoining rooms. I booked via telephone and had the confirmation via email as two rooms , after confirmation again via telephone I was told it was definitely adjoining rooms and that’s just the way they were booked . After an 11 hour journey we arrived to be told the hotel does not have any adjoining rooms and we had two separate rooms . After the long journey we just wanted to get to bed so didn’t kick up a fuss . One room was fine the other had a strange smell and a flickering strip light that couldn’t be turned off unless you pulled the key card out and sat in darkness . We phoned reception and they came up and said they would try to change the rooms for us but only one of them , we obviously wanted to be next to each other as we are a family and have several small children. Eventually they found two adjacent rooms but it was too late as the younger children had fallen asleep so my husband had to sit in a dark room using his phone for a torch with the other kids . The next morning we were offered free parking and a complimentary breakfast but we were then told they do have adjoining rooms so I’ve since queried this via email with management but I’ve had no response. So the rating reflects the way the matter was handled not the facilities.
The hotel itself is clean and the rooms fine . The breakfast was nice but they had run out of certain items and were slow to replenish. I did notice that the coffee machines upstairs had no pods so I assume they are out of order now ( see picture)
The hotel is situated quite a distance by foot from main attractions but it’s easy to get a cab/metro .

title: There are cons and pros
text:
Like I said, there are advantages and disadvantages to staying at this hotel. I stayed at this hotel from May 3rd, 2018 to May 7th 2018. I'd like to begin by the advantages:
1. The price was reasonable
2. The breakfast was of good quality, and there was a reasonable range of both hot and cold food
3. The staff were cooperative
4. The rooms were clean 
What I didn't like about the hotel was:
1. It was too noisy. For one thing, the noise from the street would never stop. Although the windows were double-glazed (you couldn't open the windows!), the traffic noise and sirens would never stop. It was also noisy in the corridors. I think my room was opposite where they kept the supplies and I could hear the noise from staff working loading and offloading their trolley. 
2. The hotel is not near any major attractions. It's like 40 min walk to Arc de Triumph, but there's a bust station where you can take the bus to Arc de Triumph and Champs Elysee. If you are a group an every one pays for themselves, definitely take a taxi. It's like 10 euros to Arc de Triumph which is well worth it. 
3. The refreshments did not get recharged. The water bottle, the tea bags, ....
4. There weren't slippers in the rooms. When we asked for them we were told to take them ourselves from the reception.
5. At night there's no one at the reception desk. There's only a security guard who does not speak English. 
6. What bothered me most was when you turn on the air conditioning, the fan made a constant maddening noise.  

Altogether, it's not a bad hotel considering  the rates in Paris.

title: Not worth the money
text: We paid over 1300 euros for 6 nights here, and it was not worth that! The accommodations were ok, but there were little fees tied to everything and the space was so tiny and not well thought out. The room is incredibly tiny and the bathroom was so small that I do not recommend staying here if you are a larger than average person or if you are elderly or uncoordinated. I am about 5 foot 7 and a normal weight and it was difficult to use the shower or get in and out of it. The shower curtain was so big that it was hard to get it away from your skin and it was so long it was blocking the drain. The towels are small and thin, and only one given per person with no face cloths. The laundry is $8 for a tiny load. There isn’t any hook or anywhere to hang a coat or purse, and not enough space for 2 people to put away all their clothes or to keep a suitcase open. We had to store all our suitcases under the bed so we could move about the room. It was nice to have a kitchen but there isn’t anywhere to prepare food because there isn’t really a counter and the table is tiny, and since it was one of the only surfaces in the room we could use it held purses and other things. Again, some hooks to hang items would have been so helpful. Really hard to use such a small space for two people! They also only allow one room key card for some reason so you have to leave the key with the front desk if you’re sharing, which was surprising for the cost of the room since it’s just a plastic room key. The bed and the staff were actually the best part. We slept so well, and the staff was absolutely lovely. I probably wouldn’t stay here again unless it’s very difficult to find something again. It’s a hard time to travel because things are quite booked up and expensive, so if the price was lower I’d maybe consider it if I was traveling solo or had a shorter stay.

To put it honestly, my first impression as I entered the Passage Dubail was an uncomfortable one. I thought probably I had made a wrong selection.
    Once we (a family of 3) entered the premises however,we were greeted by Salvatore who offered us croissants and also the storage room for keeping the luggage since we came in early (11am)

     He also suggested some areas in Paris where we can go for a few hours before check-in. 

      We were allotted Room no 4 (triple room) on the ground floor and although the rooms look a little dated and in need of some refurbishments, however they appeared quite clean and comfortable.

       Kitchenette was small but adequate. Room although small by Asian (Indian) standards was quite comfortable and had practically everything reqd for a comfortable stay including table fan, air cooler and a smartphone for guest use while in Paris.

       The service was outstanding and efficient. Staff was very polite and courteous and most of our requests (extra blanket, pillows)  were taken care of immediately.

      The only area of concern was of course the dated rooms and a very small bathroom and WC with water peeping out of the bathroom every now and then. Wifi at times was very slow.

      The location was perfect for us although a lot of reviewers have found it a bit seedy at times. There were lots of multiracial people around but I didn't find them dangerous by any chance.
 
        Perfect location for travel with direct bus to notre dame and direct metro to the louvre from gare de l'est. Excellent connectivity all around Paris.

    All in all, I had a nice time and would definitely recommend staying in Staycity Aparthotels.

title: Weekend break
text:
My partner and I were greeted by Geraldine on arrival and we were kindly upgraded to a room with a bath as on our booking it stated we had this. Unfortunately it was on the ground floor which I forgot to mention in my initial request! They were very accommodating and stated they would move us the next day as there was nothing available that night. The next day we changed rooms and we were very pleased! It was a recently refurbished room on the 3rd floor, very modern and very spacious. The beds were very comfy and we had a good night sleep for the remainder of our stay. The apartments are definitely great value for money, we didn’t cook at all but if people were trying to budget this would be very useful. It was handing having a big fridge to keep drinks and snacks in. 
One downfall was when it came to having a bath, the water wasn’t at all hot so we had to boil the kettle quite a lot to get some hot water! 
The area was not the nicest but great in terms of closeness to getting around Paris, the metro is a great system.
The staff were all very polite and helpful, definitely a good place to stay
