We stayed here for 3 nights and couldn’t have asked for a better place to stay. The welcome was warm and the check-in process was straightforward. 

The decor is very contemporary. The rooms are clean. The bar service is good. The breakfast buffet is fine, although we only went once. The other days we ventured out to a local bakery.

The location has lots of bars, cafes, restaurants and ice cream shops. All literally on the doorstep. The Eiffel Tower is just a 15 minute taxi ride. There’s also metro stops within a 5 minute walk of the hotel. 

We’d definitely stay here again.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Air conditioner
text: The only concern is that the temperature in the room was too warm despite the air conditioner. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Location was good. I would stay again. Please work on the air conditioning situation. A guest should be able to keep room cooler if so desired.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Great hotel, close to Gare Montparnasse
text: Excellent, stylish modern hotel. Friendly helpful service, comfortable, clean, quiet, spacious room. Really liked the decor. Breakfast was excellent, with a wide range of tasty food including fresh fruit and organic options. Wide range of restaurants nearby.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: unhappy
text: Outside of the location and really nice staff, the cost of the hotel per night was very high for the space occupied. The so called suite was not worth the price paid . Not even a desk was available to work on.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Much improved since my last visit
text: Stayed there on a short business trip. I had been there before (few years back) and the place is now really at a much higher standard. Rooms are still very comfy, but what really changed is the lobby and restaurant area which is now much better than before. A realy good location now.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Average
text: The staff is nice and helpful, a little too casual though. Breakfast is substandard (overcooked sausage, smelly fruit salad, 3 days in a row ...!).But overall, my room had constant smell of sewage, night and day, A real inconvenience!
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Good hotel
text:
I chose this hotel as it was close to Gare Montparnasse where we had an early morning train.  Hotel was good.
Our room was quite hot as the temperature was regulated throughout the hotel, however they provided us with a portable fan which helped.  We actually found all our hotel rooms in Europe hot.

Room was decent size, though bathroom was pretty small.  We had an issue 
with the shower head not staying up.  We reported it & it wasn't fixed properly as it kept falling down.  The maintenance man didn't speak english, so it was hard to communicate with him about the issue.
Breakfast was good, lovely freshly squeezed oj & lots of other options.  Both European & Western type choices.
Our room overlooked a garden area with a chicken pen. I am not sure if it belonged to the hotel, but was quite cute watching the chickens.  They weren't your ordinary type of chicken, they were very big fluffy ones.
Location is good, lots of shops, restaurants close by & metro stops & main train station as well.
Staff that we came in contact with were very helpful & pleasant.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Lovely hotel in a brilliant location
text: Stayed here over Easter weekend and it was a dream! Amazing location with a well connected metro station only a few minutes walk away. Can easily get to all the main attractions Paris has to offer. Montparnasse is a very cool and vibrant neighbourhood, and we would love to stay here again. Hotel staff very helpful and allowed us to check in early and also provided us with help and advice on different activities. Thank you very much!
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Quirky place in a lively part of Paris
text:
Stayed here for a few nights with a large family group. My favorite part of the room had been the little window nook behind the curtains, since my view was overlooking opera house next door, so I got proper morning sun every 8am before heading out. Place had hairdryer, shower gel, towels, soap bar, and wifi. Was spacious and comfortable enough that sleep was easy. Breakfast in the morning had a standard assortment too, breads, cereal options, cheese, yoghurt, fruits, and some meats. 

I liked how at night, it was so lively, close to a lot of places open until late at night.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Good location
text: Chosen for location to Blvd Montparnasse and private parking. Car park was full when arrived but got space late eve.  Problems getting out following day as gate wouldn’t open.  Staff helpful both times!
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: More basic than other Mercure hotels
text: On arrival the reception area appears like a youth hostel or student bar, under renovation! The range of unmatched furniture, exposed service pipes and wires all reinforce this impression. Indeed the theme is continued throughout all the public areas. The rooms are like other Mercure hotels except more basic. Even though Paris was cold there was no room heating, and the small thin towels, together with complete absence of toiletries all added to the austerity. The whole experience was poor value for money. Good location for the area, but thankfully there are plenty of other local hotels for future visits.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: 5 stars services
text: I highly recommend you to stay in this hotel during your visit to Paris there are many metro and train stations 2 mins walking to reach your destinations the size of room is acceptable and its very very clean also the important things very nice and kind stuff
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Superb reception and superb stay
text: Anthony at the front desk made this a memorable stay. His professionalism, knowledge, and responsiveness were outstanding.  The hotel itself has a wonderful location in a vibrant yet quiet location near Montparnasse. The buffet breakfast offers an array of excellent choices in as very comfortable setting. The rooms are fine.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Holidays
text:
I loved it! It’s obviously a business hotel but the rooms are personalised according to client needs (no. Of bed and all).

The decor is wonderful! It’s really enchanting with a mix of modern and old to keep the history of this hotel built in 1973. 

The breakfast in the morning is great! You eat to full capacity everyday without being able to taste everything on the buffet. My favorite: fresh juice! You have a selection of a choosing orange juice or lemon juice or even better! You have a juicer with fruits and vegetables next to it so you can prepare “the juice” that you want. 

The room are clean and well serviced. The bathroom spacious. The heater works perfectly in this cold weather and the bed is the heaven after some heavy touristing. 

I definitely recommend it.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Hotel location is excellent for using the Metro, surrounded by cafes and restaurants.
text:
Mercure serves a nice breakfast buffet with eggs, sausages,fruit, juice, waffles, potatoes, and a variety of breads, rolls and croissants.  The staff are attentive and helpful.  The rooms are rather small but comfortable.  The bathrooms have either a shower or tub/shower combo.  There are no grab bars so to me it was a little dicey getting in and out.  I'll request a room with the stand alone shower on my next visit.
If you're not a couple, make sure you're on good terms with your roommate because the twin beds are pushed together as on a cruise ship.  The little refrigerator in our room didn't work, and this went unaddressed after notifying staff.  There is a bar on the street level, and you can also order drinks in your room.

You can walk to a number of attractions, and the Metro is only a couple of blocks so getting around is pretty easy.  An exciting ride in a Paris taxi at rush hour is an experience not to be missed!  I liked this hotel so much I'm staying in another Mercure on my next visit.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: In the core of a sparkling area
text:
Large room, very clean, on the best part of Montparnasse plenty of amenities, beside the train station and metro, 50 minutes by train from CDG and 20 to the Porte de Versalles.
Breakfast is nice including natural orange juice. Nice bar a tv sports. 
Highly recommended
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: A bright and pleasant hotel.
text:
A bright and pleasant hotel.
Friendly staff, Good location.
A very trendy hotel.
There are lots of pubs around, but a very safe atmosphere.
The rice noodle was delicious across from the hotel.
and the casual bar in the hotel was good to drink beer while watching soccer.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Mediocre Hotel, Great Location
text:
My family of 4 (2 small children) stayed here for 3 nights. The location from hotel to Metro is only a 3 minute walk, very convenient. The neighborhood is surrounded with restaurants and such, so it's nice a busy but quiet at the same time. 

Our hotel room comprised of a queen size bed with a full size pull out right next to it. There is barely any room other than beds and the dressers. I have a huge bruise after running my knee into the pull out that was right in front of the refrigerator. 

One thing I did not know about European hotels, they are awesome about conserving energy. You have to put your room key into a slot that turns all the lights on for you, and when you leave, you take your room key and lights shut off.

One thing I did not like, however, was that I put my DO NOT DISTURB sign on my door. I do not like my room getting cleaned during my visit unless I absolutely have to. Both days the sign was out, and both days they ignored the sign and came in anyways. On the last day, the cleaner was in the room as we arrived, with the TV on and watching TV as she cleaned. I was not too happy about that. 

Other than that, it's not a bad hotel.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Pleasant stay
text:
Nice open buffet for breakfast, nice location, friendly staff, healthy food.
Good entertainment in the neighborhood 
Will stay in the same hotel if return back to Paris. Rating will be 8 out of ten. Mercure hotels are a good chain
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Mediocre room, terrible service
text: This hotel has been refurbished and has gone down in quality, unfortunately. The rooms are small and basic. The bar/restaurant is open-plan, attempting to be trendy but too disorganised to pull it off. Staff are also appalling - there is very rarely anyone at the table that serves as a front desk, in particular. An older woman checking out ahead of me complained about it and the staff member told her very rudely that she was wrong; she was not.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Great Location
text:
Stayed in this Hotel for 3 nights.
Location was great.
Staff where even better Pierre very helpful & friendly.
The room was basic but clean.
good view.
The air-conditioning wasnt working at night it would blow hot air and we tried to put it down, the beds were really not that comfortable.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Nice City Break
text:
Good location 
5 min walk from Metro station
It’s good location with many restaurants and bars same street as the hotel .
Hotel Staff speak good English and very helpful .
Room was very clean and modern decor .
Nice for family aswell as couples .
I will recommend to people who need easy access to public transport .

Hotel room 10/10
Staff service 10/10
Room cleanliness 10/10
Location 10/10
Tourist friendly 10/10
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Very good stay
text:
We had a really good time there, comfy bed, good room!
Breakfast choices are big and very home like, the waitress are nice and helpful.
Close to the metro stations, many restaurants and pubs around. 
Good location to get around.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Great hotel!
text: Stayed in this hotel for 3 nights and couldn’t have picked better! Staff were so friendly from the start and were so helpful if we needed anything.  The location is amazing, metro station round the corner and plenty of bars/restaurants in the area.  The only downside to this is, as the bars open quite late, it can be super loud until the early hours outside the hotel.  Room was clean and bed was super comfortable.  Had such a lovely stay and when returning to Paris we’ve already decided we’ll stay here again!
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Great rooms, check-out ruins the impression
text: So, the pros first. Great location, spacious room for four (two adults, two children) and the breakfast buffet was delicious. If the receptionist that met us at check-out hadn’t been so rude, this hotel would’ve gotten 5/5.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Nice room, avg service
text:
I'm currently staying at the hotel. 

Pros
The room is nice and I would say large for European standards. The breakfast had a wide variety of options and is very good. 

Cons
The service is OK. The cleaning service left some things scrambled (e.g. waste basket in the middle of the room. I also left a laundry bad on the table in my room (as indicated by them), when I came back at night it was still there. When I called the lobby they said the cleaning lady must have gotten confused and they couldn't do anything about it. They suggested I take it to a dry cleaner outside the hotel, which is unacceptable in my view.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Nuit du 15 Octobre 2018
text:
Il faisait tres chaud le 15 Octobre 2018; pas de climatisation dans les chamabres!!!
Explication de la reception: On est en periode hivernale, donc les climatiseurs sont hors service!! En plus impossible d'ouvrir la fenetre; trop de bruit dans la rue de la Gaité!!
Impensable pour le prix payé..
Le staff tres moyen; plutot des jeunes sans experience. Attitude de s'ont fouté!!

Horrible experience; I arrived on October 15th 2018 - very hot day and night. The air conditioning system was turned off!! The staff explained that it was off because summer was over!! 
Unbelievable for the price per room!Spend*t a sleepless night in a stuffy room on a very, very noisy street, fill of bars and restaurants that stay open late... 
Staff inexperienced and with a negatif attitude. Wondered who was the client!
Never ever will I stay there again.
Really bad compared to the hundreds of hotels that really seem to take care of their guests....
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Location to Gare Montparnasse
text:
We booked for the Ryder Cup so we needed to be close to the station and were delighted with space, modernity, cleanliness, security and customer service in the hotel. 
Whilst the booking was primarily a functional one, we were delighted with amenities surrounding the hotel, surrounded by great bars and restaurants and felt extremely safe and peaceful.
Approx 1km to swine make for beautiful walks.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: A great place to stay
text: This place was wonderful, accommodating, and a relief after spending time in a horrible hotel in London.  The staff was very friendly, went out of their way when we were a bit late for breakfast.  Drinks were wonderful!  There is a happy hour and the ambience has a young stylish vibe that is great.  Perfect location that is close to transportation, restaurants, theaters, etc.  Everyone was super friendly and approachable.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Super overprized!!!
text: This hotel is a cold hole, reception desk is a round table in the middle of the entrance hall, staff are cold, bed was good but no decent toiletries, just 2 little soaps & Gojo dispenser attached to the shower wall. This hotel is over rated, it is not a **** hotel, maybe *** & 1/2 if that!
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: WELL LOCATED
text: Only a few minutes walk from the Montparnasse station, Metro and airport shuttle this hotel is in a good location, with plenty of dining options nearby. I was a bit startled by the the reception arrangement whereby you check in at the bar instead of a formal reception desk, however I am quite old-fashioned. The room was comfortable, clean  and well-equipped.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Location
text: Hotel is located aprox. 7 min walk to/from Montparnasse station. Room was small but clean and quite. Short walk to eating places, mini market and shops. Smooth checked-in. Staff were nice and helpful.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Location & Convinience
text:
Selected the Hotel as it had easy access to the Taxi's, Buses and Metro; found out it was well placed to many lovely cafes, restaurants and pubs open till late at night. There is a amazing theater close-by as well.
The hotel breakfast was amazing with a wide selection for breakfast. Rooms were comfortable and clean and the staff were always helpful and courteous. This will be a hotel i plan to return to for my next visit as well.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Excellent service, great rooms
text:
We booked 2 rooms online from a third party website. The staff made great effort to find to contiguous rooms in the renovated areas. Rooms were modern, very comfortable and with a clear attention to the need of modern travelers (UBS charging point together with power plugs etc.). Asked the name of the supplier of their mattress: it was that good!

We took some drinks with friends in the lobby. Breakfast was really good and we had the lovely surprise of staff coming to our taxi with some pastry for our trip to the airport. Great service and quality in addition to be conveniently located close to the train station Montparnasse (walking there took us 3 minutes max)
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Perfect location and very convenient
text:
We were on a trip to France, Belgium and Holland and we stayed for three nights at Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse. The hotel is perfectly located next to two metro stops Edgar Quinet (Line 6) and Gaite (Line 13), and it is very close to Gare Montparnasse where we took a direct train to Chateau de Versailles (20 minutes ride for less than 5 euros). 

The hotel is 4 stars and it was astonishingly clean. We saw them cleaning the carpets daily. It doesn't have enough toiletries like other countries' 4-stars, but that was ok. Make sure you take your toiletries with you (toothbrush, toothpaste, headcap, etc...). Breakfast has a lot of varieties and it was really delicious. Don't miss the French crepe :) Yummyy... The staff are really friendly and very helpful. 

Around the hotel, you can find many restaurants and cafes. There is a pharmacy nearby and a mini market. Monoprix is only a 5-minutes walk. One of the Galeries Lafayette is only 5 minutes away.

For Shisha lovers, there is a shisha cafe right in front of the hotel. For Halal food seekers, there are a lot of Halal restaurants, Lebanese, turkish, etc...  The street is so lively for those who would like to grab an afternoon drink. Perfect hotel for all kind of travelers.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Rude and disappointing
text: Rude staff at the reception and help desk and terrible room service where nothing is available in the rooms and their menu includes food that they do not serve at all.  If you ask for laundry service they ask you to carry your laundry to the reception for them to receive it instead of sending their staff to collect it.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Nice hotel in funky neighborhood
text: We have stayed here several times as we like the neighborhood and its convenient location near the airport bus halt. The rooms are being renovated and the construction work made for some inconvenience and noise. For Paris, the rooms are of decent size. The price was exceptionally low and an excellent breakfast was included.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Amazing Hotel!!
text:
I stayed in this hotel with a couple of friends at the end of July and was extremely pleased with how friendly and accommodating the staff were, the room was modernly decorated and was very clean (also the beds were extremely comfy) the hotel is situated in a lively area full with bars and restaurants, and is surrounded by metro stations. Overall I throughly enjoyed my stay and wouldn’t hesistate to return again! 
Thank you so much
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Wonderful hotel in the heart of Paris
text:
Fabulous stay! 
Newly renovated, comfortable and very clean bedroom and bathroom. The rooms must be well insulated because no outside noise could be heard from within the bedroom. The lobby and bar areas have recently been renovated with a modern and convivial atmosphere. 

Very nice breakfast, freshly squeezed orange juice and good coffee! 
The staff were very friendly and helpful, everyone spoke English.  Also good value for money.

I would highly recommend this hotel for business or leisure travellers, friends and family.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Such a lovely hotel highly recommended
text: The staff were super accommodating, the bedrooms were super clean with staff restocking complimentary tea, water and biscuits every day. there's an ironing room on the -1 floor, overall really good hotel with staff that were super friendly. its close to 3 metros and lots and lots of restaurants and even two pharmacies.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Good Location: transport and local amenities
text: This hotel scores high because of location:  proximity to Gare de Montparnasse ( the reason we chose it) and also to Metro and Bus.  We also enjoyed the numerous restaurants that surround the hotel and the friendly atmosphere of Montparnasse.    Our room was comfortable and had everything we needed.   It was very hot in Paris while we were there and we appreciated the additional fans that had been provided before our arrival.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Great location & lovely area.
text: Thoroughly enjoyed my stay. Well furnished with excellent, helpful staff. Amazing breakfast. Location is great. Close proximity to restaurants, pharmacy, shopping and just over a block from the Metro. Nice quiet area with tons to do close by.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Small Hotel very close to Gare Montparnasse
text: Hotel is located closer to the Montparnasse station, Rooms are smaller in size, Excellent Breakfast spread, had enough options even for Vegetarian like me. Invariably one of the lift always had problem, some days had to take steps to reach my room in fifth floor.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Excellent location
text:
Easy to access via train, close to cafes, supermarkets and attractions. 
Our room was top floor under the eves - a perfect base for exploring this area of Paris. The room was clean & comfortable - not large, but it IS Paris! Bathroom was compact but user friendly. Very comfortable bed, and although in a busy district, very quiet at night. Good value for money.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Excellent Location + Comfort for Family Stay
text: Family of 4 (two adults and two kids under 10) stay for 6 nights in early June. Location was perfect and close to two metros. Gare Montparnasse is 10 minute walk away (from which you can take direct train to Versailles). Staff are friendly and welcoming. Lots of restaurants in the vicinity for breakfast/lunch/dinner. The Vietnamese restaurant right opposite had excellent Pho for under 10 euros. Our room was facing the street but we did not hear any street noise. There is a monoprix about 5 minutes from the hotel for supplies, etc. and a nice park 2-3 minutes away. Excellent for families with young kids.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: ACCESSIBILITY
text: Centrally located easy access (walking distance) to metro, good restaurants, train station, supermarkets. Good breakfast in hotel and around the hotel. Room comfortable, however the one I occupied was tight courters.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Hotel in walking distance of station.  Had a makeover though airconditioning needs attention
text:
I have used this hotel several times.  It is within walking distance of Montparnasse Station.  Note the main railway station is having a major makeover and line 4 of the metro does not have an exit at Gare du Nord because of separate works there.
The hotel's Reception has been reshaped and is less cluttered than before. Reception shares imperceptibly the ground floor with the Bar, restaurant and workin area.  Friendly staff, bilingual if your French is modest.
My room 207 had been modernised, and with two heavy beds.  Comfortable and spacious.  Bathroom had a walkin shower. Good but without support bar, so take care in getting in/out.
Though the room had air conditioning, I did not understand the control on the wall. Neither could I get the temperature in the room down to remotely cool.  Hot on both nights and, on the second, had to take the duvet out of its cover and to sleep under just the cover.  Just bearable
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: exceptional 9 day stay and welcome to Paris
text:
It was an exceptional experience. I have recently moved to Paris, and needed to spend few nights at the hotel before signing my lease. I have to admit that Mercure Montparnasse staff made everything for me so I can feel at home at the hotel. 

Very clean room and bathroom, nice and friendly staff, great location as I was commuting daily to Versailles and amazing price-value ratio. Folks at reception (talked to 4 or 5 people over my stay there) were friendly and smiled, spoke English well, and helped a lot with advices on travel and services.  I had a very comfortable queen bed, was happy to get very nice sleep each night. Wi-Fi connection was fast, and service was done daily with towels, shampoo and other amenities replacement. Plenty of restaurants, shops, cinemas, etc around. So, recommend for sure and will be happy to stay myself.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Room 620 had a 2nd inlet of aircon that was non-operable
text:
The hotel is very nice and in a great location. 

Staff is very friendly and helpful.

All great, but above the door in room 620 there was an additional air inlet into the room that I could not control via an aircon panel on the wall next to the bathroom. Moreover, at some point early on Friday around 7am-7.30am an air getting out of this vent smelled not nicely.

Having had a Gold status membership, I would have hoped my room was upgraded into the next level.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Superficially updated hotel in good location
text:
The reception area - indeed the whole of the ground floor - has had a make-over since my last stay a few months back. This make-over includes the staff. Gone are the smart suits/crisp skirts and tops and, in their place, has come a denim-shirt look making the staff indistinguishable from guests. As for the layout and décor: the layout is now somewhat confused/confusing as the bar seems to have been fused into the reception desk whilst the new ceiling-less look of the general area, exposing all the pipes and services painted black, seems a rather dated throw-back to the 80s or 90s.
As for the rooms and location, all remain unchanged: the rooms are still very comfortable and clean with 2 lifts servicing the 6 floors whilst the location is easily accessible from several metro lines and retains a wide mixture of busy restaurants, theatres and some lower establishments.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Good location but hotel not up to standard
text:
Business trip for four nights. When first arrived I was impressed by relaxed vibe, the decor, and excited about the area, but after a sleepless night, I was regretting the decision to stay there for the week. 

Positives: good lively location if you're a tourist, and like sleeping in warm room - comfy bed, large breakfast.

Negatives: no air conditioning despite high temperatures in April - fan useless, woke up sweating. Also, the lift doesn't regularly go above the 3rd floor so you'll be waiting around getting frustrated as it goes up and down from ground to third and back again. Then, if you put your room card anywhere near your mobile phone or anything else electrical, then it will demagnetize, as happened every single day I was there, and as I was on the 4th floor, so I had to keep running up and down 4 flights of stairs to get the card fixed. Room was dark and a little cramped, despite being described as "superior". 

Mostly, the lack of air con or a decent fan in the room, meaning I couldn't sleep properly, and the irritation of the card, making me late in the mornings, made it rank worse than some more primitive places I have stayed in the tropics. It is NOT OK to say you don't turn the air con on until June. 

Reception staff were clearly irritated by me regularly complaining about the room key card not working in the door. I will never come back here. I don't recommend it for business travellers as they can't get some of the basics right. It's a shame as location is great and the hotel could be great too.
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Food was excellent specially the breakfast 🍳
text: The food was excellent I loved everything about Pairs the best way to save money use the metro for your transportation, use your credit card and don’t not use cash there. I recommend to do the lunch in the first floor in the Effie tower and take the seine river cruise at night was the most beautiful thing to do there .
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Good location , good comfortable stay
text:
It is a good location to montparnasse, but it lacks some of the basics you would expect at a Mecure. The reception / restaurant/bar area is a bit funky when you first arrive, but the room we were given on the 5th floor was a bit dated....maybe these were the next to be fixed up??
We did lodge a complaint that the aircon/heater did not work, but that was not resolved during our 8 day stay and we were thankful that it didnt get much colder than it was otherwise we would have had to move room.
The room was a good size for Paris, reasonably clean and we had a window which was nice to get some fresh air from time to time.

We did find the cleaners using our phone chargers when we came back to the room unexpected one day, not impressed, so made sure we locked our bags and stowed everything each day.

One huge plus, was the breakfast was pretty good, and we had drinks at the bar one night, and whilst we were the only ones in the bar area, we were surprised that the bar manager kept filling our glasses, and then did not charge us for it at the end of the night. And it was not on the bill. Great service and whilst strange, we really appreciated it ..so kudos to the hotel if they do that from time to time !

The property has some good restaurants nearby and theaters in the same street, so there is always a great passing parade of interesting people. Good bars in the same street and the metro is at end of street.

There is also a fresh food market on a Saturday at end of street which is fantastic.

So it is halfway between Average and Very Good in my books
name: Mercure Paris Gare Montparnasse

title: Upmarket Hostel not Hotel
text: We were allocated a very small room and were refused an upgrade. The bed was against the wall so I had to crawl up from the bottom (I am 71). The feature light did not work. The bathroom was rusty and small. You could not alter the water temperature, just one tap with allocated water. No tea, coffee or even water facilities. Staff answered questions but gave no more help. Awful place.

title: Not a Hotel, more an upmarket hostel
text: This hotel was substituted by Easy Jet at the last minute - we were booked into an Ibis hotel, with full hotel facilities: this "Hotel" was just not comparable and a complaint has been lodged with Easy Jet. Location - good, everything else was not. The room we got, which we immediately tried to upgrade unsuccessfully, was more of a "pod" than a room. It was tiny, with a shower so small I could not use it. The bed was against a wall in the corner of the room, so my wife had to climb onto it and shuffle up the bed to use it - hugely unacceptable. The decor was not to our taste, typically garish "boutique" style, with a fancy light fitting which was unsafe and did not work. The other rooms looked a lot better - seen when passing and being cleaned, but I would stress that the room we got, 203, made our stay an endurance test, which failed. No tea or coffee facilities in the room, holes in the towels, no soap, I could go on, but simply do NOT book this hotel if room 203 is a part of the deal. Breakfast was quite good, but no other food, or other, facilities - we had to go out and find suitable places to eat. NO room service of any kind. Staff were ok, but not what I would call helpful, the one that spoke good English, the others struggled with even simple matters. All in all, I would not consider staying at the Five Hotel even if the price was attractive, it simply is not a Hotel, more of a hostel/pod facility.

title: Located near the Latin Quarter
text:
We stayed at The Five Hotel for 5 nights and had a good stay .
We stayed in a classic double room at the back of the hotel which was rather small
But it was clean and tidy and we had enough space for our belongings. 
The bathroom was really tiny though, me and my partner are petite people and we were only just  okay with moving about . I would worry about larger people not fitting in..

Our room was located at the back of the hotel where there is  currently building work  going on in the proximity  . There was a lot of noise and workers shouting to each other around 7-8am every morning .. It didn’t personally bother me
enough to ask to change rooms, but still a bit annoying and others may not be as forgiving . 

The location is good - There is a national strike on transport services in Paris at the moment and most metro lines are only running during rush hour . There is a metro called Les  Goblins about  a 6 min walk from the hotel and an RER station  called Port Royal about 8-10 minutes away .
Instead we walked pretty much everywhere in Paris , about 6 hours a day and so it was pretty tiring - not the hotels fault of course ! They helped as much as possible with transport queries . 

 The hotel is located a 10 min walk from the Latin Quarter . The beautiful cobbled street is filled  with many  french cuisine restaurants and bistros. You will find other cuisines and street food also. 
It was very ideal  being near the hotel after a long day and all the restaurants were accommodating of us just turning up without reserving . 
Many offer a fixed price menu too so helpful to budget better .

Overall , we enjoyed our stay at the five hotel . The staff were friendly and the hotel was clean . 
We didn’t have breakfast at the hotel but there are  boulangeries close by where we grabbed croissants and baguettes for our
Day. 
We would return !

title: Great staff, wonderful service. Crazy red lobby is called "The Love Lab".
text: HOW TO FIND:From Gare du Nord, go to Pont Royal (this is where it can get confusing, as the Gare is so huge) to rue Flatters. We found it much easier to get on Metro Line 7 at Gobelins (go out hotel, turn right, quick left on Pt.Royale, cross at Mc Donalds), and another quick left. Metro is about 8 minutes either way. However, and this is by far the easiest.just go out hotel door, turn right, and cross the Pt.Royal to the bus stop right there in an island.You can get to any Metro from them. We got busted twice in the Metro stations by uniformed subway police. Always keep your ticket and if you buy a pass (great value) make sure you either get a copy of your passport photo or use one of the photo booths at the main stations, and affix it to your card. The hotel is a good value, with helpful staff and good, low price breakfast (not included in price). Usually, but not always, coffee was available.I'd certainly use this hotel again. The rooms are small, but they are anywhere in Paris.

title: A wonderful experience!
text:
We stayed in this charming Latin Quarter hotel for three nights, and we have no regrets!  While the rooms are small, they are extremely comfortable and cozy, with a very chic “space age” vibe.  I felt like I’d walked onto the Barbarella set upon entering the lobby.

The staff was extremely polite and helpful, and possessed superior language skills; they even assisted my partner and I in arranging dinner reservations for a Friday evening out on the town.  When we encountered a small problem with our room key, they were quick to address the issue.  That was the only hiccup in an otherwise wonderful stay.

I would highly recommend for first-time visitors to Paris, especially English-speaking couples who are looking for a helpful and attentive staff.

Merci à vous, Five Hotel !

title: Know WHICH room you are getting!
text: I think your opinion of this hotel varies widely dependent upon which room you get.  I knew the room was going to be small -- even by Paris standards.  However, I couldn't fathom HOW small it was going to be.  My husband and I were in Paris to celebrate our 22nd anniversary over a long weekend, and we barely fit it the room; and the bathroom was literally almost not big enough for my husband to squeeze into (granted he's a larger guy).  It is not the size of the room that is the at the root of the "one" rating, however.  The condition of the room actually almost ruined our time in Paris (until we decided to avoid the room at all costs until the last possible minute each day).  The room is run-down and DIRTY.  The floors were stained all over and appeared to have hair all over it. The walls were scuffed and dinged up and not repaired or cleaned. I normally don't write such negative reviews, but I feel this is a buyer beware kind of moment.  *See pictures*  Now, as I stated, this seems to be predicated upon the room you are assigned.  We met another traveler who showed us her room, maybe 604? It was very small as well, but bigger than ours and far cleaner and more well-kept.  We stared in room 503, requested a room change -- which the front-desk clerk graciously granted--and moved to 303.  The rooms in size, layout and dirtiness were virtually identical.  So, avoid the 03's would be my advice should you be staying here.  I can't speak to the staff much.  As I said, we avoided the hotel pretty much all the time.  In our little dealing with them, they were polite and helpful.  Also, the location might keep some away from the hotel.  You need to travel some distance to get to any of the major sites.  This does, though, offer quiet nights, and my husband and I were ok with the location as we are comfortable with Paris's public transportation, and we ended up loving the local feel of the neighborhood!  We LOVED Bistro V and its proprietress Julie.  Cafe Val was amazing and had great happy hour specials.  The little bistro right across the street was fun as well.   We would likely stay in this area again even though it's a little distant from the attractions.  However, we would *never* stay at The Five again. :(

title: One by the Five:  Dirty and Disappointing Suite
text: I reserved the suite "One by the Five" for a romantic first night in Paris for my husband and myself.  It was a surprise for him and we were both excited.  However, on entering the room, we were extremely disappointed.  While the suite may have been nice a few years ago, it was badly run-down.  One of the lights next to the bed didn't work and there were scrapes and scuffs all around (worse than the expected wear and tear in a hotel room).  Even worse was the lack of cleanliness, which ultimately made us leave the hotel and find another.  It was as if the room had not been cleaned at all between guests.  The bathtub was scummy and full of hair, the carpet in the dance floor area was stained and filthy (there was even an empty toilet paper roll under one of the chairs in this area), and there was hair on the floor around the bed that a vacuum certainly could have picked up.  We honestly didn't feel comfortable touching any surface in that suite, so we left and found another hotel last minute (we had never left a hotel like this before).  The Five staff was apologetic and did refund us for our stay which was appreciated.  But needless to say it really killed the excitement and romance of the evening and was the low point of our European trip.  If the suite was clean and had some maintenance done it would be a fun and unique experience, but I would take caution upon booking.  This was for the One by the Five suite only and I cannot speak to the rest of the hotel.

title: Visiting From the USA
text:
Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Hotel Five. I was visiting from the United States and was pleased that all of the staff I encountered spoke English. This made me feel welcomed to the hotel, and made my experience less stressful. When we checked into the hotel, the front desk staff offered us a map of the city of Paris. She also circled many tourist attractions that are near the hotel, and answered any questions we had about the area. 

The hotel was very clean, and I felt safe staying here. However, the rooms are very tiny and there is not much space. The entire room was about how big my closet is back home in the United States.

There are small LED lights in the shower which gives a nice touch to the bathroom.

If you plan to use public transportation the nearest stop is “Port-Royal” on the RER B line. This is about 40 minutes from Charles de Gaulle airport. You can access the airport from the hotel via this line, but you will have to transfer trains one time.  The station for “Port-Royal” is about a 15 minute walk from the hotel. The walk is not too bad, but it is not the best if you have a lot of luggage. Luckily for me, it was about 40 degrees and raining during my stay which made the walk even worse. I think the walk would be more bearable in better weather conditions.  

There are many places to eat within walking distance. If you are looking for an authentic French bakery on your trip I would suggest going to “Artisan Boulanger Patissier”, it is about a 10 minute walk from the hotel. You will pass it as you walk to the “Port-Royal” station.  They have a great choice of French pastries, sandwiches, and baguettes. All of the items are at reasonable prices. 

There is also a McDonalds about 7 minutes away if you are missing the United States and want some familiar food. 

One last thing to add is that breakfast is not included with your stay. There is also a city tax that is added on, that you must pay at checkout. I stayed one night and the tax was around 3€. 

The hotel staff also held my bags before and after check in.

title: Fabulous birthday Weekend in Paris, bad hotel
text:
This hotel is in bad condition. The rooms are dirty, dated and very, very small. The downstairs is slightly better but the 'honesty bar' is always locked so you can't actually get into it and the breakfast is of poor quality also. There are packaged pancakes, bread and a small fruit selection. There is also cheese and ham but no warm options. No 'English Tea' only herbal/fruit teas and coffees. 
The only saving grace for this weekend was the receptionist Morgan. She goes above and beyond to try and help you and improve your stay. I would give her 5*'s!!
We were originally shown to room 502 and we immediately requested an alternative. The sheets were stained, the carpet stained and sticky, the bathroom sink leaked, had dirty towels on the floor of the shower also and the walls and tables were damaged, stained and just in need of repair! Lamps were chipped and bulbs mismatched.
We were then given room 302 by a very helpful and apologetic Morgan which was marginally better but still needing a good scrub to the walls and carpets but at least bedding was clean and sink not leaking.
The location is quite nice with local bars and shops. We went to the famous Mouffetard for drinks in the evening and perused some wine and cheese stalls en route to dinner.
Overall I wouldn't come back to this hotel but would go back to it's sister hotel the Seven Hotel as we went there for cocktails and it was much better!

title: 5 Star service for a 3 Star price
text:
Our room in this hotel was very small, but it was clean and the bed was comfortable. When we opened the balcony doors we could see a small cafe down below. Even with the cafe there, the room was still quiet and we enjoyed 3 nights of restful sleep. 

The staff was friendly and very helpful. They have a generous check out time of noon. On our last day in Paris our flight out was not until early evening. The area around the hotel has several cafes, shops and a pharmacy. The bus was nearby and we used that often to get to the heart of the city. There is a wonderful little chocolate shop around the corner that we visited twice. 

We really enjoyed our stay at The Five Hotel and would definitely stay there again.

title: Romantic birthday treat in Paris!
text:
I booked the Five Hotel via booking.com after searching for a Paris hotel that had something 'else' to offer. I looked at hotels with a view of the Eiffel Tower, Champs Elysees, all sorts - then after searching 'Paris hotels with jacuzzi' I came across the Five Hotel! We booked the suite with the outdoor private jacuzzi. The suits consists of a 'lounge'/bedroom, then the main bedroom and bathroom. All the rooms have small LED lights in either the ceiling or wall that light up and add to the romance! Even the shower head in the bathroom lights up! Then, there's the private jacuzzi! And it IS private! It is situated between the bathroom and master bedroom. There is artificial grass, then a decking area with seating/loungers and a heavy waterproof curtain to pull across to keep up the privacy (surrounded and fenced by dark bamboo). Very romantic.

I had contacted the hotel in advance to say we were coming and that it was for very special 35th birthday treat for my girlfriend/fiance. The staff were faultless. From the Manager Morgan to Cecile on Reception and Fatima - what an experience we had! We arrived early and our bags were held until our room was ready - then we went in! WOW! A full bottle of Pommery champagne on ice in a bucket, love-heart shaped balloons, rose petals and then rose petals on our bed made into a '35' with a ring of petals surrounding it all! So special, and a nice complimentary touch!

There was a cafe/bar and small convenience shop literally around the corner and a pizza restaurant across the road. Metro stations are between 5-15mins walk and Notre Dame is about a 15min walk. The are is nice, on the edge of the Latin Quarter. 

We didn't try the breakfast as we slept in, and, didn't leave our room for the entire trip as we made the most of the jacuzzi! 

Any negative comments in other review on here, I saw no evidence of that on our trip. I cannot fault the staff. The hotel is small, sure, and there is another suite bigger than the 'Jacuzzi' suite - so decide if it is space or a proper jacuzzi you are after - and this is a proper jacuzzi not a bath disguised as one. As for the other rooms, some 20+ I cannot review as I didn't see them but can only assume they are also decorated nicely.

Space is a premium in Paris so if it's a massive room you're after be prepared to pay for it, but for a romantic trip The Five Hotel Jacuzzi Suite suited our needs (which I paid around $280 euros for a Monday night).

There is a shared mini-bar and most soft drinks are $3 euros, beer $5-$6 euros and champagne half bottle is $37 euros and a full bottle is $67 euros.

I can see how the eating area would get busy if everyone came for breakfast at once, but it was quiet when we stayed and very peaceful. Each room in the suite is not big, very small but well decorated and the LED lights make a nice touch. The bed wasn't that big, a double in my memory rather than a queen or kingsize but it was comfortable enough for two people. Both the master bedroom and 2nd bedroom/lounge had flat screen smart TVs. The bathroom was big (for Paris), very modern again with LED lighting and the shower head also lit up - a nice touch. 2 Bathrobes and towels were available and you can even put an electric shutter down on the the decking/jacuzzi area from the bathroom to make it extra private (if you were staying with others).

My girlfriend was very touched by the effort this staff had made to make our trip so memorable and magical. Our free champagne was by compliments of the manager, so you'd have to ask yourself about that, but for us it was granted (I didn't ask for the champagne, it was offered to us when I said what the stay was for, a 35th birthday).

Hope this review helps with your decision, but we would definitely stay here again and were invited to do so by Cecile for 'an excellent rate' for our next stay so the staff are definitely up for making your stay as memorable and comfortable as possible.

(Only thing we noticed is that room does not have a bin/trash can. There is only one small bin/trash can in the bathroom).

title: Roundly disappointing
text:
I'd booked this based on the reviews as a boutique hotel that was worth a little extra for a significant birthday for my wife.

The room itself was disappointingly small - having booked a superior room, I thought I was going to get a little more space but it didn't have much room than an Easy Hotel.  This is Paris, so space is at a premium, but the illustrative photographs seems to be of a couple of the bespoke rooms.  There were small LEDs in the headboard, a nice touch, although someone had played join-the-dots with a pen.  Not terribly convinced on how well cleaned the room was: we had to return a pair of pajama bottoms to reception that had been left in the room, throw out a bottle of eyedrops that was on the floor beside the bed and the bed runner was badly stained.

The set up of the pillows and rose petals was certainly well thought out.

This may be the issue with a boutique hotel but we went down for breakfast to find there were no available seats. The receptionist kindly offered to phone us when one became available, but after 40 mins and no phone call we went back down to find spare tables, albeit we had to clear it ourselves.  Then ask for cutlery, mugs, the fruit juice and coffee to be replenished as well as jam.

Receptionists were very polite and helpful otherwise, the service was just a little lacking.

It builds the expectation that you're getting a luxury hotel, but it fell disappointingly short.

title: Fantastic jacuzzi suite! Happy children!
text:
We have just returned from a 2 night stay at the Five Hotel. The staff were so helpful and nothing was too much trouble. We stayed in the jacuzzi suite on the ground floor. We are a family of 4 (9 year old twins) and the children absolutely loved this hotel. The balcony is fitted with artificial grass and a hot tub and a seating area. The hot tub is totally private as its covered by a shelter and has curtains to protect your modesty 👍🏻. The children had their own room with a tv and special blue LED lights made to look like the night sky. We had a double bed and the same lights with a tv. The bathroom is a good size too with shower and bath. The room has air conditioning which is a blessing considering the temperature in Paris. 

There's an honesty bar which stocks drinks in a little lounge area which also doubles up as the breakfast area. You can select your own music from the kind of Ipad style juke box. Breakfast was a little disappointing. Not much to go around and one lady running the kitchen and laying out the places. We opted to go elsewhere for food the next day. 

The kids area was the perfect size for them. The adults sleeping area was very compact but perfectly adequate and it is a boutique hotel after all. 

We would highly recommend and will definitely be back. Thanks to all at the Five for making our stay so enjoyable 👍🏻🇫🇷

title: Great alternative to the big Paris hotels, large rooms and great service
text: Loved this small but luxurious hotel.  Pierre Cardin's old mansion converted into a small hotel.  Great location in the 8th (with lots of police street security due to government buildings).  We had a Suite Elysee (401) which was huge, large living room, 2 toilets, great bed and big bathroom.  Service from the desk was excellent and the concierge was able to find 2 great Asian fusion restaurants nearby.  It is a Relais so has an attached Michelin Italian restaurant - Tosca - where we ate the first night.  Breakfast there or in room.  No bar or gym due to small size, but the Bristol Hotel bar around the corner is excellent.
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Nice value for money
text: This is a nice 5 star boutique hotel located at the center of Paris. It has comfortable, clean rooms with friendly helpful staffs. Overall it provides an excellent value for money. This is our second stay at this hotel and we are happy to book a third stay in the future :)
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Great location and intimate setting
text: The staff here are all so friendly and welcoming. The hotel has 12 rooms. Our suite, #302, was lovely with 3 sets of large opening doors to a balcony. The bed is super comfy and the bath is spacious, except the quite small shower but it’s still quite nice. The large walk in closet was nice to keep our luggage out of site. From here it’s an easy walk to everything from Sacre Couer to Notre Dame. Blocks to Champs Elysee but yet on a very quiet street. Shopping nearby and lots of restaurant to choose from besides the Michelin Italian restaurant in the hotel. The drawbacks include no bar but there is room service. Staff is what makes this hotel special.
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Exceptional Hotel Experience
text:
We just completed a three day stay at the Splendide Royal.  It was a truly remarkable hotel visit and added so much to our experience in Paris. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by Caroline (who made our stay that much more exceptional with her professionalism, warmth and attentiveness).  She offered us a glass of champagne (and water)  on arrival as she took our details.  
Our room was spacious and lovely and well air conditioned (something that does not necessarily exist in France).  There were many small amenities in the room that were replenished on a daily basis.  The bathroom was also large and comfortable with two sinks, a separate tub, shower and commode.  We were in Room 302.
I loved the fact that everyone working in the hotel (from the manager, to the front desk staff, to the breakfast servers) were simultaneously professional and warm and extremely helpful.  The boutique hotel experience was accentuated by the fact that we were welcomed by name each morning and evening.  
We will most certainly return to the Hotel Splendide Royal the next time we are in Paris!  Merci à tous pour  votre aide!
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Most memorable Paris trip
text: Customer care and attention to detail was on a different scale.  The hotel location, amenities, ambience and food were of the highest quality. It was, however, the staff at the smallest 5 star hotel in Paris who made our trip so much more memorable and special.
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Marvelous!
text:
Stayed here with the family and had the most marvelous time.  The service was so amazing and the staff really made it one of the best experiences ever.  Everyone who works here is so sweet and kind - they really go out of their way to make sure everything is to your liking and that you are happy.  
The rooms were so clean, the beds were very comfortable and there was a nice intimacy about the hotel.  This is a hidden gem in the city of lights.  Cannot wait to come back!
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Wonderful boutique hotel
text: My husband and I spent 3 lovely nights at the Hotel Splendide Royal Paris last week.  Everything was excellent-- the service, our suite, and beautiful Paris as a backdrop!  This is a small, boutique hotel.  Service is excellent.  The staff works expeditiously to make certain that every comfort is met, every expectation is exceeded.  We stayed in room 501-- a suite with a balcony and gorgeous view of the Eiffel Tower.  It really felt more like our own luxury pied-a-terre in the city than a hotel.  The hotel staff felt more like family, welcoming us home, than employees of a hotel.  In fact, the excellent service started well before our arrival.  I exchanged several emails with the staff in preparation of our trip.  They were warm, friendly and exceptionally helpful in assiting me with preparing for our travels.  Hotel Splendide Royal is well appointed with luxury furnishings and overall a delightfully charming boutique experience.  The only negative experience we had was leaving!
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Vow Renewal in Paris
text: This is our favorite hotel of all time and we have stayed at many wonderful properties!   The staff is constantly kind and proactively helpful, the rooms are absolutely beautiful, the complimentary breakfast is outstanding and the location in just perfect for everything you will want to do in Paris.  The amazing staff even helped by ordering my bouquet and my husband's boutonnière for our vow renewal ceremony.  We had the best time and will always stay at the Hotel Splendide Royal when in Paris from now on.  Highly Recommend if you want a perfect Paris experience!
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: A Superb Place to Stay to Experience Paris
text: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris is without question one of the finest establishment in which we have ever had the pleasure of staying.  The staff, who you will likely know by the first few days are helpful and sincerely interested in your impressions of the hotel, restaurants you visit and Paris's countless sites.  This is the closest you'll get to a "French Downton Abbey" experience,  With only 12 rooms, one does feel like you are staying in a mansion rather than a hotel.  We want to add that the entire staff's helpfulness comes across as an authentic desire on their part to make sure your visit is most memorable.
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Simply perfect
text: I traveled to Paris few times a year before Covid interruption and stayed at various hotels throughout the years including the most renowned ones. But since Hotel Splendide Royal opened its doors in the fall of 2016 it became my number one choice without a doubt. Everything in this hotel is a refined perfection. Located on a quiet street just around the corner from Élysée Palace, its rooms are impeccably appointed, layout is spacious and planned for utmost comfort, the lobby is an exquisite mix of traditional French period pieces and contemporary art. The service and attention by all staff members is beyond reproach. Unlike many other places this one gives its guests a feeling of an elegant and hospitable private home rather than a big city hotel. I hope for many more returns to the best city in the world and for the chance to stay again and again at the beautiful Splendide Royal!
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris

title: Great Boutique Hotel
text: This was our first time in Paris, and the hotel was lovely! It is small, only 12 rooms, but ours was quite spacious. The staff were attentive and the service was great. The restaurant food and breakfast were delicious. The hotel is right next to the Presidential Palace, so we felt safe walking around. It is close enough to walk to the Champs Élysées, Louvre, and Grand Palais. I would return.
name: Hôtel Splendide Royal Paris
