title: the room they gave us very bad very small for 1 adult and 2 kids
text: I booked a hotel way 2 months advance and when we arrived they gave us a very bad room downstairs room 59, the bathroom was made for an open bathroom for someone on a wheelchair is an ok and very small room and the bathroom is not cleaned properly I have seen some dirt and it looks like an emergency room or spare room they gave us I feel very bad, the way they treat us I did spoke to the manager and ask him why he gave us this room he told me there were a lot of families and all the best room has taken, it should not be this way if you advertise triple room it should be a good size for 3 people and the bathroom as well not up to the standard, I was not happy we stayed for 2 nights.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good little hotel.
text:
We came as a family of 3. Mum, daughter and son. The train we got was an early arrival but the hotel allowed us to store our luggage before we checked in. When we did check in we had a room on the 3rd floor which was fine with a large bathroom fitted with bath and shower which is quite unusual for Paris.

The staff at reception and in the breakfast area were great. Breakfast for 3 people for 2 days was €71 which I thought was the only real downside of the experience as when we got there the choice was not very good, maybe if we came down earlier it would have been better.

All in all it's a great little hotel close to Rue des Martyrs and many bars and restaurants. It's very clean and affordable. We would come again.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Friendly hotel in a good location
text:
We spent 5 nights at Touring Hotel as part of a Eurostar package.  We found the hotel well positioned. We walked from Gard du Nord, about 15 mins, probably easier that attempting the stairs in the metro with a suitcase. The metro Cadet is close to the hotel and we also found nearby Notre  Dame de Loret useful, especially when we went to Versailles.

Our room on the third floor was clean, quiet and the lift, although small, was efficient.  The bathroom was good and roomy.  The shower worked well and there was always hot water.  The room was serviced daily.  French hotels do not have the kettle provided - and some of us do like our cup of teas!  However, behind the reception is a kitchen with a kettle, microwave and fridge so I was able to make my own hot drinks and fill a flask for the morning, so if you are like me it is worth taking a few teabags with you.

We ordered breakfast everyday which was 10 euros + tax.  It was lovely.  The buffet included cheese, eggs, pancakes, jams, fruit, cake, toast, cereals, yogurts as well as a roll and a croissant.  We enjoyed it and the lady serving in there was lovely and made us very welcome.

The reception staff were always pleasant and keen to advise on accessing sights.  We walked to Sacre Coeur and Montmartre twice, an uphill walk but well worth the effort. 

The metro was easy - we asked for the large (free) map and that really helped us plan journeys. We also had a two day pass on the batobus, the  hop on, hop off boat.  We enjoyed the full tour the first day ( nearly two hours) then used it to get about and visit the sights.

We would stay at Hotel Touring again if we return to Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Mr Jorge-Agnes Camposano’s family
text: We have excellent stay in this hotel plus a tremendous Manager who treat us as his family. Good breakfast service. The venue to all exciting beauty of renaissance architectural buildings is just nearby. I highly recommend this hotel.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great hotel, inexpensive, great location
text: We thought this place was a joy - an elegant former house, in a great location only 1 minute from metro stop "Cadet" and with loads of excellent cafes and bars in the immediate vicinity. The breakfast was very good for 10 euros, the staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful, and the room was spotless. This is a great place for tourists mindful of costs.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Touring Hotel Paris
text: Lovely clean hotel, big bath in the en suite, friendly staff. Easy location. Would stay again! Lovely classic Parisian feel. Close to a metro station and walkable from Gard Du Nord. Some great restaurant nearby.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Valentines weekend in Paris
text: Excellent service from start to finish of our trip. Spent time making sure that we understood directions and offered advice for getting around Paris. The room was very clean with everything we needed. The staff were polite and patient during our stay. The location is great for transport links and nearby facilities. Would definitely return.
name: Touring Hotel

title: OK hotel, great location
text:
We arrived at 14:20, the man at the reception told us that we would need to wait for 30-35 minutes for our room. We sat down to wait in the waiting area, which had comfortable chairs. Our room was ready already at 14:35.

That was positive, but otherwise the service at the reception was not that good, and certainly not proactive. He only asked if we wanted a map of Paris or breakfast. We had to go back to the reception to ask for the password for the wi-fi as it wasn't available in the room and he did not provide us with that. 

They give you a remote control for the TV with your room number on it when you check in, and you must return it when you check out.

The bathroom had a good size with a bath and 2 bottles of combined shampoo and body wash.
The room was spacious with a twin bed. Some more storage space would have been welcome. The use of electric appliances, including portable kettles, in forbidden in the room.

The location is good, the room is what you can expect (a mini-fridge would have been nice as well as a kettle though), but they should invest some more in customer service.
name: Touring Hotel

title: I would stay again
text:
Large room and bathroom, especially for a budget friendly hotel in Europe!

Comfortable beds, tub with shower, and lovely French style breakfast. The best cappuccino, and a wonderful hostess serving us. Not for the gluten free, but there was a bit of fruit and juice. 

Nearby was a Fran Prix market ( one block), a metro stop, pharmacy, Le Regent Restaurant, and a McDonsld’s (2 blocks). 

In the opposite direction many shops, restaurants, another Metro station, and a Banksy exhibit that seems permanent. Walking distance to the Opera House and a premier shopping experience. 

I would definitely stay here again.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Perfect visit
text:
The stuff was the friendliest in paris.
The location of the hotel is very convenient and close to metro stations for all paris most attractive atrcations.  
The room was big and clean.
 The breakfast was traditional french breakfast - absolutely recommend and tasty. 
We definitely return again.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent
text: Stayed last night room number 5 . A warm welcome from the staff. I was so very happy to stay there after multiple booking modifications. Thanks again. You will definitely be my main hotel for stays In Paris. I do recommend very strongly this hotel ❤️ You deserve your 3 stars. Take care and stay safe.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Surreal experience
text:
As a professional in the industry I can on say this hotel is poorly managed: the phone did not work, you have to skip dirty linen bags in the stairs, the hallway floors are repaired in a chepa sort of way...
But what striked me was the way they treat clients. I was asked by the lady at reception to leave my key even though I was only going to breakfast. When I was asked where was the ironing area she told me it was to the right of the stairs. After I finished ironing there was a toilet there and I tied my tie for the wedding I was attending. She comes barging in and shouts at me, “What are you doing here” apparently I had gone down the wrong set of stairs and was in the staff toilet area. I was impressed by her lack of customer service skills. As I checked out she had the  nerve to ask me twice if the Tv controller was in the room. If it was one of my establishments I would not have her working there as she clearly lacks the people skills for the job. But anyway you just Have to take the whole place with a pinch of salt and think it is the kind of hotel Faulty towers was based on. You understand why it is the cheapest place in the area, the staff are clearly the reason. Because the place is quite nice.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great hotel in a great location
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights on a recent visit visit to Paris. The rooms were very comfortable and the staff were friendly and helpful.
The location was handy for Montmartre,  Pigalle and the Opera areas. It was a few minutes walk to the Cadet metro and near other stations.
There was access to a kitchen with a hot plate, fridge and kettle. The was useful for making hot drinks etc.
We very much enjoyed our stay.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great location - exceptionally clean rooms - great breakfast - extremely helpful staff
text:
Hotel is in a great location - minutes walk from the Opera Garnier area and the Gallery Lafayette.  It is a minutes walk from a Metro station, which then puts all of Paris within easy reach.   The area of the hotel is nice and feels safe.  
The rooms were exceptionally clean.  The wifi was strong and consistent - did not fail us once while we there.
Breakfast was delicious and filling, in an old, stone-walled room that felt like we were eating in an ancient room - the atmosphere was extremely quaint and relaxing.   
The best part - as so many other already commented is the service.  The owners are so welcoming and friendly, and happy to go above and beyond in answering any questions.  We felt like personal guests.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Nice room. Good location. Helpful front desk.
text: Visited pre-covid.  Good location and serviced by ride shares and taxis.  Nice eateries close by.  Room was clean but a bit small.  Tidy small lobby nice for waiting on ground transportation.  Small elevator seems worked slowly but worked.  Good stay.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Decent location, rude staff, subpar experience
text: A three night stay was more than enough. Cons: rude staff, minimal amenities, bad breakfast, no effort to make you feel welcomed or like a guest. Pros: decent room and bathroom size, location two blocks from the metro. This is a 2 star hotel at best. No bottled water? They recommend you drink water out of the sink. Need directions? Why do they have to repeat themselves when they told you the day before? The construction noise from the neighbors? No excuses or apologies. Tough time here. But we didn’t let it ruin an otherwise delightful trip. Just go somewhere else.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great Hotel
text: I must say this hotel is very comfortable. The office staff speak English and are very helpful. The Breakfast is Amazing! Definitely Highly Recommend. When we return to Paris we are staying here. Oh Great Location!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent location. Comfortable and clean
text:
We were 6 friends for long weekend in Paris. 
The hotel is at the 9th quieter and in very good location near 3–4 different metro stations. Many supermarkets around as well as coffee shops and restaurants. The rooms are small and simple but clean and warm. There is no minibar or coffee at the rooms but there is a small kitchen for the gestu, with refrigerator and microwave and hot water. 
It is very comfortable for Jewish, Kosher and next to Chabad and other synagogue. 
Nice and helpful staff. Recommended!!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Classic
text:
This little gem is tucked away in the middle of Paris. It has a charm like not found in most places these days: it is old school; and by that I mean the only modern appliances in the rooms are the phone and TV (But who needs TV when you’ve got T Rex, right?). There is a shared kitchen downstairs, a most genial staff who are happy to help with anything, and nothing is more than an hour away on foot.
It’s truly a special place.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Decent hotel at a great location
text:
We recently stayed here for 3 days. We had visited London before this and hence we were already ready for small rooms. And it was no different here. The rooms were comparatively smaller and the elevator even smaller. Barely 2 person and one luggage can fit. The rooms had basic features with manual locks and one key. We got locked out 2 times in the first hour and had to go to the reception to get help.
The shower area was also very small. The common area and the dinning area were large and spacious. 

The breakfast buffet was filled with variety of delicious breads and pastry options. They bake most of the food fresh in the hotel itself. So you could smell the auroma of the food by 7 am. The best part of the hotel stay. Even on the day of our departure we were able to have the breakfast before we left. The breakfast time was 7.30. We had to leave by 7. But the hotel staff were friendly enough to suggest us to eat whatever was available early and to our surprise quite a few items were ready even that early.

Location is very good. Because of the metro strike we had to either take the bus or walk to most places. Taxi's were trying to rip off at every opportunity and Uber did not have the XL option to take 5 people (We were a family of 5).
name: Touring Hotel

title: Beyond imagination
text:
I stayed at this hotel for two weeks from December 11, 2019. The location, facilities and staff were all good. 

The  good things of location are as follows.
・ 15-minute walk from Opera Garnier
・ 15-minute walk from Paris North Station
・ One minute walk to supermarket (Carrefour City)
・ 3-minute walk to some shops where we can buy side dishes (Cade Street)

The  good things of facilities are:
・ Sufficient space
・ Proper water pressure
・ Clean room and bathroom

There were points such as "no chain on the door", "no provision of drinking water", "no refrigerator in the room (it is in the common space)", and "no security box in the box".

However, these light shortcomings are eliminated by the greatness of the above advantages and the great staffs described below.

I had booked Thalys in advance and planned to go to Belgium, but unfortunately Paris has been on strike since 5 December, the metro was not running and Thalys canceled several  their trains.

Thalys to Brussels, which I booked, were canceled. In addition, a call to the call center was needed to arrange a replacement train. 

Therefore I asked the front desk staff to call the call center instead of me, so they were willing to accept.

They called the Thalys call center for me and arranged another round-trip ticket.After the conversation with the call center was over, they waited until I confirmed my new mobile ticket from thalys. I think it took maybe 40 minutes or an hour in total. 

They devotedly made an effort to understand my bad English. 

Thanks to them, I was able to enjoy Brussels. This hotel was a great hotel.

———
私は2019年12月11日から2週間、このホテルに滞在しました。このホテルに泊まって良かったと心から思っています。

立地の面でのメリットは以下の通りです。
・オペラ・ガルニエから徒歩15分の距離
・パリ北駅から徒歩15分の距離
・スーパー（Carrefour City）まで徒歩1分
・お惣菜なども買えるお店の揃った（cade street）まで徒歩3分

設備の面でのメリットは以下の通りです。
・十分な広さ
・勢いのある水圧
・清潔な室内と、清潔な水回り

「ドアにチェーンが無い」「お水の提供が無い」「冷蔵庫が部屋に無い（共有スペースにはある）」「セキュリティボックスが無い」と言う点はありました。しかし、上記のメリットや下記の通りのホテルスタッフの対応に比べれば、大きな問題にはならないと考えます。

私は事前に長距離便のタリスを予約していて、ベルギーに行く予定を立てていましたが、残念なことに、パリは12月5日からストライキをしていて、メトロは運行しておらず、タリスも欠便が出ていました。

私の予約したブリュッセル行きのタリス もキャンセルになってしまいましたが、ホテルのスタッフに相談したところ、私の代わりにタリスのコールセンターに電話をかけてくれ、別の日の往復便を手配してくれました。

彼らはコールセンターとの話が終了した後も、私のメールアドレスに新しいモバイルチケットが届くのを確認するまで、きちんと対応してくれました。合計でおそらく40分か1時間弱かかったと思います。

彼らのおかげで、私は無事にブリュッセルを楽しむことができました。このホテルは本当に良いホテルです。
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent Choice
text: I booked through Trip Advisor and I would do so again. Rooms are small but perfect for travelers. Customer service is amazing! Easy access to Metro (when they aren't on strike). Also easy to book an Uber. The small bread stores within a block are to die for! I would return again!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good location excellent service
text: Stayed at the hotel for three nights.  The clerks at the front desk were super helpful ... very professional.  The breakfast was outstanding.  Location was good .. Louve  is about 20 minute walk.  The room was small but very comfortable ... we could open the windows to get fresh air which was nice.  I would highly recommend this location.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great customer service
text: Please post this. The Paris hotel Touring Opera Hotel was a diamond in the ruff. It should be rated much higher than it is. 4.0 - 4.5, out of 5 stars. The owners, Gil and his wife were more accommodating than most inn keepers in big name places. Clean, quiet, decorative, safe and warm. They made customers feel at home and always their priority. Paul, on the front desk, was a gentleman of endless information. Breakfast was amazing and Bon Appétit. Large variety and all homemade. The owners are hands-on with their location and their customers needs and wants. When we return, we will definitly stay there. Wait until you receive your room key. !!!! Loved the property. Central location is close to everything you need or want.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good accomodation in a great location
text:
I spent 3 lovely days in Paris in October as part of a European vacation.  The hotel is located on a quiet street in the 9th arrondissement, a beautiful area with fabulous Haussman architecture.  The hotel room was small by American standards but clean and comfortable, nice hot shower.  The room does not have a/c which might be an issue in Summer but was no issue during my stay.  There was a typical buffet breakfast daily which included delicious freshly baked breads and croissants.
Most importantly the hotel is well situated with lots of restaurants, supermarkets and cafes close by.  The Metro station Cadet on the 7 line is about 3-4 minutes walk from the hotel.  That metro line can be used to connect directly or by transfer to most attractions. There are city buses close by but I did not use them cause being from NYC I prefer trains.
Overall Paris is a beautiful city that I cannot wait to visit again.  Just I would visit in November as it was still  a little crowded during my stay.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Very good location
text: We stayed at this hotel for four nights where check-in right away the owner is very nice and informative. We stayed in room 18 on the fourth floor facing the street. The room is very basic but clean and the was comfortable and bathroom was adequate and big enough. The problem was that somebody with chip hammer would wake us up every morning at about 8 am because there was no a/c only fan. The metro stations and the opera house was very close . The hotel is very basic but very good location and the staff are wonderful.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good Choice
text: The Touring Hotel is conveniently located between 2 Metro stops in a neighborhood with lots of restaurants, a supermarket and a launderette.  The hotel is a small, older property and relatively inexpensive.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  Our room was small by American standards but well maintained and comfortable.  The lack of AC was not an isuue in October but might well be in the summer.  Breakfast was served in a lovely room in the basement.  There were fried eggs, rolls, cheese, fruit, coffee, etc. and it proved a good start for the day.  We'd stay again!
name: Touring Hotel

title: A Ten Thumbs Up
text: We LOVED this hotel! We spent three days at this hotel and loved it for its excellent service and friendly reception, its quaint bedroom with shuttered balcony overlooking a synagogue with its historical commemoration to  the Holocaust.  Unfortunately I discovered this too late to take in a visit of the adjoining building.  This hotel is located in a quiet street and it is loaded with quaint charm and architectural interest, and its foyer lounges of which there are two are inviting and very comfortable. Breakfast buffet is included - the breakfast room is downstairs to what was probably the basement/cellar previously and includes gorgeous stone walls and arched cellar doorways. The breakfast selection is generous and you MUST try their croissants - they are the real thing... buttery, flaky but light as air. Hotel is within walking distance of two Metro stations, and many historical buildings most importantly the Opera House. Pubs/restaurants abound in the area.  This is an active area for Hop on/hop off buses should y ou need one.  I hope to revisit this hotel again - it contributed to a memorable stay in Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: lovely hotel tucked into a convenient neighborhood
text: We had a lovely 5 five stay.  The room was large (for Paris).  Delightful, helpful staff.  breakfast croissants, breads eggs, cereals, cheese and salad.  make your own crepes. Wonderful roomy bathroom.  The location in a neighborhood, local shops to pickup a snack.  This is a little secret hideaway.  convenient metro stop.  Could stop back in the middle of the day.  Would stay here again.  A+.
name: Touring Hotel

title: The Perfect Place to Stay!
text: My husband and I spent three nights at the Touring Hotel when celebrating our 30th wedding anniversary and could not have been more pleased with our choice. Every person we had contact with was courteous, professional, helpful and warm. The room was beautifully appointed and the mattress, the most comfortable I have ever slept on in a hotel. To top it off, the breakfast each morning was superb! Fresh pastries homemade each day in addition to other staples such as fruit, cheeses and eggs provided the perfect start to our day. As an example, one morning we were seated and already eating when a woman walk out of the kitchen with a fresh loaf of Brioche to offer us. Ten minutes later, a man came by our table offering fresh crepes. And the croissants were the freshest and flakiest I have had in my 61 years! There was no need to search out a bakery for the best French pastries--we had it right there! IThe Touring Hotel was a highlight of our trip!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Location location location
text: The hotel is in need of an update but the location and price is right.  There is no air conditioning or ceiling fans which is a problem in summer. It has central courtyards that visitors use as smoking areas and the smell and smoke does drift up and into rooms. However, there is a kitchen that can be handy, a breakfast option that is plentiful and the staff are friendly and helpful. The owner said, that the competition of Airbnb he intends to include extra features like a fridge in the room at some point. I would stay there again.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Economy kosher hotel
text: This is a good 3 star kosher hotel conveniently located in the 9th arrondissement. They offer a fully kosher buffet breakfast for 10 € per person daily.  They do not offer Shabbat meals but they set out candles for Fri night, a white tablecloth in the dining room for meals, and a plata for keeping food warm.  There are a number of groceries nearby where tzkeout meals canbe purchased and brought back to be warmed up. Friendly, clean, and umpretentious- it handles most of the needs of the kosher traveler in a very convenient location, close to metro stops and synagogues.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Adorable Hotel
text: This adorable family owned hotel had so much character and was perfect for our first time visit to Paris. The staff was beyond helpful and kind with directions and tips to explore Paris. We felt safe and the convince of the metro close by was an extra plus. When we checked out, we were apologized to for no a/c, we told them we didn’t even notice. Staying here made it for a wonderful memory of Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Shabbat/Kosher Friendly, Good value, Staff very helpful
text: Nice friendly hotel. great for exploring central Paris. For Jewish travelers, kosher breakfast (yummy croissants)+ self boil eggs) every day. Also, for Friday/Saturday: candles, hotplates, urns, and plastic plates and cutlery.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Perfect hotel
text: Only made the booking 2 days before for a last minute holiday. Staff were incredibly helpful and friendly. Hotel was clean, accessible and very central, 2 metros within 2 minutes walk. Also around a 20 min walk to train station for the airport.
name: Touring Hotel

title: If you are on an extremely low low budget this is a good place to stay.
text: When booking my trip to Paris I was trying to save a little money. I came across the Touring hotel with so many great reviews so naturally this is where we stayed. In retrospect I wish I would’ve spent more money and stayed anywhere else. My suggestion to you would be, you don’t get to Paris very often so spend a little extra. The room was clean, however it was incredibly small,even smaller than a New York City hotel.  It did not look like the pictures, bed was made sloppily made every day with only a sheet.  It had absolutely no amenities.  You could not make your own coffee, they had no ice machine, no iron, really nothing in the room to speak of other than two towels and of course no washcloths.  To get into the shower you had to crawl over an incredibly high bathtub, I’m in great shape but I bumped my knees every time try to get over it. The closet was so small, enough to hang a few pieces of clothing and a small shelf for putting your clothes. Generally if you’re traveling to Europe you have big suitcases and need somewhere to put your stuff. We had to put our suitcases on the outskirts of the room, giving us a little place to walk. The electrical outlets are located toward the bottom of the wall so I had to blow dry my hair sitting on my knees because the cord couldn’t reach.  Spend an extra $20 a night and stay anywhere else.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great staff
text: My four night stay at touring was very enjoyable as the staff were as helpful as they could be given the language barrier.  The bathroom was small but all fixtures worked well with plenty of hot water available when time to bathe.  Thank you
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent service
text: I stayed in this hotel with my parents for two days. The location is perfect at a walking distance from the metro and very near to the centre of Paris. The staff was very helpful in assisting with enquires such as what would be the best place to eat with good value in the area...etc. A special thank you to Jilles the hotel manager who stepped up and went the extra mile to sort out an unfortunate problem with the taxi that was supposed to take us back to the airport after checking out and never turned up.He promptly called a replacement taxi and kept in touch with me to make sure I got a refund for the taxi service that was not honoured. I strongly recommend this hotel !
name: Touring Hotel

title: Smaller than you think
text: The staff is extremely nice and friendly I can’t complain there. The room was smaller than I thought. The shower itself was extremely small so if your a bigger person that might be uncomfortable. No ac or heater in the room. So you have to leave ur window open to get some air and ventilation. Thank god there was a cool breeze. Personally I need cool air to feel comfortable and had to leave my window open. Omg at night you could hear everything. If you are a light sleeper that’s going to suck. The breakfast was on point though. Great food and friendly staff. BUT I was under the impression breakfast was included with the hotel. Just checked out and had to pay 10€ for each day I had breakfast. The hotel was safe/clean/ and is in a good location.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Lovely hotel close to many attractions
text: This hotel has great access to the Cadet Metro station as well as many good cafes, and bistros in the neighborhood.   It has a fantastic breakfast that is offered that includes everything from coffee, juice, eggs, croissants, cheese, yogurt, cereal, and several sweet pastries.  It was a great way to start the day.  The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful and I would stay here again, the next time I am in Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Incredibly comfy, welcoming and well-situated
text: We felt really welcomed here, with friendly staff who took the time to get to know us. Very comfortable, quiet and clean - and a lot nicer than the photos on this site suggest. The best thing is doubtlessly the fact that it's excellent value given how close it is to everything... a pleasant 20 min walk to both the Seine and Sacre Couer. Plenty of nice bars and restaurants just a couple of minutes away. Reeeeeally good breakfasts - no need for lunch after one of the breakfasts here (so much good cake, croissants, cheese, eggs, salmon, pancakes etc.etc.!). My one and only criticism is that there are no kettles in the bedroom, so wasn't able to have my essential coffee before getting dressed. Everything else was perfect!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Old World Hotel Without The Charm
text:
This hotel reminded me of one of the hotels my grandparents used to stay at in Miami Beach, Florida before the days of key cards, electronic safes and air conditioning. When we checked in we were handed a key attached to a large brass weight and a TV remote with a sticker on it asking that we return it at check-out. The key to the safe in the room required an 8 Euro deposit to ensure that it was returned. This alone should give you an idea of the type of hotel this is. The room was quite small and the carpet was stained. The bathroom looked like it had been recently renovated, but the shower had no door, resulting in a flooded  bathroom after showering. We happened to be on the first floor, so the fact that the elevator was out of order didn't affect us.

On the positive side, we encountered a female clerk who was quite helpful when we needed someone to speak French to a customer service representative at a local French business. The hotel is located a block away from the Cadet Metro and about a 7-10 minute walk from the Roissy Bus "Opera" stop from CDG airport.

If you're looking for modern amenities, I'd say keep looking. But if this is the only hotel that fits your budget, then it might be just good enough.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent value and comfort
text:
The hotel is very comfortable and excellent value.  There is a very good and ample breakfast - the freshness and quality of the food is good.
The hotel and room was clean
The manager and staff are helpful responsive to requests - service is excellent.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Better than expected, would stay again
text:
By comparison, this was a much better hotel than a nearby one that I stayed at earlier in the week despite the two being priced similarly.  I found the room very bright, well furnished with near new pieces and spotlessly clean.

The pictures posted online actually don't do the rooms justice, if my room was typical.   The linens were all-white, unlike the stodgier coloured bedspreads that appear in many of the room pictures online, and lend the room a much more contemporary aesthetic.  And maybe the lighting was upgraded, as none of the pics I've seen reflect the bright yet warm lighting in the room.  Also, the bathroom was quite generously sized, especially by Parisian standards, and the shower was excellent.

Breakfast was not included and I didn't opt in, so I can't comment on it.  Location is very good and i would most definitely stay here again.  The closest metro is a block away, and for those who are so inclined, there also happen to be a Starbucks and Pret a Manger within a couple blocks.

This is probably going to become my go-to hotel when staying in central Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Spend more for better quality staff & amenities
text:
Airport to the hotel (CDG): There are no (visible) pickup points for Uber, and Lyft is not available in France. However, upon arrival, you will be greeted by a huge influx of locals requesting your “taxi” service. The standard rate for all airport taxis - from the airport to the Paris center (most Paris hotels) - is $55 euros. As far as I could tell, the taxis do not accept major credit cards. So come prepared with at least $100 euros in cash. 

Check-in/hotel/greeting/services etc: As far as I could tell, there were three gentlemen manning the receptionist desk. (1) gentleman appeared to be of Caucasian descent/ethnicity, the other (2) gentlemen appeared to be of Middle Eastern and/or Asian descent. The Caucasian gentleman was the most friendly and accommodating of the (2) - but not by much. My experience with the (1st) gentleman (Middle Eastern/Asian ethnicity) was during the check in process. I was greeted with a half smile and severely broken English. I was charged a Paris or local tax of $13 euros - which was to be paid in cash. The gentleman seemed impatience with my lack of French, and came across quite rude and abrupt. I don’t know if that is some sort of Parisian cultural affect - or if the guy was just plain rude. I arrived at noon and was told that they do not allow check in until after 3pm. I asked if the hotel offered early check in, the gentleman told me “no”, then berated me about booking a day in advance if I wanted to check in early. When I tried to push for more information (again with my lack of French), he rudely told me “just sit down!”. I was allowed to store my luggage in a locked room, while I explored the area, until my room was ready. This was the first gentleman of Middle Eastern descent. 

I came back to the hotel around 2pm, I was greeted by another gentleman (appeared of Caucasian ethnicity) who was “slightly” more friendly and patient with my lack of French. He told me my room was not ready yet and that I could wait in the lobby. The hotel offers free WiFi  but you have to ask for the codes. 

Room/amenities etc: the hotel only has one elevator servicing what appears to be (5) floors. The elevator is incredibly small, only fitting 1 - MAYBE 2, if the guests are petite enough - and 1 luggage bag of “normal” size. When I went to use the elevator, I had to wait in line behind a couple. The couple, seeing how small the elevator was, decided to go up separately carrying 1 piece of luggage per trip (to their room). This is no exaggeration. The room was quaint, clean, and modern/updated. It was slightly bigger than most European hotels, which was a pleasant surprise, and the bathroom appeared to be recently renovated. The bathroom does not have wash cloths. If you are traveling from the U.S., be prepared to bring your own wash cloth, bath sponge, or whatever shower item you use to wash your body and/or face. Thinking that maybe the housekeeping staff forgot to provide wash cloths, I called the receptionist desk (I believe it was the 1st Middle Eastern gentleman on the phone - I could tell by his annoyed tone and accent) and tried to explain to the gentleman (in my best French and most simplest English phrases I could think of) what wash cloths were and if they could be provided. The gentleman actually seemed annoyed and upset! He then blurted out that they do not provide washers and that I could look elsewhere for a dry cleaning service. Again, no exaggeration. The next morning, seeing the 2nd gentleman that I encountered the previous day (appearing of Caucasian descent), I asked him about wash cloths, even going a step further by using my French translator, and I was told that the French equivalent of “wash cloths” are towels. How people in Paris wash themselves with only a towel - or their hands - I’ll never know or understand. I asked about a safe - the 2nd gentleman told me there’s a safe in the room but it costs $8 euros to rent it. He also stated that if I brought the key for the safe back, that they would refund me the $8 euros. The rooms are not equipped with a refrigerator or a microwave. Having had such a difficult time retrieving basic information, I decided not to ask if one was available for usage. The hotel offers breakfast at $10 euros - a service that I did not utilize. The hotel also does not offer room service. When I arrived back at my hotel late (11pm) I asked a 3rd gentleman (also appearing of Middle Eastern descent) if room service was available because I was tired and wanted something quick to eat/wait in my room. The 3rd gentleman actually sighed and said bluntly “what do you want?”. Honestly, by this point, I was just like never mind I’ll go out smdh. 

Location: the location is pretty central and close to a lot of restaurants/bars. However, I noticed that a lot of the restaurants closed around 10pm-11pm. I don’t know why I thought they would be open later. A few feet from the hotel is Dominos (a pizza chain - I didn’t know they were an international chain lol), as well as McDonald’s. The hotel is also close (about a 3-5 minute walk) to a metro station and bus line. Paris has one of the best public transportation systems in the world. The fare for both the metro and the bus are $1.90 euro one way. You can purchase a metro ticket/packet that will allow you to take multiple rides on their metro, bus, retr for under $10 euros. Uber is also widely available in Paris. I never waited more than 5 minutes for an uber. The city also has an abundance of taxi services. As far as I know, their taxis only accept cash. The metro, that is 3 min from the hotel, will take you directly to the Louvre and Musée D’Orsay. The Eiffel Tower is about 20-25 minutes from the hotel (by car/uber/bus/metro etc). 

Housekeeping: was prompt and efficient. 

Temperature: there were moments when I was cold (arrived mid November) and there is a water/steam heater that can be manually adjusted. I kept mine at the highest, and it was still slighter cooler than I would I have liked, but not enough to complain. 

Checkout: checking out was simple. The 3rd gentleman greeted me on my last day. No great effort on his part (again), regarding pleasantries or asking about my stay, which, given how I had been treated during my stay, wasn’t really surprising. I opted for an uber to the airport which was slightly cheaper (40 euros) than the standard taxi rate of $55 euros. Also, the hotel requires 24-hour notice for any taxi requests. My suggestion: just use uber. It’s cheaper, more efficient, and you won’t need cash. 

Overall: This is a 3-star hotel at a very reasonable rate. Had the hotel had a higher star rating, or been priced more exorbitantly, I probably would have been more disappointed than I already was. Would I stay here again? Probably not. If/when I return to Paris, I would pay more money for a better hotel experience. One that provides wash cloths (Italy provides them) room service, and staff who have better attitudes and are patient to the fact that not all of their guests will be fluent in French - as well as try to make an effort to display a more pleasant demeanor, and not “sigh” , or roll their eyes because a guest has a question or a request.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Our room was NOT as the AD picture description. TOO SMALL FOR 3 BEDS.
text:
The room was very very  small as the booking picture on their website. We booked 3 twin beds and with all the luggages the room was still very small. We  asked the front desk guy to help us to weight our luggages for the airport and he didn't do it. We were 2 ladies and he saw us struggling and did not care about it.  Then we asked him to print our flight tickets and his computer and internet never worked. The service is not great in this place. The elevator so tinny only for one person and one small luggage.
The only good thing was the breakfast.
I would book next door at IBIS, which is much modern hotel with a bigger elevator.
name: Touring Hotel

title: It’s not a hotel it’s a cage
text: Please do your research before paying for anything in Paris. This hotel room is suffocating there’s no AC there’s no space to move around not enough space for our bags, it’s depressing. It’s smaller then a regular size kitchen in the states. I’m so upset I wish I knew. I do not recommend this hotel to anyone
name: Touring Hotel

title: Very rude staf!!! Could it be worse? Maybe not...
text:
The hotel is very well located, but there is not air condicioned, and if the weather is hot it's unbearable the room. 

You dont have any frigo bar as it says on the booking sites, but an comunitary one that you can share.....

The staf is very very rude... we found the front door closed very often and we had to wait at least 5 minutes till someone came to open.... 

Central but you will regret it.... Pay more and you will enjoy better ypur hollidays
name: Touring Hotel

title: Paris Vacation
text:
I have stayed at Touring Hotel a few times since 2009 and my last visit was in early December 2017. I do not use the usual hotel search engines as I usually book directly with the hotel directly. The only thing they need is you credit card. 
Touring hotel is nicely situated in the 9th Arrondissement of Paris. There are two Metro stations not far from the hotel. Galleries Lafayette and Le Printemps are at walking distance for those who do not mind to walk 15 minutes.
The hotel has a continental breakfast service. Do not expect to have an English or American breakfast. It's a typical french self serve buffet.
The staff at the hotel are courteous and very helpful.
Do not hesitate to call them or drop them a line to book you next stay in Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Excellent 3 star kosher hotel
text: We stayed a week at the Touring Hotel and loved it. The staff are very nice and accommodating. Gil, the owner, goes out of his way to help you with anything you need. Our room was quiet and located on the courtyard side of the hotel.The breakfast spread is wonderful with fresh baked croissants, pastries, cheeses, espresso, orange juice, eggs, salmon, fresh fruit, breads and more. If you keep Shabbat, there is a hot plate and fridge for your use. They even provide a white tablecloth for a Shabbat atmosphere. All the food is kosher which was a real treat. The hotel is located across from a synagogue and there are kosher markets and other synagogues within a 5-10 minute walk. Located in the 9th androssiment and convenient to the Metro and to walk almost anywhere. There is a safe in the room and if you need to check out early and are flying later in the day they have a locked luggage room.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Happy stay - hotel recommended
text:
Positive things
Location : 50 meters from metro; central and calm quarter with plenty of shops and restaurants nearby.  Rapid check-in and check out. Kind and professional staff. Room not big (difficult in Paris) but enough and better than expected. Not noisy from outside. Good breakfast and decent price for it. 
Negative things
The inside building is relatively old.  Some noise from other rooms (tv, bath). Few electric appliances in the room and no one in the bath room.

Summing up : for me, and given that in Paris the hotels are not cheap,  the value for money has been very good. I recommend this 3 stars hotel for medium budgets travelers.
name: Touring Hotel

title: 9 wonderful days at the Touring in Paris!
text: I like staying in the 9th Arr. and this hotel was a fabulous choice and value. It's on a very short quiet street so you can hear the doves in the morning. It's close to the metro and bus with great walks to shopping, Montmartre, Opera, etc. The breakfast was the BEST and most substantial I've gotten lately in many stays at hotels, offering freshly baked pastries and the best custard among the many choices of eggs, cheeses, smoked salmon, yogurt, cereals, fruit, crepes, etc. It gave my friend and me the energy to walk for miles in Paris neighborhoods every day. The rooms were clean and well furnished with easy to read lamps and BBC and CNN TV in English for news.  Best of all was the impeccable and caring service with multiple languages spoken and 24 hour front desk. Gyl and his team were quick to offer maps, local events, suggestions and help. Neither of us were new to Paris and had many plans on arrival, but the service was much appreciated. I will be sure to recommend and stay again.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Will recommend
text: Nice and clean rooms, lovely staff, located near a metro station. Breakfast had many options in food and drinks. Storageroom for luggage which is locked. Nothing negative to say and will use this hotel again for sure!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Ace 2-night Paris trip
text: Hotel is ideal with clean, cheerful rooms, plus table and chair for novel writing! VG bathroom with hot shower and hair dryer. The breakfast is an amazing spread catering for all nationalities and the staff are extremely helpful.  Quiet at night, the hotel is an ideal location for museums and galleries and we were allowed to leave our cases in the store room until the departure of our late-evening train. I'll certainly be returning.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Very well located hotel
text: The hotel is very comfortable, and the breakfast is really good taking into account the price. It is very well located in the Opera area. Rooms are not very big, but they are correct. Bathroom was remodelled.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good location for an average hotel.
text:
Best value of this hotel is location.  Near metro station.  50 Meters to two supermarkets open till late evening.  Lots of restaurants and bars nearby.   Our room at the 5th floor  wasn't the best of the comfort,  very small,  but still,  to take a shower and sleep, was ok.  The bathroom was indeed great.  Very friendly and helpful reception staff.  Staff was always there to help out with whatever we needed.
Walking distance from the Lafayette mall and Opera Garnier.  Reasonable price.
Very thin walls as we heard everything our neighbours spoke.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Lovely hotel, great stay
text: We returned to this hotel for a second visit, and were not disappointed. Lovely hotel with spotless rooms, friendly staff and great service. Hotel owners went out of their way to make us feel at home. Combined with its good location and reasonable price, this is definitely our choice for any Paris visit.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Middleclass but still ok 👌👍😀
text:
This hotel is really ok if you have one mind that is near the Metro (Cadet) and all the must Do in Paris.
The staff is gentle and polite but that is it.
The breakfast has the most you’ll nees:
Yoghurt, scrambled eggs 🍳, crepes 🥞bread 🍞🥐 fruit 🍇, cheese 🧀and so on
We’d really enjoy it and so Will you 👍😀
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great room, warm welcome
text:
Want to feel at home and comfortable in your hotel? Hotel Touring has very comfortable beds in their spacious rooms  with sparkling bathrooms. The airline lost our luggage and the English-speaking front desk bent over backwards to help us. They made numerous calls on our behalf and did everything they could to support us. McDonald's and Starbucks on The corner if you need them along with Metro stop. You can walk to the  department stores and magnificent Opera Garnier in 10 minutes.Breakfast is plentiful and delicious with excellent coffee.
Hotel Touring is our home away from home in Paris.
Susan and Bob Asher, Chicago
name: Touring Hotel

title: Lovely Hotel for a short city-trip!
text: It is a lovely and tiny Hotel that is well located to the Metrostations. The stuff is very nice and they answer every single question you have. The rooms do not have Aircondition but they do have a van in each room. The breaktfast is good and really enough for you to start in the day. If you are on one of the lesser floors you might hear some of the outside noises during the morning hours. If you have a tight sleep it won't boder you at all. I would stay here again if I hve the Chance! (Greatings from the Lady with the blue hair)
name: Touring Hotel

title: Felt at Home!
text:
We stayed at Touring for a few days on April 6 and we obviously did not arrive expecting 5-start, but let me tell you, this is now my go-too in paris and I'll take this hospitality over a 5-start hotel any-day. 

The beds were great, he breakfast was incredible (and free), the staff were extremely helpful, the location is excellent with everything you need within a few steps and all for a very affordable price considering the conversion to Euro (we are proud Canadians).

Like I said, our go-2 for Paris! See you soon.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Beautiful Hotel, Great Location, Superb Staff, Five Stars!
text: We have been staying at Hotel Touring 2-3 times yearly for the past 15 years. Always a great experience. Perfect location close to the Opera House, Montmartre, restaurants, department stores and Metro only 2 blocks away. Very comfortable rooms with large modern bathrooms. Breakfast buffet is very good with lots of options. Staff is very friendly and helpful. We will be back!
name: Touring Hotel

title: Fantastic value for money
text:
The Touring hotel is a small but excellent hotel very well situated at the 9th sector of Paris, France.
It is clean, renovated, with lovely rooms and bathrooms, very friendly staff and very good price.
The hotel offers a Kosher breakfast which was great for us, and we would most certainly not only come again but recommend it to all our friends.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great Location, Clean rooms, Helpful Staff.
text:
I booked 2 rooms for a group of 4 women for 4 nights.  The hotel was easy to find, just a few minutes walk from Cadet metro station. When we checked in, the male receptionist was efficient, friendly and very helpful. He spoke excellent English.

Both rooms were similar. Small, but clean with twin beds and perfectly adequate for our stay as we didn't really do much more than sleep there. The towels in the ensuite were changed daily and the rom was tidied. The temperature outside was quite cold and it was good to have a radiator in the room that could be used as required.

The  receptionist  helped us connect to wifi just after we checked in and throughout our stay we had no problems using  the wifi in our rooms or in the lobby. 

Although the rooms are small, the hotel also has 2 areas where the 4 of us could sit and plan our day or  enjoy a bottle of wine at the end of the day and there's a fridge in the luggage room where guests can keep food.  On our last day 6 of our friends met up with us at the hotel and again the hotel staff were very accommodating in allowing us to leave luggage and use this area to chat etc.
 
There are vending machines where you can buy a coffee, water etc. at any time but there's also a buffet breakfast available. We had breakfast one morning (cost 10 Euros) - nice coffee, orange juice decent range of food and plenty to eat, although I'd have preferred more fresh fruit to be offered but overall it was value for the price. The member of staff on duty kept topping up & clearing up with quiet efficiency, He filled the coffee machine and delivered me a fresh coffee when he noticed the milk had run out.

The hotel was an excellent base for our city trip and the staff were all top class, flexible, good humoured and most spoke good English.  I would certainly consider returning if wanting a base in Paris in the future.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great hotel
text:
We came my son and I to a 6 days visit in this graet city.
Great hotel. Location very near to the Metro station.
Clean rooms.
Great breakfast. A great various of food.
Great staff. Very kind friendly and helpful. Speaking English as well.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Homey warming well located hotel.
text:
We checked in at late night. received a very warm room by a very nice person.       
 The rich breakfast in a stone decorated hall gives you the best feeling to start the day. 
We stayed for 5 nights had any assistance we needed from the lovely staff.
 The location of the hotel is great, metro close by, the opera, the folies bergere  , many restaurants and other shops, all in a very short walking.
we recommend very much this hotel and for sure will stay there again in the next visit to Paris.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Hotel with character, convenient location, but dark and small room
text:
The hotel is very conveniently located next to the "Cadet" metro station, and about a 10 minute walk from the Gare du Nord (if you are coming from CDG, that's where you'd want to get off the train you boarded at the airport). The nightly rate was fair for a 3-star hotel in Paris. I am giving four stars to the friendly staff and the location, however I do have some reservations about the room I was given for which i am giving the hotel an overall three-star score. The room was quite dark indeed, and the wall lamps didn't provide good lighting. The room was also in the back of the building with the window facing a shaft through which not a lot of daylight came in. You may want to ask beforehand which room you will be given. As a result of the lighting condition, I can't really tell how clean the carpet and the bed comforter were. The bed sheets themselves seemed fairly clean, but were yellow in color; in other words, they were old and should be upgraded with new ones. The pillows too weren't that great. Furthermore, the room was small compared to the photos posted on the various hotel booking sites (my room was a double with twin beds), which seemed a bit misleading, in my opinion. 
The lobby is neat and clean, has a good vibe, and seems to have been recently remodeled.
 
Breakfast is not generally included in the room price. I can't comment on it because I didn't have breakfast at the hotel; instead I preferred to get a croissant and a coffee at some bar around the city. There are plenty of options near the hotel itself. 

Finally, two more things: 1) if you are traveling with a large suitcase, be aware of the fact that the elevator is really tiny; 2) if you need to mail postcards, there is a mail dropbox at the entrance of  the "Cadet" metro station (don't go down the stairs, it's at street level!).
name: Touring Hotel

title: good location
text:
Good location and good price! Around you have all the facilities you need: metro, restaurants, Sturback's, Mc Donalds and supermarkets! 
The staff was kind of okay (very french) and the landlord (I guess!) was very helpful in indicating some places to eat. Good cleaning of the room, except for our last night but 
I would recommend it.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Heart-warming hotel in the middle of Paris
text: I've visited Paris with my friend late September and stayed for 5 nights in this lovely little hotel. To start, it was very well located in the Opera area and really close to 2 metro stations : Cadet (2 steps away) and Notre Dame de Lorette. Then, the staff were really nice and helpful, they weren't bothered at all welcoming us at around 11pm for a late check in. The room was very clean and cosy and not as little as expected , au contraire , it was big enough with a big bathroom ! even with the cold weather it was warm but The view wasn't that amazing. We didn't have a refrigerator in our room so when we brought chocolate they were nice enough to put it in a safe place in the restaurant's refrigerator . Overall it was an excellent experience. I very much recommend the hotel and will be booking it surely for my next visit
name: Touring Hotel

title: Nice weekend in Paris
text: I went to Paris for a long weekend.  The Touring is nice.   Staff was kind and helpful, rooms clean, quiet and spacious.  Beds comfortable.  Bathroom had hot shower, toiletries, and was recently remodeled.  The decor is classic, not contemporary.  It is located in a vibrant area very close to three different metro stations and within walking distance to the Opera area that has lots of restaurants and shopping.  The hotel has TV and wi-fi.  I arrived early and there was no problem checking in early either.  They also kept my bag for a few hours when I checked out.  Couldn't be better.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Near Metro but no concern for the guests
text:
Bed ok
Warm  room with no aircondition
No wiew at all 
No Walter, no glasses, no waterbolier for a cup of te or coffee
Expensive breakfast, 10 euro per person 
Montmartre in walkingdistance, and near Metro. Several resurants in a few minuter walk from the hotel
name: Touring Hotel

title: Great for those on a budget
text: This hotel is very basic but the staff are friendly and the price was right. Location is great...walking distance to red light district/Montmarte. Close to transport, etc. Free wifi! There's also a safe you can pay for if you want to store valuables and they offer breakfast for 10 euros, but I think it's probably better to eat in a restaurant.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Cheap friendly and cheerful.
text:
I started staying here after the ibis next door crept their prices up and up. It's more old fashioned but the rooms are nice and new bathrooms. 
I like it as the service and reception is very friendly and helpful. 

I think the standard of the rooms can vary as it is a smaller independent hotel.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Good hotel overall
text:
Touring hotel has great location near the Opera, the hotel beds are comfortable, but the room is very plain, the bathroom is good , but basic.
The safe in the room is not working well, so if you got something of value , you better keep it on you .
The breakfast is basic with : bread, coffee, fruits, and eggs.
name: Touring Hotel

title: Simple and nice
text: Its a nice hotel, not bad for a 3 stars. Positive aspects: the location, with a metro station nearby; and for those ones that don't want to spent much in food, you have 2 supermarkets and a macdonalds! title: Probably Not the Hotel I Will Be Touring Again
text:
My hopes were high for this hotel as I had read good things about it, so we booked and pre-paid for our ten day vacation here; however, my first impression of the hotel wasn’t favorable. I had read that the staff there were friendly but it wasn't entirely true. This tainted our stay and affected my entire outlook. It’s not like it was my first time in Paris, so this was an exception. 

Granted, we arrived at Touring Hotel early in the day.  We got there at about 11:30 a.m. and were told by the desk clerk that it was too early to check in, that the rooms were being cleaned, and that check in was at 3 p.m. This was understandable at the time.  The clerk did offer to store our luggage. He then took us down the hall to a large closet that was already nearly full and walked away – leaving us to hoist our three suitcases up onto shelves with no help, not even propping the door open so that it would not lock behind us while we were trying to make space. 

After we stowed our luggage, we left the hotel to find some lunch and kill some time.  We walked around and found plenty of brasseries nearby to eat and returned about 2:00. By then we were thoroughly exhausted so we checked with the same clerk to see if our room might possibly be ready. He smirked and said no, not until 3:00. We went into the lobby and sat for another 30 minutes. I then asked the clerk if perhaps he could check on our room again; it seemed rather unusual to me that every single room in the hotel wasn’t ready until exactly 3 p.m.  Plus, it was now 2:30, which I considered close enough for a client that had pre-paid a ten day stay. I also told the clerk that my husband, who was now falling asleep in a chair, needed to lie down and take his medication.  His response was, “you just need to be patient, Madame.”  My response was a stern look and an abrupt, "No, no, I don't. I've pre-paid you a lot of money for our stay."  As I walked away he checked his computer and magically our room was ready two minutes later. 

Entering the second floor accommodation, we were impressed with the size and the arrangement.  The bathroom was also spacious by European standards, and very clean.  There was no shortage of towels, linens or bath sundries, and anything we needed for our room was quickly supplied each day. It is true, though, that the walls are actually extremely thin in the rooms and many nights we had trouble sleeping because of the noise. Also, we had a courtyard view which we thought was charming until we quickly realized that was where the smokers went to hang out and the smoke and voices waft into the upper floor rooms if you open your windows, which you pretty much have to do to get air circulation. The street side might be quieter, but then there may be issues with early morning deliveries. 

Wireless was free, but as others have mentioned, we had to go to the front desk every two hours for a password; however, we weren’t online there much and usually just timed it to when we came back for a break before dinner.  We found that there are many, many places in Paris now that have free wireless anyway, so that wasn’t too much of a problem, but I do agree that it was inconvenient to have to ask every time.  We were happy to do so when “Patrick” was on duty because he was the most delightful clerk we encountered, next to the woman on duty in the mornings who gave great directions and travel advice.  

As directions go, Touring Hotel is in the center of Paris, which is good and bad. I have stayed on the left bank and in the 1st Arrondissement near the Seine, so it was a little frustrating to walk outside and not see anything of note here.  You are basically surrounded by restaurants and office buildings. Cadet Metro is two blocks away and many things are within a "fair" amount of walking distance but the problem is that Cadet isn’t the most accessible line to many attractions and you do a bit of transferring.  Be sure to buy a Metro pass for your stay to make this easier. Also, the hotel requires that you leave your room key anytime you leave, but rest assured there is always someone on duty to let you back in. 

Finally, breakfast was included in our package and was really nice (eggs, various types of hot beverages, juice, fruit, yogurt, cheeses, croissants, cakes, breads and even a crepe table).  When you enter the dining room, you are required to give your room number to one of the attendants. The maître d', Peter, was attentive and friendly. 

This hotel was a place that I had heard good things about and one in which I wanted to set up as a recommendation. Perhaps if we had not been treated so rudely the first afternoon, my thoughts would have been more positive as it is a charming building.  Unfortunately the poor customer service that day was unfair.  A kind word, an offer of internet time while we waited, or even a cup of coffee would have gone a long way. When I am spending ten days and a lot of money at a hotel, I only need to “be patient” within reason. I plan to return to Paris but it would take something special for me to give Touring Hotel a second chance.

My biggest complaint goes to the cleaning staff in the morning. I stayed over a weekend and went out on both Friday and Saturday night so had a long sleep on Saturday and Sunday mornings. Well, almost. The cleaning staff was so loud, chitchatting in the corridors, that you couldn't really sleep! Not professional at all.

title: Mums 70th treat
text:
I chose this hotel as I got a really good deal from a website that provided us with a superior room and macaroons!  Yum.
The journey from the airport into Paris, if travelling by train and metro, is a little tiresome and long winded with all the changes, however, the metro is literally two seconds round the corner from the hotel and the main line to get you to all the places you need in central Paris.  That is why I chose this hotel due to its location.
It isn’t central by any means but only ten to fifteen mins by metro to anywhere really.
The standard of the hotel is good and the breakfast offered was adequate and lovely enough for us to fill up ready for the day ahead.  The decor is relaxing and modern and we enjoyed it.  The best bacon I’ve tasted for a long time!!
Another lovely touch if you have toddlers, is the sweet station and kids corner.
Yes the rooms are small and so is the lift, but do you know what, if you can’t all fit in do it in two separate journeys.  It is an old French building and they have done their best with the facilities the building allows space for.
We found the rooms and hotel decor to be tastefully furnished and the beds lovely and comfy.  
We had a lovely meal just across from the entrance to the metro at a Pizzeria and the food was lovely.
Overall it was a lovely stay and we chose this hotel due to the fact that it wouldn’t be as long a journey back to the airport on our return home.
